author: mdrewt
body:
## lp-03 — Nightly failure notification

The five nightly gates had teeth and no voice: `mutation-server` was RED for five consecutive
nights with nobody reacting, because failure handling existed only as a prose triage comment above
each job. This slice gives them a voice, and pays the price the spec warned was *not* free — the
`if: always()` an artifact upload needs is exactly the line `jobIsNotNeutered`'s flat scan rejects,
so the predicate is rewritten in the same commit.

**Items: none**

### What changed

- **`notify` job** (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`): fans in over all five jobs (`needs:`), opens
  **exactly one issue per non-success job** via `gh`, naming the job and linking the run. The
  failing set is enumerated from `toJSON(needs)` with `jq` — never five hardcoded branches, so a
  sixth job cannot be silently dropped. No `--label` (a nonexistent label fails the API call), no
  `|| true`, no `continue-on-error`; the step `exit 1`s if it fires and opens nothing.
- **`issues: write` lands in the SAME diff as the step** (the spec's CRITICAL clause), scoped to
  the `notify` job. Top level stays `contents: read` — the mutation jobs compile third-party build
  scripts under `cargo-mutants` and must never hold issue-write. A committed predicate asserts that
  negative space.
- **`mutants.out/` uploaded from both mutation jobs** with `if: always()` and distinct artifact
  names (v4 hard-errors on duplicates).
- **`jobIsNotNeutered` carve-out** (`evals/nightly-smoke-wiring.eval.mjs`): admits `if:` only on an
  `actions/upload-artifact` step and only with the value `always()`. Everything else got *stricter*
  — see "hardening" below.
- ADR-0200; `ARCHITECTURE.md` note; `DIGEST.md` regenerated by `just adr-digest`.

### EARS → proof

| EARS | Proof |
|---|---|
| WHEN any nightly job fails → open exactly one issue naming the job and linking the run | Real-file Check 21 + TEETH Q/R; **drill arm B: two issues, correct attribution, run URL in each body** |
| WHEN several jobs fail → not more than one issue per job | TEETH U4 (a second live `gh issue create` REDs); drill arm B opened exactly 2 for 2 failing jobs and 0 for the 3 green ones |
| WHEN a mutation job **fails** → upload `mutants.out` | Checks 18/19 + TEETH P (a step with no `if:` at all REDs — the default `success()` is the bug); **drill: `mutants-out-core` present on the failing path** |
| A scope-narrowing flag still REDs; the carve-out admits `if:` only on an upload step | Check 13 (`mutateServerRecipeIntact`, unchanged) + TEETH O (24 fixtures: `if:` on a run/checkout step, adjacency-smuggle, impostor `uses:`, `if: false`/`success()` on the upload step, job-level `if:`) |

### Forced-red drill (ADR-0010 — assert the ISSUE EXISTS, not that a step exited 0)

Run for real on a throwaway `drill/lp-03-forced-red` branch with the gate jobs stubbed (now deleted):

- **Arm A — grant reverted** ([run 32088740459](https://github.com/mdrewt/monster-realm/actions/runs/32088740459)):
  `notify` fired and `gh issue create` failed with `GraphQL: Resource not accessible by integration
  (createIssue)`; the step exited 1, `notify` concluded **failure**, and **no issue was created**.
  This is the empirical proof of the premise the slice is built on — and it fails *loudly* only
  because there is no `|| true`.
- **Arm B — grant restored, two jobs RED** ([run 32088793844](https://github.com/mdrewt/monster-realm/actions/runs/32088793844)):
  `notify` concluded **success** while the run concluded failure; exactly two issues
  (`nightly failure: mutation (run …)`, `nightly failure: mutation-server (run …)`), none for the
  three green jobs, `mutants-out-core` artifact present.
- Cleanup: both drill issues closed, drill branch deleted local+remote, `gh issue list --state open`
  diffed back to its pre-drill baseline.

### Hardening the carve-out bought (found by red-teaming our own gate)

An adversarial pass wrote the *cheating* implementation and got the whole eval green with a broken
notifier; a second wrote the *cheating workflow*. Both are closed and pinned by teeth:

- **The recipe must be the FIRST `run:` step**, and no `env:` in a guarded job may carry `PATH:`.
  A step ahead of the gate can write a shim `just` onto `$GITHUB_PATH` — the exact recipe text is
  still present, no `if:`, no `continue-on-error`, and the job reports success having tested
  nothing. Demonstrated end-to-end against the first implementation.
- **`continue-on-error` is now an allowlist** (literal `false` only). The old truthy blacklist
  admitted `${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' }}` — false under the `workflow_dispatch` a drill
  uses, true on every real cron night: a neuter calibrated to hide from its own verification.
- **Own block extraction.** A 2-space comment inside a job truncates the shared `extractJobBlock`,
  which hid a neuter below it. `jobIsNotNeutered` now uses an in-file `strictJobBlock`;
  `extractJobBlock` is untouched (10 callers, 4 evals, outside `touches:`).
- **Anchored key matching** (`"if":`, `if :`), **comment-stripped condition matching** (`if: true #
  …failure…skipped…` passed before), and **fail-closed** on flow-style steps, flow `steps:`
  sequences, YAML aliases/merge keys, a missing `steps:` key and a missing step dash.
- **`cancelled` added to the notify condition**: a `timeout-minutes` expiry concludes a job as
  `cancelled`, satisfying neither `failure` nor `skipped` — a red-and-silent night. `smoke-republish`
  carries a 20-minute timeout; the mutation jobs run 1.5–2.5 h against the 6 h cap.

### Gates

- Full `just ci` green locally (exit 0, run twice by the verifier): 87 evals PASS / 0 FAIL, 2461
  client tests, rustfmt/clippy/nextest/wasm/typecheck clean.
- **Verifier PASS** with 11 mutation bite-proofs — deleting `issues: write`, flipping the upload
  `if:` to `success()`, deleting an upload step, dropping a `needs:` entry, appending `|| true`,
  moving `if:` to the run step, inserting the shim step, adding `env: PATH:`, duplicating the
  artifact name, dropping the `cancelled` term, removing the zero-guard — each REDs with a specific
  message. Teeth census: 101 → 194 labels, set only grew; the pinned pre-existing teeth
  (`I-coe/I-if/I-absent/I-good/I-smoke-positive-control`, `M5-*`) are byte-identical to master.
- Lenses: `planner` → `reviewer` + `red-team` (plan) → `tester` (RED, two hardening rounds) →
  implementer → `reviewer` + `red-team` + a GitHub-Actions-semantics auditor → `verifier`.
  Domain auditors (`reducer-security-auditor`, `desync-guard`) were **not** run: the diff contains
  no `server-module/`, `game-core/` or client code — stated rather than skipped silently.

### touches-delta

Declared `touches:` — `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`, `evals/nightly-smoke-wiring.eval.mjs`.
Beyond the literal set (all standard doc companions):

- `docs/adr/0200-nightly-failure-notification.md` — **the supervisor assigned no ADR number**; 0200
  was next-free and no sibling branch or open PR existed on this repo at branch time. Flagging for
  the audit.
- `docs/adr/DIGEST.md` — generated by `just adr-digest`, drift-gated in CI; adding an ADR requires it.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — one targeted paragraph in the nightly-gates section.

`docs/adr/0183-*.md` was deliberately **not** touched: ADR-0183 D5 recorded "no issue-creating
Action" as the *reversible default* while decision-hook #14 was open, so lp-03 exercises that
reversibility rather than amending it — and the reciprocal `**Amended-by:**` back-link an `Amends:`
relation would demand is outside this slice's boundary. Supervisor follow-up if a formal relation
is wanted.

### boyscout-delta

None. The three comment blocks in the eval that asserted "decision-hook #14 is OPEN — do NOT add a
notification Action" were rewritten because this diff makes them false (doc-vs-code honesty on a
file the slice already changes), not as opportunistic cleanup.

### Risks / follow-ups

1. **Issue volume.** One issue per failing job per night, no cro

author: oluwafemidiakhoa
body:
## Summary

Adds a governance-preserving national FAAC evidence automation pipeline.

- discovers FAAC releases only on allowlisted official government domains
- archives exact official HTML bytes in Postgres with SHA-256 fingerprints
- deterministically extracts core national claims and explicit month semantics
- matches only existing real jurisdiction periods and hardens missing month fields under strict consistency checks
- reuses the existing national import/validation/reconciliation pipeline
- defers missing/unpublished periods, quarantines unsafe evidence, and prevents jurisdiction-source reuse
- never approves or publishes automatically
- adds a dedicated national review API and UI with active reviewer/administrator identities loaded from the database
- preserves four-eyes publication enforcement in the existing pipeline
- adds a daily GitHub Actions collector with no reviewer or publisher credentials
- adds migration and automation tests

## Governance guarantees

The collector has no approval or publication identity. Evidence reaches the public API only after explicit human approval followed by publication by a different active administrator. Existing provenance and source-precision reconciliation rules remain authoritative.

## Notes

The durable archive uses `national_evidence_candidates.content` for the retained exact official bytes. `SourceDocument.storage_path` is rewritten to a stable `db://national-evidence-candidates/<id>` reference after import, avoiding ephemeral `/tmp` provenance.

author: tedus-ai
body:
Second half of the folder-first work. #21 made the folder the source of truth; this removes the Save step, matching `Thermal-Test-Report-Builder`, where every action writes straight through.

## The flush

Each screen store already tracked its unsaved edits. That flag used to gate a Save button; it now signals that a flush is due. One watcher covers all six — the rule is identical for each, and a scheduler per store would be six chances to miss one.

`solverStore` is **deliberately excluded**. Its `DIRTY` means a solved result is stale, not that something needs writing. Re-solving is an engineering decision the tool must never take on the user's behalf, so auto-persist never touches it. There is a test asserting exactly that, because conflating the two `dirty` meanings would silently break staleness detection.

Timings chain deliberately: store flush 350 ms → project commit 400 ms → folder write 800 ms, so a burst of typing produces one flush, one commit and one file write, in that order.

## What was removed

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Header | Save action |
| Screen 01 | Save Project, Save & Continue → **Continue**, Cancel |
| Screen 05 | Save button |
| Six screens | `● Unsaved / 未儲存` badges |
| Status bar | Dirty State and Save Status cells → one **Project State** cell |
| Routing | `navigationGuard`, `UnsavedChangesModal`, `useGuardedNavigate` |

The route guard existed to protect unsaved work. There is none, and a modal that can never fire is worse than no modal, so `useGuardedNavigate` collapses back to `useNavigate` across all 17 call sites.

## Creating a project stays explicit

Until the first create there is no file to write into, the project id is still editable, and committing per keystroke would leave `F.tnv.json`, `FR.tnv.json`, `FR1.tnv.json` in the folder. So new projects get a **Create Project** button; everything after that is automatic, and the action bar says so rather than leaving it to be guessed.

One consequence worth naming: validation no longer blocks persistence for an existing project. A field you have half-filled is written as it stands, exactly as a document editor would. The validation panel and project health still flag it — they just no longer stand between you and the disk.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/data/autoPersist.ts` | New. Watches the six stores, flushes each shortly after it goes dirty. |
| `src/data/autoPersist.test.ts` | New. 6 tests. |
| `src/project/ProjectActionBar.tsx` | Create / Continue / Duplicate / Archive; no Save or Cancel. |
| `src/app/TopHeader.tsx` | Save action gone; project switching no longer asks about unsaved work. |
| `src/app/BottomStatusBar.tsx` | Two save cells → one Project State cell. |
| `src/app/AppShell.tsx` | Starts auto-persist; drops the modal and save handler. |
| 17 screen/panel files | `useGuardedNavigate` → `useNavigate`. |
| deleted | `navigationGuard.ts`, `useGuardedNavigate.ts`, `UnsavedChangesModal.tsx` |

## Verification

- `npm test` — 471 passed (24 files), 6 new
- `npm run build` — `tsc -b` clean
- **Chromium**, against an injected directory handle: header actions are exactly `Import, Export, Settings, Help`; no `Unsaved` or `未儲存` text survives anywhere in the rendered app; no `Save Project` button; the action bar states that changes save automatically; renaming a project reaches the file with nothing pressed; moving between screens no longer stops to ask. No page errors.

Tests cover: a dirty store flushing without any Save; a burst coalescing into one flush; silence while the project is new; solver staleness never triggering a re-solve; an existing project's edit persisting unaided; and a never-created project staying off disk.

author: indrolend
body:
## What changed

- Added one canonical desktop scene-sun definition: `const Vec3 SCENE_SUN_VECTOR{30.0f, 60.0f, 25.0f}`.
- Kept stylized fake-shadow projection amount separate as `constexpr float SHADOW_PROJECTION_SCALE = 0.5f`.
- Made both `GL_LIGHT0` and `drawGroundShadow()` consume the canonical scene-sun vector.
- Changed no fill-light, phone-light, ambient, fog, material, shadow opacity, or other renderer values.

## Why

The desktop renderer previously encoded the same conceptual sun direction twice: once in the `GL_LIGHT0` position and again as component ratios in fake ground-shadow projection. Changing one without the other could make illumination and shadow direction diverge while still compiling and passing unrelated tests.

The new ownership contract is:

`SCENE_SUN_VECTOR` → `GL_LIGHT0` and fake ground-shadow direction

while `SHADOW_PROJECTION_SCALE` remains an independent artistic property.

## Numerical behavior

The existing values are preserved:

- `30 / 60 = 0.5`
- `25 / 60` remains the Z/Y ratio
- `0.5 * 30 / 60 = 0.25`
- `0.5 * 25 / 60 = 25 / 120`

The scene-sun object is `const`, rather than `constexpr`, because the current `Vec3` constructor is not `constexpr`; MSVC caught this during the first focused build attempt. This changes no runtime values.

## Verification

Validated on Windows using the repository's current desktop release path:

- renderer-only `git diff --check`: passed
- CMake configure: passed
- MSVC Release build: passed
- `ctest --test-dir build/desktop-release -C Release --output-on-failure`: **18/18 passed**
- `DigitalBreakdown.exe --smoke-test`: passed with `SMOKE_TEST_OK frame=8 room=1 battery=100.00 targets=32`
- final commit was constructed directly from base `86066c3c20879d2b3cc2b84bfc536869d3dc9a99` with only `native-desktop/DesktopRenderer.cpp` staged

Deterministic visual proof was subsequently run in disposable PR #48 against exact refs A=`86066c3c...`, B=`4f6f9c0...`, C=`b76953e...` using Xvfb + Mesa software OpenGL and isolated persistent state.

- established `--capture-cpu-demo`: **150/150 A↔B frames byte-identical**, MAE `0.0`, max channel delta `0`
- cinematic camera sweep: **90/90 A↔B frames byte-identical**, MAE `0.0`, max channel delta `0`
- final verifier run `32097431945`: passed

This directly proves the ownership refactor preserves rendered output in both deterministic fixtures. A manual physical-Windows-GPU visual comparison has not been executed, so no cross-driver parity claim is made.

## Out of scope

This PR intentionally does not address the separate fixed-function OpenGL question of model-view state when `glLightfv(GL_POSITION, ...)` captures directional light coordinates.

author: fahadqtr
body:
## Summary

Fully retires the legacy Talabat CSV export branch. INT.2F.1 decoupled `channel_variant_mappings` persistence into the certified `syncTalabatMappings` boundary; this phase re-homes the **trigger** off the CSV route, then retires the route, its UI, and the dead CSV serializer. The Export Center is now the **only** operator-facing Talabat export path.

**No behavioral change** to Talabat XLSX/ZIP package output, `SELLABLE_LISTING` flattening, mapping semantics/cardinality/keys, order-deduction, inventory, availability, lifecycle, or ECL. No schema change. No production writes.

Base `d9edb55` → head `a01a13d`.

## Remaining legacy Talabat surface — before → after

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/export/[channel]` talabat branch | live CSV + mapping side-effect | **410** for every channel → Export Center |
| `components/TalabatExport.tsx` (CSV UI) | rendered | **deleted** |
| `/import-export/export` page | hosts CSV trigger | **redirects** to `/v2/export/talabat:malikas` |
| `talabatResultToCsv` (+ `csvCell`) | CSV serializer | **removed** (dead) |
| mapping persistence | route GET side-effect | **re-homed** to `catalog-sync.server.ts` |
| `buildTalabatExport` / `resolveExactChannelId` / `decideExportGate` / `isApprovedForTalabat` | route + shared | **retained** (now used by catalog-sync + shared) |
| `TALABAT_HEADERS` | route + package | **retained** (package + actions) |
| `/api/export/images` | TalabatSync dependency | **retained + documented** |

## Mapping sync — new caller

Per the agreed design (**package-route side-effect**): new server-only `lib/talabat/mapping-sync/catalog-sync.server.ts` → `syncTalabatMappingsFromCatalog(actor)`. It lifts the legacy route's mapping logic **verbatim** — same bounded reads, candidates via `buildTalabatExport` over the **full valid catalog** (identical cardinality/keys/`mapping_status`), exact-channel resolution, fail-closed `decideExportGate` — and delegates to the INT.2F.1 `syncTalabatMappings` boundary (**`persistTalabatMappings` not duplicated**). Invoked from the **writer-gated** `/api/export/talabat/package` route after a successful generate; counts surfaced in `X-Talabat-Mapping-*` headers; a mapping-write hiccup never deletes the generated package. Never throws.

## Legacy route retirement behavior

`/api/export/[channel]` → **410 Gone** for `shopify`/`snoonu`/`rafeeq`/`talabat` (each pointing to its Export Center destination), `400` for unknown. No CSV generation, no reads/writes remain.

## Legacy UI retirement

`TalabatExport.tsx` deleted; `/import-export/export` permanently redirects to the Export Center. Talabat Orders and other Talabat workflows untouched.

## /api/export/images decision

**Retained.** `components/TalabatSync.tsx` still calls it (two live fetches). Not retired speculatively; the guard pins the dependency.

## Order-deduction compatibility proof

`lib/talabat/resolution-context.ts` is **unchanged** — still reads `channel_variant_mappings` by `channel_id + master_product_id + master_variant_sku` (+ `channel_product_id`, `exported_sku`, `exported_barcode`, `mapping_status`). Because candidates are still computed by `buildTalabatExport` and written by `persistTalabatMappings` (via the boundary), the persisted rows are identical → order dedup reads the same keys, same cardinality. Guard-asserted.

## Dead symbols removed

`talabatResultToCsv`, `csvCell` (CSV serializer, route-only). Everything else classified in the audit was proven still-used and kept.

## Tests / guards / gates

- **New** `int2f2-retirement-guard.test.ts` (6): route fully retired (410, no CSV/flatten/persist, no reads); mapping re-homed to server-only catalog-sync delegating to the boundary (no dup writer); no legacy ids / fuzzy / inventory / availability writes; Export Center sole path (UI deleted, page redirects); order-dedup keys intact; images retained.
- **Updated** `int2f-retirement`, `int2f1-mapping-sync`, `ch3b-writer-allowlist`, `talabat/export`, `hub-cleanup` guards to the retired + re-homed reality.
- **typecheck** 0 · **test** 3965/3965 · **lint** 0 errors (73 warnings, −1) · **build** exit 0 (placeholder env; sandbox lacks Supabase env for the unrelated `/catalog/health` prerender) · **audit `--audit-level high`**: no `package.json` change → zero new deps → unchanged; CI runs the real audit.
- **Vercel:** preview build runs on this PR.

## History

Talabat package export already records durable Export History via the existing `malak_audit` framework (`talabat_package_export`), unchanged. The re-homed mapping sync adds the existing `talabat_mapping_sync` audit row via the boundary. No new history logic invented. **Remaining Integration debt:** none introduced; a per-run mapping-sync summary surface (beyond the response headers) could be a future nicety but is not required.

## Confirmations

- Production changed: **NO**
- Schema changed: **NO**
- Order deduction changed: **NO**
- Talabat package output changed: **NO**
- Inventory changed: **NO**
- Availability changed: **NO**
- Lifecycle changed: **NO**
- ECL semantics changed: **NO**
- Legacy Talabat export reachable: **NO**
- PR merged by Claude: **NO** (Draft)

author: ewoooo
body:
## 요약

로컬 main에 쌓인 네 갈래를 stage로 올립니다.

### 1. 저장소 경계 정규화 (`refactor/repository-boundary-normalization`)

저장소 경계에서 Payload 관계(depth>0)를 id로 좁혀, 관계가 문서 객체로 바뀌며 `=== id` 비교가 조용히 깨지는 계열을 막습니다(`src/lib/payload-relationship.ts` 신설).

### 2. 스튜디오 계약 중복 정리 (`refactor/studio-boundary-and-fps-constant`)

- template-customization이 template-core의 `*.payload.repository.ts` 구현 파일을 직접 import하던 것을 공개 Service(`published-template-catalog.service.ts`)로 좁힘
- video FPS(24/30/60), PPI(72/150/300), `StudioKind`, 이미지 출력 크기가 여러 파일에 리터럴로 흩어져 있던 것을 각 소유 모듈의 공유 상수로 정본화

### 3. 참조 이미지 생성 — 원본 유지 (`feat/image-reference-generation`)

카메라 컨트롤로 시점을 재생성하면 참조한 원본이 화면에서 사라지던 문제를 고칩니다. 원인이 렌더가 아니라 계약 선택이라는 진단에 따라 구조를 바꿨습니다.

**서버 — 유스케이스 경계가 셋에서 둘로**

`adjustImageCamera`와 `/api/generate-image/camera-adjustment` 라우트를 없애고 `generateImages` 하나로 수렴했습니다. 생성 플랜 IR(`ImageGenerationPlan.seedImage`)이 원래부터 참조를 일급 입력으로 갖고 있었고 러너도 모델 호출도 참조 유무로 갈라지지 않았습니다 — 갈라져 있던 것은 그 위 유스케이스 층뿐이었습니다. 카메라가 더하는 것은 flat 프롬프트 JSON의 키 두 개(`camera`, `camera_rules`)뿐입니다.

프롬프트 규칙 하나로 통일됩니다: **사용자가 프롬프트를 새로 썼으면 그것을 정규화해 쓰고, 비워 뒀으면 참조가 준 프롬프트를 물려받습니다.** 둘 다 없으면 400입니다. 그 결과 "참조 이미지의 모습을 유지하면서 주제를 바꾸는" 생성이 새로 가능해졌습니다 — 옛 카메라 라우트는 스키마가 `.strict()`라 프롬프트 필드 자체가 없었습니다.

서버 3개 파일이 −47줄입니다(`generate-image.service.ts` 473→456, `camera-control.ts` 130→117, `generate-image.client.ts` 156→139). 기능이 늘면서 코드가 줄었습니다.

**클라이언트 — 응답 DTO에서 세션 모델로**

`results.result`의 타입이 API 응답 타입(`ImageGenerationResult`) 그 자체였습니다. 응답은 본질적으로 "직전 한 번"이라 새 응답이 통째로 교체하는 것이 그 타입 선택의 논리적 귀결이었고, 원본 소실은 버그가 아니라 그 귀결이었습니다. `{ images, reference }` 세션으로 바꾸니 **참조 고정이 `session.reference ?? selected` 한 줄**이 되었습니다 — 별도 상태도, 언제 비울지에 대한 규칙도 없습니다.

**확장 지점은 "참조가 어디서 오는가"에 둡니다**

`loadGeneratedImage` → `resolveGeneratedImageReference`/`ResolvedReference`. 참조를 *어떻게* 쓰는지에는 변주가 없으므로(언제나 `seedImage`로 모델에 들어감) 참조 생성기 레지스트리는 만들지 않았습니다. 사용자 업로드·브랜드 자산 소스가 앉을 자리만 비워 뒀습니다.

**스키마 — `generated-images.sourceImage`**

참조 계보를 nullable self relationship으로 영속화합니다. **기능 종류는 기록하지 않습니다** — `derivationType` enum도 `cameraAzimuth`/`cameraElevation` 칼럼도 없습니다. 저장하는 사실은 "이 이미지는 저 이미지를 참조해 만들어졌다" 하나뿐이고, 각도는 이미 `effectivePrompt`에 굽혀 있습니다. 색 변형·배경 교체가 뒤에 붙어도 스키마가 그대로입니다.

설계·계획 문서: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-image-reference-generation-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-18-image-reference-generation.md`

### 4. 이미지 결과 그리드 Figma 정합

`xl:grid-cols-3`을 제거했습니다 — 배치 상한이 4장이라 3열은 2×2로 떨어지지 않고 4장을 3+1로 깼습니다. 한 장뿐일 때는 열을 나누지 않아 카드가 캔버스 폭을 그대로 씁니다(Figma `16:8487`). 로딩 스켈레톤도 같은 열 구성으로 맞췄습니다 — 다르면 생성이 끝나는 순간 카드가 자리를 옮겼습니다.

## 스키마 변경

`migrations/20260818_024535_generated_image_source_image` — `generated_images`와 버전 테이블 `_generated_images_v`에 nullable FK 컬럼 + 인덱스를 더합니다. `down`이 FK 2개·인덱스 2개·컬럼 2개를 모두 되돌립니다. `ON DELETE set null`이라 참조 원본을 지워도 파생 이미지는 남고 계보만 끊깁니다.

🔴 **`PAYLOAD_DB_PUSH=false`인 새 DB에서의 적용 검증은 아직입니다.** 리뷰어가 리포만으로는 확인할 수 없는 항목으로 남겼고, 작성자가 직접 수행할 예정입니다.

## 검증

Node 22에서 실행했습니다.

- `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm check` — clean (792 파일)
- `pnpm vitest run` — 194 files / 1248 tests 통과

## 리뷰 과정에서 잡힌 것 (참고)

머지 전에 고친 것들입니다. 리뷰가 실제로 일한 지점이라 남겨 둡니다.

- **참조 고정이 프로파일 교체를 건너뛰던 회귀** — 카메라를 한 번 돌린 뒤 프로파일을 바꾸면 카메라 그룹이 열린 채 남고 버튼이 항상 실패했습니다(서버가 `scenario == profileId`로 걸러 거부). base 대비 회귀였습니다.
- **재생성이 `aspectRatio`를 빠뜨리던 결함** — 캔버스가 단일 비율을 모든 카드에 먹이고 `overflow-hidden`이라 참조 카드가 잘렸습니다. 이 변경의 존재 이유가 깨지는 지점이었습니다.
- **카메라 신뢰 경계 검증이 유료 호출 뒤로 밀린 순서 회귀** — 허용되지 않은 각도를 담은 요청이 400을 받기까지 참조 이미지 1장 다운로드와 Haiku 호출 1건을 소모했습니다. 삭제된 옛 경로는 반대 순서였고 그 순서를 단언하는 테스트가 함께 삭제되면서 드러나지 않았습니다.

## 남은 후속 항목

- "잘못된 각도 + 참조 있음" 조합 테스트가 없어, 카메라 거부 시 참조 다운로드를 건너뛰는지는 테스트가 잡지 못합니다(유료 호출 쪽은 잡힙니다)
- 참조가 "전체 저장" zip에 포함되고 첫 결과 파일명이 `hd-image-2`로 밀립니다
- 재생성 중 스켈레톤이 그리드를 통째로 덮어 참조가 잠깐 사라집니다 — 최종 상태는 설계대로지만 진행 중에는 이 변경이 없애려던 증상이 재현됩니다
- `referenceIndex` 계약(`number | null`)이 구현(0/null)보다 넓습니다

author: paulfidika
body:
**5 modules / 2,863 lines → 2 modules + 1 shared rig / 2,409 lines. 86 tests in, 85 out.**

| new | what it is |
|---|---|
| `test_procsplit.py` | the split boundary, and the authorization it carries |
| `test_pod_isolation.py` | what the child may touch on the host: uid, OOM rank, host RAM |
| `tests/harness/split.py` | the shared pgw#763 rig — **new**, see below |

## A test module was doubling as a fixture library

Four other modules did `from test_procsplit_pgw763 import SplitHarness, captured_dials, ...` — a *file name* that stops existing the moment the module is folded. `SplitHarness`, `CHILD_MAIN`, `_payload`, `captured_dials`, `captured_reports`, `isolated_postmortem` and their dependency closure now live in `tests/harness/split.py`, where the other shared rigs already live. `test_procsplit`, `test_pod_isolation`, `test_child_faults` and `test_receipts_trust` all import from there.

**`TESTS_DIR` had to become `parent.parent`.** The hoist moved it one directory deeper, and the un-fixed version spawned every child from `tests/harness/harness/...`. The suite caught it as a boot-crash loop — the good failure; a path fixture that silently no-opped would not have been caught.

## The value pass found almost nothing, and that is the finding

Probing `actions.authorize` and `capability.decide` produced guard-groups of **3** and **8** tests — but each red set spanned *distinct shapes*, not variants.

**Exactly one deletion survived probing**: the `"unlisted path"` row of `test_action_table_refuses`, whose subject (path matching) reddens `test_delta1_parent_refuses_a_hub_call_the_allowlist_does_not_name` — the same property through a real split child. The `"wrong method"` row beside it is **uniquely guarded**: breaking method matching alone reddens that row and nothing else.

### The journey hypothesis is REFUTED for this cluster

The plan (recorded on pgw#1362 last session) was to replace 23 narrow security rigs with one broad journey. The probes say those 23 are **not variants of each other**, so a journey would have to assert every refusal individually anyway — it would save **fixture setup, not properties**. Recorded so no later wave re-proposes it from the file count alone.

### Two refinements to the mutation-probe rule (DESIGN-RULINGS 4.34a), both paid for here

1. **A coarse mutation fuses distinct guards.** Breaking path *and* method matching together reddened both `test_action_table_refuses` rows and made them look like one property. Narrowed to each separately, they are two. **The probe must be as narrow as the property.**
2. **A green probe is a claim about the mutation as much as about the tests** — third occurrence this session. Disabling the privilege drop via a regex that did not apply gave "72 passed". Re-aimed at `plan_drop`'s real early return: **1 RED**.

## Fold probes

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| the delta-1 credential strip removed | **2 RED**, one in *each* merged module (the in-process and containerised halves of the same property) |
| `privdrop.plan_drop` always returns None | **1 RED** |

## Both ratchets turn the right way

- mypy `ignore_errors` **235 → 231**, none added; `mypy src tests` green over **910 files**
- the pgw#1362 intake baseline **375 → 370** — and that gate's **first real use was catching this very fold**, refusing the branch until the five folded names left the list. It works.

## Counts, in the ruling's format

**deleted-as-vacuous 0 · deleted-as-low-value 1 · folded-into-module 85 · kept-focused 0**

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_{procsplit,pod_isolation,child_faults,receipts_trust}.py` → **199 passed, 14 skipped** (213 collected, matching master's 214 minus the one deletion)
- `mypy src tests` → Success, 910 files
- 25 fast-gate lint scripts incl. both ratchets → all pass
- Full `tests` suite runs here in CI. **Not enqueuing until it is green**, and `gh pr merge` is not being called before then.

body:
Phase 2 of the close-out plan. Takes the register from seven actionable entries to **one** — C-92, which closes when branch protection is enabled.

## What is in here

| Entry | Change |
|---|---|
| **C-86** | README tree rewritten from the filesystem — it omitted 11 of 36 modules and named two `tests/` directories that do not exist. §9 sent consumers to `tests/conformance/`, **a path never created**; the suite is `src/views_frames/conformance/`. README is the PyPI long-description. `scripts/check_arch_tree.py` now covers both trees. |
| **C-87** | `__all__` added to both sibling conformance modules. Two lines. |

The inert head-to-head file keeps its purpose and names its CI coverage route. Two CIC §10 gaps filled. Three `FrameMetadata` guarantees that §3 states and nothing pinned now have tests. |

author: badbradda1
body: ## What Adds a way for admins to download sponsor logos from `/admin/sponsors`: - **Download logo** button on each sponsor row — downloads that sponsor's logo with a clean filename based on the sponsor name (e.g. `acme-roofing.png`). - **Download all logos (.zip)** button above the sponsors list — bundles every unique logo into one zip named `sponsor-logos-YYYY-MM-DD.zip`. Sponsors who bought multiple packages (same logo across rows) are deduped so each logo appears once. ## How - New admin-only API route `app/api/admin/sponsors/logos/route.ts` (`requireAdmin()` gated, like the other sponsor admin endpoints): - `GET ?id=` fetches the logo from its public R2 URL and returns it with `Content-Disposition: attachment`. - `GET` with no id fetches all unique logos and streams back a zip built with `jszip` (new dependency). Logos that fail to fetch are skipped; filename collisions get a `-2`, `-3` suffix. - File extension is derived from the R2 `logo_key`, falling back to the response content type, then the URL. ## Verification - `npx tsc --noEmit` passes. - `npx eslint` clean on both changed files (repo-wide lint has pre-existing errors in unrelated check-in components). - `npm run build` succeeds; `/api/admin/sponsors/logos` appears in the route manifest. ## Deploy note The first Vercel preview (`dpl_ADn7brMufcM5DUN6StqA8jqnbHbz`) failed because `jszip` was added to `package.json` without updating `pnpm-lock.yaml`. That lockfile is now in sync (`jszip@3.10.1`).

author: ellyfd
body:
## Why

Sprint 8 now tracks failed formal travel attachment deletion with durable D1 tombstones, but the release runbook also requires operational monitoring. Pending cleanup existed only in the database, so admins could not tell whether cleanup was healthy, aging, or repeatedly failing.

## Change

- add admin-only `/api/admin/health`
- report total pending cleanup count, oldest pending age, max attempts, and the oldest 100 records
- never expose R2 object keys to the browser
- add bounded manual retry grouped by owner/trip and preserve tombstones on failure
- audit manual retry actions
- add System Management → 系統健康
- update release runbook with 48h monitoring and stop thresholds
- add regression tests for admin boundary, object-key privacy, bounded retry, audit, and UI/runbook presence

This does not change ordinary user travel flows or add another storage browser.

author: liujuanjuan1984
body:
## 变更说明

为 lifeos-web 建立轻量应用版本管理：

- 版本置为 `1.0.0`（整体完成度已达到正式发布水平，非 alpha）；
- 新增 `Release Web` 工作流：以 `v*` tag 推送为主触发（与 `lifeos-cli` 一致），校验 tag 与 `package.json` 版本一致且从 `main` 可达，跑完整验证基线后发布 GitHub Release，notes 记录钉住的 `lifeos-cli` 契约版本；手动触发保留为修补已存在 tag release 的备用通道；
- 发布流程细节只写入 `CONTRIBUTING.md`，不放入根 README。

## 为什么用 tag 触发而不是手动触发

1. tag 本身就是版本声明与审计记录，不存在"输入版本与 package.json 漂移"；
2. `git tag && git push` 可脚本化、可被自动化驱动，UI 手动触发难以自动化；
3. 事件记录谁、何时、哪个 commit 发布；与 CLI 的发布模式保持一致；
4. 手动触发保留为修补通道，与 CLI 的 `Release Publish and Repair` 一致。

## 变更清单

- `package.json` / `package-lock.json`：`0.0.0` → `1.0.0`
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`：tag 触发发布 + 手动修补通道
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`：发布流程说明（唯一入口）

## 验证

- `bash ./scripts/validate.sh` 全绿（含 Playwright E2E，2 passed）

Closes #35

author: konstantinosstouras
body:
Signed in as the owner, the jobs page showed **Edit / Take down on some cards and not others** — never on the postings the Google tracking sheet publishes. Three separate faults sat behind that, and fixing them properly reached every dataset the site serves.

## The three faults

**1. The tracking sheet's postings had no editing handle** — 16 of the 25 cards on the page. A control is drawn only where `docIdFor` can name a `jobSubmissions` document, and the workbook's rows deliberately had none. Each now gets a **mirror**: an inert document, `status: 'sheet'` — a value no query in the pipeline reads — created and refreshed from the workbook by `syncSheetMirrors`. `post-a-job.html` already sets `status: 'queued'` on every edit it saves, and **that alone is the hand-over**: the build then publishes the document and drops the workbook's row. The workbook keeps deciding which postings **exist**, via a `sheetId` pin. A hand-over that cannot *build* falls back to the workbook and is reported, so a bad edit can never make a posting disappear.

**2. Take down did nothing, on all 110 rows.** Removal was keyed on the form-issued `ref`, and **no published row has one**. The document was marked hidden, the button said "Taken down", and the orphan carry republished the row verbatim. `removalSpecs` + an `{ id }` spec in `mergeRows` fixes it in all three pipelines. Only the maintainer was ever affected — every published row's `uid` is null, so no poster has owned one.

**3. The three frozen archives were read-only for everybody.** `past-postings`, `recent-faculty` and `universities` are written once by the legacy import and have no Firestore backing. New `assets/oa-rowedit.js` corrects a row **at read time** from a public-read, admin-write `rowOverrides` collection — the `newsOverrides` pattern generalised. The committed file stays the source of truth, the correction reaches every visitor, and re-running the import cannot undo it. Deliberately **not** an add path: a school the archive lacks is added upstream, in the sheet.

## What five adversarial review passes then found

Every pass found real defects, most of them introduced by the previous one. All are fixed, each with a regression test verified by breaking the code and watching the suite go red.

| | Defect | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| 🔴 | `publishedId`/`sheetId` trusted from any document | **any signed-in account could delete any posting** |
| 🔴 | `sheetId` trusted on a live document | any account could replace a workbook posting's content |
| 🔴 | `sheetId` unguarded in one last place (the hand-over) | any account could silently delete a workbook posting |
| 🔴 | `mergedFrom` client-writable, and `accountKeys` maps e-mail → uid | any account could take down another's posting |
| 🟠 | a bare `ref` removed a row whoever posted it (**pre-existing**) | would have gone live with the first form posting |
| 🟠 | taking a posting down deleted its renumbered same-day sibling | wrong posting deleted, silently and permanently |
| 🟠 | withdrawal after an account merge never applied, then stamped `removed` | permanently un-takedownable, silently |
| 🟠 | the archive editor drew on real job postings | Take down emptied the card and left the posting up |
| 🟠 | a taken-down row was invisible to the maintainer too | no Restore anywhere; only the Firestore console |
| 🟠 | an override pinned **every** field, not the changed one | masks a later upstream correction for ever |
| 🟡 | entry-point guard no-opped on a path with a space | scheduled publish green while publishing nothing |
| 🟡 | pinning a sheet id after `assignIds` could collide | one posting silently replaces another |
| 🟡 | the admin-only module was a **hard dependency** of 3 public pages | every reader got a blank list if it failed to load |
| 🟡 | every save re-fit the map to the whole world | correcting a run of schools meant re-navigating each time |
| 🟡 | What's-new hiding was still one-way past the 5th entry | `.v3-news-hidden` had no CSS either |
| 🟡 | two test gaps: guard pinned where declared, not applied | the exact bug reintroducible with CI green |
| 🟡 | stale contracts: `migratable()`, all three `mergeRows` docs | next reader designs against a rule that no longer holds |

## ⚠️ Deploy step

**None of the Firestore half is live until `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules` is run from the repository root.** No workflow can do it — the CLI needs an interactive login. `_SETUP-FIREBASE.md` said `cd v2`, wrong since the promotion; it now says the root and says the step is one a human has to remember. The rules now also carry the `mergedFrom` pin that closes one of the holes above.

The 16 mirror documents appear on the first `build-jobs` run with `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` set.

## Tests

| Suite | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `_scraper/selftest.mjs` | 1800 | **2091** |
| `_scraper/page-test.mjs` | 356 | **408** |
| `_scraper/link-check.mjs` | green | green |
| `_scraper/archive-v2.mjs --check` | green | green |

`data/` is untouched — this change is code only.

## Known gaps, left deliberately

No admin queue for submissions that fail validation; `my-postings.html` is uid-scoped with no maintainer branch; `accountKeys` denies `list`/`delete` to the admin as well (and lets any signed-in account overwrite an identity claim — **pre-existing, not addressed here**); and `data/candidates.json` / `data/placements.json` are empty, so those editors — whose admin branches are correct — cannot be exercised end to end yet.

author: akiomik
body:
## Summary

Second scaffolding change of the kernel mainlining: **cleanup hooks
(RFC 0014 §4.4, INV-RC8) and the composition surface (RFC 0014 §2.5,
INV-RC2/RC3)** — `Command::on_teardown` and the cleanup ledger on the
kernel side; `ScopeValue`, `Keyed`/`Slot` with removal journals, and
`ReducerExt`'s `scope`/`for_each`/`presented`/`into_program` on the
reducer side. Everything is `pub(crate)`; production behavior and the
public API are unchanged (`tests/api_surface.rs` green, public API
diff empty), and the old runtime remains the production owner.

The combinator signatures are RFC 0014 §2.5's block verbatim — no
aliases, no reshaping — with one deliberate exception recorded in the
findings below (`ScopeValue`'s bound list).

## What lands

1. **Cleanup hooks.** Registration travels the command as its own
   carrier (qualified by `scoped` and the combinators — RFC 0005
   INV-18's coverage), arms in the spawn phase after the same
   command's cancel phase (§3.4's teardown-and-reregister rule), and
   starts when a teardown selects its scope. A cleanup run joins the
   kernel's one `JoinSet` but counts toward no gauge, neither joins
   nor triggers the admission barrier, marks no dirt, and has **no
   route back into the runtime**: its harness holds a join set, a
   task index, and the gate — no lane sender, no directive path. That
   absence is the no-output clause's structural review (INV-RC8),
   written at the construction site. Termination discards unfired
   registrations and cancels running finalizers, with no grace
   window.
2. **Collections with removal journals.** `Keyed` and `Slot` record
   *removals* — `remove`, `dismiss`, insert-over-occupied,
   present-over-occupied — never state diffs, so a same-update
   remove-and-reinsert still yields the old instance's teardown and a
   fresh successor in one command (INV-RC3). Building a collection
   (`from_iter`, literals) records nothing: an entry that only ever
   existed in an iterator never placed a run, so there is nothing to
   tear down.
3. **Combinators.** Each boundary qualifies every identity carrier of
   its child's returned command — spawn keys, cancel ids, teardown
   prefixes, cleanup registrations — and the child's subscription
   declarations, with its segment (INV-RC2); equal local ids under
   sibling boundaries never alias; stacks nest (a whole
   `for_each`/`presented` stack composed as another boundary's child
   is exercised end to end). Journal drains merge one teardown per
   removal into the update's own command **without constructing a
   batch**: the entries are appended to the command's teardown
   carrier directly, so a boundary adds identity carriers and
   nothing else — the update's redraw directive (including
   `without_redraw`) survives, and no spurious diagnostics fire.
   Origination stays one surface (RFC 0013 R8): `Command::teardown`
   is the only constructor of a teardown entry crate-wide.

## Evidence

- **Suite**: 687 lib tests under `--all-features` (+66 over `main`),
  all targets green, clippy `-D warnings` clean in debug and release,
  fmt clean, no sleeps/timers/clock reads, `#[ignore]` zero among
  additions. New and changed rows repeated ×10.
- **Counterexamples killed, with the mutation run** (applied,
  observed, reverted — an independent review pass re-ran them):
  - *diff-based removal detection*: a diff-equivalent journal fails
    the kernel recreate row on its **unkeyed-run** assertion (an
    unkeyed run has no identity to supersede, so only the journal's
    teardown reaches it) plus five unit rows; the fixed suite
    passes.
  - *batch-fold merge* (the shape the boundary drain deliberately
    avoids): restoring it fails exactly the two directive/diagnostic
    rows — `without_redraw` preserved, no false "child key ignored"
    warning (with an in-recorder control showing the zero is
    silence, not suppression).
  - *cancel-phase cleanup registration*: moving the registration to
    the cancel phase fails the three spawn-phase rows.
- **RFC 0013 §7.2's kernel rows** are all present, including the
  ST8 routing pair (a key-addressed message after a same-key
  remove-and-reinsert reaches the **new** instance's state; one for
  an absent key is discarded) and the final-update row (teardown and
  quit in one update; termination fires no hook). The final-update
  row reads the two RFC 0011 §4.4 postconditions through the
  driver's terminated report plus the bounded settle; the
  postconditions proper are owned by the existing termination row.
- **R8 one-surface review** re-verified by grep after the merge
  redesign: one origination site; `merging_teardowns` and `batch`
  extend already-originated entries.

## Deliberate exceptions

Two pre-existing test-code edits, both mechanical, no assertion
semantics changed: an exhaustiveness-forced match arm in a lowering
test helper (the new dispatch step variant), and an `.expect(...)`
where a test-surface constructor became `Option`-returning
(structural replacement of an `unreachable!`).

## Findings for the contract documents

1. **INV-RC12 (a)'s cleanup half cannot be behavioral.** A
   stop-requested cleanup run is not constructible outside
   termination — teardown selection excludes the kind, cancel and
   supersession address keyed slots, re-evaluation addresses
   subscription runs, and at termination no admission site remains.
   Verified independently by enumerating every stop-request call
   site. The reachable half (an in-flight cleanup run defers no
   admission) is behavioral here; the rest is carried structurally by
   the barrier predicate reading subscription runs only. RFC 0014
   §12 marks all of (a) behavioral — an enforcement-class amendment
   candidate for the RFC, not an implementation change.
2. **A boundary-merged teardown does not redraw; a hand-written
   `Command::teardown` does** (it inherits the default directive).
   Both are intended — directives belong to the update, and a
   boundary adds identity carriers only — but the sentence belongs in
   RFC 0014 §2.5 when this surface goes public at the switch.
3. **`ScopeValue` drops `PartialEq`**, which `Eq: PartialEq` makes
   redundant. RFC 0014 §2.5's block still writes it; a wording sync
   for the RFC when this surface goes public, not an implementation
   change.
4. `Keyed` iterates in insertion order off a linear scan —
   determinism is what the driving contract rides on; the O(n)
   lookup is stated mechanism (RFC 0013 §3.7) and joins the
   load-measurement list for the acceptance re-derivation.

author: tedico
body:
Athena's **first live run failed**: `missing or empty env secret(s): IG_USER_ID_ATHENA, IG_ACCESS_TOKEN_ATHENA` — even though both secrets are set on the repo and show up in `gh secret list`.

GitHub Actions exposes no secret unless it is **mapped by name** into the step's `env:` block, and there is no wildcard. Per-project credentials went into the code and `channels.yaml` but never into `tick.yml`.

## The part that went right

**Nothing posted, and the row stayed `Ready`.** Rather than quietly publishing Athena's carousel to Useful Math's account, the tick refused and named the missing secrets. That is exactly the failure the no-fallback rule was built to produce — and it produced it on the first real attempt, which is the cheapest possible moment to find out.

## Also corrects the README

It claimed adding a project is "one config block plus its secrets — there is no code to change." Wrong. It is config, secrets, **and two lines in `tick.yml`**. That third step is the one that looks done but isn't: `gh secret list` shows the secret while the tick reports it missing. The README now lists the four steps in order, and the env block carries a comment saying the same.

## After merge

Re-running the tick should publish Toni Morrison — her queue row is `Ready`, dated 2026-08-17 18:20 ET (overdue), 7 cards verified 1080x1350 and hosted on Drive.

author: macstudio-4[bot]
body:
## 为什么通用 d 定理必须 `3 ≤ d`

`#2380` 的通用 d 有限深度定理带着前提 `3 ≤ d`。**这不是四舍五入的让步,是结构性的。**

通用冠军值是

```
championValue β = (β² − β − 1)/(β² − 1)
```

**分子恰是黄金比的极小多项式**,故在 `β = φ` 处精确为 **0**。而黄金塔自己的冠军值是
`goldenThreshold = φ⁻²/2 ≈ 0.190983 > 0`。**二者相差的是整个阈值,不是一个扰动。**

| | 值 |
|---|---|
| `championValue φ` | **0** |
| `goldenThreshold` | 0.190983… |
| d=3,4,5,6 的 `championValue` | 0.2282 / 0.2902 / 0.3138 / 0.3241(皆 > 0)|

## 同一个量的两处显形

`β² − β − 1` 既是冠军值的**分子**,又是通用证明里 `mid ≤ β⁻¹` 约束的**判别式**
(该约束化简后即 `β ≤ β² − 1`)。在 `φ` 处一个为零、另一个**取等** —— 是同一件事。
末条定理 `golden_reciprocal_boundary_is_tight : φ = φ² − 1` 记的就是取等这一面。

## 一处已改正的错误

初稿把该约束写成 `φ⁻¹ · (φ² − 1) = φ`。**那是假的**:`φ² − 1 = φ`,故乘积为 **1**。
编译器 `linarith` 失败后核算发现,已改为 `φ = φ² − 1`,即取等的正确形式。
**命题本身错,不是证明技巧不够** —— 记在此处以免后来者照抄初稿。

## 价值

把这条记在**后来者最可能想去放宽 `3 ≤ d` 的地方**。
没有它,「为什么不顺手把 d=2 也覆盖了」是个看起来合理的问题。

## 核验

- `lake build` 绿;`sorry` 0、私 axiom 0、警告 0;6 条定理,66 行
- `order_two_is_outside_the_general_formula` 公理闭包 `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`
- 落地链 `PRECHECK=0 / REPORT=0 / EMIT=0 / APPEND=0 appended_freezes=1`

## CI 预期为红,原因在 dev 侧

本地 `make preflight` 的失败集恰为 **#2385** 记录的两个 dev 侧测试,`rule findings: none`。

body:
This PR adds a self-adapting repair automation pipeline for CI failures and drift detection.

Link back to chat: (Automatically tracked by agent)

**Triggers**:
- **Scheduled**: Proactive runs computed based on repository cadence (defaulting to 0 2 * * *).
- **CI Failure**: Reactive fixes if the CI workflow fails.
- **Manual Dispatch**: Fallback manual run.

**Initial Schedule / Telemetry**:
The initial schedule is set to `0 2 * * *` (run once daily during off-peak hours) based on a fallback heuristic due to limited git history available locally at bootstrap. 

**Periodic Recompute**:
The `compute-schedule.yml` workflow periodically reads PR velocity and commit telemetry (using `git log` and `gh pr list`) to calculate optimal active/inactive periods, adjusting the schedule expression. It creates a PR when cadence changes.

**Manual Override**:
You can manually edit `.github/self-heal-schedule.yml` to enforce a desired schedule.

**Reviewer Checklist**:
- [ ] Confirm all repair steps passed by checking the artifact log links.
- [ ] Review the PR diff to ensure no secrets or unintended logic changes are included.
- [ ] Ensure the file modifications are confined to formatting, snapshots, and explicit package config changes.

author: renanarturdemetrio-ai
body:
Regra informada pelo operador em 17/08/2026:

| Preço do produto | Etiqueta |
|---|---|
| até R$ 29,99 | **R$ 4,50** |
| R$ 30,00 a 49,99 | **R$ 6,50** |
| R$ 50,00 a 78,99 | **R$ 6,75** |
| **R$ 79,00 ou mais** | *não existe valor exato* → **média do realizado** |

Isso **não é estimativa** — é o que a Amazon cobra do vendedor. Por isso a tabela precede a faixa de peso do #1070 na precedência: tabela é cobrança, faixa de peso é mediana que nós calibramos.

A tabela termina no limiar em vez de ganhar um quarto degrau porque inventar um valor fixo acima de R$ 79 seria trocar o zero de antes por outro número errado, só que com cara de tabela.

## Precedência nova

```
sku > real > TABELA_PRECO > MÉDIA_ACIMA > faixa_peso > default
```

Na prática isso resolve o balde `sem_frete` **inteiro abaixo de R$ 79 sem depender de peso cadastrado no Tiny** — que era exatamente o gargalo do #1070.

## A regra que não pode ser simplificada depois

🔴 **A média só aceita amostra de SKU acima do limiar.** Misturar a etiqueta de R$ 4,50 de um produto de R$ 25 com a de um de R$ 200 puxaria a média para baixo e subestimaria o frete do item caro — erro na direção que **infla** a margem, que é a direção que esta frente inteira existe para impedir. SKU sem preço conhecido também fica de fora: não dá para saber de que lado do limiar ele está.

`mediaFreteRealizado` devolve a **média** (foi o que você pediu) mas carrega a **mediana** ao lado: as duas distantes significam um punhado de etiquetas caras puxando o número de todo mundo. Sem o par, o defeito ficaria escondido atrás de um valor de aparência sadia. Sem amostra o valor é `null`, nunca `0`.

## Flag

`AMZ_FRETE_TABELA_PRECO` (default `false`). **Uma só**, porque é uma regra com dois lados. Com ela off a cascata sai idêntica — há teste travando.

O diagnóstico que já existe passou a comparar a cascata de **hoje** contra as duas regras novas ligadas:

```bash
/api/amazon/atacadaoshow/frete-faixa/diagnostico
```

Ler `delta.pct_receita_recuperada` e `media_acima` (compare `valor` × `mediana` antes de confiar).

## Se a Amazon reajustar

Mexe em `TABELA_DBA_POR_PRECO` em [core/amazon-frete-dba.js](core/amazon-frete-dba.js) — e o `frete_fonte: 'tabela_preco'` em cada linha é o que permite achar as telas afetadas.

Suíte **483 arquivos / 9117 testes** verde (era 9100).

author: baldwinspc
body:
A Group rendezvous that hangs is undiagnosable from the assertion alone:

```
phase = "Error", want Passed: collective[...]=Error(the collective did not complete within
its window — 1 of 3 rank(s) did not report (rank 0 (...worker) never finished) …)
```

That does not say whether the workers reached the root and it miscounted, or whether a
worker never got in at all. **Those are different bugs with different fixes**, and the two
facts that separate them — the root's last `rank joined (N of 2)` line, and each worker's own
`joined` / `could not reach the root` verdict — live in pod logs that `newNamespace`'s
teardown was destroying.

#385 has already cost one wrong root-cause hypothesis, published and then disproved, for
want of exactly this evidence.

## What it does

On failure only, prints the namespace's `BurnInRun`s (phase, and each result's nodes, phase
and message) and every pod (phase, node, container termination state, then a tail of its
log).

Green runs print nothing. CI output that is mostly noise is output nobody reads.

## The ordering is the point, and it is verified rather than assumed

The dump is registered **after** the namespace-delete cleanup, so it runs **before** it —
`t.Cleanup` is LIFO. Get that backwards and the dump runs after teardown has reaped the pods
and captures nothing, which is a diagnostic that silently does the opposite of its job.

Proved with a standalone test rather than trusted from the docs:

```
cleanup order = [dump-logs delete-namespace]
```

## Details worth noting

- A typed clientset is added beside the controller-runtime client for the one thing it
  cannot do: read a pod's log.
- Every step is best-effort and *reported*, never fatal. This runs when the test has already
  failed, and a diagnostic that panics replaces the real assertion with its own.
- Per-pod output is bounded at 4 KB with an explicit `(truncated)` marker. A rank that spun
  in its retry loop for the whole window prints thousands of identical lines, and burying
  the one line that differs is the same failure as capturing nothing.
- A pod that never started says `(unavailable: …)` rather than showing an empty block, which
  would read like a runner that printed nothing.

## What this does not do

It does not fix #385. The flake is real and reproduced on `main` independently of any of my
branches, and I do not yet know why rank 0 hangs — my first explanation was wrong and is
retracted in the issue. This is the instrumentation that makes the next occurrence
answerable instead of speculative.

`make lint`, the full module suite, the arm64 cross-build and `go vet -tags e2e` all pass.

Refs #385

author: tmatens
body:
Second product bug from the OS smoke's Windows leg (ref #572, follow-up to #585): **any run with findings crashed on Windows with `UnicodeEncodeError`** — pipes and redirected files inherit cp1252, which can't encode the report's `⚠`/`·`/`│` characters. This is what killed the Windows pre-commit smoke (`'charmap' codec can't encode character '│'`) and explains the bulk of the 54 Windows pytest failures (clean files "exiting 1", findings missing from output — the process was dying mid-print).

Fix: `main()` reconfigures stdout/stderr to UTF-8 when they're `TextIOWrapper`s with a narrower encoding. No-op on Linux/macOS and on interactive Windows consoles (wide-char API); piped/redirected Windows output becomes UTF-8 — the bytes every other platform already produces, and PEP 686's direction.

The regression test reproduces the Windows condition cross-platform with `PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252` and asserts the gutter character arrives intact — **verified failing before the fix** (with the exact production error) and passing after. Full gates green (ruff, mypy strict, 1790 tests).

After this merges I'll dispatch the OS smoke again; the expected residue is the POSIX-only test tail (`mkfifo`, chmod semantics, Linux-image Docker pulls), which gets skip guards in a follow-up informed by that run.

author: d-addison
body:
Unified execution route, plus the dispatch-integrity work recovered alongside it.

## What this is

Five tasks integrated by dispatch, six recovered from preserved refs after the
orchestration failed to integrate them, and five defects found while getting
those to land. Devel has since moved under it, so the diff is 45 commits rather
than the 189 it carried before.

## Dispatch integrity — the theme

Each of these was a check that reported success without checking anything.

- **The critique stage yielded zero findings on every real dispatch.** Its
  runner iterated the retired `waves[]` shape only, so a canonical graph
  produced no findings at all, and its artifact check actively reported the
  canonical shape as malformed. It now reads both, and still fails a graph
  carrying neither.
- **The jsonl-writes gate could not fail.** The baseline was an allowlist while
  its test required the baseline to equal the scanner's output, so every current
  site was permitted by construction. The snapshot and the ceiling are now
  separate, and the ceiling only shrinks. **This lands red**: one appending
  write is outside the permitted set, which is correct — it is a real ad-hoc
  JSONL append that should route through the canonical funnel.
- **The scanner counted one write twice.** A signature matched on either
  `OpenOptions::new()` or `.append(true)`, and rustfmt puts those on separate
  lines. Builder statements are now counted once, which is why the snapshot
  drops from thirty keys to twenty-six with no site removed.
- **Worker memory could lose a section silently.** The overlay picks sections
  out of CLAUDE.md by heading and skipped any that no longer matched, guarding
  only the case where all of them vanished. Renaming one heading stripped the
  build and test commands from every dispatched worker. A missing required
  section is now an error.
- **`banso quick ask` exited 0 on failure**, so an automated caller could not
  distinguish a finished investigation from a dead one.

## Authorization

`ExecuteStage` hardcoded `--allow-contractless-tasks`, `--skip-spec-lint` and
`--target-branch devel`, silently granting on every execution. All six
authorization bypasses are now typed configuration defaulting to false, emitted
only behind an explicit opt-in, and recorded with their config keys and
provenance in the durable log before execution. No existing test depended on the
silent grant. The target branch resolves config → checked-out branch → omit, and
never invents `devel`.

This path had just become reachable: it was dead for canonical graphs because
the file collector it depends on read only the retired shape.

## Test injection

The execute seam existed but was private and `#[cfg(test)]`-guarded, so
integration tests could not reach it — a test-only backdoor that failed exactly
when needed. A public process executor now serves both execute and verify, and
the end-to-end fixture runs offline through a recording fake that asserts the
concrete commands requested. It completes in under a second where it once took
188 seconds by spawning real planning agents.

The vacuous-verification guards were not weakened to achieve this.

## Recovered work

Four preserved refs were genuinely unintegrated and are recovered here: canonical
task-graph artifact analysis, one-shot admitted dispatch, in-process
verification routing, and the TDD compound rename. A triage of all 35 preserved
refs found 28 had already landed by other routes and two were superseded — those
are deliberately not recovered.

## Review notes

The jsonl gate is red on purpose. Turning it green means routing that one write
through the canonical funnel, not editing the baseline.

author: isaacgarciawh3
body:
Covers **TASK-011** (boundary correction), **TASK-012** (battery + peak shaving), **TASK-013** (external configuration) and part of **TASK-008** (tests).

## 1. The boundary was wrong, and this fixes it

You called it: `Sim.Energy` knew about seeds, noise, weather and EV schedules. That is the Simulation context living inside Energy.

The test that settles it — *swap the simulation for real IoT telemetry and see what has to change*:

| Context | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| **Energy** | computed physics from seed + weather | **describes only**: `Neighbourhood`, `House`, `Asset`, `Battery`. Nameplate data. |
| **Simulation** | clock and weather only | owns clock, weather, `DeterministicNoise`, all five behaviours, emits `PowerReading` |
| **Accounting** | took `EnergyEntry` with an asset-type string | takes `PowerReading`, classifies by **sign**. Zero asset vocabulary. |
| **Control** | did not exist | owns `PeakShavingStrategy`. See §2. |

`PowerReading` moved to the shared kernel — the producer must not own the contract it produces.

Verified:
```
grep -rn "Seed|Noise|Irradiance|Temperature|Weather" src/Sim.Energy   -> nothing
Sim.Energy      references -> Sim.SharedKernel only
Sim.Accounting  references -> Sim.SharedKernel only
Sim.Control     references -> Sim.SharedKernel only
```

**`ContextTranslator` largely disappeared.** Most of what it translated existed only to compensate for physics sitting in the wrong context. That deletion is the evidence the boundary is now right.

**OP-02 and OP-03 resolved structurally**, not patched: the stringly-typed category has nowhere left to cross, and `MeterKind` was deleted — a battery turned out to be just a meter whose reading changes sign.

## 2. Your six-item checklist

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| Move noise + synthetic behaviour to Simulation | Done |
| Remove Seed from Energy | Done — world generation moved to `NeighbourhoodBuilder` in Application |
| Remove obsolete `Sim.Domain` | Was already gone in PR #1 |
| Do not commit `sim.db` | **It was tracked.** `git rm --cached` + ignore rules |
| PV assumption consistent with netting | **The doc overclaimed.** A-003 rewritten: settlement is a single neighbourhood-wide sum; there is no per-house netting step |
| Remove `ITickBus` if pointless | **Zero subscribers.** Deleted. ADR-0004 rewritten to record why, with Kafka/Event Hub as the real future step |

## 3. Battery and peak shaving (new requirement)

The battery did not fit any existing context, which is what made it a good test of the model. Applying the same IoT swap: the nameplate is Energy, the physical response is Simulation, and **the peak-shaving policy survives the swap** — so it is its own context (ADR-0009).

**The first implementation failed, and the failure is in the ADR rather than quietly patched.** Fixed 45 kW threshold:

```
peak without battery  107.61 kW
peak with battery     107.61 kW    reduction 0.00 kW (0.0%)
battery SoC           0% - pinned empty
```

Winter load sits above 45 kW most of the day, so the battery drained from the first interval and had nothing left for the evening peak. A fixed threshold encodes a guess about the load, and the guess was wrong. Replaced with rolling percentiles — discharge above the 80th, recharge below the 40th (ADR-0010):

```
peak without battery  127.32 kW
peak with battery     107.61 kW    reduction 19.71 kW (15.5% cumulative since start)
within the 24h window 127.3 -> 64.8 kW  (49.1% flatter)
battery SoC           cycling 2% - 68%
```

Those two percentages measure different things and are labelled as such everywhere. The cumulative figure includes the controller's warm-up day.

The tick ordering means both figures exist without a second simulation run: non-storage assets are measured first (net load *without* battery), then Control acts.

## 4. External configuration (TASK-013)

Your hardcoding finding split three ways, and only one group was actually wrong:

1. **30 houses / 6 chargers — correctly constant.** The assignment says *exactly*. A config file that can set it to 25 could violate a stated requirement.
2. **Seed, proportions, tick, battery sizing — already configurable**, persisted in SQLite, runtime-editable.
3. **Physical parameters — your finding.** Now in `appsettings.Simulation.json`, validated at startup, file optional.

## 5. Tests

36 passing: energy accounting (conservation, closure, import/export exclusivity, kW→kWh), determinism (identical seeds byte-identical, different seeds differ), domain invariants (30/6 counts, base-load requirement).

## Known gaps, stated plainly

- **Architecture tests are empty** — the NetArchTest assertions locking the context isolation are not written. The isolation is currently enforced by project references, which is stronger, but the lock is missing.
- **Dashboard is not in this PR.** The battery visualisation (R-48..R-50) and R-18..R-23 remain open.
- Peak reduction is reported on two bases; both are labelled but the UI must not conflate them.

author: spenny18
body:
Google shows `riversrealestate.ca` and a generic globe in search results instead of the brand name and logo.

## What was already correct

Verified against a running server before changing anything — all of this serves fine today:

| Signal | Status |
|---|---|
| `favicon.ico` (16/32/48) | 200, `image/x-icon` |
| 96px PNG, SVG icon, apple-touch-icon | 200 |
| `WebSite` schema with `name: "Rivers Real Estate"` | present in the homepage `@graph` |
| `og:site_name` | "Rivers Real Estate" |
| robots.txt | does not block the icon |

So nothing was broken. Google simply has not refreshed its cache for this domain — a new domain gets the bare-domain treatment until it does. The fix on the site side is to remove every remaining ambiguity; the accelerator is a re-index request in Search Console.

## Changes

**Site-name signals** (`d5c74e7`)
- `WebSite.alternateName` — "Luxury Homes Calgary", "Rivers Real Estate Calgary" — plus `inLanguage`. Google only adopts a site name it sees used consistently, and `alternateName` declares the shorthand the brand actually uses rather than leaving it to be inferred.
- `site.webmanifest` with `name`/`short_name` matching `WebSite.name` and `og:site_name`, linked from the head. Another source Google reads for site names, and it gives Android a home-screen icon.
- 192px and 512px icons, so the set covers Google's preferred multiples of 48 and the manifest sizes.
- `application-name`, `apple-mobile-web-app-title`, `theme-color`.

**Favicon redrawn from the logo** (`0b10654`)

The favicon was a different house than the logo — a chunky cottage with a door, where the brand mark is a tall trapezoidal house with a skewed roofline and a 2×2 window grid. It now carries the logo's silhouette and gold gradient, with two departures made for small sizes: the inner room outline is dropped (below 48px it merges with the outer wall into a stack of rectangles) and the windows are enlarged so they survive downscaling.

Three treatments were rendered at 16/24/32/48px and in Google's circular crop before picking this one; a solid-fill variant read more clearly but lost the line-art character the logo is built on.

The whole raster set was regenerated from the new SVG: `favicon.ico` (16/32/48, PNG-encoded), `favicon-96x96`, `favicon-192x192`, `favicon-512x512`, `apple-touch-icon` at 180.

## Verification

- Manifest, both new icons, and `favicon.ico` all return 200 with correct content types
- Homepage `@graph` carries the expanded `WebSite` node
- Every generated raster renders correctly when fetched over HTTP, down to the 16px ICO entry
- Typecheck adds no new errors to the existing baseline

## Note for later

`WebSite.name`, `og:site_name`, the manifest `name`, and the homepage `<title>` must be changed together. If they disagree, Google falls back to the bare domain — which is the failure mode this PR is addressing.

After merge, request indexing for `https://riversrealestate.ca/` in Search Console. Google's refresh is on its own schedule — typically days to weeks.

author: vigilanty0x
body:
## Scope

Bind clean-venv historical wheel smoke tests to the machine-readable portfolio compatibility contract instead of relying on naming coincidence.

- resolve each matrix package through `portfolio-compatibility.v1.json` by `canonical_path`
- read the expected distribution name, version, and CLI from that manifest row
- install the built wheel into a fresh venv
- require installed distribution metadata version to equal the manifest version
- require exactly one console script with the manifest-declared CLI name
- load the installed entry-point target and require it to be callable
- require the manifest-declared CLI executable to exist in the smoke venv
- preserve the existing 20-job matrix, workflow-security gate, Node 24 pins, non-persistent checkout credentials, timeouts, and retained wheel evidence

## Why

All nine current packages happen to use the same folder, distribution, and CLI names. The manifest is nevertheless the canonical compatibility contract. This change makes wheel verification follow that contract directly, so a future intentional rename/version change must be reflected consistently rather than passing due to an accidental naming convention.

## Gate

No package/version changes are included. Merge requires 20/20 CI jobs, all historical wheel metadata/CLI checks on Python 3.11/3.12, and 20 retained wheel artifacts on the final head.

| 1.6.24 | `get-session` gains `no-store` cache headers, preventing stale session data |
| 1.6.22 | Unproven credentials not revoked during email OTP sign-in |
| 1.6.19 | Single-use verification flows hanging on connection-limited adapters by reusing active transactions |
| 1.6.17, 1.6.18 | Password reset tokens changing a password more than once under concurrent requests; `getCookieCache` returning stale sessions past expiry |

Given `emailOTP` with a custom `sendVerificationOTP`, a `pg` Pool, and permission re-checks on every protected request, that list is a good argument for the bump on its own.

## The generated schema changed

Migrating from a destroyed volume, `account` comes out **without** the `issuer` column and **without** the unique index on `(issuer, accountId)` that 1.6.11 generated. Confirmed against the live table, not just the CLI's output.

Nothing is deployed, so this only affects fresh databases. It matters for **#18**: whoever baselines the Drizzle schema must generate it from the better-auth version actually in use, or they will baseline a column that no longer exists. I have noted it there.

## Verification

Clean-volume rebuild — `db:local:destroy`, `db:local:up`, `db:local:migrate` — succeeds, all four Better Auth tables generate, app schema and seed apply.

`pnpm check`: 59 tests, audit clean.

Dev server route pass, identical to the pre-bump run:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `/login`, `/first-time-access`, `/forgot-password` | 200 |
| `/portal` unauthenticated | 307 → `/login?redirect=%2Fportal` |
| `/portal` as `active-member` | 200 |
| `/portal` as `inactive-member` / `email-mismatch` / `missing-member` | 307 → matching `access-blocked` reason |
| `/admin/members`, `/admin/organizations` | 200 |
| `/api/auth/get-session` | 200, null session |

## What I could not verify, and one thing worth a look

The issue asks for the OTP claim exercised end to end. I could not drive it: TanStack Start's server-function URLs are build-generated and the dev server SSRs every path, so `requestMemberClaimOtp` is not reachable over plain HTTP. Clicking through `/first-time-access` in a browser is the way to close this.

While trying, I hit something worth checking independently of this PR. Posting `casey.claimable@njmca.test` — the seeded active, unlinked member — to better-auth's `email-otp/send-verification-otp` returns `{"success":true}` but writes **no `verification` row and logs no OTP**, presumably anti-enumeration for an address with no auth user yet. The claim flow calls the same `auth.api.sendVerificationOTP`, and nothing in it creates the user first.

**This is not a regression from this bump** — I A/B tested it by checking out `main`, reinstalling 1.6.11, and issuing the identical request: same `{"success":true}`, same zero rows, same zero OTPs. It behaves the same before and after. But if it reflects the app's real behavior rather than an artifact of calling the endpoint directly, first-time claim cannot work at all, which would be a live bug in a flow marked done under #3. Worth ten seconds in a browser to settle.

author: brcampidelli
body:
Itens **10 e 14** do roteiro do terminal — que na prática são o mesmo defeito visto de dois lados.

## O que estava lá

O `DockerSandbox` passava `--memory 512m` e parava aí. Pior: `network` e `memory` eram parâmetros de construtor que o `get_sandbox` **nunca repassava** — aceitos, documentados e inalcançáveis. O container ficava cravado em sem-rede/512m independente do que as settings dissessem.

**Knob que a fábrica não repassa é knob que não existe.**

## Três limites

- **`--memory-swap`**, fixado no mesmo valor de `--memory`. Sem ele o Docker concede swap **igual ao limite, por cima dele** — então um container de 512m encosta em um giga e o teto vira enfeite.
- **`--cpus`**, porque laço ocupado sem teto mata a máquina em que o agente está rodando, o agente incluído.
- **`--pids-limit`**, que não é copiado de ninguém: PID **não** é namespaced por padrão, então fork bomb dentro do container esgota a tabela de processos do **host**. Existe a regra léxica `fork_bomb`, mas ela só dispara sob governança — e governança é off por padrão.

## O que ficou de fora, de propósito

`--storage-opt size=` é o quarto limite óbvio e é o errado de adicionar. O Docker **recusa** a flag fora de xfs com pquota, então o caso comum (overlay2 em ext4, todo laptop) viraria falha dura no primeiro comando. Tem teste afirmando a **ausência** dela — "quarto limite óbvio" é exatamente o que um leitor futuro adiciona sem saber por que foi deixado fora.

## E os knobs

`CHIMERA_SANDBOX_NETWORK=none|bridge` (mais `MEMORY`/`CPUS`/`PIDS`). A rede continua `none`; o knob existe para o número de adoção virar **mensurável** em vez de teórico.

**Não é allowlist de egresso, e isso não é esquecimento:** o Chimera é um `pip install` em laptop, e Docker Desktop no Windows/macOS não tem cadeia `DOCKER-USER` para enganchar. Se o número um dia justificar filtrar, o caminho é proxy de saída no compose, nunca iptables no host.

## ⚠️ O que NÃO foi medido

O roteiro pedia **fork bomb e laço de CPU rodando sob o sandbox, com e sem as flags**. **Isso não aconteceu** — não há daemon Docker nesta máquina nem no CI.

O que está verificado é que as flags **chegam à linha de comando**. É uma alegação mais fraca que "o fork bomb foi contido", e está escrita como a mais fraca — inclusive no topo do módulo de teste, não só aqui. A medição real está no arquivo atrás de um `skipif`, para rodar em quem tiver daemon.

| quebra | resultado |
|---|---|
| fábrica voltar a não repassar | 2 de 10 reprovam |
| remover `--memory-swap` | outros 2 reprovam |

| portão | resultado |
|---|---|
| `ruff check .` | limpo |
| `mypy chimera` | 305 arquivos |
| `pytest -q` (WSL) | 3274 passando, 13 skipped |

author: takumin
body:
`build/<name>/mrbgems/gem_init.o`, the object that boots every gem of a
build, is the one object `tasks/mrbgems.rake` declares by hand: a `file`
task without an action, with the generated `gem_init.c` and `LEGAL` as its
prerequisites. Rake finds the rule for it, but only when the task runs,
after it has already answered `needed?` from those two files alone. The
`.d` its compile writes and the flags record beside it are read by the
prerequisite procs of the rule, and for this object those never ran. A
header it includes changing, or a define reaching the build by a way that
leaves `MRUBY_CONFIG` untouched, left the old object in `libmruby.a`.

The header case is visible from the outside. `gem_init.c` reads `mrb->c`
and `mrb->exc`; add a field at the top of `struct mrb_state` and run
`rake`:

```console
$ rake                        # built once
$ sed -i 's/^  struct mrb_jmpbuf \*jmp;$/&\n  void *probe_pad;/' include/mruby.h
$ rake                        # 152 CC, gem_init.o not among them
$ bin/mruby -e 'p 1'
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
$ rake                        # nothing to do
$ bin/mruby -e 'p 1'
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

Every other object of the build is compiled again; `gem_init.o` keeps the
old offset of `mrb->c`, and `mrb_init_mrbgems` dies at `mrb->c->cibase`
under `mrb_open`.

## Why

`file objfile(gem_init) => [gem_init.c, LEGAL]` (2013, 15871eb84) exists to
have a build write `LEGAL` without archiving it: `LEGAL` used to sit in
the object list of `libmruby.a` and was moved to a prerequisite of this
object. Rake's `Task#execute` runs `enhance_with_matching_rule` for a task
without an action, so the rule's action does compile the object, and its
prerequisite procs do run then; but that is after `invoke` decided from
the written prerequisites whether to execute at all. `mrblib.o`, the other
generated object of core, declares no task and is built by the rule from
`Compiler#define_rules` alone, which reads the `.d` and discards an output
whose recorded flags differ (#7236).

## What this does

- `tasks/mrbgems.rake` no longer declares the object. The rule pairs
  `mrbgems/gem_init.o` with `mrbgems/gem_init.c` in the build directory as
  it does for `mrblib.o`, and its `.d` and flags record take effect.
- `LEGAL` becomes a product of the build in `tasks/libmruby.rake`, beside
  the `libmruby.a` whose contents it describes. It stays out of the
  archive as before, and it is still written by a plain `rake`. A build
  without a gem writes it too now, with the mruby license alone; the
  `mrbc` build (`disable_libmruby`) still does not.

## Verified

`rake -m -j16`, `CCACHE_DISABLE=1`, gcc; `default` gembox with
`enable_bintest` and `enable_test`; the build directory built once on
`master` (0122b457d) before each row, and the run after each row does
nothing in both columns.

| change | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| a field added to `struct mrb_state` in `include/mruby.h` | 152 `CC`, `gem_init.o` not among them; `bin/mruby -e 'p 1'` segfaults, and still does after another `rake` | 153 `CC`, `gem_init.o` among them; `bin/mruby -e 'p 1'` prints 1 |
| `touch include/mruby.h` | 152 `CC`, `gem_init.o` not among them | 153 `CC` |
| `conf.cc.defines << "PROBE_FLAG=1"` from an environment variable the config reads (`MRUBY_CONFIG` untouched) | 165 `CC`, `gem_init.o` not among them, its flags record has no `PROBE_FLAG` | 166 `CC`, `gem_init.o` among them, its flags record has `-DPROBE_FLAG=1`; the variable removed: 166 `CC` again |
| `rake -m -j16 test` from an empty build directory | bintest OK 111, mrbtest OK 2073 | bintest OK 111, mrbtest OK 2073, 0 KO, 0 crash |
| `rake -m -j16 test MRUBY_CONFIG=ci/gcc-clang` from an empty build directory | | every target 0 KO, 0 crash; `LEGAL` in every target's build directory |
| `LEGAL` after a clean build | `build/host/LEGAL`, none in `build/host/mrbc/`, `ar t libmruby.a` has no `LEGAL` | the same file, byte for byte, in the same places, and none in the archive |
| a config with no gem | no `LEGAL` | `build/host/LEGAL` with the mruby license alone |

The 165 in the master column is 208 objects less the 42 Prism objects
(#7248) and this one.

## Environment

<details>

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Linux 7.0.0-29-generic, x86_64 |
| Compiler | gcc 13.3.0 |
| binutils | 2.47 |
| Ruby | 4.0.6 |
| rake | 13.3.1 |

The compile line of `gem_init.o` in the default build, unchanged by this
PR (the record beside the object; `%{flags}` is the `flags:` line):

```console
gcc -MMD -c -std=gnu99 -g -O3 -Wall -Wundef -Werror-implicit-function-declaration -Wwrite-strings -DHAVE_MRUBY_REGEXP_GEM -DMRB_USE_SET -DHAVE_MRUBY_IO_GEM -DMRB_USE_RATIONAL -DMRB_USE_COMPLEX -DMRB_USE_BIGINT -DMRB_USE_DEBUG_HOOK -I"include" -I"build/host/include" -o "build/host/mrbgems/gem_init.o" "build/host/mrbgems/gem_init.c"
```

</details>

No C source changes and the compile line is the same, so `.text` is
unaffected in every build.
