<!-- PR_BODY_START -->
## Summary
- Gives `lib/test/regenerate-artifacts.py`'s batched pass per-row progress on stderr and a per-row wall-clock bound, so a caller can attribute the wait to a row and a wedged row is terminated rather than hanging the pass.
- A timed-out row is killed together with its whole POSIX process group and reported by name as an INFRASTRUCTURE (exit 2) outcome, because it established nothing.
- Test-only: the change is confined to `lib/test/`, which the vendor slice prunes from the shipped plugin.

## Changes
**Batched pass (`lib/test/regenerate-artifacts.py`)**: `run_row` now emits an attributed `start`/`done` line per row on stderr (`_emit_progress`) while the accumulated `report` keeps its stdout `finally` flush byte-for-byte. The single `subprocess.run` dispatch is replaced by `_run_bounded`, which launches the child in its own session (`start_new_session` on POSIX), enforces a wall-clock timeout, and on expiry calls `_terminate_tree` to `os.killpg` the whole group (falling back to a direct-child kill off POSIX or when the group is gone). A bounded-out row is reported as `[<row>] INFRASTRUCTURE ... exceeded its declared bound` and routed to exit 2, never the exit-1 "action required" state.

**Per-row declared bound**: every command-backed `ROWS` entry (5 rows) now declares an integer `timeout_seconds`, validated at import by `_validate_registry` exactly like `preflight_eligible` (absent / non-int / bool each raises). Each bound is `measurement x multiple` recorded in the row comment: `capability-profile-literals` 0.064s x500 = 32; `plugin-identity-regions` 0.044s x500 = 22; `coverage-map-ratchet` 0.623s x50 = 31; `exact-module-floors` 137.44s x4 = 550; `env-freeze-advisory-region` 0.044s x500 = 22. The superseded 465.9s figure in the `exact-module-floors` preflight comment is corrected to the re-measured ~137s under the landed `--heavy-units smoke` bounding.

**Override**: `DEVFLOW_ARTIFACT_ROW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (`_row_timeout_override`) replaces every row's bound when set to a positive integer; empty behaves as unset; a malformed or non-positive value is refused loudly with an exit-2 message naming the variable and the value. All new APIs are stdlib-only and POSIX-only calls are guarded.

**Tests & provenance (`lib/test/modules/regenerate-artifacts.sh`, `.inventory.md`, `coverage-map.json`)**: adds the `#1457` arms and a contract-group inventory row; registers issue 1457 under the `regenerate-artifacts` owner in the coverage map.

## Resolves
Resolves #1457

## Test Plan
- [ ] `lib/test/run-module.sh regenerate-artifacts` passes (the module carries the `#1457` arms; CI ran it at 401 assertions passed, exit 0).
- [ ] AC1: a clean fixture run writes `regenerate-artifacts: row <name>: start`/`done` lines to stderr and no progress line leaks onto stdout, while the stdout report keeps its `[<row>] clean` line.

- [ ] `ruff check lib/test/regenerate-artifacts.py` is clean (AC8 portability / stdlib-only).

author: kyh
body:
## What

Takes the material from [`improve-threejs`](https://github.com/millionco/react-doctor/tree/main/skills/improve-threejs) in `millionco/react-doctor` and integrates it into the skills that already own each topic. No new skill is added — the earlier version of this PR added one beside `threejs`, and this replaces it.

## Where each piece landed

**`threejs/references/debugging-and-profiling.md`**

- **"Auditing a scene you didn't just write."** Debugging starts from a symptom; an audit doesn't, so the failure mode is fixing whatever you read first. Adds the hot-path map, the HIGH/MEDIUM triage ranked by where code runs, and the by-hand checks no tool reports. Every item routes into the section that already covers the fix (§ Performance, § Memory leaks, § Physics) instead of restating it.
- **React Three Fiber.** `vg new --engine react-r3f` is a shipped preset that routes to the `threejs` skill, and the repo had **zero** R3F content anywhere. Adds a vanilla→R3F mapping of the same failures — `useFrame` allocation, `setState` in the loop, `useMemo` and `args` identity, `<Instances>`, `useGLTF`, `frameloop="demand"` — plus `react-doctor` scoped to the React half it can actually see.
- **"Visual defects — sweep with evidence."** The 10-row rubric, run against `vg playtest` frames rather than source, with each usual cause pointing at the existing reference.

**`threejs/references/graphics-recipes.md`** — the two visual-defect families with no coverage at all:

- Shadow acne / peter-panning / shadow flicker — `bias` vs `normalBias`, and frustum sizing (halving the frustum buys what doubling `mapSize` does, for free).
- Texture shimmer / crawl / moiré — anisotropy, AA silently lost once you render through an `EffectComposer`, geometry too thin to rasterize.

**`threejs/SKILL.md`** — routing rows for the new sections, and the description now carries the audit triggers ("my three.js game is slow", "why does it look washed out") and R3F/drei trigger words, so the `react-r3f` preset resolves here.

**`playtest/SKILL.md`** — one line: a visual diff catches a *change*, not a frame that was wrong to begin with; pair the screenshots with the 3D rubric.

## What was deliberately not copied

Z-fighting (already a full section with four ranked fixes), color management, DPR capping, the `disposeObject` walker, and transparency sorting were all already covered. Those rubric rows link to the existing material rather than duplicating it.

The upstream skill is React-Doctor-first; here the scanner is one optional input for R3F projects, since the primary preset is vanilla Three.js and a React scanner sees nothing in a vanilla scene.

## Testing

- `oxfmt --check` clean across 1069 files.
- `scripts/check-skill-refs.ts` clean — 114 markdown files, no broken cross-references.
- The `threejs` and `playtest` skills reload with the edited frontmatter/content.

## Note on provenance

Because this is integrated prose rather than a vendored file, there's no separate `LICENSE` in the tree. Upstream is a Modified MIT license (its restrictions cover ML training data, and selling the software as a product deriving substantially from it) — flagging it so you can decide whether you want an attribution line somewhere; say the word and I'll add one.

author: sylophi
body:
## Description

Only one copy of the app may run against a data root now. The lock is requested before the data root is resolved and before anything with side effects starts, so a second copy (typically a fresh download sitting beside the installed app) never spins up a rival state watcher, background fetcher, updater or script registry. The losing process leaves through `app.exit`, which skips `before-quit` entirely, so it cannot show the busy prompt or reap the running instance's scripts. When a second launch arrives, the running copy restores and focuses its window instead of saying anything to the user, since seeing the app is what the launch asked for. Dev builds now get their own userData directory, because Electron scopes the lock to userData and dev and packaged builds otherwise resolve the same one.

author: ruby-dlee
body:
Found by driving the first real cloud crewmate. The slot-2 create failed with:

```
(OperationNotAllowed) Cannot modify extensions in the VM when the VM is not running.
```

## Why it happens

A create does not always build a new VM. The ARM deployment is idempotent, so a create that replays, or one that follows a failed attempt, converges onto the worker that already exists. Meanwhile the TTL shutdown schedule deallocates idle workers, so the VM a create converges onto is very often stopped.

Azure refuses run commands against stopped compute, and **nothing else in this provider can start a VM**: every other power operation here deallocates. So the slot wedges with no owned way out, and the only recovery is an operator running `az vm start` by hand. That is what unblocked the live drive, and it should not have been a manual step.

## Fix

The create proves the worker is running before any guest-facing call and starts it if it is not. The start carries its own bound, since an ARM power operation is measured in minutes rather than the seconds a control-plane call takes, and that bound is added to the create budget the controller timeout is checked against.

## Verification

`tests/fm-azure-pilot.test.sh` exits 0, judged by exit code. The create-replay driver answers the power query with a **deallocated** worker, which is the ordinary state of one whose TTL has fired, and asserts the start is issued before the first guest-facing call and carries more than the ordinary bound.

Four mutations at production call sites, each verified as actually applied before the result was recorded, each red:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| `ensure_worker_running` call site removed (not the definition) | red |
| call moved after the bootstrap run command | red |
| start reverted to the ordinary control-plane bound | red |
| power check made to treat every state as running | red |

author: lonsetnik-dot
body:
…d one

CI failed on main with two failures out of ~1,850 checks. Neither was a product defect — both were assertions that depend on timing, which is why the local runs were green (CI also runs verify_qr_decode.py, skipped locally for a missing PIL; it passed 80/80).

1. "peds: deep link lands with card 16 in view" (mine). The check slept a fixed 600 ms for the deep-linked card to settle; a slower CI runner had not finished. It now polls for the settled state.

   Investigating that surfaced a real bug in the re-anchor itself: it compared the card's VIEWPORT position to decide whether layout had settled, and that is ~0 immediately after scrollIntoView — so it declared victory on the first retry while the cards above were still growing. It now compares the document-relative position, so it detects growth as intended.

   Verified under 6-8x CPU throttling (a loaded CI runner): 15/15 landings, no misses. Also confirmed the re-anchor yields to a reader who scrolls — zero scrollIntoView calls after user input. (A deep-linked page still jumps once as it finishes loading; that is the browser's own fragment anchoring, not this code.)

2. "12. it agrees with the browser clock" (pre-existing, from f7f3671). It compared the page's stamped time of death against a single new Date() at assertion time, so it failed whenever the minute rolled over in between — got=19:53 want=19:54. It now accepts any minute the pronouncement actually spanned, and no others, so a genuinely wrong stamp still fails.

A flaky suite is worse than no suite: it teaches the next person that red is normal, which is exactly when the harness stops protecting anyone.

author: alphabet-h
body:
Phase 4, PR 5 of 5 — the last one. #173 added `Origin` validation, #174 rebuilt
`/ui`, #175 turned the README back into an entry point, #176 gave it a face.
This publishes what #175 moved out.

## Source: `docs/`, not the repository root

Branch publishing offers exactly two folders, and the difference is not small:

| | root `/` | **`/docs`** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Markdown published | 94, **32 of them synthetic test fixtures** | **40** (22 reference pages + 18 ADR files) |
| Everything else | Jekyll copies unprocessed files as static assets — the source tree, 109 `.rs` files | nothing outside `docs/` |
| Front page | the README | `docs/index.md`, added here |
| Upkeep | an exclusion list, maintained forever against a repository that is mostly not documentation | none; a directory is an allow-list by construction |

## Both languages

Every page already linked to its counterpart, and `jekyll-relative-links` is on
by default on GitHub Pages, so **the language switch is the text that was
already there**. The two `stability` pages were the only pair missing the link.

Worth recording how that was counted: grepping for the wording found four gaps,
because two pages write `> **English**:` where the rest write
`> **English version**:`. Checking for a *link whose target is the counterpart
file* found two. The structural check is the one that is right.

## Six links pointed outside the published tree

`docs/clients{,.ja}.md` and `docs/configuration{,.ja}.md` linked to
`../grooveseek/examples/…` and `../grooveseek/groove.toml.example`. On a site
rooted at `docs/` those resolve to nothing. They are absolute now — the same
rule the README's images follow: **a reference that crosses the published
boundary cannot be relative.** A script that resolves every relative link in
`docs/` against its own directory reports zero escapes now.

## The one real risk, measured before merging rather than after

The site is rendered by **kramdown**, not by GitHub's markdown pipeline — and
the 14 cross-file anchors verified during #175 were verified against the
latter, with `gh api markdown`. Seven of them are Japanese.

kramdown's documentation says *"Only ASCII characters are used in headers IDs"*
in the passage motivating its transliteration option, which reads like non-ASCII
is dropped. The workarounds if that were true are all closed: `{#custom-id}`
renders as literal text on GitHub, and `transliterated_header_ids` needs a gem
Pages does not ship.

So it was rendered through kramdown in a container instead of guessed at:

```
<h2 id="設定ファイルの探索順">
<h4 id="信頼する置き場所--しない置き場所">
<h2 id="http-トランスポート-複数クライアント同時接続">
<h2 id="ライブ同期-file-watcher">
<h2 id="frontmatter-スキーマ検証">
<h2 id="huggingface-の-tls-失敗への対処-初回-dl-時">
<h2 id="コマンドラインからの一発検索">
```

**Byte for byte what GitHub generates.** Nothing to work around.

## What happens after merge

Pages is not enabled yet (`gh api repos/…/pages` returns 404). Enabling it is
a settings change and was agreed separately:

```
gh api -X POST repos/alphabet-h/grooveseek/pages \
  -f 'source[branch]=main' -f 'source[path]=/docs'
```

Then the build result, the rendered pages, the language switch and the anchors
get checked on the live site, and **only then** does the README gain a link to
it. A link that is dead on arrival is worse than one added a minute later.

## Not in this PR

- Custom domain, analytics, sitemap
- An ADR index page — no link inside `docs/` refers to `decisions/` as a
  directory, so nothing would reach it
- Any edit to `docs/decisions/**`. ADR-0003's filename still says
  `kb-mcpignore`; an ADR is not edited after merge, and ADR-0007 explains why
  `kb-mcp` in anything dated before 2026-08-17 means this project. The site
  index says so too, since the URL will show it

## Checks

Link checker: **317 relative links, 0 broken**, and 0 escaping `docs/`.
`cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
clean — no code changes here, but the tree is verified.

## Summary
Fixes a crash: `TypeError: The "string" argument must be of type string or an instance of Buffer or ArrayBuffer. Received an instance of Object` thrown from `@neondatabase/serverless`'s `addCString`/`startup`.

## Root cause
`frontend/src/lib/db.ts` created the `Pool`/`PrismaClient` eagerly at module scope. This module is imported (via `page.tsx`/`auth.ts`) during `next build`'s page-data collection step, which runs even though `DATABASE_URL` is only provided at runtime. The previous hardcoded fallback connection string was also malformed, which caused the `Pool` to end up with an invalid value in its Postgres startup packet.

## Changes
- `frontend/src/lib/db.ts`: The Prisma client is now lazily instantiated via a `Proxy`. The connection string is only read and the `Pool`/`PrismaClient` only constructed on first actual use (at runtime), not at module import time.
- Removed the hardcoded fallback connection string entirely. If a query is attempted without `DATABASE_URL` set, a clear `DATABASE_URL environment variable is not set` error is thrown instead of silently falling back or crashing with an obscure low-level TypeError.

## Verification
- Importing `db.ts` with `DATABASE_URL` unset succeeds (no eager DB connection attempt).
- The "not set" error only surfaces on the first actual `prisma.*` call.
- `next build` progresses past the DB initialization step.

## High-Assurance Engineering Upgrade

This PR implements the supplied ClearGlass high-assurance specification as a repository-native control layer.

### Included
- Adds `tools/high_assurance_verify.py` for dependency-free evidence, secret, workflow-gate, baseline-semantics, provenance-integrity, and governance checks.
- Adds `.github/workflows/high-assurance-verify.yml` with least-privilege permissions, pinned GitHub actions, reproducible checkout, artifact retention, and an explicit release decision.
- Upgrades `bots/artemis_provenance_bot.py` to schema v2 with source, publisher, license status, processing version, generator, validation/security state, confidence, limitations, SHA-256, size, and Git metadata.

### Evidence constraints
- Missing external analytics remain UNKNOWN/not collected; null is never treated as zero.
- The verifier fails on high-confidence secrets, broken provenance hashes/sizes, missing required governance files, invalid baseline semantics, or suppression of critical test/security gates.
- Informational/non-critical `continue-on-error` usage is reported rather than misclassified as a release-blocking defect.

### Release policy
This PR does not claim production success. GitHub Actions results are the authoritative validation evidence. Merge should occur only after the assurance gate and required repository protections pass.

author: ohdearquant
body:
## Summary

- The daemon auto-spawn path (`kkernel mcp` / `kkernel exec` spawning `kkernel mcp --daemon` when no warm daemon is reachable) only forwarded an explicit `--config`/`--db` override to the freshly spawned child, relying on ambient OS environment inheritance for everything else — including pack selection.
- That works when `KHIVE_PACKS` happens to be a plain OS environment variable, but a client whose pack selection came from an explicit `--pack` CLI flag, or from a discovered `[runtime].packs` entry in a project/home `khive.toml`, has nothing for the child to inherit.
- Result: the spawned daemon silently falls back to the built-in default pack set. Its config fingerprint then disagrees with the client that spawned it, so every subsequent request from that client falls back to local, in-process dispatch instead of the warm daemon — multiplying writer contention on the shared SQLite store.

## Root cause

- `crates/khive-mcp/src/server.rs` — the primary auto-spawn site hit by every interactive MCP stdio client — called the daemon-forward seam with no pack information at all.
- `crates/kkernel/src/exec.rs` — the `kkernel exec` daemon-forward seam — already forwarded `--config`/`--db` in narrow cases, but never forwarded packs either.
- `Command::new(exe)` inherits the parent's full environment by default (no `env_clear`/`env_remove` on this path), so `KHIVE_PACKS`-as-env-var cases mostly worked by accident; CLI-flag and config-file-derived selections did not.

## Fix shape

Forward the spawning client's already-resolved pack list explicitly as `--pack <name>` arguments on the spawned child, using the existing highest-precedence CLI-flag tier the config resolver already defines (`RuntimeConfigInputs::packs`) — no new precedence tier is introduced, and the daemon's own boot-time resolution is otherwise untouched.

- `crates/khive-mcp/src/daemon.rs`: `spawn_daemon_with_exe_and_config` and `forward_or_spawn_with_config` gained an `packs: Option<&[String]>` parameter, appended as `--pack` args when present. The bare `spawn_daemon`/`forward_or_spawn` helpers keep their old (no-packs) behavior unchanged.
- `crates/khive-mcp/src/server.rs`: the primary MCP stdio auto-spawn call site now forwards the loaded verb registry's own pack list (`self.registry.pack_names()`).
- `crates/kkernel/src/exec.rs`: the `kkernel exec` daemon-forward seam now forwards the client's resolved `cfg.packs` unconditionally, alongside its pre-existing conditional `--config`/`--db` forwarding.

## Test plan

All commands run from `crates/`:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → exit 0
- `cargo clippy -p kkernel -p khive-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` → exit 0
- `cargo test -p kkernel` → all test binaries green, including two new regression tests:
  - `env_khive_packs_reaches_daemon_spawn_seam` — a client with `KHIVE_PACKS` set forwards exactly that resolved list to the daemon spawn seam.
  - `no_env_control_forwards_built_in_default_packs_to_spawn_seam` — control: with no pack-selection input, the client forwards exactly the built-in default set (proving the fix is additive and the unconfigured default path's effective outcome is unchanged).
- `cargo test -p khive-mcp` → 142 passed, including new/updated `daemon::tests::spawn_daemon_with_exe_and_config_*` cases proving `--pack` flags reach the spawned child's actual command line (and are omitted when no packs are given).
- From repo root: `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` → exit 0

author: dt616
body:
Found while reviewing every call we make against Kent County's GIS server.

## What

Both `fetch_kent.py` and `fetch_grcity.py` do:

```python
session.headers["User-Agent"] = None
```

In `requests`, assigning `None` **removes** the header rather than sending an empty one, so every request from this workflow has been anonymous.

## Why it is worth changing

This job runs every 5 minutes forever. Against Kent County it hits the exact same endpoint the ingest host polls every 5 minutes, so the two together are ~576 requests/day, and **this workflow is a standing third of all Kent traffic from us, and was the only untraceable third.**

If Kent wants to rate-limit us, ask what we are doing, or tell us to stop, they had no way to know who to contact. An unidentified client is also a far better candidate for a WAF rule, on the upstream we least want to lose access to.

## Risk

None identified. `CanticaBlotter/1.0` already serves the identical Kent URL from the ingest host ~288 times/day without issue, so a branded UA is empirically fine on that exact endpoint.

Verified the constant resolves at import (a typo would be a `NameError` every 5 minutes, which `py_compile` does not catch) and that `requests` actually puts it on the wire.

Contact point is `cantica.dev`, not a personal email, since this repo is public.

## Deliberately not included

**Conditional GET.** The ingest-side twin sends `If-None-Match` and this one does not. I left it out on purpose: the Kent feed is a live ~20-record rolling buffer that changes on nearly every tick (our stored state currently reads `consecutive_304s: 0`), so the bandwidth saving is close to zero, while the change would add cross-run ETag state to a repo whose entire job is to never miss a snapshot. The ingest side also needs a force-refresh-every-6th-tick escape hatch because ETags on this endpoint are not fully trustworthy, and porting that machinery here buys nothing.

author: zmazza-mtech
body:
Closes #92.

The `backend tests` job failed on PR #48 for a reason that had nothing to do with #48, and the duplicate run of the same commit passed. The cause is in the test, not the code.

## What was wrong

```ts
// Flip one byte in the ciphertext portion
const tampered = parts[0] + ":" + "00" + parts[1]!.slice(2) + ":" + parts[2];
```

The comment says flip; the code assigns. When the ciphertext already begins with a zero byte the value is unchanged, GCM authenticates it, `decrypt` returns the plaintext, and `expect(...).toThrow()` fails. The nonce is random per call, so the leading byte is uniform over 256 values and the failure lands on an arbitrary PR.

## Measured before fixing

20,000 encrypt/tamper/decrypt cycles against the real `src/lib/crypto.ts`:

```
silently-untampered: 79/20000 = 1 in 253
```

Within sampling noise of the 1/256 the arithmetic predicts.

## The fix

`tamperFirstByte` XORs the byte that is actually there with `0xff`, so the value always changes. A second test drives 10,000 cycles through it and asserts every one throws — the property is pinned rather than sampled once per run. It costs 189ms for the file.

Nothing in `src/` changes. The Web Crypto port in `worker/tests/crypto.spec.ts:32` already flipped rather than assigned, so only the Node-side test needed it.

## Verification

```
backend  npx vitest run tests/unit/crypto.test.ts   7 passed (189ms)
backend  npx vitest run                             333 passed (12 files)
```

Landing this ahead of the rest of the Phase 0 chain (#63) so the chain is not re-run against a suite that fails 0.4% of the time — and ahead of #74, which makes CI a required check.

body:
### Motivation

- Prevent admin UI from entering an indefinite "Finalizing result" state when saving match results and ensure failures surface to the admin instead of hanging. 
- Ensure Gaming Alerts uses the platform's existing Tournament data and fixtures rather than allowing freestanding, tournament-less match entries. 
- Make push notification delivery a best-effort side-effect so missing/invalid FCM configuration cannot block or fail the core save.

### Description

- Added strong server-side validation in `createMatchResultAlert` to require and validate a `tournament_id` and a `source_id` that references a real `tournament_matches` fixture, and prevented insertion of disconnected match results (`src/features/notifications/server.js`).
- Decoupled FCM dispatch from the core save by wrapping push delivery in `try/catch` and returning/logging push errors rather than letting them fail the whole request (`src/features/notifications/server.js`).
- Hardened the admin match-entry UI to require selecting an existing tournament and a tournament-owned match, with `saving` state, `try/catch/finally` around the submit, and visible success/error messaging instead of an indefinite message (`src/app/admin/match-results/page.tsx`).
- Added an admin API to list tournament fixtures (`/api/admin/tournament-matches`) and updated the admin match-results POST handler to validate required fields server-side (`src/app/api/admin/tournament-matches/route.js`, `src/app/api/admin/match-results/route.js`).
- Updated the fantasy match finalization path to catch and log Gaming Alerts linkage failures so fantasy stat saves succeed even if notification linkage fails (`src/app/api/admin/fantasy/matches/[id]/stats/route.js`).
- Updated the Gaming Alerts feed UI to use platform tournaments and simplified per-result display to: Result (winner), MVP, 3rd place, 4th place (`src/app/gaming-alerts/page.tsx`).
- Added a DB migration to introduce `tournament_matches`, add `placement_3_name` and `placement_4_name` columns to `match_results`, normalize legacy source types to `tournament_match`, and add a constraint that future `match_results` must reference a tournament (migration: `supabase/migrations/202608180002_link_match_results_to_tournament_matches.sql`).

### Testing

- Ran targeted ESLint on modified frontend files with `npx eslint src/app/admin/match-results/page.tsx src/app/gaming-alerts/page.tsx`, which completed successfully for those files. 
- Ran project-wide lint `npm run lint`, which failed due to unrelated, pre-existing lint issues elsewhere in the repo (these are not caused by the changes in this PR). 
- Ran TypeScript compile check `npx tsc --noEmit`, which failed due to unrelated pre-existing TypeScript errors in other parts of the codebase; the changes in this PR do not introduce new global type regressions.

body:
🚨 **Severity:** HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** The internal API key check in the storage check route used strict string equality (`===`), making it vulnerable to timing attacks where an attacker could theoretically guess the key by measuring response times.
🎯 **Impact:** An attacker could potentially bypass authentication on the internal `/api/admin/storage-check` route.
🔧 **Fix:** Replaced strict equality with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` using Buffers. Added buffer length checks to prevent `RangeError` exceptions and ensured that empty string bypasses are mitigated if the `.env` value is missing.
✅ **Verification:** Run `pnpm test` and `pnpm lint` to ensure no regressions. The route logic was visually inspected to ensure `timingSafeEqual` fails securely on empty strings or mismatched lengths.

## What changed

Two gates this repository already owns were not being run.

### 1. `civvis_inert.py` has documented a CI ratchet since it was written

Its own docstring says `--max 0  # CI ratchet`. No workflow ever called it. It
needs nothing but the repository, so nothing stood in the way — and a data key
whose consumer is refactored away goes on doing nothing with every gate green.
That is the exact failure the docstring describes: the Sphinx kept two dead
effects through fourteen iterations and no test noticed.

Wired at `--max 1`. Of the three findings:

| key | verdict |
|---|---|
| `ai_value` (nazca_line) | **waived** — the engine values improvements from yields, not from a data-supplied score |
| `scenario_only` (11 improvements) | **waived** — all eleven are already `unbuildable: true`, which is the real gate |
| `force_retreat` (winged_hussar) | **not waived — a real defect** |

`force_retreat` is Poland's Winged Hussar ability, present in `data/units.json`
and read by nothing, so the unit is a plain Cuirassier replacement with no
unique. Left unwaived deliberately so the ratchet keeps pointing at it; fixed
separately, and the number drops to zero with it.

### 2. The Lua mod tests were named one per step

Six steps, six files. That is the same shape that left **twenty-five `tools/`
suites ungated** (fixed in `collaboration-policy.yml`) and one of `beta/`'s six
scripts broken for two separate reasons with nobody running it (#1905). The list
is complete today; what it cannot do is stay complete on its own — and a mod
test no gate runs fails *inside Civilization VI*, on a machine with a 45-minute
feedback loop.

Now discovered, and **fails when the glob comes up empty**, so a rename cannot
quietly empty the gate the way a hand-written list quietly shrinks it.

Injected a fake effect key into `data/improvements.json`: the ratchet names both
the key and the file, and passes again once reverted.

```

  totally_fake_key     improvements.json
```

`--max 1` passes and `--max 0` fails, which is the ratchet doing its job against
the one outstanding defect.

body: ## 用户反馈 登录成功、右上角挂着自己的名字，`/chat` 却顶着「登录状态已过期，当前提问按游客额度计算，也不会存入你的账号」。 ## 她不是错觉——生产证据 user 638（显示名 CFFF，无 BYOK）。时间全部换算成 CST： ``` 08:43:24 notifications/unread-count 401 + chat/sessions 401 ← 票在这一刻死了 08:43:30 登录 200 08:47:29 登录 200 ← 4 分钟后又登一次 08:55:12 登录 200 ← 再登一次 09:16:01 截图：横幅仍在 09:16:11 last_active_at 被顶到这一刻 ``` `LastActiveMiddleware` **只在 `verify_token` 通过时才写库**（`main.py:379-386`），所以 09:16:11 那次更新证明她当时握着的是一张**有效**票。横幅在说谎。35 分钟内登录三次，就是「登录成功了它还这么说」的现场。 ## 机制 `/chat/quota` 对过期票**不回 401，而是 200 + `authenticated: false`**（`chat.py:336-347`，#1196 有意立的契约，为的是让前端分得清「你是游客」和「你的登录刚死」）。 于是： 1. 票死掉 → 这份「你是游客」的答案被缓存到 `["chatQuota", 638]` 2. 她重新登录 → **还是 638** → queryKey 一模一样 3. 全局 `staleTime: 5min`（`main.tsx:23`）→ 直接命中缓存，不重取 4. `user && quota && !quota.authenticated` 恒成立 → 横幅活过了修好它的那次登录 #1196 把常量 key 换成带 user id，只隔得开「游客 ↔ 本人」，**隔不开「本人·票已死 ↔ 本人·刚换票」**。全项目没有任何一处在登录后 `invalidateQueries`。 ## 修法 配额答案只对**取它时用的那张票**成立，所以票属于 key 的一部分： ```diff - queryKey: ["chatQuota", user?.id ?? "anon"], + queryKey: ["chatQuota", user?.id ?? "anon", token ?? "anon"], ``` 滑动续期（#1198）换票时也会换 key，代价是每次轮换多一个 2ms 请求——值。 `ProfilePage` 同源同修：#1199 给 `chat-quota` 加 user id，在同一人重登这一格上一样漏，过期期间缓存的 `limit 10` 会继续冒充本人上限 200。 ## 为什么门禁没拦住 **两个测试 harness 的 `QueryClient` 默认 `staleTime` 都是 0**，任何情况都会重取，结构上复现不出「缓存命中」。新用例自己注入带生产 `staleTime` 的客户端并跨两次渲染复用它。 两条回归用例都**实测过「撤掉修复会红」**： - `ChatPage`：撤掉修复时报 `expected 登录状态已过期，当前提问按游客额度计算… to be null` —— 复现出的正是用户截图里那一行原文 - `ProfilePage`：撤掉修复时 `200 free questions a day` 等不到 ## 门禁 ESLint 0 · tsc 0 · i18n 0 · vite build 0 · **vitest 519/519**（均按退出码判定）

author: bre77
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Disabling every Teslemetry entity on a vehicle did not stop its polling. The
vehicle coordinator consumed firmware (`sw_version`) through an
integration-owned listener that stayed registered for the life of the config
entry. Because that listener was always attached, the coordinator's listener
set never emptied, so Home Assistant kept it scheduled and the metered
60-second `vehicle_data` poll continued even when the user had disabled every
entity fed by it — leaving no way to stop a poll that can be charged.

This removes that listener and consumes firmware opportunistically inside the
coordinator's update instead. The only listeners left on the vehicle
coordinator are now its entities, so disabling all of them empties the listener
set, Home Assistant unschedules the coordinator, and polling stops entirely —
zero calls, not a smaller request. Enabling at least one entity resumes
polling.

Endpoint selection is deliberately **not** the lever here. The coordinator
still requests its full fixed set of `vehicle_data` endpoint groups every
cycle, because the complete payload feeds both the cached vehicle data and the
SSE stream that publishes it. Narrowing the requested endpoints would starve
the cache and the stream, so it must not be reintroduced.

What this deliberately does not solve:
- Polling is all-or-nothing per vehicle: as long as one entity on the vehicle
  coordinator is enabled, the full `vehicle_data` request runs. There is no
  per-endpoint reduction, by design (see above).
- The unconditional first read at setup/reload runs regardless of entity state.
- The hourly metadata coordinator is left unchanged: its two listeners drive
  subscription discovery and repair synchronisation independently of entity
  state, and `metadata()` is a free (non-metered) call.
- Energy-site info is out of scope here; #178735 removes its recurring polling
  by moving it to SSE.

body:
## Summary

Four defects surfaced while investigating funeralworks run `2d7527f1`, which died in phase 2½ after 55 workers and $12.46. **That abort was correct behaviour** — the task fenced off `src/lib` and then required fixing a constant defined only inside it — and is not what this PR fixes. The four are: the resolved `source_of_truth` never reaching planners on one branch; the reconciler being told to read a `scope_note` the payload never sent; `extent: external` lacking a carve-out for a surface the task itself fences off; and the phase-2½ abort message steering operators to the wrong repair.

## Which layer(s) does this PR touch?

(See [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md) for the three-layer rule.)

- [x] `docs/DESIGN.md` (architecture)
- [x] `docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md` (code surface)
- [x] `orchestrator/leerie.py` (code)
- [x] docs (`README.md`, `docs/USAGE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, etc.) — `CLAUDE.md`, plus `prompts/{planner,reconciler,pr_writer,implementer}.md`
- [x] tests (`tests/`)
- [ ] CI / repo meta (`.github/`)

If multiple, has the change propagated **top-down** per the three-layer rule
(DESIGN → IMPLEMENTATION → code)?

- [x] yes
- [ ] not applicable (single layer)

DESIGN §5 gained the third `extent: external` kind and DESIGN §11 was disambiguated (a non-feature task skips the *question*, never the *setting*) before the code changed; IMPLEMENTATION was updated to match; the code follows both. Where the code and a prompt disagreed (`scope_note`), the payload was changed rather than the prompt, because the alternative was narrowing a documented resolution channel.

## Task-completion checklist

(Mirrors `CLAUDE.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.)

- [x] `docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md` updated if code surface changed
- [x] `docs/DESIGN.md` updated if architecture changed
- [ ] `pytest tests/` passes — **not run on the final tree, deliberately; see Testing notes**
- [x] `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('orchestrator/leerie.py').read())"` passes
- [x] `git diff --stat` reviewed for scope (no collateral edits)

## Testing notes

**51 new tests** across three files, plus a manual behavioural harness.

The discipline this change kept relearning is now recorded in `CLAUDE.md`: **a test asserting structure must be paired with one asserting substance.** Four measured instances drove that, each caught only by mutation and each initially green:

| structural assertion | what passed it |
|---|---|
| payload has key `scope_note` | `"scope_note": ""` — key shipped, planner text discarded |
| `phase_plan` calls the helper | ctx reads the preference directly, or omits the key |
| every remediation phrase present | the wrong repair hoisted to lead |
| `die(_unresolvable_die_message(...))` in source | the gate reads a key that never exists, never fires — **140 tests green** |

So the new tests execute rather than inspect wherever possible: the phase-2½ gate aborts for real, all three `State`-holding consumers are driven end to end, and every value is asserted against its own subject rather than "somewhere in the output". `tests/manual/planner_fence_probe.py` is the behavioural probe for the prompt change — not collected by pytest (`python_files = test_*.py`), following the `tests/fixtures/incident_2026_07_19/generate.py` precedent — and its docstring records the exact invocation that produced the 17/18 figure, so the number is reproducible rather than merely cited.

**Verification actually run:**

- `ast.parse` on `orchestrator/leerie.py`, and `tests/test_no_undefined_names.py`.
- The 19-mutant matrix, still 19/19, plus 12 further mutants proven individually.

**Why `pytest tests/` is unticked.** The maintainer asked that the full suite not be used as a validation step for this work, so it was not run against the final tree. It did pass earlier in the branch (7346 passed, 85 skipped), but that was several rounds of edits ago and I am not citing it as evidence for what is here now. Worth a full run in CI or before merge.

**Not covered by any test here:** a live end-to-end leerie run against a task carrying a scope fence. Every layer below that is verified; that one is not.

author: jonathan308
body:
Resubmission of #2609 (closed unmerged during a batch close, no review feedback). Content unchanged, rebased onto current main (v0.6.1) and re-tested — targeted suite passes. Production-validated on our serving fork since Aug 12.

---

## perf(scheduler): drop per-token cumulative output id copy in decode

`_process_batch_responses` built every streamed `RequestOutput` with `output_token_ids=list(request.output_token_ids)`, copying the entire output history at each decode step. Over an N-token response that's O(N²) element copies (~32M for 8k tokens), multiplied by batch size — pure Python overhead on the engine thread between GPU steps.

Mid-stream outputs now leave `output_token_ids` empty; the finished output still carries the complete cumulative list (owned copy), so the final-output contract is byte-identical. Consumer audit: the output-collector merge only forwards the latest list, the stop-sequence buffer reads it solely on terminal outputs, `generate()`/`generate_batch_sync()` keep only finished outputs, and the SSE layer never reads token ids — all benefit automatically with no behavior change. `new_token_ids` is untouched.

Adds `TestOutputTokenIdsCopy` regression coverage: mid-stream outputs carry no history, the finished output matches the request's `output_token_ids` at finish. 507+ scheduler/output/server/engine tests pass; ruff on touched files unchanged vs main.

author: boxpkaka
body:
## What changed

- score short terminal speech from its real PCM before Speaker VAD decides whether to reject the final result
- preserve a diarization-proven non-target suffix across native stream resets so it cannot leak as a later final
- when a target-to-other split is discovered only at `finish`, publish the clean target endpoint/final first and let the replayed suffix own the unique terminal result
- stop exposing a synthetic `-1` speaker similarity when no score exists
- align Android terminal scoring when Speaker VAD is enabled without voiceprint-result output
- measure finish-recovery latency from the recovered non-empty final instead of an earlier partial

## Root cause

Short PTT utterances could finish before streaming Speaker VAD produced a confirming window, so Harmony rejected the final before attempting its terminal PCM score. For target-to-other speech, the clean split replayed the non-target suffix into a new native stream, but subsequent stream resets cleared the rejection state. A split found only during `finish` also marked the clean target prefix as the session's last result, preventing the suffix from being gated separately.

## Behavior and scope

Business callers do not need to append artificial silence before `finish`. The SDK scores real speech PCM, publishes exactly one terminal result, and rejects a suffix independently proven to belong to the departing non-target speaker. Ambiguous margins, overlap, and unsupported turn shapes remain fail-open; no synthetic score or silence is introduced.

## Automated validation

- 52 Harmony speaker-turn, PCM-buffer, and rejected-final lifecycle tests pass
- 33 device-stress harness tests pass
- automatic AGC static release gate passes
- Android Release AAR assembly and both `sdk` / `sdk-dingqiao` Release unit-test suites pass locally with the same four tasks as CI
- full AGC evidence rerun on the current Harmony Runtime source: 500 normal-volume utterances, 500 controlled -30/-40/-50/-60/-70 dBFS cases, customer SNR scan, 213.28 s long audio, and repository -80 dB regression

## Harmony device validation

Device: VYG-AL30, OpenHarmony 6.1.1.120, ZH_EN test carrier.

Current PR HEAD `f0eb5f6`:

- finish compatibility release gate PASS: callback-api-reentrant 3 cycles and finish-shutdown 10 cycles; unique last then complete, empty-final rate 0
- speaker-vad-turn PASS on three target-to-other fixtures (100 ms gap, 250 ms gap, no gap); required/forbidden text and one non-empty public final per case; empty-final rate 0

Harmony Runtime-identical HEAD `cf19430` (the only later change is Android Release-test keep configuration):

- voiceprint-fallback PASS, 6 cycles including cold/warm extraction; first non-empty final scored; empty-final rate 0
- voiceprint-vad-begin PASS, 3 cycles
- paced PASS, 3 cycles and >60 s
- user-sequence PASS, 30 cycles; RSS growth 4.8 MiB; empty-final rate 0

Two short cold voiceprint runs are retained as non-canonical memory failures: SDK contracts passed, while the default 64 MiB RSS threshold counted the one-time voiceprint model residency (about 92–95 MiB). The six-cycle canonical run records the residency with a 128 MiB mode-specific ceiling; transcript, score, callback, and lifecycle assertions were unchanged.

## Review status

- all GitHub review threads, including automated suggestions: none open at the latest check
- current-head Android CI: pending

author: mordam
body:
The Epic Advocate's stall sweep now knows the difference between a window that died and a window that finished the way the brief asked it to, so it stops opening unattended windows on beads nothing is wrong with. Two facts do it, and both are free off reads the sweep already makes: a child carrying `human` has a question on it and is Adam's move, not a supervisor's; and a child parked behind an open `pr-delivery` card or `merge-queue` bead has a pull request waiting on a tap. Both drop the child out of the stall clock beside `busy`, and both put it straight back the moment the ending is taken back — so a window that died *after* its question was answered is still a stall, an hour later. A dead window with no pull request and no question is untouched: that is the failure the sweep exists for, and it still fires. The delivery half is knowable without asking GitHub anything because delivery is structural: `bin/deliver.js` parks the work bead behind whichever bead it filed with `bd dep add`, since the close gate refuses a bead with an open blocker and that is what stops a worker closing its own work. So `waitingOnMerge` is one pass over `index.edges` — the same cached `bd export` the sweep is already looking at — and no new spawn. I checked it against the two beads the bead names before writing any of it: bc-8t3b has a `blocks` edge to bc-rnk4, open and `pr-delivery`; bc-xl7n.25 carries `human`. bc-8t3b carries no `human` label of its own (delivery calls `park` with `label: false`), which is why one test is not enough for both. On this tracker tonight, fifteen `in_progress` beads were sitting behind an open delivery card. Building the handback half uncovered a second, older gap and I fixed it in the same diff rather than leaving it: `advocatedRoots` was handing `reentryFor` the rows `treeUnder` builds, which are the *board's* wire shape and deliberately carry no labels. `leasesOf(undefined)` is `[]`, so the third arm of `busy` — the sweep's own published sentence, "and no live lease elsewhere" — had never once been answerable for a child. The epic itself was fine, because `busy(epic)` gets a bead off the index, which is exactly why no suite caught it. `labelled` puts the labels back on this tree only; `treeUnder`'s shape and its measured 3.3KB inbox payload are untouched. The consequence is that a child another Mac holds a live lease on no longer reads as stalled, which is what the sentence always claimed. What I chose against: reading the outcome the advocate already recorded (`delivered`/`handback`), which the bead's notes float as an option. It is written to the park register, and that register is switched off by `parkIdleWindows: false`, skipped under `OBSERVING`, and needs a `sessionId` and a `dir` — so it would have answered "not delivered" in states where the tracker plainly says otherwise. The edge is on the tracker and survives a daemon restart, a second Mac and a lost state file. I also left the Epic Advocate's *brief* alone: its child list still prints a delivered child as bare `in_progress`, which is the other half of the cost the bead describes, and it is filed as bc-xl7n.99 (unendorsed) rather than folded in here, because it is brief prose with its own static guards. Unsure about one thing worth a reviewer's eye: `leaseMinutes` and `reenterStallMinutes` are both 60, so a bead whose window died can now be held out of the stall report for up to one lease life by its own lapsing lease before firing. That is bounded, it is the documented intent of the sentence, and it errs toward not opening a window — but it is a real behaviour change on top of the two the bead asked for. **Tests:** node scripts/coverage.mjs (the no-bail parallel runner): 335 suites ran, 334 green. The one red is test/adoptsweepreal.mjs, a known load flake — re-run alone immediately afterwards it is 12/12, exit 0. test/reenter.mjs is 38/38, up from 36; I proved the three new cases red first by reverting each half of the change in turn (35/38 either way, and a different case failing each time), so none of them is vacuously green. **Worth knowing:** reentryFor now silently declines to report a class of child. If waitingOnMerge were ever wrong in the permissive direction, a genuinely dead window would go unreported and its bead stays invisible to bd ready — so the test pins the negative cases (closed blocker, wrong edge type, reversed edge, unlabelled blocker, missing blocker, no edges at all) harder than the positive ones. Separately: leaseMinutes and reenterStallMinutes are both 60, so the now-live lease arm of busy can delay a real stall report by up to one lease life. **Left undone:** The Epic Advocate's brief still prints a delivered or handed-back child as bare in_progress in its child list — the other half of the cost this bead describes. Filed as bc-xl7n.99 (unendorsed), not folded in, because it is brief prose with its own static guards. The brief's stall paragraph still tells the advocate to go looking for a branch or an open pull request; that is now redundant for the delivered case but still correct for a worker that pushed and died before deliver.js ran, so I left it.
Files changed — 4 files · +385 −13 · against `main` ``` test/reenter.mjs +218 −8 lib/reenter.js +130 −3 README.md +27 −0 lib/advocate.js +10 −2 ```
--- _Opened by a beadcause worker session on bc-xl7n.98 — *The two endings the brief asks a worker to reach are the two the stall sweep reports as stalls*. It merges itself once the checks report; merging is what closes the bead. If this is still open, something stopped that, and the reason is on bc-xl7n.98 and in Adam's inbox._ bead: bc-xl7n.98

author: alimobrem
body:
## What
The UI's dashboard queries PromQL directly against the cluster's Prometheus/Thanos stack via `/api/prometheus/` (node CPU/memory, etcd leader changes, apiserver latency, firing alerts, etc.), but `nginx.conf` never had a matching location block. Every one of those requests silently fell through to the SPA catch-all (`location / { try_files ... /index.html }`) and got back `index.html` with a real **HTTP 200** — nothing in the proxy chain ever errored, while the frontend failed to parse an HTML page as PromQL JSON. Symptom: CPU/memory charts showing dashes, "metric unavailable".

Confirmed live: every `/api/prometheus/*` request in the nginx access log returned exactly 1621 bytes — the same size every time, matching the static SPA shell, not real (variably-sized) Prometheus responses.

## Fix
Added a `/api/prometheus/` location proxying to `thanos-querier.openshift-monitoring.svc:9091`, forwarding the same OAuth access token `/api/kubernetes/` already forwards (reading this endpoint requires the logged-in user to hold `cluster-monitoring-view`, same as the OpenShift console's own dashboards).

`thanos-querier`'s serving certificate is signed by the service-ca operator, not the kube-apiserver CA the SA token's `ca.crt` verifies — verifying it needed a real trust source rather than `proxy_ssl_verify off`. Added `reconcileUIServiceCABundle`, which creates an empty ConfigMap annotated `service.beta.openshift.io/inject-cabundle: "true"` (the same mechanism this operator already uses in reverse for the UI's own serving cert), mounted into the `openshiftpulse` container at `/etc/pki/service-ca` so nginx's `proxy_ssl_trusted_certificate` has a real bundle to check against.

## Tests
- `nginx.conf` contains the new location block ahead of the SPA catch-all (same ordering check already used for `/api/agent/`).
- The new ConfigMap carries the `inject-cabundle` annotation and an `OwnerReference`.
- The Deployment's pod spec has both the volume and the container mount at the right path.

Full suite green locally on the first run: `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l .`, `golangci-lint run ./...` (0 issues), `go test ./...`.

Resubmission of #2610 (closed unmerged during a batch close, no review feedback). Content unchanged, rebased onto current main (v0.6.1) and re-tested — targeted suite passes. Production-validated on our serving fork since Aug 12.

---

## perf(scheduler): skip full-vocab logprobs when no row requested them

mlx-lm's `GenerationBatch._step` materialises one [vocab] fp32 array per row per decode step (`list(logprobs)` → `async_eval`, plus eval of the previous step's arrays) and omlx discards those arrays host-side whenever the request didn't ask for logprobs — a full B×V materialisation (~800KB/row at 200k vocab) wasted on nearly every token.

This records each uid's `sampling_params.logprobs` flag in the uid-row registry at insert; when no registered row wants logprobs AND no speculative-decode path can read `_next_logprobs`, the patched step runs a variant that elides the per-row materialisation/retention while keeping the `logits − logsumexp` normalisation (omlx's top-p/min-p samplers require true log-probabilities), so sampled tokens are bit-identical and Responses simply carry `logprobs=None` — the same state the host-side discard produces today.

Consumer audit: native MTP/dspark read `_next_logprobs` for acceptance math, including lazily at activation, so their per-load model markers and any live MTP state force the upstream step; grammar accept reads `_next_tokens` only; VLM-MTP never touches `GenerationBatch` logprobs. Any consumer at all runs the upstream step unchanged, keeping requested logprobs identical to before.

Tests: 16 new (dispatch gates, skip-vs-upstream token equality, `async_eval`/`eval` materialisation spies, sampler-input normalisation, requested-value exactness, mixed batches); full scheduler/grammar/speculative suite green (1138 passed).

author: gavinmcfall
body:
Follow-up to #2579. That PR made `_author_dir()` prefer whichever author folder actually exists, falling back to the **primary** author otherwise. The fallback is right for an incidental collaboration but wrong for a writing partnership.

## The rule

**Primary author** when the collaboration is incidental to one author's series — Janny Wurts co-wrote three books inside Feist's Riftwar Cycle, and they belong beside the rest of that series:

```
Fantasy/Raymond E. Feist/Riftwar Cycle/(2) The Empire Trilogy
```

**Joined name** when the pair is a standing partnership with its own series — Caroline Peckham & Susanne Valenti write theirs together *and* publish solo, so the pair is its own author identity:

```
Romantasy/Caroline Peckham & Susanne Valenti/...
Romantasy/Caroline Peckham/...              <- solo work, still separate
```

`_partnership_dir_exists()` lets the tree answer which is which: if that exact pairing already holds a folder in **any** genre room, it's a partnership. An existing folder still wins outright — this only decides the form for a book that has none yet.

## Verification

7/7 against the live tree, including the cases that separate the two rules:

| Room | Authors | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Fantasy | `Raymond E. Feist & Janny Wurts` | `Raymond E. Feist` |
| Romantasy | `Caroline Peckham & Susanne Valenti` | joined (existing folder) |
| Fantasy | `Caroline Peckham & Susanne Valenti` | joined — no folder in that room, partnership recognised from Romantasy |
| Erotica | `Raymond E. Feist & Janny Wurts` | `Raymond E. Feist` |
| Fantasy | `Caroline Peckham` | `Caroline Peckham` (solo) |

Cost is a couple of dozen `isdir()` checks against the top level of DEST, and only for a multi-author book with no folder.

Identical to `tools/reconcile.py` in nerdz-reading (`8c0c97c`). `ebook-reconcile` remains **suspended** — this does not run on merge.

### Motivation
- The Score Management page exposed internal numeric/UUID IDs via free-text filters, requiring administrators to enter database IDs instead of friendly names.
- Administrators need convenient, discoverable filters that show human-readable `Division`, `Community`, and `Host Location` names while preserving stable internal IDs for API requests.

author: marinoscar
body:
## Summary

Closes the security gaps found during #44 that are not dependency versions: missing CSP/HSTS, a location block that silently discarded every security header, and four credentials committed to the repository.

> Stacked on `chore/infra-images` (#59) → `chore/ts-alignment` (#57) → `fix/otel-upgrade` (#50) → `fix/dep-vulns` (#48).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] CI/CD or infrastructure change

## Related Issues

Relates to #44

## Changes Made

**Security headers.** Added `Content-Security-Policy`, `Strict-Transport-Security` and `Permissions-Policy` to the four already set.

**Fixed a location block that dropped every security header.** nginx's `add_header` *replaces* rather than merges — a location declaring its own `add_header` loses everything inherited from the server block. `location /nginx-health` did exactly that with `add_header Content-Type text/plain`. Replaced with `default_type text/plain`, which sets the content type without touching the header set. The replacement rule is now documented inline.

Measured against a real nginx 1.30 container:

| Endpoint | before (`main`) | after |
|---|---|---|
| `/nginx-health` | **0** security headers | **7** |
| `/` (proxied) | 4 | **7** |

**Credentials moved out of the repository.** `infra/otel/uptrace.yml` and `infra/otel/otel-collector-config.yaml` carried four hardcoded values: the Uptrace `secret_key`, the project token (also embedded in the collector's `uptrace-dsn`), the admin UI password, and the metadata Postgres password. All four now come from the environment, with the previous values preserved as compose defaults so `docker compose up` still works with no `.env` present, and documented in `.env.example` under an explicit warning.

**Removed `@fastify/helmet`** — installed but never registered. See reasoning below.

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests pass (`npm test`) — 1011 API tests, 0 failures
- [x] Type checks pass (`npm run typecheck`) — clean
- [ ] E2E tests pass (if applicable)
- [x] Manual testing completed — every change verified against real containers

**Env substitution was verified, not assumed** — the two config formats differ and neither is obvious:

- **Uptrace 1.7.2 expands `${VAR}`.** Proven by substituting into the `pg` address and watching the container log back `"addr": "SUBSTITUTION-WORKED:5432"`.
- **The collector uses the distinct `${env:VAR}` form.** Verified by starting 0.145.0 against the edited config: `Everything is ready. Begin running and processing data.`, zero errors.

`npm audit`: **0 vulnerabilities**.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's coding standards
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [ ] Any dependent changes have been merged and published — depends on #48, #50, #57, #59

## Additional Notes

### Why the CSP is shaped the way it is

Scoped to what this app actually needs rather than copied from a template:

- **`style-src 'unsafe-inline'`** — MUI/emotion injects styles at runtime. Removing it requires migrating to nonce-based styles, which is a real piece of work, not a config tweak.
- **`img-src ... https:`** — avatars come from Google (`lh3.googleusercontent.com`, stored as `providerProfileImageUrl` in `auth.service.ts`) and uploaded images are served from a **configurable** S3 endpoint that may be AWS or MinIO. A stricter host list would break avatars on any non-AWS deployment.
- **`connect-src 'self'`** — the frontend calls `/api` same-origin and makes no cross-origin requests (verified by grep).

**HSTS is inert in local development** — browsers ignore it over plain HTTP — and takes effect once the app is served over TLS.

### Why `@fastify/helmet` was removed rather than registered

I initially planned to register it. On checking, the `api` service publishes **no ports** in any compose file, so nginx is the sole ingress and now sets the complete header set.

Because nginx's `add_header` appends rather than replaces, registering helmet would have produced **duplicate** headers on every proxied response — and duplicate CSP headers are *intersected* by browsers, which fails in ways that are unpleasant to debug. Carrying an unused dependency purely for a deployment topology that does not exist is worse than removing it.

nginx is the security-header boundary. If the API is ever exposed directly, helmet should be reinstated **together with `proxy_hide_header` rules** so the two do not both emit.

### Not addressed here

`img-src https:` is permissive. Tightening it to an explicit host list is possible once the S3 endpoint for a given deployment is known, but it cannot be done generically in this template repo without breaking non-AWS users.

author: jeremyjpj0916
body:
## Summary
- Live HTTP `backend_read_timeout_ms` / `backend_write_timeout_ms` expiry now returns **504** with `X-Gateway-Error: backend_timeout` and `{"error":"Backend timeout"}` instead of the same 502 / `backend_error` / `{"error":"Backend unavailable"}` pair used for a down backend.
- Connection-refused and other genuine connect/unavailable failures stay **502** with `connection_failure` when pre-wire. Retry, circuit-breaker, transaction-summary, metrics, and `BackendResponse::connection_error` still derive from `ErrorClass` / `request_reached_wire` so a post-wire timeout is never treated as a connect failure.
- Gateway API black-box `/weight` no longer aborts on a transient 404 after neighboring rules on the same HTTPRoute are already live. Convergence waits up to 60×2s; once the path is served, the original 20-probe budget rapid-samples both backends and prints `seen_a`/`seen_b`/sample count/last body/last HTTP on failure.
- Closes #3922

## Changes
- Added a shared HTTP-family mapper (`http_backend_failure_status_and_body` / `http_backend_dispatch_error_response`) keyed on typed `ErrorClass::ReadWriteTimeout`, not a one-off string check.
- Wired that mapper through reqwest initial + retry dispatch, H3→HTTP reqwest bridge, direct-H2 send failures, H2 pool sender errors, native H3 dispatch, and the existing H2/HBONE/sidecar/unix header-wait and body-collect timeout arms.
- Eager-buffer body-read failures reuse the same 504 timeout pair. gRPC keeps Trailers-Only / `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`.
- Documented live-dispatch timeout parity in `docs/error_classification.md`. README already promised 504; OpenAPI is unchanged.
- Split Gateway API weighted-route waiting: `wait_for_weighted_backends` in `scripts/gateway_api_data_plane_conformance.sh` so a missing path fails as convergence and a single-backend product defect still fails after ~20 live samples.

## Test plan
Hosted CI is the execution gate (no local cargo/fmt/clippy/tests in this worktree).
- [ ] Unit: `cargo test --test unit_tests test_http_backend_dispatch` and related retry mapper tests
- [ ] Integration: `cargo test --test integration_tests in_process_backend_read_timeout_maps_to_504_backend_timeout in_process_backend_refused_stays_502_connection_failure`
- [ ] Functional: `cargo test --test functional_tests backend_read_timeout_fires_after_backend_read_timeout_ms backend_refuses_connect_maps_to_502_with_connection_refused -- --ignored`
- [ ] Clippy/fmt via CI (`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --lib --tests -p ferrum-edge -- -D warnings`)
- Confirm a delayed backend (headers never arrive) returns 504 + `backend_timeout` + `{"error":"Backend timeout"}`
- Confirm a connection-refused backend still returns 502 + `connection_failure` + `{"error":"Backend unavailable"}`
- Confirm Gateway API black-box weighted selection reaches both backends after `/weight` converges, without `curl --fail` aborting on a first-probe 404

author: jonathan308
body:
Resubmission of #2611 (closed unmerged during a batch close, no review feedback). Content unchanged, rebased onto current main (v0.6.1) and re-tested — targeted suite passes. Production-validated on our serving fork since Aug 12.

---

## Why

A k-block prefix-chain store wrote `tuple(block_ids[:i+1])` for every depth — ~k²/2 block-id slots per turn (a 586-block/150k-token chain: ~172k slots, rebuilt each turn). Lookups re-hashed the whole prompt even after the first index miss, and the store path hashed each block three times (dedup probe, block tag, registration).

## What

- `_update_prefix_index` stores one tip-level entry per chain: `(prefix_len, tip_block_id, num_blocks)`. Intermediate block ids are resolved at acquire time through `cached_block_hash_to_block` and still re-validated via `acquire_cached_block` (self-heal on stale entries kept).
- `_find_best_prefix_match` stops at the first depth with neither an index entry nor a live block (chain hashing makes deeper matches impossible); `fetch_cache` hashes the prompt once outside the paged lock and shares the chain hashes between `find_shared_prefix` and the index lookup (when extra-key ranges allow).
- `store_cache` memoizes the per-block chain hash: 3k → k hashes per store.

Measured on a 64-block store: index entries 64→1, id slots 2080→1, hash calls 192→64.

## Compatibility

Digest algorithm and inputs are byte-identical — existing SSD block filenames remain valid. `_on_block_hash_dropped` and exact-terminal isolation semantics preserved. One test-only contract changed: the index no longer serves chains after the hash map is wiped while blocks stay allocated (a state no production path creates); hit/miss behavior is otherwise identical (194 pre-existing tests pass, 7 new regression tests added).

author: vultix
body:
First, thank you for building this! Ahab found multiple good findings on our monorepo, and we are adding it to our automated checks. Great tool. 

While trying it, one class of false positive accounted for 22 of our 62
findings.

## Symptom

```
hermeticity violation: CopyFile action for target //alphadb/web:build_copy_srcs_to_bin
references absolute path "/+page.svelte" in an argument:
alphadb/web/src/routes/axes/[...id]/+page.svelte
```

The argument is a relative path. `/+page.svelte` is the tail of one. Every
action touching the file repeats it — CopyFile, RunfilesTree, and the
runfiles param file — so one SvelteKit rest-parameter route directory
produced 22 findings, and none of them were real.

## Cause

In `absolute_paths`, the boundary test is `!is_path_char(bytes[i - 1])`,
and `is_path_char` admits only `[A-Za-z0-9]` plus `/ . - _ + ~ @ %`. So
every character outside that set counts as a separator, `]` included. In
`.../[...id]/+page.svelte` the `/` after `]` reads as boundary-anchored and
the run is extracted.

Nothing here is specific to SvelteKit — any relative path with a segment
containing `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, `!`, `#` and so on does it.

## What this changes, and the part that is your call

I want to be explicit that this narrows behaviour you chose deliberately.
`a_closing_brace_alone_does_not_excuse_an_absolute_path` says outright that
"brackets that merely happen to precede a `/` are just brackets", and the
readme's argument that treating silence as approval is how a total check
stops being total cuts against loosening any boundary rule. You may prefer
the false positives, and that would be a reasonable answer.

The rule here is the narrowest one I could find that distinguishes the two
cases. A `/` after a non-filename character still roots a path, unless the
whitespace-delimited token it sits in was *already* a relative path and the
preceding character is not one of the separators that restart a value
(`=`, `:`, `,`, quotes, whitespace):

- `[pwd]/usr/lib` — bracket at the start of the token, no earlier `/`, so
  nothing was under way for it to continue. Still a violation.
- `src/routes/axes/[...id]/+page.svelte` — the token was a relative path
  three segments before the bracket. No longer a violation.

Both existing tests that pin this down pass unmodified —
`a_closing_brace_alone_does_not_excuse_an_absolute_path` and
`an_unrecognized_expansion_is_not_trusted` — as does
`${pwd}/external/ok:/usr/lib`.

The residual risk is a genuine absolute path glued directly after a bracket
*later in a token that already contained a slash* — `foo/bar[x]/etc/passwd`
would now be missed. I could not construct a realistic action argument of
that shape, but you know the corpus better than I do, and if you would
rather have that coverage than the false positives, closing this is a fine
outcome.

## Verification

- `bazel test //...` green: 329 unit tests, rustfmt, buildifier, and
  `//:clippy` under your `-Dwarnings`.
- On our monorepo: 60 → 38 distinct findings, 62 → 40 occurrences. All 22
  absolute-path findings gone, every other category byte-identical.

Added test:

```rust
#[test]
fn a_bracketed_segment_does_not_start_an_absolute_path() {
    assert!(
        absolute_paths("src/routes/axes/[...id]/+page.svelte")
            .is_empty()
    );
}
```

author: gianelo
body:
Task **3.14b**. **377 authored lines**, inside budget.

The only client component in the publish flow, and the only screen in the product where SISTEMA.md allows JavaScript. The reason is specific rather than conventional: a phone photo is 3–8 MB, six of them on a Venezuelan mobile connection is the slowest thing this product ever asks anyone to do, and compressing before the bytes leave the device is the only fix that works **on** the connection rather than around it.

## The order is the design

**Compress → measure → sign → upload.**

The presigned PUT pins `ContentLength` into its signature, so a body of any other length fails at R2's edge. That means the exact byte count must be known **before** the signature is requested. Compressing after signing would invalidate every URL just issued. It reads as an implementation detail and it is the whole sequence.

## 1600px, chosen against what consumes it

The detail derivative is **1280** on its longest edge. Uploading below that would make `sharp` **upscale** — inventing pixels and losing quality for no saved bytes. 1600 keeps a real margin while cutting a 4032 × 3024 phone photo to under a fifth of its area.

That relationship is asserted against `DETAIL_MAX_EDGE` itself, not against a copy of the number, so moving either value fails the test and says which.

## `computeResize` is pure and separately tested

It is the only part of this that can ship wrong without anyone noticing. Covered: never enlarging, the portrait case (a rule written against width alone leaves upright phone photos full size — and upright is the common case), and the panorama that would otherwise scale to a **zero-pixel side**, which no decoder accepts and which would arrive as a corrupt upload rather than a refused one.

## Nothing here decides what is acceptable

- `validateUploadRequest` (#42) refuses a request worth no signature.
- `inspectUploadedPhoto` reads the file's own header **after** upload.
- `deriveListingPhoto` produces what is actually stored.

**A client that lies gets a signature it cannot use.** The count limit is repeated here only so a publisher who picked ten photos learns it before waiting for ten uploads.

Uploads run sequentially, matching the server pipeline: six parallel uploads on a constrained connection make every one slower and tell the publisher nothing about which is progressing. Progress is announced through `role="status"` / `aria-live`, because this is the slowest step in the flow and a changing paragraph is silent to a screen reader.

## Proof

`lint`, `typecheck`, `test:coverage` (267 passed), `build`, `lint:tokens`, **`budget:bundle` — `/publicar/fotos` at 102.29 KB against 130 KB**, so the one screen that ships client JS is still measured and still inside the budget.

## What is left

**3.14c**: run `processUploadedPhoto` over each uploaded key, then `publishListing`. Until then the photos reach the bucket's incoming prefix and no listing row is written — which the page says plainly rather than implying it published.

author: jonathan308
body:
Resubmission of #2612 (closed unmerged during a batch close, no review feedback). Content unchanged, rebased onto current main (v0.6.1) and re-tested — targeted suite passes. Production-validated on our serving fork since Aug 12.

---

## perf(scheduler): pressure-gate the decode-time Metal cache clear

`Scheduler.step()` ran `_sync_and_clear_cache` unconditionally every 1024 decode tokens: two `mx.synchronize()` calls plus `mx.clear_cache()` under the process-wide buffer lock — a full GPU pipeline drain mid-decode for every model, even when the MLX buffer pool held almost nothing to release. The clear exists for the macOS IOGPU resource-residency limit (~4096 entries) and must stay; the unconditional drain does not.

- The 1024-token counter still drives the check cadence, but the clear now fires only when `mx.get_cache_memory()` exceeds the shared `_periodic_clear_threshold_bytes()` (same condition as `_should_periodic_clear_cache`). When it fires, the synced clear is byte-for-byte the same — the #300/#888/#1106 synchronization is not weakened.
- mlx-lm's `BatchGenerator._next` runs its own **unsynced** `mx.clear_cache()` every 512 decode steps — the exact in-flight-buffer race class omlx documented in #300/#888/#1106. A new `_patched_batch_generator_next` (next to the existing mlx-lm patches) sidesteps the upstream boundary while preserving the 512-step cadence exactly, and re-fires through `_sync_and_clear_cache` under the same pressure gate. Only omlx-created generators are affected.

Net effect: idle/low-pressure decode pays zero GPU drains; pressured decode gets the same safety clears at the same cadences, all of them synced.

Tests: 7 new tests in `tests/test_scheduler.py` covering zero clears at low pressure over thousands of tokens, gated firing through `_sync_and_clear_cache` at high pressure, 1024-token check cadence, and the mlx-lm reroute (neutralize/refire/passthrough). Full scheduler suite green (401 tests); ruff clean vs. main.

author: thuongtin
body:
## Vấn đề

Viewer của MCP Apps không render trên claude.ai (cả web lẫn ứng dụng di động): kết quả tool hiện ra dưới dạng JSON thô, hoặc báo "failed to load the MCP app". Đo trên endpoint đang chạy bằng một probe gọi thẳng `initialize` + `tools/list` cho thấy hai khoảng trống độc lập, mỗi cái đã có một bản vá upstream chứng minh hiệu quả:

1. **Thiếu khoá binding phẳng.** `src/tools/viewer-meta.ts` chỉ phát khoá lồng `_meta.ui.resourceUri`. SDK MCP Apps deprecate khoá phẳng `"ui/resourceUri"` cho *bên viết server*, nhưng vẫn hướng dẫn *host* đọc cả hai (`meta?.ui?.resourceUri ?? meta?.["ui/resourceUri"]`), và chính helper `registerAppTool` của SDK ghi cả hai. Server này dựng `_meta` bằng tay nên nửa tương thích bị thiếu. Host nào chỉ đọc khoá phẳng sẽ hiện JSON thô thay vì viewer (tham chiếu: claude-ai-mcp#71).

2. **Không khai extension ở `initialize`.** `server.ts` không khai `capabilities.extensions`. Nhiều host đàm phán extension TRƯỚC rồi mới quyết định render, chứ không suy ra khả năng UI từ sự tồn tại của resource `ui://` - dù binding `_meta.ui` từng tool có đúng đến đâu (tham chiếu: actionhero/keryx#505).

## Thay đổi

**`src/tools/viewer-meta.ts`** - mỗi binding phát dưới cả hai khoá. Sửa ở một chỗ là đủ cho ba bề mặt: `buildToolListing()` chép `_meta` nguyên vẹn vào `tools/list`, `buildToolCallResult()` chép `_meta` của tool định nghĩa lên `CallToolResult`, và `listResult()` đóng dấu chính các hằng số này lên payload. Kiểu `ViewerToolMeta` là giao của `MCPToolMeta` với khoá phẳng nên vẫn gán được ở mọi nơi đang chờ `MCPToolMeta`.

**`server.ts`** - khai `extensions: { [MCP_APPS_EXTENSION_ID]: { mimeTypes: [MCP_APP_MIME_TYPE] } }`, **có điều kiện** theo `servesUiViewers`. Khai extension khi trên đĩa không có bundle nào là mời host đi xin một resource tiến trình này không phục vụ được - với người dùng, thứ đó tệ hơn là không có widget. Việc hoist `resolveViewerDistPath` lên trước constructor cũng bỏ được một lượt `statSync` trùng lặp (trước đây chạy lại trong vòng đăng ký).

Cả hai thay đổi đều **thuần cộng thêm**: khoá lồng vẫn nguyên, không tool nào đổi tên/schema, không đường nào bị gỡ.

## Kiểm chứng

- `src/tools/viewer-meta_test.ts` (mới): 7 hằng số phải đặt cả hai khoá và cả hai phải trỏ cùng một resource; mọi URI phải nằm trong namespace `ui://hvgerp-mcp/` và tên viewer phải có trong `UI_VIEWERS`; chiều ngược lại - mọi entry của `UI_VIEWERS` phải có hằng số binding, nên thêm viewer mới mà quên binding là đỏ test.
- `src/transport_wire_test.ts`: thêm một cặp dương-âm cho `capabilities.extensions`. Test âm dùng fixture không khai extension và đòi `capabilities.extensions === undefined`, để test dương thật sự có thể đỏ. Thêm hai assertion nguồn vào test `server.ts configures the stateless transport`, gác cả việc khai extension lẫn việc nó phải có điều kiện.
- `deno test`: **562 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored**.
- `deno fmt --check` (259 tệp) và `deno lint` (184 tệp): sạch.
- `deno check`: bị chặn bởi 403 của jsr.io trên IP hiện tại. Chạy qua import map thay thế cục bộ thì ra **20 lỗi, y hệt baseline `origin/main`** (đều là `TS2307` trong `mod.ts` của gói vendor và `TS7006` ở `src/auth/caller-middleware.ts:72`, tệp diff này không đụng tới). Diff không thêm lỗi kiểu nào.

## Sau khi merge

Dựng lại image connector rồi đo lại trên dây: `initialize` phải quảng bá `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`, và `tools/list` phải có đủ 68 tool mang `_meta["ui/resourceUri"]`.
