author: juncaj93
body:
Infrastructure and resilience only. No football logic is touched, and that is
now enforced structurally rather than promised — see the last section.

## Which season is it, answered once

Four services each carried the same expression — `now.getUTCMonth() >= 2 ? year : year - 1` —
with a fifth spelling in the Sleeper connect route and a sixth in Setup. Six
copies of a calendar guess is six chances to disagree, and they already did:
connecting on 1 January 2027 asked Sleeper for the **2027** leagues, a season
that does not exist until March, and got back an empty list indistinguishable
from "you are in no leagues".

`core/season/context.ts` is the single authority. Sleeper's `/state/nfl` first,
the selected league second, the calendar last and marked `assumed`. The four
functions stay as fallbacks delegating to one implementation; callers that can
reach the database pass the authoritative answer in.

What it deliberately refuses to do is infer the season from stored data. That is
the rollover failure mode: with no current-season feed published, the newest rows
in every table are last season's, and "newest wins" promotes them to current
truth on the first Sunday of the new year.

## Rollover

- **`lifecycle.ts`** — eight deterministic states (offseason, preseason,
  draft-open, draft-live, post-draft, regular season, playoffs, season complete),
  every one read off a provider field rather than a date. A live draft outranks
  every other witness, because Sleeper flips `season_type` to `regular` before
  week one and leagues that draft late are still drafting when it does. The
  existing four-state `season` field is unchanged and still served, so a client
  mid-deploy degrades rather than breaks.
- **`keys.ts`** — Week 3 2026 and Week 3 2027 are structurally different keys,
  and readable back, so a rollover sweep knows what it is deleting and leaves
  alone what it does not recognise.
- **`rollover.ts`** — carry-forward-with-decay (manager FAAB and trade
  tendencies, model grading) split from rebuild-from-truth (roster, draft,
  injuries, ADP, waiver pool, standings, props, schedule, recommendations).
  Rebuild is the default, so a store added later without thought resets rather
  than persists. Successor-league discovery takes Sleeper's own
  `previous_league_id` silently and only ever *proposes* a name/size/scoring
  match.
- **`readiness.ts` + `GET /api/diagnostics/rollover`** — asks each source for the
  current season *by name* and refuses "here is the newest thing I have".
  `waiting` (not published yet, and not expected to be) is kept distinct from
  `stale` (published, wrong season) and `failed`, so it does not cry wolf every
  March.

## The board survives a dead zone

The refresh controller already handled losing the network mid-session. It could
not survive a reload: close the tab in a tunnel, reopen it, and every request
fails with nothing to fall back on.

`web/offlineCache.ts` keeps the last good board in `localStorage` and the screen
reads it only when the server is unreachable **and** nothing better is already on
screen — a board on screen is one the server actually sent, and replacing it with
an older copy of itself would be a downgrade. What comes back is always rendered
as a capture, with its age, in an undismissable alert-role banner: a stale board
read as a live one is how somebody drafts a player who went three picks ago.

Nothing is stored that did not come from Sleeper. No offline pick queue, no
optimistic state. Every failure mode — private-mode browser, full quota, payload
from a previous deploy, corrupt JSON — returns "no cache", which is where the app
was before this existed.

The write is deferred to `requestIdleCallback`. It was synchronous at first and
that was a real regression: a `JSON.stringify` of up to four hundred rows plus a
blocking, disk-backed write, in the same tick that had just rebuilt the board
after a pick. It showed up as a gesture test failing in two of three full e2e
runs while passing on `main` and in every subset.

## Budgets

`npm run perf:budget` gzips the built assets against `perf-budgets.json` and
fails CI. Bytes rather than milliseconds — a gzipped size is identical on a
laptop and on a loaded shared runner, so a failure is always a real regression.
Currently 88/140 kB JS, 98/160 kB total.

`e2e/performance.spec.ts` covers the flows that genuinely need a browser, with
deliberately generous ceilings: they catch a flow going from milliseconds to
seconds, not tens of milliseconds. One assertion in there is not a timing at all
and matters more — **typing in the search field must produce zero API requests**,
because search that reaches the server is unusable exactly where a draft happens.

`docs/BUDGETS.md` writes down the free-tier ceilings that were already being
respected but documented nowhere: Worker CPU, the two separate D1 write ledgers,
refresh cadences, and why the heavy work lives in `scripts/`.

## One shared player search

`core/search/players.ts` replaces the substring matcher, built on the identity
layer's normalizer so a name means the same thing to the search box as to the
resolver. `Amon Ra` now finds `Amon-Ra St. Brown` and `JaMarr` finds
`Ja'Marr Chase` — neither worked before, in either direction.

Results are ranked (exact, prefix, word-prefix, substring, then typo) with the
board's own order breaking ties, so search never re-ranks the board by string
similarity. Typo budget scales with word length, so `joe` cannot reach `Zoe`.

**One deliberate behaviour change:** `matchesQuery('Kai Brennan', 'brennen')`
used to return `false` and a test asserted it. A one-letter slip on a surname is
the most common thing a thumb does on a draft clock, so that assertion is
reversed rather than worked around.

## The identifier is tried before the name

Both published-file pipelines carry a GSIS id per row — it is why
`stats_player_week` was chosen over `snap_counts` — and both matched on the
**name** first, consulting the identifier only to break a tie.

The cost was not a worse tie-break. A player the two sources spell differently
("Cam Ward" against "Cameron Ward", a suffix on one side only) did not resolve
ambiguously; he did not resolve **at all**, because the name lookup returned no
candidates and the identifier in the same row was never read. His injury and his
usage went silently missing, indistinguishable in the counts from the source not
mentioning him.

The old ordering had a reason: `external_ids_json` is an unindexed blob, and an
in-memory index of four thousand players measured 17 ms of CPU against a Worker's
10 ms allowance. Migration 0020 adds `gsis_id` as a generated **VIRTUAL** column
with a partial index, so the identifier lookup is the same shape and cost as the
name one — verified as `SEARCH players USING INDEX idx_players_gsis`. An id two
players claim abstains rather than picking, and is no longer credited as an `id`
match when the row then resolves by name — that count is what somebody would read
to judge whether the mapping is healthy, so it must not flatter itself.

### A deploy failure this nearly shipped

0020 was written `STORED` first. SQLite accepts
`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN ... STORED` against an **empty** table and refuses it
against a populated one (`cannot add a STORED column`) — and every test applies
migrations to a fresh in-memory schema, so the whole suite went green against
precisely the case that cannot fail. It would then have run at
`wrangler d1 migrations apply --remote` against the four thousand players in the
deployed database and taken the deploy down at the migration step.

`tests/migrations.test.ts` now applies every migration in order to a database
that already has rows, re-seeding between each pair so a migration meets whatever
rows the ones before it made possible. Confirmed to fail with
`cannot add a STORED column` when 0020 is put back the way it was.

## No football output can change

Asserted structurally in `tests/infrastructureIsolation

body:
## Summary

Closes the §10 lane-visibility gap tracked in #809: a user looking at a Track must immediately know it contains multiple lanes.

The track's primary row now shows a lane-stack SVG icon + owned-lane count just left of the M/S/R buttons (contract style: "≡ 3"). Single-lane tracks show nothing — no noise for the common case.

## Why

The FD-14 lane model is fully functional (tracks own lanes, record-arm materializes lanes, every lane renders as a row) but the connection between a track header and its lane rows was invisible. The contract's §10 discovers the count from the track's authoritative `laneIds` list — never derived from lane index — so it stays correct as record-arm adds lanes.

## Details

- **`TrackControlIcons.h`**: `kLaneStackIconSvg` — three rounded bars drawn as SVG paths. Deliberately not the U+2261 union glyph: the bundled Manrope/Geist fonts lack it, and an SVG icon is font-independent. The contract explicitly leaves glyph/count treatment unprescribed.
- **`TrackUIComponent`**: `m_laneCountIcon` + `m_laneCountLabel` created in the ctor, driven in `updateUI` from the resolved track (`lane->trackId` → `getTrack`), laid out in `onResize` in a fixed 54px slot left of the M/S/R cluster (name label flexes around it). Shown only on the track's primary row (`laneIds.front() == m_laneId`) and only when the count is > 1.
- Unowned/legacy lanes (trackId 0) and count ≤ 1 render nothing.

## Citation

```text
Objective: TS-2 — producer-loop finishing
Decision:   FD-14 @ 89a00af
Kind:       planned
```

## Producer note

Track headers now show how many lanes each track holds, so multi-lane tracks are visible at a glance.

## Testing performed

- `TrackUIComponent.cpp` syntax-checked against the UI-enabled compile db (clean)
- Headless full pass not required — UI-only change, no audio/serialization surface touched
- Visual verification is manual — folded into #809 phase-5 validation

## Also in this PR — stale volume-knob slot removed

Found during founder app testing: channel-backed lanes still reserved the historical 4th layout slot, where a ghost volume knob rendered. It ate left-click presses (hidden-cursor drag capture) before button routing — hover lit the ghost arc, clicks vanished — and could silently write SetVolumeCommand to the mixer channel on drag. The fader was already removed; the knob outlived it. Removed the whole subsystem: layout slot (4 -> 3 buttons), render block, hover/drag/tooltip mouse handling, cursor-capture path, dead fader member/handlers. Track headers are now exactly M/S/R; the rec toggle always reaches the button.

## Risk / rollback notes

- Pure additive UI: no serialization, no DSP, no command-path change. Revert is a 3-file revert.
- The indicator is static per-render — it updates via the existing UI refresh when lanes change (same path that rebuilds lane rows).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
- No breaking changes.
- Added a lane-count indicator for multi-lane tracks on the primary lane row.
- Show the lane-stack icon and owned-lane count in a fixed 54px slot beside the M/S/R controls.
- Hide the indicator for single-lane, unowned, legacy, and non-primary rows.
- Source the count from the resolved track’s authoritative `laneIds` list.
- Removed the stale volume-knob slot and related interaction and tooltip handling.
- Added the public `kLaneStackIconSvg` constant.

body:
Fixes a real-data productization defect found during June 2026 CSV acceptance.

Historical CSV windows were inheriting authoritative stale-data suppression, which eliminated otherwise valid advisory waste/harvest candidates. CSV is explicitly non-authoritative and non-executable, so historical analysis should retain the stale freshness label and confidence penalty without hard-suppressing advisory candidates.

This change:
- sets CSV-only `suppressStale=false`
- keeps stale freshness state and the 0.5 confidence factor
- keeps lineage confidence penalty
- keeps governance persistence, execution, permits, and Amazon mutation disabled
- adds canonical contract assertions for these semantics

Production, Amazon credentials, sync triggers, and execution authority are untouched.

author: tfausak
body:
A cast an effect instructs "if able" is no longer forced when the spell's
mandatory additional cost involves cards of a stated quality in a hidden zone:
`Pawl.Engine.Cost.statesHiddenQuality` classifies the candidate costs and
`offerCast` turns that mandatory branch back into the `Prompt.OfferedCast` it
already knows how to raise. Closes #110

CR citations (each re-grepped in docs/rules.txt this session): 118.8c is the
rule; 118.8 for the "applied from another effect" half; 118.9d for why Wild
Evocation's free cast keeps the discard; 400.2 for the hidden/public split;
701.23b/701.23d for "stated quality" vs a bare quantity; 701.9a, 702.29a,
702.133a, 113.6m at the classification's arms; 608.2g, 601.3, 608.2n, 701.20a,
704.5b, 104.2a in the spec.

Design calls:

- The classification lives in `Pawl.Engine.Cost`, beside `zoneFunctionedFrom`
  and `isLoyaltyCost`, exhaustive over all eighteen `CostComponent`
  constructors with a reason per arm. Two conjuncts must hold: a hidden zone
  and a stated quality. `Filter.statesAQuality` is reused for the second — CR
  118.8c and CR 701.23b spell the phrase identically — rather than a second
  predicate; its haddock is amended, since it now has two callers.
- `zoneOfComponent` is deliberately NOT reused: it answers CR 113.6m about the
  object the cost is on, and answers `Nothing` for `DiscardCards`, so reading
  it here would excuse nothing.
- The check reads the CANDIDATE costs, not `Face.additionalCosts` and not
  `Cost.total`'s output. Every candidate already carries the face's additional
  costs (CR 118.9d), and CR 118.8's "applied from another effect" half is
  unreachable for a spell: `spellAdjustments` hard-sets
  `CostAdjustments.components = []` and the only writer is
  `PlayerEffect.additionOf`, which matches `AddActivationCost` and feeds
  `activationAdjustments`. Recorded as a plain comment at the branch; no
  elision, no issue owed.
- The excuse is attached to `Optionality.Mandatory` rather than to a new "if
  able" flag: every printing that instructs a cast states it with "if able", so
  the two coincide today. A producer instructing one without the phrase would
  be the reason to split them.
- The excused branch raises the SAME `Prompt.OfferedCast`. CR 118.8c creates no
  new decision; it says the player "isn't required to". That prompt stamps
  `GameState.lastChoice`, which is correct for `Engine.checkMandatoryLoop`: a
  loop containing a real choice is not a loop of mandatory actions (CR 104.4b).
- Rejected: putting the check in `Pawl.Engine.Cast`, which would reach every
  cast rather than only the ones an effect instructs.

Verification: 5741 -> 5744 (main gained #1790 mid-run; the branch's own
baseline was 5740 -> 5743). Three legs added inside the existing
`wildEvocationSpec`, all gameplay level, all re-run after merging origin/main:

- Magmatic Insight ("discard a land card") is OFFERED rather than cast: ask
  count 1, and declining leaves the Insight and the Forest in hand.
- Cathartic Reunion ("discard two cards", `And []`) is NOT excused: ask count
  0, the two discards and the Reunion reach the graveyard, and the three drawn
  cards are in hand. This pair is one Filter apart on identical machinery, and
  is what proves the classification reads the component's criterion and not the
  card.
- The offer can be TAKEN on the first leg's board, with its own accepting
  answerer (the stock answerers decline): the Forest pays the cost and the
  Insight resolves. This is the payability witness that separates CR 118.8c
  from the CR 601.3 guard, whose own control leg (Plummet with no flier, ask
  count 0) stays green throughout.

Every leg stocks bob's library, because CR 704.5b is live and a draw off an
empty one would lose him the game (CR 104.2a) and leave the assertions reading
a finished board.

Mutations, each run alone and read: `DiscardCards -> False` reddens leg 1 only,
at "bob was ASKED", ask count 0 vs 1 — which is also the falsifier for "gate
the excuse on unpayability", since `castableWhenOffered` has already passed by
that point so such a gate is constantly False; the Plummet control stays green,
so the two behaviours are distinguishable. `DiscardCards -> True` regardless of
the filter reddens leg 2 only, at "nobody was asked", 1 vs 0. Neutering the
excused branch's `mayCast` reddens legs 1 and 3 and leaves leg 2 green. Leg 3
does not redden under the first mutation, by construction: with the excuse gone
the cast simply happens unasked and the board is the same — it is a payability
witness, not a completeness leg.

`-Werror` blind spots: this unit adds no constructor, no field and no codec
arm, so `eventBindings`, `boundSlots`, `everyTriggerCondition`,
`representativeEvents`, `CardSpec`'s traversals and the `Arm.tagged`
`_ -> Nothing`s are all untouched and #1715's silent-codec trap does not apply.
The one wildcard the change could have introduced was avoided: the
`Optionality` case is spelled out in three arms rather than a guard plus `_`.

Prose swept for claims the change falsifies: `Types/OfferCast.hs`'s "what it
removes is the question" was true and is now qualified. Both live `#110`
elisions die here — `Types/Face.hs`'s and the one PR #1784 added to
`offerCast`'s haddock; `docs/progress.md`'s mention is frozen milestone prose
and is left. `script/check-gaps.sh` and `script/check-census.sh` both pass.

Does the rules core case on an effect's identity? No. `offerCast` reads one
Bool derived from the candidate costs' `CostComponent` and `Filter` structure;
it never asks which card or which effect is offering.

No card work: `data/cards/magmatic-insight.json` and
`data/cards/cathartic-reunion.json` were already in the pool, and both were
diffed against Scryfall's Oracle text this session.

Deferred: nothing. The unit-level `CostSpec` leg the brief marked optional was
skipped — legs 1 and 2 discriminate the classification at gameplay level, which
is the bar `docs/design.md` section 4 sets. #110 has no dependents.

author: tobi
body:
Make container toolchain HOME-independent, add jq and user mode

The toolchain was wired to /root via mise's ~-relative defaults, which broke
two real use cases:

1. Non-root uid (podman --userns=keep-id): /root is 0750, so uid!=0 cannot
   traverse it to reach the mise shims. node/bun/go/python all vanish while
   /usr/sbin tools (git, rg, curl) keep working — a confusing partial failure.

2. Overridden HOME (e.g. HOME=/workspace/.sandbox-home): mise looks for its
   config and installs under the new HOME, finds nothing, and every shim fails
   with "<tool> is not a valid shim".

Changes:

- Pin MISE_DATA_DIR / MISE_CONFIG_DIR to absolute paths under /opt/mise, and
  make /opt world-readable so any uid can exec the shims.
- Put MISE_CACHE_DIR / MISE_STATE_DIR under /tmp. These are runtime-writable
  and must not live under /opt, where a non-root uid cannot create dirs; that
  failure surfaces as "failed to write cache file ... Permission denied" and
  breaks bin-path resolution.
- Set MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS. mise only auto-trusts a global config it
  resolves through $HOME, so with the config outside HOME an overridden HOME
  made mise silently ignore it ("No version is set for shim: <tool>").
- Add jq, which release.sh and scripts/pre-push both require.
- Add an unprivileged `user` (uid/gid 1000) with passwordless sudo, owning
  /home/user and /workspace. Opt in with WRAP_MODE=user; default stays root.
- Add an entrypoint that corrects HOME when running as a non-root uid, since a
  bare `--user 1000` otherwise inherits HOME=/root, which that uid cannot read.
- Install skeleton dotfiles (.zshrc/.profile/.zprofile/.bashrc/.gitconfig) for
  both root and user. git safe.directory=* because /workspace is a bind mount
  whose host owner uid usually differs from the in-container uid.

Verified: node, bun, python3, go, jq, git and rg all resolve in four modes —
default root, WRAP_MODE=user, --userns=keep-id, and --userns=keep-id with
HOME overridden. Ran the real qmd test:types against a bind-mounted workspace
under the last of those; passes.

Note for rootless podman: container uid 1000 maps into the subuid range, so a
plain WRAP_MODE=user cannot write a host bind mount owned by the host user.
Use --userns=keep-id (or run without WRAP_MODE) for writable bind mounts.
Documented inline.

author: kindleops
body:
Canary #1 failed before provider submission. This fixes the cause.

**No SMS sent. No queue controls changed.**

---

## The defect

```
invalid input syntax for type uuid:
"send-one-a1728dc9-4903-4957-ad8b-6d3d46d86d53-1787021279552"
```

`queue_atomic_claim_send_row` declares `p_processing_run_id` as **uuid**. The route built a label:

```js
processing_run_id: `send-one-${queue_row_id}-${Date.now()}`
```

`queue-atomic-claim.js:50` forwards it verbatim, so Postgres rejected the call **at the claim step**. `send_one_queue_row` was therefore broken for **every row**, not just the canary.

It failed closed — the row was never claimed, so nothing reached the provider — but it could never have succeeded.

## Fixed at the caller, not the database

The UUID type is correct and stays. Every other caller already generates a real one:

| Caller | Value |
|---|---|
| `run-send-queue.js:166` | `crypto.randomUUID()` |
| `run-scoped-campaign-canary.js:324` | `deps.… \|\| crypto.randomUUID()` |
| `sms-engine.js:1070` | falls back to the lock token |
| **`control/route.js:1181`** | ❌ the label — **lone deviation** |

`crypto.randomUUID()` is used rather than omitting the field. Omitting also works — the RPC does `COALESCE(p_processing_run_id, gen_random_uuid())` — but then the caller never learns the id and `hasCurrentProcessingRun()` can no longer verify that this run owns the claim it's about to dispatch. Generating one keeps that check meaningful. No hashing/truncating of the row id; the row id is untouched.

## Bug-class sweep

Every caller reaching the atomic claim was checked. **`control/route.js:1181` was the only offender.** `run_targeted_queue_row` passes no `processing_run_id` at all — which is why that path kept working.

## Tests — 8 new

The double **enforces the real column type**: any non-null, non-UUID value raises the same `22P02` Postgres error. A mock accepting arbitrary strings would not have caught this.

Covers: UUID accepted · the exact production label rejected · legacy shape fails the UUID pattern while `randomUUID` passes · `null` forwarded as `null` so the RPC defaults it server-side · claim addresses the intended row and doesn't alter its id · **a failed claim performs zero provider calls** · route no longer contains the label shape and imports `crypto` · no queue caller assigns a literal-string `processing_run_id`.

Branch **83 pass / 1 fail** vs origin/main **75 / 1** — same pre-existing `emergency-stop` failure, zero attributable regression.

author: sirelves
body:
Terceira tentativa da v0.2.0: Windows falhou de novo em `Trust VPS host key`, agora com as cinco tentativas estourando 20 s cada.

Investiguei o servidor antes de mexer no workflow e confirmei que **não é bloqueio nosso**. Ou seja: **não é bloqueio nosso** — é restrição de saída do runner de Windows do GitHub. Os outros três runners alcançam o servidor normalmente. Insistir com retry só queimava um build de 10 minutos que tinha dado certo.

## Conserto

Os jobs de build passam a **só publicar artefato no próprio GitHub**. Todo o envio pro VPS acontece no job `release`, que roda em , alcança o servidor, e já precisava dos quatro artefatos pro `latest.json` de qualquer forma.

Menos quatro caminhos SSH paralelos, um só sequencial.

## De quebra

O release deixa de publicar aos pedaços. Antes cada plataforma subia assim que terminava — então por alguns minutos o diretório de downloads misturava versão nova e antiga, e quem baixasse nessa janela levava um conjunto inconsistente. Agora sobe tudo junto, depois os symlinks, depois o `latest.json`.

## Histórico desta série

Quarta tentativa. As três anteriores falharam na entrega, não no build — que passou nas quatro plataformas todas as vezes. Em ordem: caminho relativo depois de um `cd`, corrida entre runners escrevendo o mesmo script, e agora o egress do Windows. Nada chegou a ser publicado pela metade, porque o `latest.json` exige as quatro plataformas e falha se faltar alguma.

author: justinchuby
body:
## Why

Two problems with the master benchmark doc as it stands on `main`:

1. **§21.2/§21.3 are stale.** They describe the input-binding copy as an open gap and explicitly decline to say what closing it would be worth. #1146 closed it — `bind_inputs` on `rope_llama3_s128` went from ~601 µs to 0.7 µs. Every ratio in the document that predates that merge is being read against the wrong baseline, and nothing in the document says so.
2. **§23.7 frames the remaining losses as five independent kernel problems.** They are mostly one problem, and it is not in any of those kernels.

## What this adds

### §24 — Phase 6 (#1146)
What the borrowed `DeviceBuffer` does and the exact preconditions; the sequence-storage choke point (`read_seq_element` *moves* a buffer into cross-run `shared_buffers`, so guarding the slot was not enough); the 57-cell result (56/57 improved, 342/342 parity PASS); and precisely which §21 claims it supersedes.

### §25 — Phase 7 (#1175)
The two independent `RotaryEmbedding` defects, with the measurement that made them visible once #1146 left `exec_kernel.compute` at 96% of the run:

* the fan-out was **net-negative at every thread count** (t=16: 195 µs parallel vs 127 µs serial; 36 µs of pure Rayon bookkeeping to fan 128 tasks over a *one-worker* pool);
* the inner loop was scalar at ~1.4 cycles/element.

Plus why the new AVX2 arms deliberately avoid FMA (a tensor must not change value because a different thread count split it in a different place), and the 21-cell matrix: 21/21 improved, 0 regressed, 5 now beat ORT.

### §26 — the root cause behind the `t=8/16` column
An isolated 524 288-element region on 16 workers, varying only the idle gap between regions:

| gap | region cost |
|---|---|
| none | 67 µs |
| 20 µs | 226 µs |
| 500 µs | 236 µs |

A 20 µs gap — less than the serial glue between two graph nodes — costs ~160 µs. Rayon parks its workers; ORT's intra-op pool spins first, so its workers are hot when the next op arrives and ours are not. `rope_llama3_s128` at t=16 is 59 µs of kernel against ORT's ~30 µs, but a 189 µs paired wall.

`decode_spmd` already implements the right policy (bounded `KMP_BLOCKTIME` spin) and is wired only to the decode GEMM path. A prototype routing RoPE through it takes t=16 from **79 µs to 25 µs native-only, past ORT's ~30 µs**.

It is documented rather than merged, for two reasons that are both worth recording:

**(a) A latent correctness hazard.** `SharedState::publish` writes the job into a single `UnsafeCell` slot (`decode_spmd.rs:243`); `wait`'s doc comment states "the dispatcher is a single, never-idle thread" as an assumption, not an invariant. Two concurrent dispatchers overwrite each other's job pointer and both sets of workers run whichever closure landed last — **silently wrong tensors, not a crash**. Found empirically: new fan-out unit tests reported 6 tasks run when 5 were dispatched, and separately 0, depending on what else in the 1350-test binary was dispatching; `--test-threads=1` passes. A per-module CAS guard is *not* sufficient because the 11 existing dispatch sites do not take it. Latent today (the decode engine dispatches inline on one thread, and the plugin EP calls `disable_persistent_decode_pool()`), live as soon as two sessions in one process both run decode GEMM — which is exactly the concurrency the paged-KV work has to preserve.

**(b) Two spinning pools oversubscribe.** With the prototype on and an ORT session alternating in-process, t=16 is bimodal — 0.030 ms on one run, 0.441 ms on the next, same binary, same command. `ONNX_GENAI_CPU_DECODE_THREADS=16` confines the process to CPUs 0–15, which on this host is **8 physical cores** (siblings are adjacent). A blocktime sweep over 500/200/50/20/5/0 µs gave ratios from 0.233 to 72.3 with no monotone trend. The section also records that the compact mask is *correct* and must not be "fixed" to spread — one thread per core across 0,2,…,30 straddles two CCXs and measured worse (0.133 vs 0.079 ms).

### §26.3 — the consequence for the work queue
Softmax, Transpose, Concat and the MoE cells should not be attacked as separate kernel problems until (a) is fixed; their t=8/16 numbers are mostly measuring thread wake-up, so per-kernel tuning against that column will have to be redone. The stated exception is §11.5's paged/appendable KV cache, which is a real algorithmic cost no scheduler change touches.

## Scope

Documentation only — one file, append-only. No code, no test, no behaviour change.

author: windchargerj
body:
**Project creation now runs the XMake executable selected in the wizard, and Quick Start no longer freezes the UI while XMake starts.**

## What Changed

- The new-project wizard now captures the selected toolkit once, uses that toolkit's executable to create the project, and reports a clear setup error if no toolkit is selected.
- Quick Start launches `xmake create` on a background thread instead of the event dispatch thread. Success and failure notifications, project refresh, and console activation work as before.
- Corrected the capitalization of the CMake generation action, its implementation class, action ID, and menu label from `CmakeLists` to `CMakeLists`.

## Why

- Users select a toolkit in the wizard because they expect that installation to be used. Calling plain `xmake` depends on `PATH` and can invoke a different XMake executable.
- Continuing without a toolkit previously led to an unsafe null assertion. Failing early with a clear message is easier to understand and fix.
- Starting a process can block, so the IDE action should not do that work on the event dispatch thread.
- `CMake` is the official capitalization; using it consistently avoids a small but visible naming inconsistency.

## Impact

*New projects are created with the toolkit chosen in the wizard, and Quick Start stays responsive while XMake starts.*

body:
## Summary

Implements `.ai/plans/2026-07-31-02-next-version-ui-enhancements.md` (the docs half of #1) in full — all six threads.

|---|---|
| `930afd0` | Semantic colour layer + the Tymebox palette |

### Decisions taken

The plan asked two open questions rather than describing a change:

- **Signature accent** is a violet (`--tw-violet-500`), picked from the cool half of the wheel so amber and red keep meaning *only* "running late" and "overdue".
- **Responsive scope** is settled as **desktop-first but phone-usable** — facilitating is a lean-in task, but running a standup from a phone is a real case, and the sidebar already leaned that way.

### Notes for review

- Colours are now two layers: raw hues, and the semantic roles components may reference. Nothing outside `tokens/` names a hex. That restructure is what let the dark variant land **without touching a single component rule**.
- "System" theme is resolved in JS, not CSS, so the stylesheet keeps one `[data-theme='dark']` block instead of repeating every override under `prefers-color-scheme`. An inline boot script in `index.html` stamps it before first paint.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured globally in `base.css`, and read again in JS for the chart — Recharts animates outside CSS's reach.
- `eaad41d` is worth a look: `getPropertyValue` returns a custom property's *declared* value, so the tinted chart tokens were coming back as literal `color-mix(...)` strings headed for a serialized SVG and a canvas `fillStyle`.

### Test plan

- [x] `yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint`, `yarn test` (31 passing, 4 new for the theme store), `yarn build`
- [x] Rendered in the browser in both themes; tokens verified to resolve to concrete colours
- [ ] Signed-in pass over dashboard / report / history — the routes behind Google auth weren't exercised
- [ ] Check the countdown pulse and check-off animation against a real running event

author: yonasb
body:
## TL;DR

The check that keeps the sample reports honest about which version of the scanner
produced them could not fail until after the damage was done. It verified the recorded
commit against the branch it was running on, and on a pull request that is always
satisfied by the branch's own commits — so it stayed green through review and only went
red on the main branch, after the merge had already thrown that commit away. That is not
theoretical: it happened with #60 and #64 had to clean up by hand. This moves the check
to ask whether the recorded commit is already on the main branch, so the same mistake now
stops the pull request instead of following it in.

```
before:  example stamps a branch-only commit  ->  PR green  ->  squash drops it  ->  main RED
after:   example stamps a branch-only commit  ->  PR RED    ->  never merges
```

## What changed

`tests/test_examples_provenance.py` only. No shipped skill code, no example artifacts, so
no changelog entry.

- The ancestry leg resolves the stamped engine commit against the **base branch** rather
  than `HEAD`.
- Base-branch resolution, first hit wins: `GITHUB_BASE_REF` (as `origin/<base>` or
  `refs/heads/<base>`), then `origin/main`, `main`, `origin/HEAD`, then the first parent
  of `HEAD` on a GitHub `pull_request` run. That last one carries the CI case:
  `actions/checkout` checks out `refs/pull/N/merge` and fetches only that ref, so no
  `origin/<base>` exists in a pull-request job however deep the fetch, while the merge
  commit GitHub generated has the base branch tip as its first parent. It is guarded on
  the event being a pull request *and* `HEAD` genuinely being a two-parent merge, so an
  ordinary local merge commit can never be mistaken for a base ref.
- The **tip** of the base branch, not the merge base with it. A commit that landed on
  `main` after this branch was cut is perfectly legitimate to stamp — a squash cannot
  discard it — and measuring from the merge base would reject it.
- The `ci-speedup` leg now delegates to the single shared ancestry implementation instead
  of carrying its own copy, so this fix cannot drift back in one of two places.

Nothing else was touched. The report-versus-findings cross-check, the coverage-claim
check against the raw gap keys, the sanitization leg, the archive-era date bound and the
family registry all stay exactly as they were.

## The cost, which is the point

An example can no longer be generated from an in-flight branch commit and landed in the
same pull request. When an engine change and an example regeneration coincide, the engine
lands first and the example is regenerated in a follow-up. A branch-commit stamp is
exactly what a squash merge discards, so forbidding it is the fix rather than a side
effect of it.

## Proof it can fail

A positive control builds the situation from #60 with a real git repository — one commit
on `main`, one commit only on a feature branch, that branch checked out, an artifact
stamping the branch-only commit — and asserts the guard rejects it. Run against the
unfixed guard first:

```
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError, match="only on this branch|not reachable"):
>       _assert_engine_sha_is_an_ancestor(
            _stamped("branch-only", branch_only), branch_only[:7])
E   Failed: DID NOT RAISE <class 'AssertionError'>
```

The old guard accepted precisely what it must reject. It passes after the change.

Three more controls stop the new leg from being over-eager or quietly inert:

- an on-main stamp still passes, and so does a commit that landed on `main` after the
  branch point (the tip-versus-merge-base decision above);
- the pull-request merge-ref shape resolves its base through the first-parent fallback,
  and still rejects the branch-only stamp even though `HEAD` reaches it;
- with no base ref resolvable at all, the leg skips loudly off CI and **fails** in CI.

## When the check cannot run

| situation | behavior |
| --- | --- |
| shallow clone | skips loudly, as before — CI pins `fetch-depth: 0` and a separate leg keeps it pinned |
| pull request, same-repo or fork | resolves the base through the merge ref's first parent; fork pull requests are checked out from the base repository, so this is the same path |
| local clone or worktree | uses `origin/main`; a stale one is named in the failure message with the `git fetch origin main` remedy |
| no `main`, no remote, no base env (a vendored copy) | skips loudly off CI, **fails** in CI — a silent skip in CI is the same rot this change removes |

## Tests

`python3 -m pytest -q`: 4042 passed, 14 skipped, plus the two failures already known to be
unrelated on this machine's Python 3.9 (`test_the_grammar_guard_can_actually_fail` and one
`test_page_text_strips_every_legal_script_end_tag_form` case). The provenance suite itself
runs 21 passed, 0 skipped, so the ancestry legs really executed against the shipped
examples rather than skipping past them.

## What

Extracts manifest v1 from `crates/swath-core/src/manifest.rs` into the standalone `swath-manifest` crate per ADR 0016: types/serde/validation, `compare()`, and the schema snapshot test travel with it, plus the normative `SPEC.md`. `swath-referencer` and `swath-source-virtual` consume the crate directly; `swath-core` re-exports it as `swath_core::manifest` so every other caller resolves unchanged. Closes #187.

## Why

Boundary mechanics per the extraction-boundary design note: the crate is a leaf whose deps are exactly serde + serde_json (the `ManifestError` Display/Error impls are hand-rolled to drop thiserror — the recorded published-dep set, zero new deps). The schema's `GeoTransform` becomes the crate's own data-only six-field record (identical serde shape); the core keeps the geometry math and converts field-for-field at the shim, both directions. `From<&GeorefCrs> for Crs` moves into `swath-core/src/crs.rs` (orphan rule). The crate carries its own `LICENSE` (standalone REUSE posture) and stays `publish = false` until the pipeline (#192).

## Validation

- Zero behavior change: the pinned schema snapshot is byte-identical (only its `source:` metadata path moved); error text identical; full suite (487 tests) green.

author: marslavish
body:
Makes `nextjs/constructive-app` build as a static export and fixes the template gaps found while deploying a generated app to the static site gateway.

## Gaps fixed

**Static export config (`next.config.ts`)**
Repro: `pnpm build` produced a server build; the static site gateway needs `out/`. Turbopack also mis-inferred the workspace root in the generated pnpm monorepo.
Impact: generated apps could not deploy as static sites.
Fix: `output: 'export'`, `images: { unoptimized: true }`, and a `turbopack.root` that walks up to the nearest `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, so the path resolves both standalone in this repo and as `packages/app` in a generated monorepo.

**pnpm 11 global virtual store (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`)**
Repro: with pnpm 11 defaults, Turbopack resolves `next` outside the workspace and rejects it.
Impact: `pnpm dev`/`pnpm build` fail in fresh checkouts.
Fix: `enableGlobalVirtualStore: false`.

**Install is broken out of the box (found while verifying)**
Repro: `pnpm install` exits 1 with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`; pnpm 11 ignores the `pnpm` field in `package.json`, and the committed `allowBuilds` values were literal `set this to true or false` placeholders.
Impact: no script (`lint:types`, `build`, `dev`) can run.
Fix: moved the `graphql` override into `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, set `allowBuilds` to real values, removed the dead `pnpm` field.

**Dynamic org routes cannot static-export (route conversion)**
Repro: `src/app/orgs/[orgId]/*` has no `generateStaticParams`; `next build` with `output: 'export'` fails (and `[]` would export routes that 404 on a static host).
Impact: the B2B org surface blocks the static export entirely.
Fix: converted to query-param routes per this PR's own convention doc — `/orgs/{members,invites,settings,activity}?orgId=…`, `useEntityParams` reads `orgId` via nuqs `useQueryState`, `buildOrgRoute` builds the links, sidebar configs and callers updated. Side effect: the org routes now match `getRouteKeyFromPath`, so their `access: 'protected'` guard actually applies (the bracket paths never matched).

**Shell scroll (`app-shell.tsx`)**
Repro: `<main>` was `overflow-hidden`, so every page needed its own `h-full overflow-y-auto` wrapper; pages without one could not scroll.
Impact: nested scroll containers and easy-to-miss unscrollable pages.
Fix: `<main>` is `overflow-y-auto`; removed the per-page wrappers.

**Query retry predicate (`src/lib/query-client.ts`)**
Repro: SDK hooks throw plain `TypeError` on network failure and `GraphQLRequestError` with an `HTTP 5xx` message on gateway hiccups; the predicate retried neither.
Impact: transient infra errors surface as hard failures.
Fix: retry both (5xx only for `GraphQLRequestError`).

**Conventions doc (`docs/CONVENTIONS.md`, linked from the README)**
New: no `[param]` routes (query-param detail routes with Suspense instead), create/edit via stack cards, every query error state renders a `refetch()` retry control, scrolling lives in the shell. `docs/B2B.md` route references updated to match.

**Build runs codegen when the SDK is absent (`scripts/ensure-sdk.sh`)**
Repro: `pnpm build` fails in a checkout without the generated SDK (the repo commits only stub `src/graphql/sdk/*/index.ts`; the generated dirs are gitignored).
Impact: generated apps need a manual `pnpm codegen` step before the first build.
Fix: `build` runs `ensure-sdk.sh`, which runs codegen only when `src/graphql/sdk/*/types.ts` is missing, and skips it when a generated SDK is present.

## Out of scope

- Endpoint hostnames belong in `.env.local` handling in `@agentic-kit/pi` (scaffolder), not this template.
- The `pnpm-workspace.yaml` placeholder writer is scaffolder-side (`@agentic-kit/pi`); this PR only fixes the copy committed here.
- The generated SDK typing `unknown` for some fields is in `@constructive-io/graphql-codegen`, not chased here.

## Verification

- `pnpm install` passes (it exits 1 on `main`).
- `pnpm lint:types`: 0 errors with a generated SDK in place. Without one, `main` and this branch fail with the identical 52 stub-SDK errors (sorted lists diff clean) — this PR adds no type errors.
- `pnpm build` with a generated SDK and `NEXT_PUBLIC_DB_NAME` set: all 20 routes prerender as static content into `out/`, including the four converted `/orgs/*` routes (their HTML contains the Suspense shell skeleton, confirming the nuqs query-param reads are prerender-safe).
- `ensure-sdk.sh` guard exercised both ways against a fixture tree (runs codegen when a `types.ts` is missing, skips when present).
- Not verified (needs a live backend, none was available): shell scroll behind auth in `pnpm dev`, the 5xx retry against a real gateway, and org navigation end to end. Static checks for these pass; runtime behavior needs a backend.

## Summary
Resolves every valid issue raised in the audit report:

**P0 — Engine lifecycle** (`src/vr/Engine.ts`)
- `start()` is now idempotent (no repeated `sessionstart`/`sessionend` listener registration)
- XR `visibilitychange` handler is retained and detached on session end / `dispose()` (was an anonymous callback that leaked when the XRSession outlived the Engine)
- `_contextRestored()` bails when already `disposed` (no resurrection)
- `exitVR()` returns `Promise<boolean>` so UI/telemetry can surface a failed exit instead of a dead button

**P0 — Signalling in-band auth** (`src/network/SignallingServerCore.ts`)
- Token-required connections without a URL token are now admitted unauthenticated and given the 5s in-band `auth` window — the advertised in-band auth flow was previously unreachable dead code
- Independent network-gateway validation of room/peer identifiers (charset + length, close 4003)
- Capability semantics made honest: removed the misleading `TokenClaims.capabilities` (server-derived from role via `ROLE_CAPABILITIES`, never honoured from a claim) — in both `SignallingServerCore.ts` and `SignedTicket.ts`

**P1 — `FrameTask`** (`src/vr/Engine.ts`): removed `| unknown` so the union no longer collapses to `unknown`; `addUpdatable(123)` is now a compile error. Added `update?` to `PanelLike`/`HandWheelMenuLike`.

**P1 — EventBus escape hatch** (`src/utils/EventBus.ts`): removed the `[key: string]: unknown` index signature and arbitrary-string `on/off/emit/once` overloads; added named `onDynamic/offDynamic/emitDynamic/onceDynamic` for runtime-computed topics; promoted the off-map `'userMode:applied'` topic into the typed map (which surfaced and fixed two real payload-type bugs: `history:seek`, `performance:throttle`).

**P2 — VR-exit result**: `World.exitVR()` propagates the boolean.

**Low — hygiene**
- Walked back the false ROADMAP claim that `@deprecated` World.ts properties were removed (17 are still present)

Note: the audit's item 15 (E2E test is a cross-layer integration test, not a true production-wiring smoke test) is an observation tracked as a follow-up, not addressed here — a real-browser smoke harness is separate scope.

author: diegoloayza88
body:
## Problema

Los reportes semanales se sentían limitados a Colombia, México y USA, con solo 1-2 bandas destacadas. Investigación completa reveló la causa raíz y varios bugs relacionados.

**Hallazgo principal:** de 739 conciertos en DynamoDB, solo 11 eran "watchlist matches" — y **10 de esos 11 eran Slayer**, la única banda mainstream de la watchlist de 26 bandas ultra-underground. El resto (Mgła, Bewitched, Beherit, Warmoon Lord...) casi nunca gira por Latinoamérica ni aparece en Ticketmaster/Google Events.

## Cambios

### `src/shared/user_config.py`
- **Watchlist ampliada de 26 a 57 bandas**: se agregaron bandas activas en gira internacional del mismo circuito (black metal: Mayhem, Immortal, Dimmu Borgir, Watain, Enslaved, Deathspell Omega...; war/bestial: Archgoat, Blasphemy, Conqueror...; OSDM: Autopsy, Undergang, Gatecreeper...; thrash clásico: Kreator, Sodom, Sepultura...), priorizando bandas con historial real de giras para aumentar la tasa de match real.
- Nuevo método `genre_hint_score()`: score parcial (4.0-5.0) para conciertos que coinciden con géneros preferidos (black/death/war/thrash metal) sin matchear ninguna banda específica — alimenta la nueva sección de "Descubrimiento".
- Agregado `thrash_metal` a `preferred_genres` por defecto (faltaba pese a estar en la watchlist y en el texto del reporter).

### `src/agents/orchestrator/handler.py`
- `classify_and_filter` ahora confía directamente en las 3 fuentes activas (`serpapi_events`, `ticketmaster`, `festivals`) en vez de re-clasificar con LLM. Ticketmaster ya filtra server-side (`classificationName=metal`), Festivals solo scrapea 9 festivales de metal curados a mano. El prompt del LLM decía literalmente "si no estás seguro, NO la incluyas" — descartando bandas underground legítimas, que es el objetivo mismo del proyecto. El paso LLM se mantiene como red de seguridad para fuentes futuras no confiables.
- Score por género como fallback cuando no hay match de banda (`watchlist_match` se mantiene estrictamente ligado a matches reales).
- Búsqueda de vuelos por corrida: 5 → 8 (margen de sobra con cadencia semanal y timeout de 900s).

### `src/agents/flight_agent/handler.py`
- Agregados aeropuertos faltantes: NO (OSL), DE (FRA/MUC), GR (ATH), RO (OTP). `COUNTRY_AIRPORTS` solo cubría 7/11 países — cualquier concierto en Noruega, Alemania, Grecia o Rumanía (incluyendo Inferno Metal Fest, con matches reales de watchlist) nunca generaba búsqueda de vuelo, por lo que nunca podía aparecer en la sección "PRIORIDAD MÁXIMA" del reporte.

### `src/plugins/festivals.py`
- Eliminados "Underground for the Masses" (CO) y "Candelabrum Metal Fest" (MX): ambos apuntan a Facebook/Instagram, que bloquean IPs de AWS, así que solo producían placeholders "[lineup por anunciar]". SerpApiEventsPlugin ya captura ambos festivales como conciertos reales con nombres de banda reales.

### `src/agents/reporter_agent/handler.py` — el fix más importante
- **Bug de sesgo por país en el truncamiento**: `watchlist_concerts[:15]` e `isolated_concerts[:30]` se construían concatenando listas por país en orden fijo (`CO→CL→BR→US→MX→FI→ES→NO→DE→GR→RO`), luego se ordenaban con sort estable por score/fecha. Como los scores empatan en pocos buckets discretos, los empates preservaban el orden de inserción — los primeros 15-30 slots quedaban dominados por los países listados primero, excluyendo silenciosamente matches de FI/ES/NO/DE/GR/RO aunque existieran en DynamoDB. Corregido con nueva función `_round_robin_by_country()` que intercala los buckets por país antes de cualquier truncamiento.
- Watchlist matches divididos en `exact_matches` (banda conocida, score 8-10) vs `genre_discoveries` (señal de género, score 4-5) — nueva sección **"Descubrimiento"** en el reporte que introduce activamente bandas fuera de la watchlist en vez de ignorarlas.
- `USER_PROFILE` ahora lista los 11 países monitoreados (faltaban NO/DE/GR/RO), lo cual hacía que el LLM los despriorizara implícitamente sin importar qué datos hubiera en el prompt.
- Eliminado código muerto: `upcoming_concerts` hacía 11 queries extra a DynamoDB por corrida pero nunca se leía en `generate_report()`.
- Consolidado a una sola query por país (antes eran dos: una para aislados/festivales a confidence>=0.7, otra para watchlist a confidence>=0.5) — ahora un solo fetch a 0.5, filtrado en memoria.
- `max_tokens` 2000→2800 y tope de palabras semanal 1800→2200 para que la nueva sección de Descubrimiento no desplace contenido existente.

## Verificación

Probado localmente: scoring de `user_config`, intercalado round-robin, construcción completa del prompt en `generate_report()`, y una corrida end-to-end simulada de `lambda_handler` con DynamoDB mockeado — todo produce el resultado correcto (bandas de Alemania y festivales de Noruega llegan al prompt final). Suite de tests existente pasa (1 fallo preexistente no relacionado en `test_whatsapp_parser.py`, confirmado presente en `main` antes de este cambio).

## Test plan
- [ ] Merge y ejecutar el orchestrator manualmente
- [ ] Verificar que el reporte incluya una sección "Descubrimiento" con bandas nuevas

author: chasevandiver
body:
Owner request: *"I want to be able to add people to groups by name along with join code."* Along with, not instead of — the code is untouched and is still the only path for someone who has no account yet.

## GRP-1 — the second door (migration 0064)

Three admin-gated RPCs:

- **`search_group_candidates`** — typeahead over accounts, carrying each one's membership state (`none` / `removed` / `member`) rather than filtering members out, `%` and `_` escaped so a name is a name, and nothing answered under two characters.
- **`add_group_member`** / **`add_group_member_by_name`** — `join_group`'s insert minus the code and the throttle, keeping its SEC-02 role rule: an admin who was *removed* comes back a member through either door. One rule, two doors.

`join_group` is a boundary because the caller asserts a claim about themselves. An admin naming an existing account asserts a privilege they demonstrably hold, so the gate is `is_group_admin` and there is nothing to throttle — the worst case is a wrong person added to a group the admin already runs.

**`display_name` has no unique constraint** and never has, so the typed-name path refuses a shared name instead of resolving it. The search returns ids, and the Add button never goes through the name at all.

**UI:** an "Add someone by name" block on the roster in group settings — debounced search, per-row Add / "Add back" / "already in", and a typed-name fallback that surfaces the database's refusal.

## GRP-1b — settings stopped redirecting the other two group kinds

`/groups/[slug]/settings` is built around the board, so it refused betting and survivor groups outright, which meant *their* admins had no page for the roster, the name, the visibility, the join code or archiving — five RPCs with nothing calling them. The board load is now a `loadBoard` split that runs for a pick'em admin only (it had been fetching the whole slate for plain members too), `GroupAdmin` hides the two pick'em-only controls, and both homes gained the Members link they never had.

## GRP-2 — being added tells you so (migrations 0065/0066)

The `added_to_group` notification kind, split across two migrations because Postgres refuses to use a new enum value in the transaction that adds it.

`default_enabled` is **true**, the opposite of bad beats and for the opposite reason: that one is a firehose, this fires a handful of times ever and is always about you, so silent-by-default would miss exactly the people who never open the notification settings. The copy names the admin — "you were added to Saturday Boys" reads like something the site did, where "Chase added you" is a person, and a person is who you ask about it.

Sent from the server action inside `next/server`'s `after()`, and it swallows its own failures: a notification that failed to send is not a membership that failed to happen. Subject is the group, so it fires once per person per group, ever.

**Found in passing:** `updateNotificationSetting`'s allowlist never carried `watchdog`, so 0037's "the copy is editable from /admin like every other kind" has been false since it was written. Fixed alongside.

## Verification

- **354 DB assertions** against a real Postgres 16 cluster, 0 failed — 27 of them new, including two accounts sharing a name, an archived group refusing an add, and a removed admin coming back a member.
- **1301 tests across 96 files**, `tsc`, lint and `next build` all clean in-session.
- **Migrations 0064–0066 are already applied to production** (2026-08-18, in order, ahead of this deploy — all three only add things, so they are inert against the running code). Verified live afterwards: 3 new functions present, neither the add nor the search executable by `anon`, `added_to_group` on the enum, its settings row seeded correctly. The 3 new security-advisor rows are the pre-existing definer-RPC pattern.

Not seen rendered in a browser — the UI review pass was against the code.

`docs/STATUS.md` carries GRP-1 / GRP-1b / GRP-2 with the evidence; `docs/CHANGELOG.md` has the dated entry.

author: mikaelh
body:
**`create_invoice` has been broken against production since 2026-08-12.** Not a hypothetical — the field the API requires is not the field this package sends.

## The break

Product-repo PR #1243 moved invoice line prices from integer cents to integer **micro-euros** and renamed the field to `unitPriceMicros`, so SAF-T can carry the 4–6 decimals a discount-apportioned unit price needs (AT's own worked example: 100 × €0.55 less 8.8% = **0.5016/unit**, not representable in cents).

This package kept sending `unitPrice` in cents — a field `/api/v1` does not accept, while omitting the one it requires. Products were unaffected; `ProductInput` still takes cents. Only the invoice path rotted.

## Money in, euros

Rather than make the model emit micro-euros, **every price on the tool surface is now a decimal euro string** — `"80.00"`, `"1.789"`. The wrapper converts to whatever unit the endpoint takes: cents for products, micros for invoice lines.

A model emitting `80000000` instead of `80` mints a legally certified invoice off by four orders of magnitude, and nothing downstream can tell it is wrong. The MCP server is exactly the caller with no compiler to catch it — #1243's own commit message calls a silent 10,000× unit change *"the one failure mode worth the larger diff"*. So the multiplication happens in code, once, under test.

Parsing goes through `BigInt`, not `parseFloat`: `1.789 * 1e6` is `1788999.9999999998`, and truncating that loses a micro on a signed document.

This also covers the goods-seller case for free — `"1.789"` per litre works exactly like `"80.00"` per hour.

## Why nothing caught it, and what now does

`smoke.mjs` and `live-smoke.mjs` both run against mocks written from **this package's own idea of the contract**. They agreed with each other and with nothing real, and stayed green through a breaking rename.

`conformance.mjs` closes that gap: it fetches the **published** `openapi.json`, drives the built server against a recording mock, and validates every request body actually sent — required fields present, no field the schema does not define, line items included. Wired into `npm run smoke`; skips loudly if the spec is unreachable.

The `ai-first` spec already says *"the MCP surface tracks the API, never leads it."* Nothing enforced it. Now something does.

## Validation

- **Mutation-tested the guard.** Restoring the old cents behaviour makes conformance fail with exactly the original bug:
  ```
  FAIL  POST /invoices items[0]: missing required field "unitPriceMicros" (sent: description, quantity, vatRate, itemType, unitPrice)
  FAIL  POST /invoices items[0]: sends "unitPrice", which the published schema does not define
  ```
  Reverting passes. It would have caught this on day one.
- **live-smoke asserts on the wire**, not in a unit test: `"10.00"` → `10000000` micros, `"80.00"` → `8000` cents for products, sub-cent `"1.789"` → `1789000`, raw `unitPrice` never leaks, and a malformed amount (`"80 euros"`) is refused as a readable tool error instead of being sent.
- Full `npm run smoke` green, including conformance against the live spec.

## Not in this PR

The regime/VAT work discussed alongside this — `/api/v1` deriving VAT treatment from the issuer's regime so `vatRate` becomes optional, and the MCP server dropping the profile-first dance. That touches the certified `invoicing/` module and the public API contract, so it belongs in the product repo with its own review.

author: tokuhirom
body:
## Summary
- `todo/tickets/whenever-target-var-binds-wrong-value-in-react.md` was filed as a narrow VM binding bug (`my $tap = whenever ...` binds `$tap` to garbage). Investigation shows the actual root cause is a missing language feature — the parser has no rule for `whenever` as an expression term at all, so the construct fragments into four unrelated statements, with `$tap` literally bound to the bareword string `"whenever"`.
- The one existing mechanism that lets `whenever` appear in expression position (`do { whenever $s {...} }`, gated by `compiler::whenever_bind_target`) is independently broken even for its own narrow designed-for case: it only fires when the whenever'd expression is a bare `Expr::Var`, and works by clobbering that source variable with the result — which direct testing shows isn't even a real `Tap`, just the original `Supply` value.
- A real fix needs parser + AST + compiler + VM design work (a genuine, non-clobbering target-var binding for any whenever expression shape), not a one-shot patch. Moved to `todo/deep/` with the full investigation write-up (repro commands, exact code locations, and what a real fix needs to cover) so the finding isn't lost.

## Test plan
Docs-only change (`todo/deep/`, `todo/tickets/`) — no code touched, so this qualifies for the docs-only CI fast path.

author: keithcu
body: ## Problem `make build` / `make deploy` can abort with: ``` ValueError: ZIP does not support timestamps before 1980 ``` Python's `zipfile` refuses to add files whose mtime is before 1980. Two common situations produce such files: - Freshly vendored wheels — `uv`/pip extract many wheel files with an epoch-0 (`1970-01-01`) mtime. - Reused Cloud Agent snapshot checkouts — the snapshot restore resets `/workspace` file mtimes to `1970-01-01`. When any bundled file carries a pre-1980 mtime, the OXT zip step aborts mid-write, leaving a truncated (22-byte) `build/WriterAgent.oxt`, which then fails `unopkg add` and blocks hot-deploy. ## Fix Pass `strict_timestamps=False` to the three OXT `zipfile.ZipFile(...)` writers (WriterAgent, LibrePy, LibreHarper). With this flag, `zipfile` clamps out-of-range timestamps to `1980-01-01` instead of raising, so packaging never fails on restored/normalized timestamps. Contents are unchanged; only the stored zip entry timestamp is clamped. ## Testing Set a bundled source file to an epoch-0 mtime and rebuilt: - `touch -d @0 plugin/main.py` - `make build` → **succeeds**: `Created build/WriterAgent.oxt with 1345 files` (previously aborted with the pre-1980 error). - OXT integrity: `ZipFile.testzip()` → OK; the `plugin/main.py` entry `date_time` is clamped to `(1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)`. - `unopkg add build/WriterAgent.oxt` → registers `org.extension.writeragent` cleanly. - `make build` runs `ty` + `ruff` first and completed, so the change is type/lint clean. ## Why it helps This removes the root cause behind the Cloud Agent mtime workarounds (per-boot `start` mtime normalization and pre-baking `vendor/`), so those environment scripts can be simplified back to lock-cleanup only.

body:
The real-time fix for the sweep-latency finding: stop waiting for the platform's webhooks and poll its orders API every hour from the Actions runner.

## How it works
- `scripts/poll-paid-orders.js` reads `GET /orders` per store (EN/ES/FR), keeps orders that are **paid** (`financial_status 230` — the same constant WebhookAction keys on) within the last 14 days, and links each to its 3D design through the €0 preview line (`inner_title` `{"type":"3d-preview","order_no":…}`, title fallback — both verified against order kz1cgjw0oh's real strings).
- Customer renders come from the preview product's images; new orders go through the existing `admin-orders` **ingest-and-send** (confirmation email + day-4/day-10 lifecycle). Orders already in KV dedup, and when the late webhook sweep finally delivers the same order, it dedups against this record — no double emails in either direction.
- The vendor's orders-read API is an **unverified surface**, so the script maps fields defensively, re-fetches single orders when the list omits a field (documented trap), and ships a `--probe` mode that dumps the raw shape (emails masked). Documented in `docs/oemsaas-api-notes.md`.

## Two-stage arming — merging is safe right now
1. Without the `MOMUTO_API_SECRET` repo secret (same value as Vercel's `D3_ORDER_SECRET`), every run logs "not armed" and exits 0.
2. With the secret, **scheduled runs stay dry** (decisions logged, nothing sent) until the repo variable `POLL_LIVE=1` is set — set it only after reviewing a manual probe + dry run.

Also: `admin-orders` ingest accepts `image_back` so both renders reach the email.

## Rollout (owner)
1. Merge. 2. Actions → "Poll paid orders" → Run with mode=**probe** (needs no secret) — paste me the output so the field mapping gets verified against reality. 3. Add `MOMUTO_API_SECRET` secret. 4. Run mode=**dry-run**, review decisions. 5. Set repo variable `POLL_LIVE=1` → hourly live.

- one `FlowDescriptor` literal in `pack.rs` gains `entry`, derived the same way as the sites the patch itself updated (`tags_indicate_entry(flow.tags…)`)
- ten `FlowEngine` literals in the test module gain `messaging_provider_pack_ids: Default::default()` — an empty set, which is the behaviour those tests were written against
- one caller passes `&entry` where the ported helper takes `&Value`
- `Cargo.toml` keeps this lane's `1.3.0-research.0`, not `main`'s `1.1.7`

## Why a cherry-pick and not a lane sync

`main` is 20 commits ahead of `research`, and the obvious move is a merge. It is the wrong instrument here, which took measuring to establish rather than assuming:

| main-only commit | already on research? |
|---|---|
| `flow.goto` (#682) | **yes** — plus #686's loader fix, which `main` lacks |
| billing dimensions (`d185ad5`) | yes — 31 `project_id` refs in `agent_node.rs` |
| pack identity as `project_id` (#653) | yes — `billing.rs` documents it as the pack identity |
| in-process `dw.agent` metering (#665) | yes — 37 metering refs |
| OTLP_HEADERS / OTEL_SERVICE_NAME | yes — its `main` commit message reads "(research port)" |
| 3 × `chore(release)`, 5 × CI | `main`-lane only, irrelevant to `1.3.0-research` |

A whole-lane merge conflicts in **29 blocks across 6 source files**, precisely because both lanes implemented the same features independently: `research` has `stream_observers` and a `conversational` `AgentInput` that `main` lacks, while `main`'s `project_id` plumbing is shaped differently. Resolving that is feature reconciliation, not a merge, and one wrong block silently drops either streaming observers or billing attribution.

This PR is the one substantive fix `research` was actually missing. (`#616`'s dead-`pre_cache` cleanup is the only other, and it is cosmetic.)

## Verification

`cargo check -p greentic-runner-host --all-targets --all-features` clean, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --workspace -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean, and the ported `tags_indicate_entry_treats_internal_as_non_entry` passes.

author: will383842
body:
Une fois le lockfile réparable (#718), Gate A va jusqu'aux tests — et y trouve **trois échecs déjà présents sur `main`**, sans rapport les uns avec les autres. Aucun n'appartient à une PR ouverte : ils bloquaient **toute** PR, quel qu'en soit le contenu.

Vérifié en lançant les trois specs sur `origin/main` seul, sans aucun commit ajouté.

---

## 1. Le parcours de session comptait encore quatorze étapes

`session-parcours.spec.ts:576` — `expected 15 to be 14`.

#709 a ajouté `convention_contresignee` : la contresignature de l'organisme est un acte **distinct** de la signature du client, et c'était tout l'objet de cette PR de la faire apparaître. L'étape est légitime ; c'est le compte qui n'avait pas été reporté. Le test passe à quinze.

Ce test n'est pas décoratif — son propre commentaire le dit : *« sans ceci, une liste vide ferait passer tout le bloc au vert »*. C'est précisément pour cela qu'il doit rester exact.

## 2. Le garde-fou carte-lien accusait du code sain

`admin-card-anchor-display.test.ts` — `imprimes/page.tsx:58`.

La page posait **bien** `display: block`, mais par `style` inline. Le garde-fou ne lit que `className` : il signalait une ancre `display: inline` **qui ne l'a jamais été**. Le défaut de rendu qu'il décrit — le fond de la carte qui recouvre le contenu voisin — n'existait pas ici.

Le correctif porte sur la **page**, pas sur le test. Apprendre au garde-fou à reconnaître un `style` inline l'obligerait à rattacher la propriété à la bonne balise, donc à parser le JSX : il deviendrait plus large et moins sûr. Une seule façon de poser `display` sur une carte-lien, c'est ce qui rend la garde vérifiable.

## 3. Un prix en dur — et deux montants qui ne sont pas de même nature

`no-hardcoded-prices.spec.ts` — `content/imprimes.ts:129` (#708). La ligne portait **deux** montants, que la doctrine du garde-fou traite différemment.

**« au lieu de 650 € » est un tarif Axion-IA**, dupliqué hors de la SSOT — exactement ce que ce garde-fou existe pour empêcher. Ni le token ni l'exemption ne convenaient : il n'y a **aucun tier à 650 €** dans `pricing.ts`, et le champ `resume` est rendu brut (`{imprime.resume}`), donc un `{{price:…}}` s'afficherait tel quel à l'écran. Le montant est donc **retiré** : ce résumé décrit un imprimé, le prix vit dans le PDF et dans la SSOT, pas en double ici.

**« 0 € de reste à charge » n'est pas un tarif** : il décrit l'effet du financement OPCO. Aucun changement de barème ne peut le périmer, il n'a rien à dériver. C'est l'usage prévu du marqueur `price-exempt` — posé **sur la ligne**, et non deux lignes plus haut où il ne servait à rien : `lineIsAllowed` teste ligne à ligne.

> ⚠️ Le point 3 touche une formulation commerciale. Si vous préférez garder « au lieu de 650 € » dans ce résumé, dites-le : l'alternative est d'allowlister `imprimes.ts` en entier, au prix d'un prix qui pourra se périmer en silence.

---

## Vérifications

- Les trois specs : **62 tests verts** (elles échouaient toutes les trois avant)
- `pnpm typecheck` : propre
- `git diff --stat` : 3 fichiers, **22 insertions / 5 suppressions**

## Ordre de fusion

**#718 (lockfile) d'abord** — sans lui, Gate A ne dépasse pas l'étape `pnpm install` et ne verra jamais ces tests. Ensuite celle-ci, puis #717.

author: madmax983
body:
## Summary

Diesel records applied migrations **by version** (the leading `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS` directory prefix). When two differently-named migration directories share one version, a fresh database applies exactly one of them and records the version as done — the other is skipped forever, with no error anywhere. This has caused real incidents in downstream apps built on Autumn, where two concurrent branches (or a plugin and an app) both picked the same version.

This adds three layers of protection, from preventive to enforcing to last-resort:

- **`autumn migrate new <name>`** — creates `migrations/<version>_<name>/{up,down}.sql` with a version guaranteed free across the working tree, every local and remote-tracking git branch this checkout has fetched, and the framework's own compiled-in migrations. The generated files carry the same WHY/LOCKING guidance headers as a well-run migration-review checklist.
- **`autumn migrate check-collisions`** — the CI-time backstop for a collision `migrate new` couldn't see (a branch pushed after, a teammate's concurrent PR). Fails when a version this checkout introduces is already claimed elsewhere; stays silent about a collision between two *other* branches (that's their own gate to fail on). Degrades to a working-tree-only check with a loud warning on a shallow clone rather than failing closed. Wired into this repo's own CI (new `migration-collisions` job in `ci.yml`) as the reference implementation downstream apps can copy.
- **Framework-level runtime guard** — neither CLI command can see a *plugin's* migrations (they live in a compiled crate, not a directory the checkout's git history contains), and an app can't be expected to coordinate versions with every plugin author who might register alongside it. So `autumn_web::migrate::check_migration_version_collisions` checks every registered `EmbeddedMigrations` set (framework, plugin, and app, via `AppBuilder::migrations(…)`) for cross-set version collisions at startup, and aborts loudly before any migration runs — this is the layer that actually solves the "can't rely on plugin authors to coordinate" problem as the framework picks up wider adoption.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit tests for `check_migration_version_collisions` in `autumn/src/migrate.rs` (4 tests, using two new fixture migration dirs sharing a version) — `cargo test -p autumn-web --lib migrate::tests::check_migration_version_collisions`
- [x] New unit tests for the version picker and name validator in `autumn-cli/src/migrate/versions.rs` (12 tests) — `cargo test -p autumn-cli --bin autumn migrate::versions::`
- [x] Manual end-to-end test in a scratch git repo: `autumn migrate new` avoids a working-tree collision; `autumn migrate check-collisions` fails on a real cross-branch collision (via simulated `origin/*` refs) with the correct exit code, and passes once renumbered
- [x] Manual verification against this repo's own `autumn/migrations` (17 real framework migrations) — confirmed a deliberately introduced collision is caught, including a subtle `git ls-tree` CWD-relative-output bug found and fixed along the way (affects any migrations dir that isn't the repo root, like this monorepo's `autumn/`)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p autumn-web --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p autumn-cli --bin autumn --all-targets -- -D warnings` — both clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo check --workspace` — clean
- [x] `./scripts/check-panic-gate.sh`, `./scripts/check-determinism-gate.sh`, `./scripts/check-migration-guides.sh`, `./scripts/check-docs.sh` (intra-doc links) — all pass
- [x] New CI job (`migration-collisions`) validated locally by running the exact command it runs (`cd autumn && cargo run -p autumn-cli --bin autumn -- migrate check-collisions`)

author: dereuromark
body:
The README described a CI shape that no longer exists after #44 and #46, in two places a reader would take at face value.

**The lag.** It said the lag "never gates" and then, one clause later, that `--max-age-days` gates on age. That flag is gone. What is worth keeping is the reason rather than the flag: age is a proxy for "has the engine changed in a way that matters", and the number that answers the question directly is measured by `corpus-drift`.

**The corpus.** It described one job running the corpus against "the spec". There are two now, and they ask different questions - `corpus` gates against the spec commit the embedded engine pins, `corpus-drift` reports the same comparison against spec `main` without blocking on it. A reader who assumed the gate was against spec `main` would draw the wrong conclusion from a green build, which is the whole reason it is written down.

Docs only; no behavior change.

body:
## Summary

- The Hosts UI told operators to run `pnpm local:agent start` — a script that has
  never existed (the real one is `local:daemon`) — and gave no endpoint or key, so a
  newly created host slot could never actually be connected from the instructions
  shown.
- Replaces the transient add-host success message with a persistent
  `ConnectHostPanel` on the host detail page (Overview tab), shown whenever a host
  has no live daemon connection, with a copyable command:
  ```
  HARNESS_HOST_ID=<hostId>
  HARNESS_API_URL=<controlPlaneUrl()>
  HARNESS_API_KEY=<bound service-account key>
  pnpm local:daemon start
  ```
- `controlPlaneUrl()` (`services/web/src/lib/control-plane-url.ts`) resolves the
  control-plane origin: an explicit `NEXT_PUBLIC_HARNESS_CONTROL_PLANE_URL`
  build-time override locally/in e2e, or `window.location.origin` in the browser —
  mirroring the existing `viewerWebSocketUrl()` pattern in `live-session-logs.ts`.
  It never emits a raw API Gateway endpoint (see #170's `ws-url.ts` for why that
  matters on the host-daemon side).
- **Hydration-safety fix caught in review**: `app/hosts/[hostId]/page.tsx` is
  server-rendered (`force-dynamic`), so calling `controlPlaneUrl()` directly in the
  render body would diverge between the server (no `window`, falls back to a local
  default) and the browser on a cloud build (`window.location.origin` is the real
  CloudFront domain) — not just a React hydration-mismatch warning, but a misleading
  `127.0.0.1:7420` command actually present in the server-rendered HTML before
  hydration corrects it. `ConnectHostPanel` now resolves the origin in a `useEffect`
  instead, rendering a brief "Loading connect instructions…" state only when the
  value isn't already build-time-stable. A local/e2e build bakes the override in, so
  it resolves synchronously there with no loading state — this is the path both the
  existing unit tests and e2e already exercised, which is why the mismatch wasn't
  caught until traced through deliberately.
- Also fixes five stale `local:agent` / `local:agent-web` references: `cli.ts` usage
  text (landed in #170), `attach-local-repo-form.tsx`'s empty-state message, and
  comments in `scripts/agent-web-e2e.test.ts`, `scripts/local-cli-e2e.test.ts`,
  `e2e/real-cli/real-cli-helpers.ts`, `e2e/control/orchestration.spec.ts`.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run services/web/src` — 93 files / 305 tests pass.
- [x] `connect-host-panel.tsx` and `control-plane-url.ts`: 100% statement/branch/
      function/line coverage (both the build-time-configured and browser-origin-effect
      paths are exercised, including the loading-state branch).
- [x] `pnpm exec oxlint` / `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on all changed files — clean.
- [x] `e2e/control/hosts.spec.ts` extended: asserts the emitted command contains the
      real endpoint and `pnpm local:daemon start` (never `local:agent` or
      `execute-api`), and that the copy button round-trips through the clipboard.

Depends on nothing from #170, but is easiest to review after it (same host-connection
context).

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019fdyYcAti5DQZywBwT6N1N

## Shepherd Journal

- Applied Codex P1 fix (shell-injection via unquoted hostId in the connect command): added POSIX single-quote escaping for HARNESS_HOST_ID/HARNESS_API_URL in connect-host-panel.tsx, with a regression test covering an embedded single-quote in the hostId.
