author: maribakulj
body:
## Un trou de couverture, pas une dépendance en retard

`docs/10` disait le reste de xiiif « bloqué sur W0.6 ». **W0.6 est terminé depuis longtemps**, et `RemoteArtifactRef` n'existait pourtant *nulle part* — ni schéma, ni type, ni mention hors de cette ligne de blocage.

W0.6 a livré les schémas LEP ; ce type-ci est un contrat **entre** locusolus et xiiif, et aucun item ne le portait. Même forme que le trou de §7.1 relevé en tête de roadmap : ce qui n'est assigné à personne n'est pas en retard, il est **invisible**. Trois items ajoutés — W6.f ici, W10.7 et W10.8 côté xiiif.

## Ce que §19 refuse de laisser confondre

> « Une ressource distante modifiée après le run ne doit **jamais** faire croire que la preuve historique a changé. Le snapshot/hash reste la référence de reproduction ; la ressource live sert à constater l'évolution. »

Deux verdicts distincts, et **aucun accesseur qui les résumerait** : `proof_standing` parle de la preuve, `live_drift` n'en parle jamais.

Un « intégrité : divergente » unique laisserait croire que le résultat scientifique est en cause quand c'est la source qui a bougé — et, dans l'autre sens, tairait la divergence d'une source qu'on continuerait de citer. Le test les tient séparés sur les **quatre** combinaisons.

`Drift::Unknown` quand rien n'a été relevé au run : l'absence de relevé n'est pas l'absence de dérive, et répondre `Unchanged` ferait passer une ignorance pour un constat.

## Le motif de W6.b, répété là où il fallait

§19 nomme cinq locators et n'en autorise qu'un. Le schéma porte `maxProperties: 1` — **Rust ne sait pas l'exprimer**, donc le type engendré offre cinq champs facultatifs.

Un document à deux locators traverse le type engendré sans bruit, et l'exclusivité ne serait tenue que par le validateur JSON — c'est-à-dire **nulle part**, dès qu'un producteur construit la valeur en mémoire. `from_wire` est donc le lecteur validant qui refuse zéro locator comme il en refuse deux.

Sans lui, le test de sortie de cet item aurait été tenu par le schéma seul, et j'aurais reproduit exactement la faute que W6.b avait corrigée pour le manifeste.

## Le schéma vit sous `artifacts/1.0`, pas sous `lep/1.0`

Ce n'est pas un message du protocole d'exécution, c'est une référence qu'un viewer reçoit et relit. `lep/1.0` est **gelé**, et l'y ajouter aurait mêlé deux cycles de vie qui n'ont aucune raison d'avancer ensemble.

## Mutations

Dix, toutes vérifiées rouges, restauration confirmée verte, **aucune muette**.

| Mutation | Tests rouges |
|---|---|
| la preuve suit la ressource live | 3 |
| une dérive casse la preuve | 2 |
| l'absence de relevé devient une absence de dérive | 1 |
| la dérive ne se constate plus | 2 |
| deux locators passent | 1 |
| zéro locator passe | 1 |
| l'instantané local demande le réseau | 1 |
| un media type malformé passe | 1 |
| une identité vide passe | 1 |
| un locator vide passe | 1 |

## Périmètre

`schemas/artifacts/1.0/remote-artifact-ref.schema.json`, `packages/artifacts/src/remote_ref.rs` et `tests/remote_ref.rs`, neufs. Trois fixtures — une valide, deux intentionnellement invalides — et leur entrée au registre. SDK régénéré. `docs/10` gagne W6.f, W10.7 et W10.8.

**Écart avec la spec.** Un, nommé. `to_wire` n'existe pas : rien ne produit encore de `RemoteArtifactRef` côté locusolus — c'est l'ingestion d'artefacts qui le fera, quand un artefact portera un `viewer_hint: iiif`. Écrire la traduction sortante avant son producteur donnerait une fonction que seuls ses tests appellent.

**xiiif est débloqué.**

`npm run check` vert localement (les dix portes).

author: markiewee
body:
Dead-weight pass, evidence first. Every deletion was checked against something other than the import graph, because the graph does not know about a path stored in a database or a URL a crawler types. Two candidates were dropped for exactly that reason: `/llms.txt` and `/.well-known/ai-plugin.json` look unreferenced in code and are both live at 200.

## Two open doors

**`node_modules` was committed, as a symlink**, pointing at this repo's own absolute path on one machine. In the main checkout that is circular, which is what broke the build on 18 Aug 2026. In a fresh clone anywhere else it is a dangling link. It survived because `.gitignore` said `node_modules/` with a trailing slash, and a trailing slash matches a directory, not a symlink. Untracked, and the slash is gone so neither shape comes back.

**`/pitchv1/` served 200 to every crawler.** An investor deck titled "Institutional Housing Partnership", linked from nothing, absent from the sitemap, and deliberately carved out of the SPA rewrite so the URL keeps working. `robots.txt` invites 35 named crawlers including the AI ones, and none of them were told to leave it alone. Now disallowed and noindexed. The link still resolves for anyone we sent it to; it just stops being something a search engine can hand to a stranger. **Delete the two lines if it was meant to be found.**

## Deleted, and why it is safe

| What | Size | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `public/cms` | 30MB | Sanity-era images. Only `neighborhood` and `page` rows in `cms_content` point at them, and nothing queries either type. BlogPage and BlogPostPage use `blogPosts` and `blogPostBySlug`, which reference no local asset. |
| 42 of 114 `public/sketches` | 36MB | Hive articles name 72 by exact path in their markdown. The other 42 are named by no file in the repo, of any type, and by no row in the database. |
| `design-preview/photos` | 27MB | All 55 files are byte-identical to files already in `public/photos`. Pure duplication. |

`public/` drops from 179MB to 113MB, `design-preview` from 30MB to 2.4MB. Brand assets and the 30 HTML prototypes stay: they are the design record and they are small. The 14 prototypes that used the duplicated photos now point at `../public/photos`, and all 16 distinct paths resolve.

The 10 `cms_content` rows are left alone. Rows are cheap and dropping them is not reversible from here.

## Verified

- Full `npm run build` including prerender passes, 344 sitemap URLs
- Nothing in `dist` references `/cms/` or any deleted sketch
- Every sketch `dist` does reference is still on disk
- Lint byte-identical to master at 242 problems, all pre-existing and mostly `dist-ssr`, which `eslint.config.js` does not ignore

Dead code itself is a separate PR, so a revert here stays surgical.

body:
## Intent Stop an escalated decision from silently disappearing when a worker follows bin/fm-brief.sh rule 8 by appending needs-decision and then captain-held with the same key. First run and report the four-way matrix that independently varies the documented-equivalent before-colon and note-head key positions on both lines, settling which line controls closure before implementing a fix. Preserve the documented equivalence of both key positions. The OPEN DECISIONS fold is a pure text transform and cannot verify separate backlog state, so a captain-held parking line that a worker can write unilaterally must not close a decision when no durable backlog item exists; reconcile rule 8 with that fold contract. A worker following rule 8 verbatim, with or without a matching key on captain-held, must leave the decision visible in OPEN DECISIONS or durably held in the backlog, never neither. Add a red-first behavioral regression for the exact lost sequence needs-decision [key=x]: followed by captain-held [key=x]:, run it before the fix, and record the observed failure. Cover the real fleet-wide OPEN DECISIONS path and any persisted fold-cache migration needed by the semantic change. Run the full local suite and state which scripts ran. Herdr lifecycle behavior is not enabled and must not be added. Pipeline-authored risk rationales, fix summaries, and PR bodies must use role-neutral prose with no second person and no captain, user, firstmate, or crewmate role nouns; this constraint does not apply to product code, prompts, or user-facing copy. ## What Changed - Keep keyed decisions open until an explicit `resolved` event; `captain-held` now records parking without closing the status-fold entry, regardless of key position. - Rebuild version-4 incremental fold caches under the corrected semantics so previously hidden decisions reappear in fleet-wide OPEN DECISIONS output. - Align decision-hold bookkeeping, generated guidance, documentation, and regression coverage with the explicit-resolution contract. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change consistently makes explicit resolution the sole status-fold closure path, preserves both documented key positions across the four-way behavioral matrix, and invalidates persisted caches from the prior semantics. ## Testing No baseline commands were reported; focused automated tests exercised the exact lost sequence, both documented key positions, fleet-wide presentation, v4 fold-cache migration, durable hold lifecycle, snapshot rendering, watcher parking cadence, and rule-8 brief scaffolding, while a manual four-way CLI transcript demonstrated that all combinations remain visibly open. All checks passed; the full suite was intentionally left to the outer pipeline under this phase’s targeted-validation boundary.
Evidence: Four-way OPEN DECISIONS end-user transcript ```text CASE needs-decision=before-colon captain-held=before-colon STATUS LOG: needs-decision [key=x]: choose a release route captain-held [key=x]: parked at the review gate END-USER DRAIN OUTPUT: OPEN DECISIONS (still open, folded from the durable status logs - not just the latest line): task-held [key=x] needs-decision: choose a release route OPEN DECISIONS: close one by answering it: bin/fm-send.sh --resolve-key '' CASE needs-decision=before-colon captain-held=note-head STATUS LOG: needs-decision [key=x]: choose a release route captain-held: [key=x] parked at the review gate END-USER DRAIN OUTPUT: OPEN DECISIONS (still open, folded from the durable status logs - not just the latest line): task-held [key=x] needs-decision: choose a release route OPEN DECISIONS: close one by answering it: bin/fm-send.sh --resolve-key '' CASE needs-decision=note-head captain-held=before-colon STATUS LOG: needs-decision: [key=x] choose a release route captain-held [key=x]: parked at the review gate END-USER DRAIN OUTPUT: OPEN DECISIONS (still open, folded from the durable status logs - not just the latest line): task-held [key=x] needs-decision: choose a release route OPEN DECISIONS: close one by answering it: bin/fm-send.sh --resolve-key '' CASE needs-decision=note-head captain-held=note-head STATUS LOG: needs-decision: [key=x] choose a release route captain-held: [key=x] parked at the review gate END-USER DRAIN OUTPUT: OPEN DECISIONS (still open, folded from the durable status logs - not just the latest line): task-held [key=x] needs-decision: choose a release route OPEN DECISIONS: close one by answering it: bin/fm-send.sh --resolve-key '' ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

body:
## Final status

> **`gate0_stop_source_transport_blocked`**

The Hydrilla candidate stopped before any response, geometry, colonization, or extinction row was opened. It is not evidence for or against the post-Glanville label-invariant Layer-B predictor.

## Why this candidate was screened

Public study reporting established an unusually strong event-count profile before EOG response access:

- 506 randomly selected rock pools;
- five monitoring years, 2017–2021;
- more than 5,000 surveys;
- 147 pools with detections;
- 133 colonization events;
- 55 extinction events;
- 147 persistence events;
- repeat surveys and detection-aware dynamic occupancy modelling.

This passed the event-count feasibility screen added after Chiricahua. Aggregate counts were not used to tune worlds, Layer-B features, holdout, comparators, metrics, or decisions.

## Frozen source metadata

- Dryad DOI `10.5061/dryad.jsxksn0fn`
- publication DOI `10.1002/ece3.11558`
- resolved Dryad version ID `296642`
- all seven expected file names, sizes, SHA-256 digests and official file relations were available through public API metadata.

The complete 506-pool geometry still had to be frozen from exact source bytes before structural Gate 1.

## Transport result

### Official per-file route

Workflow `32093871518` reached the Dryad file endpoint and received HTTP `401 Unauthorized` before file bytes.

### Official full-dataset bundle route

The first bundle implementation stopped before source access because it assumed a numeric top-level version ID. Dryad supplies linked-version metadata; only that parser was corrected.

Authoritative workflow `32094591434` then reached the official bundle endpoint and received:

```json
{"error":"Unauthorized, must have current bearer token"}
```

- artifact ID `9309483998`
- artifact ZIP SHA-256 `4d8538aa01668fa7cf1079fd31e4f25b2a813f8da404a9d9164f52f3d74e402d`
- result fingerprint `8d39874422089f100a41f28838c0d34ebf990f996a3258d3ec2a73ad15709fbf`

## Response-firewall state

- response rows opened: **false**
- response values parsed: **false**
- geometry rows parsed: **false**
- EOG worlds constructed: **false**
- Layer-B prediction evaluated: **false**

## Scientific boundary

The candidate cannot proceed merely because its event count is attractive. Complete public geometry is a pre-response requirement. Two official Dryad download routes required authorization in the execution environment, so structural Gate 1 was never run.

Do not:

- use an authenticated private bearer token and call the result publicly reproducible;
- use browser-challenge workarounds or response-bearing mirrors;
- reconstruct geometry from response rows;
- replace full geometry with nearest-neighbour or river-distance summaries;
- revive this attempt as fresh independent confirmation.

Durable evidence is preserved in `validation/hydrilla_two_layer/`. The one-time workflow was removed. This PR closes unmerged so candidate-specific code does not expand production `main`.

author: datlechin
body:
Fixes the red `macOS Tests` gate on `main` ([run 32092492520](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/actions/runs/32092492520)).

## Root cause

The `Test Dameng native bridge` step added in #2114 loops over four cargo manifests with `--locked`:

```
error: cannot create the lock file .../Vendor/dameng-types/Cargo.lock
because --locked was passed to prevent this
```

Only the bridge lockfile is committed; `Native/DamengBridge/Vendor/*/Cargo.lock` was gitignored. The first iteration passed, the second exited 101, and the required `macOS Tests Gate` went down with it. Reproduced locally on a pristine tree.

## Fix

Make the vendored crates real workspace members, so the single committed lockfile covers all four and one command tests them.

- **`Native/DamengBridge/Cargo.toml`** — added `[workspace]` / `members = ["Vendor/*"]`. The glob tolerates the non-crate `Vendor/UPSTREAM.md` and picks up a future re-vendored crate automatically. `Cargo.lock` is **byte-identical** afterwards (`02bba5b9…` before and after), because lock format v4 records a path package the same way whether it is a member or a path dependency, and no vendored crate has real `[dev-dependencies]`. The MIT vendored manifests are untouched; the table lives in TablePro's own manifest.
- **`.github/workflows/macos-tests.yml`** — the loop becomes `cargo test --workspace --locked` with `working-directory: Native/DamengBridge`. The working directory is load-bearing: rustup resolves `rust-toolchain.toml` from the CWD, not from `--manifest-path`, so running from the repository root tested under the runner's default Rust instead of the pinned 1.91.1 that `scripts/build-dameng.sh` builds the shipped `.a` with. The preceding build step already installs that toolchain.
- **`.gitignore`** — removed the now-dead vendored-lock line.
- **`Plugins/DamengDriverPlugin/README.md`** — one command. The documented pair only ever covered 2 of the 4 crates.

## Related gap closed

`Native/` was in **neither** the `push: paths` list nor the `changes` job grep, so a pull request touching only the Rust bridge skipped every macOS suite — the Dameng build and test steps never ran for the code they exist to cover. Added to both, and the two filters were compared programmatically to confirm they stay symmetric.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --workspace --locked` from `Native/DamengBridge` | **201 passed** — dameng 32, dameng-protocol 134, dameng-types 33, bridge 2 (+1 ignored, needs a live DM8) |
| Toolchain | 1.91.1, matching `build-dameng.sh` |
| `Cargo.lock` after test and release build | unmodified |
| Stray `Vendor/*/Cargo.lock` | 0 |
| Release build + `nm -gU` | 19 `_tp_dm_*` symbols, `_tp_dm_connect` present |
| YAML parse, filter parity | OK, no asymmetry |

## Reviewer note

`cargo test --workspace` on a package with **no** `[workspace]` table exits 0 having run only that package's own tests — a lone package is its own single-member workspace, and there is no warning. Without the manifest change in this PR, the workflow change alone would report green while the 199 vendored tests never execute, which is worse than the current red. Worth confirming the per-crate `test result:` lines in the CI log rather than the step's exit status.

No changelog entry: CI and build configuration, not user-visible behavior (AGENTS.md).

The cross-vendor Codex review could not run — the plugin is not installed locally and the CLI reported the workspace is out of credits. Its threat list did drive the glob members and the toolchain pinning before it failed.

author: garfieldstoun
body:
## Summary

sqlx's strict struct-scan (no `Unsafe()` used anywhere in `internal/`) refuses to scan a column with no matching struct field. That means any `SELECT *` — bare or alias-qualified (`SELECT a.*`) — breaks every reader in that repository the instant an additive migration adds a column, until the binary redeploys. This was first found and fixed for `AgentRepo` in #578 (`agentSelectCols`); this PR applies the same fix to every other reader in the package.

- Rewrites **50 unsafe sites across 16 repository files** to explicit column lists: 43 bare `SELECT *` sites plus **7 alias-qualified `SELECT a.*`/`SELECT p.*` sites** found via a broader sweep (`grep "SELECT \*"` alone misses the qualified form).
- Leaves `agent_repo.go`'s 2 recursive-CTE `SELECT *` branches untouched — they're never themselves the scan target; only the CTE's outer `SELECT` is, and that's already explicit (#578).
- Fixes 3 sqlmock tests whose `ExpectQuery` regexes hardcoded the old query text and would otherwise break against the new column lists.
- Fix pattern: a package-level `const xSelectCols`/`xSelectColsQualified` string constant per row struct, referenced via compile-time string concatenation — same shape as the reviewed `agentSelectCols` precedent, to keep this mechanical PR low-risk.

## New tests

- `select_star_guard_test.go` — AST-walks every non-test `.go` file in the package and flags any `SELECT *`/`SELECT alias.*` outside a `WITH RECURSIVE ... AS (...)` CTE body. Mutation-verified in both directions via `t.TempDir()` fixtures against the real production scan function (red on a fresh unsafe star, red on a star outside a CTE's own parens, green on the legitimate CTE pattern and on explicit columns).
- `select_star_negative_control_db_test.go` — live-DB reproduction of the exact production failure, against a scratch table: struct-as-is + `SELECT *` → `nil` err; `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` + same query/struct → err contains `"missing destination name"`; explicit column list → `nil` err.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./internal/repository/... ./internal/service/...` green
- [x] `go test ./... -race` green (via `make ci`)
- [x] Live-DB negative control passes against a real Postgres
- [x] Guard test mutation-verified both directions, including a manual live check (temporarily reintroduced a real unsafe `SELECT *`, confirmed the guard goes red, reverted)
- [x] `make ci` (lint + test + build, incl. frontend) green

body:
## Summary

Stacked on #53. Adds optional `&self` receivers to `#[hooks]` entry points, cbak entries and in-impl helpers, so declared state/parameters are accessed as `self.<field>` — and adopts that as the canonical style across the examples and the book.

```rust
#[hooks]
impl Vault {
    #[hook(0, on = [Invoke])]
    fn deposit(&self) -> i64 {
        let Ok(cfg) = self.config.get_or_default() else { /* ... */ };
        // ...
    }
}
```

Design: [`docs/HOOKS_SELF_RECEIVER_DESIGN.md`](docs/HOOKS_SELF_RECEIVER_DESIGN.md) — investigated, measured, and reviewed before implementation.

## Measured: zero cost

Through the real build pipeline (discovery + selected build + clean/flatten/unnest/guard/validate):

- A macro-generated `&self` entry produces **byte-for-byte identical wasm** to the receiver-less form.
- `&self` on `#[inline(never)]` helpers is also byte-identical to the no-receiver control (the ZST reference vanishes entirely; no argument-spill cost survives).
- All migrated examples (02, 09, 12, 80_governance both hooks) rebuilt **byte-identical** — WCE, size and nesting unchanged.

## What changed

- **Macro** (`rshooks-macros`): receiver classifier accepting exactly two shapes — no receiver, or `&self`. `self` / `mut self` / `&'a self` / `self: T` and `&mut self` / `&'a mut self` get dedicated diagnostics; `#[cfg]`/`#[cfg_attr]` on a receiver is rejected (mirrors the entry-level cfg ban). Leading receiver attributes (e.g. `#[allow(unused)] &self`) are classified correctly. The export wrapper calls `Type::entry(&Type)` — the same expression works for named-field statics and unit-struct constructor values, so no additional static is generated.
- **Helpers** inside the annotated impl may take `&self` (previously rejected); `&mut self` stays rejected.
- **Canonical style**: entries that use declared fields take `&self` (`self.<field>`); declaration-less entries stay receiver-less; free functions outside the impl keep the same-named static, now documented as the outside-the-impl access path.
- **Fixtures**: receiver diagnostics catalog pinned by trybuild (7 fail cases incl. attributed and cfg'd receivers; extended pass coverage).
- Additive change: existing v0.2 code keeps compiling unchanged.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy` (`-D warnings`, root + examples/wasm32v1-none), `mise run build-examples` (16 artifacts + `rshooks check`), `mise run book:build` — all green.
- Reviewed by an independent cross-vendor pass (Codex / GPT-5.6, read-only); all six findings fixed in the final commit, including the one real gap (attributed receivers bypassing classification).

author: joaoh82
body:
**All three of M7.1's known items.** Every claim below was measured against real Modal, and two of them corrected the plan.

---

## (c) The live-worker cap — "one at a time" is behaviour now, not documentation

Nothing enforced it. `spawn_worker` counted nothing before launching, so a loop, a retry, or an orchestrator ignoring the skill **spent money rather than erroring**.

The mechanism is in the **store**, not `spawn_worker`, because it must be atomic — `create_worker(max_live=N)` counts and inserts inside one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. Counting in `provision` and inserting after would race, and two spawns starting together would both see room. A test asserts a refused spawn leaves **no row behind**.

Policy stays in `provision`: explicit arg → `$FLOTTA_MAX_CONCURRENT` → **default 1**; `0` means unlimited.

```console
$ uv run flotta spawn "cap demo B" --dry-run
refusing to spawn: 1 worker(s) already live and the limit is 1 (w-2ff351f10734)
Inspect with `flotta ps`, free a slot with `flotta kill <id>`, or raise the cap with…
exit=2
```

Exit **2**, not 1 — a script can tell "fleet busy" from "task failed".

Also collapsed real duplication: `TERMINAL` was declared in `store`, `provision` **and** `cli`, guarded only by a test asserting two of three matched.

## (a) Credentials move to a named Modal secret — spec corrected

The plan said "resolved at **call time**." Measured with a marker value:

| step | marker |
|---|---|
| deploy with `MARKER=before` | `before` |
| rotate, no redeploy | `before` ← warm container |
| redeploy, still warm | `before` |
| `app stop` + redeploy | **`after2`** |

It is **container start**. Rotation needs no code change and no redeploy — new containers pick it up — but a warm container serves the old value until it scales down. `modal app stop flotta-provision -y` forces it. The justfile, `.env.example` and code comments now say so; my first `secret-sync` message claimed "the next spawn uses it" and was wrong.

Nearly got this wrong twice: the first live run failed with `missing provider config` and I almost concluded `from_name` binds at deploy. A probe inside the same app disproved it — warm container again.

## (b) Stranded-worker reconciler — and results turn out to be recoverable

The open question was whether a stranded worker's answer is merely uncollected or **gone**, since that decides whether a reconciler can recover or only close. Measured: **a 9-hour-old call result was still retrievable.**

So `flotta reconcile` attempts recovery first. Verified end to end — spawned without `--wait`, backdated to look 3 hours stranded:

```console
$ uv run flotta reconcile
w-ad38977b47aa  done       recovered
1 reconciled, 1 with a recovered result

$ uv run flotta logs w-ad38977b47aa
timeline : spawned -> running -> completed
response : RECOVERED     api_calls: 1     reconciled: true
```

That's the agent's **actual answer** rescued from a worker that would otherwise have been closed as failed.

When the result can't be fetched, the row is marked `failed` with a reason — **never `completed`**. Inventing a success for unobserved work is exactly the lie D10's watcher design exists to prevent, and a test pins it.

**Deliberate deviation:** the plan said reconcile "on `flotta ps`". It's a separate command instead — `ps` is documented as a pure store read needing no Modal credentials, and auto-reconciling would make the cheapest command in the CLI write to the store and require cloud auth.

---

212 tests (180 → 212), ruff clean. `just e2e` 21/21, `just e2e-live` 22/22.

author: peterfriedrich
body:
The Development view's 100 m grid now carries the **Industrial** metric, which
was choropleth-only because `dev_grid.json` held no industrial cells.

## Measured before building, and the measurements changed the design

**Permit count does not form a surface at 100 m.** 89% of 5yr industrial cells
hold exactly one permit; the tallest holds ten.

**A bigger cell does not fix it** — 100 m → 400 m is a **16× area increase that
removes 19 of 184 cells** (singletons 89% → 78%); even 800 m leaves 145 cells and
75% singletons. Industrial permits aren't clustered at the sub-kilometre scale,
so merging cells merges nothing. The dollar spread is near-invariant to cell size
(281× at 100 m, 292× at 400 m), which is what proves the differentiation comes
from permit *size*. So the 100 m cell stays, and keeps its shared geometry with
the Glass grid.

**Declared construction value carries the pattern**: 723 distinct heights across
835 long-window cells, vs ~10 levels under count.

## Two honesty problems came with the dollars

**They were nominal.** Summing 2009–2025 encodes construction-cost inflation as
development — an identical building permitted in 2009 drew a spike **1.72×
shorter** than a 2025 one. Now deflated to constant 2025 dollars from StatCan
18-10-0289 (Edmonton / Industrial buildings), pinned in
`data/construction_price_index.json` as a manual reviewed input, off the weekly
refresh. A permit year with no deflator hard-fails rather than passing at
nominal. ⚠️ Both predecessor tables are **archived** (they stop in 2022 and
2024) and still answer queries, so a stale pin fails silently — the fetcher
checks `archiveStatusEn`.

**They can be $0.** 12 of 1,281 industrial permits declare exactly $0, which on a
dollar-driven height is a permitted building that vanishes. Cells are kept on the
permit count and floored to 6 m. The floor is small deliberately: a first attempt
at 60 m lifted **64–78% of cells**, including projects worth up to **$4.6M**, to
the same height as $0. Residential never needed a floor because dwelling units
are quantised (0% of its cells render under 5 m) while dollars are continuous to
zero (39–44% of industrial cells).

The dollars are a **declared estimate at permit application** — not audited
spend, land excluded — and the blurb says so, reading the basis and deflator from
the file so the disclosure can't drift from the data.

## Verification

- `pytest` 661 passed (7 new tests: deflation arithmetic, $0 retention, missing
  deflator, missing/rebased index, industrial-absent degradation)
- `verify-ind-permits.js` ALL PASS (11 new grid checks)
- `verify-development.js` 70/70 — **residential cells are byte-identical**
- doc-citation guard OK, `build_site.py` OK

## One thing left open, deliberately

`DECISIONS.md` 2026-07-23 tagged Industrial `/full/`-only for exactly one
reason: it was choropleth-only and would leave the Detail selector with dead
options. That reason no longer holds. **Nothing was changed** — the question is
open at the top of `TODO.md` rather than settled quietly either way.

author: christianspliid-ui
body:
`baseDetectionDeltaForCost` returned the `CHOICE_ESSENCE_COST_*` constants — `1 / 2 / 3` — into a quantity clamped to `[0, MAX_DETECTION_PRESSURE = 1]`. A whole-unit resource spend added to a normalised fraction. The **smallest write the system could make** (`small_breath 1 × 0.8` primary-sphere visibility) was `0.8`, clearing `NOTICE 0.5` **and** `TURN 0.8` together; at `1.0` or `1.2` it cleared `ENCOUNTER` too and seeded a `shadow.rival_strike` on the spot. "Rivals notice → rivals turn → rivals move against you" was unreachable by construction.

## What changed

**The two quantities are separated, not divided.** New `DETECTION_DELTA_SMALL / FULLER / DEEP` = `0.15 / 0.30 / 0.50`, genuine fractions on the pressure scale, sized against the three thresholds and the only sphere-visibility multipliers the phase emits (`0.8 / 1.0 / 1.2`). A divisor constant would have been arithmetically equivalent and left the next reader finding pressure priced by an essence constant — which is the shape that produced the bug.

**The ladder now arrives band by band.** At neutral visibility from a quiet region: fuller breaths reach *notice* on the 2nd choice, *turn* on the 3rd, *encounter* on the 4th; small breaths take 4 / 6 / 7; a deep draught is deliberately loud — noticed at one, saturated at two. Pinned with **literals**, not the constants the code reads: that test would have passed just as happily on `1 / 2 / 3`.

**The second Done-when is pinned as a property, not an example.** A single `small_breath` from every start `0.00…1.00` across all three multipliers crosses at most one band — it holds because `0.15 × 1.2 = 0.18` stays under the 0.2-wide turn→encounter gap.

**Falsified for real:** putting `1 / 2 / 3` back fails six tests, the ladder among them.

**Three suites had encoded the defect as an expectation** and were corrected rather than widened — `phaseDetectionPressure.test.ts` asserted that one `small_breath` emits an `encounter` trace, and contract `4.3` seeded a rival strike from a single `deep_draught`. A new phase test pins that one small breath now emits **no** threshold trace at all.

**Still latent either way.** `pendingChoiceCommits` has no live producer, so `regionalDetectionPressure` is `[]` after 120 ticks on seed 42. What changed is that the ladder is correct whenever a producer is wired.

## Beyond the ticket

`check:wiki-freshness:blocking` went green while `stealth-rivals-reference.html` — whose blurb leads with region detection pressure — carried three passages this change falsified, one an accuracy note reading *"verified against code this pass — do not 'correct' back"* that would have sent the next reader to restore the wrong numbers. Its `sources` globs covered the dormant per-actor stealth model and the rivals, never the two modules implementing its headline system, and both live one directory deeper than the neighbouring page's `src/engine/encounter*.ts` glob reaches. Page updated; both modules added to its `sources` so the next detection-pressure change trips the gate normally. Logged as impediment #661, with #662 for a CRLF/line-ending trap hit during closeout.

## Verification

```
npm test                      -> 1032 files / 16780 tests passed
npm run check:typecheck       -> OK, 3160 errors, unchanged from baseline
npx vite build                -> built in 9.72s
engine smoke (seed 42 medium) -> tick 30, 384 agents, 46 events, no throws
check:generated-freshness     -> OK, 34 artifacts match HEAD
check:wiki-freshness:blocking -> OK, 24 pages, no stale
check:impediment-ids          -> OK, 662 rows, every # unique
```

No browser-verify owed: the diff touches `src/data/`, `src/engine/`, `public/` and tests — none of them UI-pillar trigger paths.

Fixes THR-963

body:
## What

Adds sort/ordering **drag & drop** to the post composer's Media & Files panel — when **creating** posts/comments (and Messenger messages) and when **editing** posts — as requested. Every tile and file row with 2+ items in its section gets a ⠿ grip: drag it (pointer events, so mouse AND touch work), or focus it and use Arrow keys / Home / End. The hovered drop position shows an accent outline; the move commits on release.

## How order persists (end-to-end)

- **Create**: the composer's upload order (as reordered) IS the attachmentIds order sent to the server. The bind hook now stamps attachmentSortIndex on each bound attachment thing per its list position (order lives on the relational child docs, per FUNDAMENTALS §3 — the post never stores an id list).
- **Edit**: the edit composer previously rendered a dead-end upload panel (uploads there were silently dropped — things.update never bound them) and hid existing attachments entirely. It now shows the post's existing attachments as a reorderable gallery instead; Save sends the ordered ids only when the order changed.
- **Server**: PATCH /api/v1/things { id, attachmentIds } re-stamps a bound set. It must be a *pure permutation* of the currently bound ids (verified against live state; additions/removals 409). Same gates as attachment creation: full user session, same-origin, JSON. Runs before updateThing so the response projection already carries the new order; idempotent, so a failed crystal write + retry converges (observed live — see Verification).
- **Read**: resolvePostAttachments (posts/comments) and Messenger's message-attachment resolve sort stamped docs by attachmentSortIndex, with legacy unstamped docs keeping their createdAt order after stamped ones.

## Follow-up fixes surfaced by the preview E2E

- c5ef265: attachment-only posts had a dead Save in edit mode — contentValid now counts the post's existing bound attachments (the upload snapshot is empty in edit mode).
- bbab057: updateThing validated post crystals without the postAttachments context creates get, so every edit of an attachment-only post 400'd with the say-something rule. It now resolves live bound-attachment presence (server-authored state, as trusted as create-time inspection); covers PUT via upsertThing's delegation.

## Notes

- MediaGalleryTile grew optional dragging/dropTarget/containerProps; the shared gesture logic is one hook (useMediaReorder) used by both the upload composer and the new edit gallery. Grips keep React.memo effective (stable callbacks + primitives).
- Reordering is per-section (media grid / file list), matching how PostAttachments renders them grouped; cross-section drags are inert.
- matchesCommittedPostCreate + addComment reconciliation compare attachment sets unordered, so ambiguous-create recovery is unaffected.
- Custom emoji picker (maxFiles=1) shows no grips; profile avatar/banner slots untouched. Adding/removing attachments during edit stays out of scope (binding is create-only today); the gallery says so honestly.

## Verification

- npm run test:unit passes (106 attachment-family tests incl. new orderAttachmentDocsByStoredSort, planAttachmentReorder, PATCH-reorder postAttachmentRequest cases); lint:files clean; Web CI + API suite green.
- Local dev (real mouse + keyboard): grip drags both directions, ArrowLeft/Right + Home/End with focus following the moved tile, file-row drag with drop outline, cross-section drags inert, desktop + 375px mobile with no horizontal overflow.
- **Vercel preview E2E (real S3 + DB, throwaway account dragdrop-e2e-0818, private post)**: uploaded 3 images + 2 files, dragged to [bravo, charlie, alpha] + [doc-two, doc-one], posted → order persisted after full reload. Edited: gallery rendered saved order, dragged to [charlie, alpha, bravo] + [doc-two, doc-one], Save → 'Post updated', card + reload + /post/:id permalink all render the new order. The intermediate failed-save attempt also proved the reorder-first PATCH semantics: order stamped, crystal 400 surfaced, retry converged.
- TESTING.md gained two permanent checklist items covering both flows.

author: chethan123
body:
## Summary

This PR implements the Settings section of the application, enabling users to manage household members and their financial accounts. It includes the complete backend logic for people and accounts management, along with the UI routes and components to create, edit, and close accounts.

## Key Changes

**Core Domain Logic**
- Added `people.server.ts`: Manages household members with create, list, rename, and remove operations. Prevents removal of people who own accounts.
- Added `accounts.server.ts`: Manages financial accounts with create, list, get, update, and close operations. Accounts are never deleted, only closed with a timestamp.
- Added `account-options.ts`: Centralized definitions of account kinds and tax treatments used by both validation and UI rendering.
- Added `input.server.ts`: Shared validation error handling and input parsing utilities using Zod schemas.
- Added `first-run.server.ts`: Determines setup progress (People → Accounts) for fresh installations.
- Added `forwarded.server.ts`: Handles `X-Forwarded-*` headers for reverse proxy deployments to correctly determine request scheme and client address.

**Routes & UI**
- Added `/settings` layout with tab navigation for People and Accounts sections
- Added `/settings/people`: List, create, rename, and remove household members
- Added `/settings/accounts`: List accounts and create new ones
- Added `/settings/account/:id`: Edit account details or close an account
- Added `AccountFields` component: Shared form fields for account creation/editing
- Added `FirstRunPrompt` component: Guides new installations through initial setup
- Added `EmptyState` component: Displays empty dashboards without showing zero figures

**Styling**
- Extended `app.css` with comprehensive styling for settings UI including:
  - Tab navigation and active states
  - Form panels and input validation states
  - Record lists and tables
  - Danger zones for destructive actions
  - First-run and empty state messaging

**Testing**
- Added comprehensive test suites for people and accounts management
- Added tests for reverse proxy header handling
- Added tests for first-run prompt rendering
- Tests verify business rules are enforced (e.g., cannot remove person with accounts)

**Documentation**
- Added `docs/operating.md`: Comprehensive guide for self-hosters covering reverse proxy setup, TLS termination, backups, environment variables, and phone installation.

## Notable Implementation Details

- **No soft deletes**: Accounts are closed (timestamped) rather than deleted, preserving historical valuation data
- **Validation at domain layer**: All business rules live in `*.server.ts` modules, not routes, ensuring consistency across callers
- **Proxy trust model**: The app unconditionally trusts `X-Forwarded-*` headers; deployment must ensure the app port is not directly exposed
- **First-run ordering**: People must be created before accounts since accounts require an owner
- **Shared validation**: Account kinds and tax treatments are defined once and used by both validation and UI

author: cet-blaster[bot]
body:
## What

A quality profile carried a `platform_slug`, and a unique index allowed exactly one profile per platform. Two things had nowhere to live in that model:

- **"I want the Japanese revision of this one game."** The platform's profile is the only profile, so per-title intent could not be expressed at all.
- **A platform nobody has set up yet.** Before a title on a new platform could be acquired sensibly, someone had to go make a profile for it first.

Three moving parts now, each where it belongs:

| Question | Where the answer lives |
|---|---|
| What policy applies to *this title*? | `wishlist.profile_id` — 0 means "the platform's default" |
| What does *this platform* default to? | `platforms.default_profile_id` on the registry row |
| What does a *brand-new* platform default to? | a **template**, cloned on first add |

Resolution is one function and never returns nil: the title's own profile → the platform's default → the legacy `platform_slug` column → the global default row → the lowest-id global row → the built-in. The legacy step is a migration courtesy; nothing writes that column any more.

## Templates and lazy materialization

Two profiles ship flagged `is_template` — **Carts Default** and **Discs Default**. Ordinary profile rows, editable, never used directly. The first title added on a platform with no default clones the template matching that platform's class, names it `<Platform> Default`, attaches it to the platform row, and reports it once in the add response so the operator learns a profile now exists rather than being asked to create one.

**The class comes from the platform's DAT authority** where it has a lane (No-Intro → carts, Redump → discs) — the assignment the catalog already makes, not a second opinion about what a platform is. The registry's `media_class` covers laneless platforms; carts is the conservative last resort.

Editing a template retunes what *future* platforms inherit and does not touch profiles already materialized from it.

## The archive.org region drop yields to the profile

The driver dropped obviously non-English dumps before the selector ever saw them, so a profile ranking `japan` could not see a Japanese dump **at all**. Under collection mode that is not a missed grab — it is a gap that can never fill, and it reads as a short catalog rather than as a filter.

The profile's region priority is now passed to the search fan-out (`search.Opts`), and the rule the driver follows: it may skip work the caller will clearly reject, but it must never drop a region the caller asked for. English-only interest still drops it; the filter yields to a stated interest rather than disappearing.

## Two smaller things that belong with it

- **The scheduler resolves once per item, not twice per platform.** The same profile now drives both the sources' region policy and the tier sort. It used to be resolved in the closure and again in the selector, from the platform only, so neither could see a title's own intent.
- **The per-platform acquisition switch gets its consumer in the same change that ships it.** A platform with acquisition off is not searched; its wishlist rows survive so flipping it back resumes rather than having silently discarded them; the skip is logged, because "nothing happened for this title" has to be traceable to the switch that caused it. A toggle nothing reads is worse than no toggle.

## Migration

`idx_qp_platform` is dropped — one profile per platform is exactly the constraint this removes; "PSX CHD" and "PSX raw" are both legitimate. Each legacy mapping moves onto the platform row once, guarded by a settings key rather than by "no platform has a default yet", so an operator who clears a default deliberately does not get it back on the next restart. `wishlist.profile_id` is added by ALTER, since `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op on an existing install.

## API

- `POST /api/wishlist` accepts `profile_id`, validates it, and returns `materialized_profile` when the add created a platform default.
- `PATCH /api/wishlist/{id}` changes or clears (0) the override.
- `GET /api/quality-profiles/{id}` — the editor used to hydrate from the list query's cache, so a deep link or a refresh had nothing to show. Returns the platforms defaulting to it.
- `DELETE /api/quality-profiles/{id}` refuses with **409** when a platform defaults to it, naming what would be orphaned.
- A template cannot be chosen for a title (400) — picking one would couple that title to every future platform's defaults.

## Testing

- **Replayed against production's own rows, not only a fixture shaped like them.** Its ten profiles and forty platform rows were loaded into a temp DB and run through the migration offline: every platform resolves to the profile it resolved to before, no user-facing profile added/removed/renamed, the index gone, a cleared default not resurrected on restart. 12/12.
- A computed unit test does the same for every platform in the registry, deriving the expectation from the fixture's own data rather than restating it.
- Materialization: silent, idempotent, class-correct (gbc inherits carts formats, saturn inherits CHD-first).
- `#274`: the fixture's Japan-only Gran Turismo is invisible to a profile with no stated region interest, visible to one ranking `japan`, and still invisible to an English-only profile.
- Acquisition off: the platform is not searched, the other one still is, and the rows survive.
- `gofmt`, `go vet`, `staticcheck`, `go test ./...`, frontend `typecheck` + `vitest` clean locally.

Docs: `docs/profiles.md`.

body:
## Summary
**Issue:** [LIFT-1149](https://github.com/aschung212/Lift/issues/1149)

Fix LIFT-1149: the sync indicator (App.vue) was an icon-only `role="status"` span whose human-readable label lived only in a `:title` tooltip — VoiceOver doesn't reliably surface `:title`, and a live region wrapping no text node announces nothing. So screen-reader users got no notice when the app dropped offline or a sync failed (WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 status messages; SC 1.1.1 icon lacks a text name). Move the label into an sr-only live region and give the icon a real accessible name.

## Changes
- `src/App.vue`:
  - The icon-only sync indicator span now carries `role="img"` + `:aria-label="syncStatusLabel"` so it has a text accessible name, instead of relying on `:title` alone (SC 1.1.1). `:title` retained for the mouse tooltip.
  - Added a persistent polite `srOnly` live region (`{{ syncAnnouncement }}`) mirroring the existing `viewAnnouncement` pattern, so status changes announce reliably even across offline→error transitions (SC 4.1.3).
  - Added a `watch(syncStatus, …)`: announces offline/error via the shared `syncStatusLabel`, announces "Back online — changes synced" only when recovering from offline/error, and deliberately skips transient `syncing` to avoid per-batch noise. Not `immediate`, so an at-load offline state isn't spuriously announced.
- `src/lib/__tests__/syncAnnouncementRegression.test.ts`: new source regression pinning the accessible name, the persistent live region, the state ref, and the announcement logic.

author: rohitjindal1184
body:
## Summary
Adds a small preview control to the homepage (top-right of the hero, desktop-only) that lets you pick one of the 4 hero scroll variants from a dropdown. Selecting one navigates to `?hero=<variant>` and does a full page reload, so it renders exactly like a real visit with that variant active — no more editing `.env.local` and restarting the dev server to compare them.

**Important tradeoff:** this requires reading `searchParams` in the homepage, which is a Next.js "Dynamic API" — it opts the homepage into dynamic (per-request) rendering instead of static generation. There's no way around that for a true per-request override. This is fine for now while you're actively comparing variants, but worth revisiting before final launch if static generation / ISR matters for the homepage by then (options at that point: gate the switcher behind an env flag so production stays static, or remove it once you've picked a winner).

## What changed
- `src/lib/experiments.ts` — exports `isHeroVariant()` so the query param is validated the same way the env var already is.
- `src/app/page.tsx` — now an async Server Component that reads `?hero=`, validates it, passes it to `<Hero variant={...} />` (falls back to the `NEXT_PUBLIC_HERO_VARIANT` build default when absent/invalid).
- `src/components/hero/Hero.tsx` — accepts an optional `variant` prop overriding the default for that request.
- `src/components/hero/HeroVariantSwitcher.tsx` — the picker. Desktop-only (`lg:`) so it never shows to mobile visitors or competes with the mobile CTA bar; uses a full `window.location` navigation rather than client-side routing.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint`, and the impeccable design detector all clean
- [x] Verified in browser: switcher renders correctly, selecting a variant updates the URL and reloads with that variant showing (tested `pinned-curtain` → `stats-rise`), no console errors

author: zehuili1
body:
## Why

PuttTrack needs to lock the real player experience before the full hardware/software architecture is frozen. Public Puttshack material shows that the strongest part of the experience is the full loop: assigned smart ball -> automatic player recognition -> clear ready cue -> hole-local screen guidance -> automatic strokes / bonus / hazard scoring -> live leaderboard -> digital result.

PuttTrack preserves that frictionless loop while deliberately improving guest onboarding, recovery UX, non-blocking feedback, 18-hole continuity, scoring auditability and architecture independence from a specific sensing technology.

## This PR implements

- Deterministic, sensor-agnostic `GameplayEngine`.
- Flexible player order within a group.
- One active player/ball on a standard hole at a time.
- `tee.presented`, `tee.cancelled`, `stroke.confirmed`, `feature.confirmed`, `cup.confirmed`, `pickup.detected`, and audited `operator.adjustment` event contracts.
- Idempotent event handling to prevent duplicate score mutations.
- Configurable per-hole completion score curves and bonus/hazard/route features.
- Normal final-hole completion rather than a hidden one-shot terminator.
- Ranking with skill/strokes/hazards ahead of speed in tie-break logic.
- UI-safe presentation snapshots and evidence snapshots.
- End-to-end simulator.
- Unit tests covering flexible order, duplicate events, feature trigger limits, lane exclusivity, unknown balls and final-hole completion.
- `docs/PRODUCT_LOGIC_LOCK.md`: locked player/product behavior and authority boundaries.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW_BRIEF.md`: the handoff for the next full end-to-end architecture pass.
- README integration and explicit separation between locked product logic and still-open engineering topology.

## Locked experience

`docs/PRODUCT_LOGIC_LOCK.md` is now the product-behavior source of truth. Key constraints include guest-first check-in, assigned smart balls, flexible player order, DETECTED -> READY feedback, touch-free play during a hole, automatic scoring, conservative scoring evidence, non-blocking feedback, normal final-hole completion, audited correction and local operation during WAN loss.

## Architecture boundary

The Gameplay Engine consumes **confirmed semantic evidence** and does not know whether evidence came from Bluetooth Channel Sounding, IMU, optical sensors, cup sensors, cameras, UWB, or a future implementation.

The next architecture pass is explicitly allowed to challenge the current anchor count, gateway topology, backhaul, compute placement, service boundaries, storage, OTA and custom-ball design while preserving the locked product behavior.

## Next architecture step

Use `docs/ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW_BRIEF.md` to perform an independent end-to-end architecture review before production topology is frozen.

## Implementation follow-up after architecture review

- course/rule configuration loader;
- session/check-in + server-side ball assignment;
- sensor-fusion -> gameplay evidence adapter;
- tee-screen presentation prototype;
- operator correction/audit persistence;
- 18-hole pacing/congestion simulator.

body:
## Summary

The raw `monitor_historical` table dominates database file size, and rows older than `dataset.retention_days` were never deleted. This PR enforces the existing retention policy online and adds a one-time offline compaction path to shrink the on-disk file.

## Changes

- **`CleanupWorker`** (`worker_cleanup.go`): scheduled worker that runs one pass at startup and then every `dataset.cleanup_interval_minutes`:
  - Deletes expired `monitor_historical` rows one UTC day at a time, chunked by the new `dataset.cleanup_batch_size` so no statement removes unbounded rows.
  - Prunes derived daily/region aggregate rows older than the cutoff (they cannot be recalculated once raw rows are gone).
  - Runs `CHECKPOINT` (with a bounded retry for transient concurrent write transactions) to reclaim free blocks inside the file.
  - Emits `eyrie.database.size.*` gauges and `eyrie.cleanup.*` run/deletion/duration metrics via Sentry; errors are reported as exceptions and counted as `status=error`. A cancelled context (shutdown) stops a pass early without error status.
- **Config** (`config_server.go`): new optional `dataset.cleanup_interval_minutes` (default 60) and `dataset.cleanup_batch_size` (default 100000), validated to be positive.
- **Wiring** (`main.go`): cleanup worker started alongside existing workers, stopped before the database closes.
- **Compaction script** (`scripts/compact_duckdb.sh`): offline `COPY FROM DATABASE` compaction via the DuckDB CLI; copies source read-only to a fresh file (default `<source>.compacted`), prints both file sizes, and leaves the swap to the operator. Does not modify the source.
- **Example config**: new keys documented in `server.example.yaml`.
- **Tests** (`worker_cleanup_test.go`): retention-boundary deletion, aggregate pruning, no-op on no expired rows, prompt `Stop` without goroutine leaks.

## Verification

- `go test ./...` passes.
- Live server behavior test: with a 3-day retention and 1-minute interval, submitted check results with mixed ages; after one tick only rows within retention remained (raw + both aggregate tables), `CHECKPOINT` executed, and run logs/metrics were emitted.
- Compaction script tested against a copy of the production database in a safe location; the compacted copy was substantially smaller and the server started successfully against it (SPA and API endpoints served).

author: p0mvn
body:
## Motivation

Zakura should consume the proving-stack forks from [`zakura-core/libraries`](https://github.com/zakura-core/libraries) as git dependencies with the zakura-branded package names. `[patch.crates-io]` cannot replace crates.io `orchard` / `halo2_proofs` / … after [libraries#61](https://github.com/zakura-core/libraries/pull/61) renamed those packages, so every direct edge has to name `zakura-*` explicitly. That keeps the crates.io originals out of the graph.

## Solution

- Point `orchard`, `sapling-crypto`, `halo2`, `reddsa`, `redjubjub`, `sinsemilla`, `zcash_keys`, `zcash_primitives`, and `zcash_proofs` at `zakura-core/libraries` git rev [`3042ed06`](https://github.com/zakura-core/libraries/commit/3042ed06d758147360c2d38bb3e258491fcf379b) (`main` tip: *Add reproducible Orchard benchmark harnesses*, #77).
- Keep dependency keys and `use` paths unchanged (`package = "zakura-orchard"`, lib name still `orchard`, etc.).
- Bump the `zcash_protocol` workspace requirement to `0.10.2` so it unifies with `zakura-keys` (`^0.10.2`; lockfile resolves `0.10.4`).
- Allow that git source in `deny.toml` and mark the unpublished `zakura-*` crates `audit-as-crates-io = false` for cargo-vet.

## Testing

- `cargo check --workspace --locked --all-targets`
- `cargo deny --workspace check sources --allow unmatched-skip-root`
- `cargo deny --workspace check bans --allow unmatched-skip-root`
- `cargo vet check --store-path ./qa/supply-chain/`
- `./scripts/changelog.py check`

## Changelog

`docs/changelog/unreleased/714.md` records the operator-visible proving-stack source change.

### Specifications & References

- https://github.com/zakura-core/libraries
- https://github.com/zakura-core/libraries/pull/61
- https://github.com/zakura-core/libraries/commit/3042ed06d758147360c2d38bb3e258491fcf379b

### Follow-up Work

- crates.io publishing of these forks is not done yet (names are `0.0.0` reservations owned by ebfull). Until `1.0.0-rc.1` is on crates.io, this PR uses git deps and will fail `check-no-git-dependencies` / crate packaging on an `A-release` PR.
- Downstream apps that still `[patch.crates-io]` the old names (Vizor, `zcash_voting`) cannot use this rename as a drop-in patch.

author: silvareal
body:
Merges 13 staging-only commits into `main` so release-please can cut **0.6.0**
(three `feat:` commits + `bump-minor-pre-major` ⇒ minor, not patch).

## Why now

The staging CDN has been serving an **Aug 15** build of `iqcollect.js` since
Aug 16. Objects were uploaded with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000,
immutable` on *both* targets. Production is written once so that is correct
there — but staging is republished at the same version, and an immutable edge
entry never revalidates. The CDN workflow verifies by re-reading the **origin**,
so every run passed while the edge stayed frozen.

Confirmed before this branch:

| | last-modified | sha384 |
|---|---|---|
| origin | Sun 16 Aug 23:45:37 GMT | `Q7LZd2vji9K0ulAu866yw…` |
| edge   | Sat 15 Aug 08:03:08 GMT | `wUErWmll1WWgesjXvSN93…` |

The RN SDK's staging pin equals the **edge** hash, so SRI passed and the SDK
silently ran the older widget with no error anywhere.

## What's here

- `fix(cdn)` — `immutable` scoped to production; staging gets
  `max-age=60, must-revalidate`. Prevents this recurring. It cannot rescue the
  already-poisoned `v0.5.3` edge entry, which is why 0.6.0 (a fresh prefix) is
  the actual fix.
- `feat(fanout)` — staging SRI pin computed in its own `environment: staging`
  job, since staging and prod bake different Maps keys and so hash differently.
  RN moves to CDN-only per-deployment pin files.
- Collect UX: searchable country/state comboboxes, back navigation, shorter
  consent copy, accurate terminal screen.
- `feat(sdk)` — verification gated to the native host; web stays collect-only.

## After merging the release PR

`main` must be merged back into `staging`, or the staging CDN never publishes
`/v0.6.0/`. The fanout writes `v0.6.0` into the staging pin, but `cdn.yml` only
publishes staging on a branch push — until that lands the RN staging pin points
at a version the staging CDN does not serve, and with the vendored bundle gone
(8409579d) that fails closed rather than falling back.

author: madhanalagarsamy
body:
Fixes #23453 by updating the PyTorch Multi-GPU distributed training guide (`guides/distributed_training_with_torch.py`):

1. **Multiprocessing Start Method (`spawn` vs `fork`)**:
   Changed `start_method` in `torch.multiprocessing.start_processes` from `"fork"` to `"spawn"`. Initializing CUDA contexts prior to forking leads to process deadlocks; using `"spawn"` ensures clean child process initialization.

2. **Target Dtype (`int64`)**:
   Explicitly cast `y_train` and `y_test` targets to `int64` (`LongTensor`) to satisfy PyTorch `nn.CrossEntropyLoss()` requirements.

3. **DistributedSampler Epoch Sync**:
   Added `sampler.set_epoch(epoch)` call at the beginning of each epoch iteration so dataset shuffling changes across epochs.

4. **Rank 0 Logging & Zero-GPU Guard**:
   Scoped loss printing to `current_gpu_index == 0` and added a validation check when `num_gpu < 1`.

- [x] I am a human, and not a bot.
- [x] I will be responsible for responding to review comments in a timely manner.
- [x] I will work with the maintainers to push this PR forward until submission.

author: bata-san
body:
Adds `tools/thinkserve-switch`, a small MIT-licensed Windows tray controller for using a workstation as a llama.cpp inference server while retaining a fast way to prioritize local work.

Modes:
- `SERVER`: llama-server running + Tailscale Serve enabled
- `LOCAL PRIORITY`: remote Serve disabled, model kept loaded for fast recovery
- `FREE GPU`: remote Serve disabled and llama-server stopped to release VRAM

Other behavior:
- binds llama-server to `127.0.0.1` only
- waits for llama.cpp `/health` before exposing the server
- settings dialog for model/server/Tailscale paths, context size, GPU layers and idle sleep
- GPU usage shown in the tray via `nvidia-smi`
- optional startup shortcut
- runtime/log files ignored

Tailscale integration is intended only for environments where its use is permitted by the network/organization policy.

This is intentionally self-contained under `tools/thinkserve-switch/` so it does not alter the Rust workspace.

author: rahatsheikhleon
body:
## Summary

The tagged-release workflow could not run: `actions/checkout@v2` and `actions/setup-node@v2` execute on GitHub's removed Node12/16 runtimes, and Node 20 leaves the runners on **Sept 16, 2026**. This pins everything to node24-runtime actions, moves the build to Node 22, and makes installs reproducible. Also ships **1.4.0**.

No application behavior changes. The `@wordpress/*` / React / Babel modernization is deliberately **not** included.

## Changes

**GitHub Actions**
- `actions/checkout@v2` → `@v5`, `actions/setup-node@v2` → `@v5` (both `using: node24`)
- `assets.yml`: `actions/checkout@master` → `@v5`
- `10up/action-wordpress-plugin-deploy@stable` → `@2.3.0`; `...-asset-update@stable` → `@2.2.0`
- `node-version: '14'` (EOL Apr 2023) → `'22'`, with npm caching
- `npm install` → `npm ci`

**Reproducible installs**
- Un-ignored and committed `package-lock.json`; added `.nvmrc`

**Dependencies**
- Removed `react-masonry-component` — verified unused (no import in `src/`, `config/`, or the built bundles; masonry runs via vendored Isotope)
- Kept `array-move` and `react-sortable-hoc` — both still used by `src/sortable-filteritems.js`

**i18n**
- `block.json` and the plugin header declare `image-gallery-block`, but all 90 translator strings passed `essential-blocks`, so none could resolve. Now consistent.

**Build artifacts**
- Removed `dist/**/*.* export-ignore` from `.gitattributes` — it would strip the compiled bundle from a `git archive` export
- Deleted `Gruntfile.js` (grunt was never in `package.json`, `makepot` pointed at a nonexistent `eb.php`, build uses wp-scripts)
- Deleted stale `build/` output

**Release 1.4.0**
- Version synced across plugin header, constant, `Stable tag`, `package.json`
- wp.org serves 1.3.4 and 1.5.0 was never published, so this is still a forward release
- `Tested up to: 7.0.4`

## Test plan

Verified on Node 22.23.2 / npm 10.9.8:

- [x] `npm ci` → exit 0 (root, from wiped `node_modules`)
- [x] `npm run build` → exit 0, webpack 5.109.2 compiled successfully
- [x] `npm ci` → exit 0 (`controls/`)
- [x] `npm run build` → exit 0 (`controls/`, warnings are bundle-size only)
- [x] Both workflow YAML files parse; pins and `node-version` confirmed
- [x] `php -l` clean across `image-gallery-block.php` and `includes/*.php`
- [x] All 14 enqueued asset paths resolve on disk
- [x] Replayed 10up's `rsync --exclude-from=.distignore --delete --delete-excluded` → 1.3MB archive with `dist/` present, no `src`/`node_modules`/`controls`/`config` leakage
- [x] `npm audit --omit=dev` → 0 production vulnerabilities

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

1. **`controls/` submodule needs its own PR.** `npm ci` there fails with ERESOLVE (`react-sortable-hoc` peers `react@^16||^17` vs `@wordpress/block-editor@12` requiring `^18`). Fix is an `overrides` block in `controls/package.json` plus committing its lockfile — that lives in `EssentialBlocks/controls` and then needs a submodule pointer bump here. Not `--legacy-peer-deps`.
2. **`.wordpress-org/` assets are gone.** They existed only on the deleted `trunk` branch, so `assets.yml` has no banners/icons to upload. Recoverable from the local `archive/trunk` tag.
3. **`dist/modules.js` is not reproducible from source** — rebuilding from pinned commit `807ed39` yields 906,132 bytes vs the committed 867,312. Left untouched; it is outside the CI build path.
4. **`react-sortable-hoc` → `@dnd-kit`.** React 19 removes `findDOMNode`, which every `react-sortable-hoc@2.0.0` bundle calls; WP targets React 19 for 7.1. The controls side is already migrated on `1105-dnd-kit` (merged to controls `master`), but this plugin's `src/sortable-filteritems.js` is not.
5. **`@wordpress/scripts` 19 → 34** and the React/Babel modernization — clears 61 dev-tier advisories and the Dart Sass legacy-API deprecation.

body:
## Describe
채팅방 헤더의 placeholder 버튼을 토큰 사용량 아이콘으로 교체하고, 탭하면 오늘 사용한 AI 토큰 사용량을 보여주는 팝업을 추가합니다. 토큰을 다 쓰면 채팅 입력창도 막습니다.

## Works made
- 아이콘 교체: `iconTokenUsage` 에셋 추가
- API 연동: `GET /api/members/me/token-usage` — `TokenUsageResponseDTO` → `TokenUsage`(Domain) → `MemberRepository.fetchTokenUsage()` → `GetTokenUsageUseCase`
- 팝업 UI: `TokenUsagePopoverView` — 제목/퍼센트/진행률 바/리셋 안내 문구, 로딩·에러(재시도) 상태 포함.
- 한도 초과 시 입력창 차단: `ChatViewModel.isTokenExceeded`를 두 경로(팝업 조회 결과, 메시지 전송 응답의 `commentStatus == .limitExceeded`)로 감지하고, `ChatView` 진입 시에도 선제적으로 조회해 이미 초과한 사용자는 처음부터 입력이 막히도록 함
- 최적화: 대화 중 새로 보낸 메시지가 없으면 팝업을 다시 열어도 API를 재호출하지 않고 마지막으로 받아온 값을 그대로 보여줌

## Changes Made

### As-Is
**기존 로직**
헤더 우측 버튼이 다음 이터레이션을 위해 미리 만들어둔 placeholder(`ellipsis` 아이콘, 탭해도 아무 동작 없음)였음.

### To-Be
**변경 로직**
아이콘 탭 시 오늘의 토큰 사용량(퍼센트 + 진행률 바)을 보여주는 팝업이 뜨고, 한도를 다 쓰면 입력창이 비활성화됨.

4. 메시지를 보내지 않고 팝업을 다시 열기 → API가 재호출되지 않고(네트워크 로그로 확인) 같은 값이 그대로 보이는지 확인
5. 메시지 전송 후 팝업을 열기 → 최신 값으로 갱신되는지 확인

author: wombat164
body:
Closes #424.

## What this changes

Four tests ran, passed, and executed none of their own assertions. Each is
repaired so its case occurs, and **each now asserts that it examined
something** - because a check whose non-vacuity is hoped for is a check that can
go quiet again without a single build going red. That is what happened to all
four.

## The before-and-after, by #424's own measurement

Not by reading. The suite under `coverage run --source=tests`, with every
`assert` line cross-referenced against the lines that actually executed. A test
whose body ran and whose every `assert` line did not is reported.

**On `main` (`e346266`):**

```
tests that ran and executed none of their own assertions: 4
  tests/test_guardrails.py:186::test_rate_states_its_direction_in_words
  tests/test_observed_days.py:178::test_a_refusal_carries_no_numerator
  tests/test_retirement_removal.py:179::test_a_key_the_shipped_corpus_still_writes_is_not_scheduled
  tests/test_units.py:179::test_a_named_scale_is_one_the_scale_registry_knows
```

**On this branch:**

```
tests that ran and executed none of their own assertions: 0
```

The measurement was written fresh rather than carried over, and it reproduces
#424's list exactly - same four, same file, same line. That is worth as much as
the fix: it says the issue's finding was right and that this branch closes all
of it rather than most of it.

## 1. `scale` - pointed at the data, per the issue's first horn

The guard read `units(ds, f).get("scale")`, and **no entry in the units registry
uses the key `scale`**. Measured: the keys in use are `ucum` (58), `label` (81),
`aliases` (33), `unit_of` (8), `ordinal` (5), `scale_of` (4), `machine_scoped`
(4), `unit_in` (1), `unstated` (1). The guard could not open.

**Where the slug really is, and why.** Which scale a rating sits on is a fact
about the ROW, not the column - two athletes' `rpe` sit on different Borg scales
in one corpus, and a spec-level answer would have to pick one and be wrong about
the other. So `units()` publishes `scale_of`, the name of the field that names
the scale, and the slug lives in the data: **690 values** across
`sessions.rpe_scale` (453 `borg-cr10`, 41 `borg-rpe-6-20`), `daily.mood_scale`
(113), `daily.pain_scale` (52) and `sets.rpe_scale` (31).

The check now reads those, and the test's own name still describes it exactly.
**The scale-bearing fields are derived from `scale_of`**, not from the `_scale`
suffix - a suffix is the naming convention this module exists to stop trusting,
and a field renamed out of it would silently leave the check.

#424 says "either point it at the data, or delete it and say the spec has no
`scale` key. Not both." This takes the first horn and says the second in the
comment. The registry key itself is left alone: `units()` lists `scale` as one
of the shapes a spec may take and none takes it today, which is the schema's
decision to revisit rather than this test's - and the check no longer claims to
be watching it.

## 2. G69 - the property, not the spelling

`if "kg/week" in text`, and the rollup stopped emitting that string on this
fixture. `nursing_mother` now renders:

```
**Rate:** losing over 13 days, a thin sample (no phase targets configured)
```

**This is a safety guard.** The line once showed `+1.10 kg/week` to an athlete
who had LOST 1.5 kg, because positive means losing here; for a scale-anxious
under-eater that misreading is actively dangerous. It was unguarded while the
suite reported it covered - and it went quiet twice over, since #185 removed the
figure from the direction line and nothing noticed the check had switched off.

So `g69_problem(line)` reads the line the rollup actually emits and asks what
G69 asks: a signed quantity with no direction word beside it fails; a line with
neither a direction word nor a stated refusal fails; an explicit `NOT READABLE`
/ `NOT COMPARABLE` states no rate and owes no direction word.

**Two fixtures**, because one shape proves nothing about the other -
`nursing_mother` states a direction, `glp1_athlete` refuses outright - and the
control runs the predicate against the string from the original finding, so its
failure has been seen at least once:

```python
assert g69_problem("**Rate:** +1.10 kg/week")           # the finding
assert g69_problem("**Rate:** 0.45 kg/week")            # bare, no direction
assert g69_problem("**Rate:** losing over 13 days ...") is None
assert g69_problem("**Rate:** NOT READABLE - the two readings behind this "
                   "are 27 days apart, ...") is None    # hyphens are not signs
```

## 3. `observed_days` - a fixture that actually refuses

The assertion sat inside `if row["value"] is None`, and the fixture - three days
of 12,000 steps against a step floor - produces exactly one verdict row and it
carries a value.

A refusal needs a metric that is **scored and has no input**. The fixture now
configures a phase and gives fourteen days of steps with weigh-ins in the first
week only, so `weight_rate` refuses the second week with `no_data` / `no_input`
and a null value. The test asserts it got at least two of them before checking
the property.

A companion runs the same property over `yasmin`, whose 38 refusal rows nobody
wrote for this test - the synthetic fixture proves the engine *can* refuse
without a numerator, the corpus is where some other path filling one in would
show up.

## 4. Retirement - the control the other three had

This is the honest case: every `KEY_REMOVAL` entry is unscheduled, so the loop
body never runs, and `removal_problems`' own docstring plus
`test_the_corpus_really_does_still_write_retired_keys` already say so. It was
the one check in that file **without a control** - the three tests above it
exercise `removal_problems` against synthetic registers, and the corpus scan was
inline logic nothing could reach.

The rule is now `_scheduled_and_still_written(removals, carried)`, a pure
function, exercised against a scheduled removal this repo does not contain: a
scheduled key the corpus still writes reports; one already migrated does not; an
unscheduled entry does not; and a key no measurement reached counts as
unwritten, so a broken corpus reader cannot manufacture a finding.

**Nothing pins which entries are scheduled.** That file's docstring states the
rule and it is right: "No control asserts that a particular key is unscheduled
today. That would make scheduling one - the whole point of the register - fail a
test whose name says nothing about scheduling."

## The gate: deliberately not shipped

#424 is explicit - "Filing the four first; the gate is a second question" - and
states the objection itself: a zero-iteration loop is sometimes correct, as
entry 4 shows, so the gate shape would have to be a register with stated reasons
rather than a red build, and it costs a coverage run in CI.

So the measurement is used here as **evidence, not as a gate**, and the script
is reproduced below rather than committed. An unwired script in `scripts/` that
nothing runs is the same disease one level up.

```python
import ast, pathlib, sys
from coverage import CoverageData

root = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
data = CoverageData(basename=str(root / ".coverage")); data.read()
executed = {pathlib.Path(f).resolve(): set(data.lines(f) or [])
            for f in data.measured_files()}

for path in sorted((root / "tests").rglob("test_*.py")):
    ran = executed.get(path.resolve())
    if not ran:
        continue
    for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))):
        if not isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
            continue
        if not node.name.startswith("test_"):
            continue
        body = {n.lineno for s in node.body for n in ast.walk(s)
                if hasattr(n, "lineno")}
        asserts = {n.lineno for n in ast.walk(node) if isinstance(n, ast.Assert)}
        if asserts and (body & ran) and not (asserts & ran):
            print(f"{path.relative_to(root)}:{node.li

author: fatalversion
body:
Two related bodies of work: a new template family, and the editor fixes that make
v3 able to replace v1.

They share a branch because the section-toggle work sits between them — Palm Hour
exposed that the editor's block list was hardcoded, and fixing that led into the
v1/v3 parity audit. Happy to split into three PRs if you'd rather review them
separately; the commits are independent.

## 1 · Palm Hour — `hospitality:BI` (`0bca71f`)

New family for hotels, villas and short-stay rentals. Terracotta over deep lagoon
shade: every inverted band is lagoon green rather than black, so the flat phone
photography these owners actually supply gains apparent contrast instead of dying
against cream. Rooms render as a published tariff ledger; rooms and gallery come
before the story, because this vertical is bought with the eyes.

**No backend change.** Hospitality meaning is carried by labels and layout over the
existing content keys — `services.items` are rooms and rates, `why.items` amenities,
`faq.items` house rules, `area.places` what's nearby. 77 editable hooks, no new schema.

Two palette laws hold throughout: a solid button fill is always `--ink` with a
`--paper` label — never a mid-tone — and `--accent` is never text. Zero baked hex
outside `PageBI`'s `:root`, and **zero `!important`**.

An adversarial pass found 15 defects and refuted 15 more. All 15 are fixed here,
including a blocker where a literal `</style>` inside a CSS comment ended the
stylesheet 383 lines early and broke `astro build` for *every* route — with no
compiler diagnostic.

## 2 · Section toggles that match the template (`19da34d`)

The Blocks tab rendered one hardcoded list of 16 switches for all 61 templates, so
it was wrong in both directions. A scan of every wrapper found three distinct
section shapes, differing only in MARQUEE (11 templates) and CREDENTIALS (absent
from generic A–E).

- **MARQUEE had no toggle at all** and rendered unconditionally, so the section
  owners most often want gone could never be removed. Gated in all 11 wrappers.
- CREDENTIALS offered a dead switch on generic A–E.
- CLICK-TO-MESSAGE and SCROLL-TO-TOP are deliberately *not* offered — no wrapper
  gates on either.

`blocksForTemplate()` is the single source of truth; `scripts/check-template-blocks.mjs`
re-derives it from the wrappers and fails on drift. I broke a wrapper on purpose to
confirm the guard catches it.

## 3 · Editor v3 parity (`faccc22`, `12ee21b`, `1624da7`)

A 15-agent audit of v1 vs v3 found 25 gaps, 11 of them blockers. All 22 code items
are closed. The two that mattered most:

**v3 was discarding edits behind a "Changes saved" toast.** It seeded its draft with
a bare spread while Groq emits five blocks as *bare arrays* and the schema reads
`.items`/`.steps`. Writing `why.items` hung a property on an Array — which
`JSON.stringify` drops — so edits died between the toast and Convex. Submissions
previously saved through v1 were immune, so it hit exactly the new ones.

**One `+ Add` click shipped a blank `<h1>`.** `getValue` was draft-only, so a derived
list read as empty and Add committed a one-element array over it.

Also: dirty-gated Save, Reset, per-photo delete, favicon card, Approve/Reject
status-gating, the colour picker no longer hiding 10 of 15 schemes, `sandbox=""`
restored on 55 thumbnail iframes, and the inline-edit gate inverted from a
hand-written skip regex to an allow-list derived from the schema.

**`jest.config.ts` required `ts-node`, which isn't a dependency** — so `npm test`
couldn't parse its own config and *no test in this repo ran*. Converted to plain JS:
323 pre-existing tests went from unrunnable to green.

## Verification

`astro build` clean · `tsc --noEmit` clean · 338 tests green · both template guards
pass (55 codes = 55 previews, 61 wrappers) · `hospitality:BI` rendered end to end
producing 77 hooks · marquee toggle confirmed against built HTML.

## Not done, and deliberately so

**v3 has never been run against a live submission.** Everything above is static
analysis plus unit tests. The runtime QA should be treated as discovery, not
confirmation — expect it to add items.

**v1 is still the default and nothing here changes that.** The sequence should be:
QA a real submission per family → flip the default at `page.tsx:206` → run a week
with v1 present as the escape hatch → *then* delete v1. Don't combine the flip and
the deletion; one is reversible in a line, the other isn't.

Two known issues left alone on purpose: `pickOn()`'s 0.5 threshold gives six colour
schemes a sub-AA button label (fixing it restyles all 55 templates at once), and
`filipino:BB–BH` are missing from v1's content allow-list.
