body: ## Summary V4 — Calendar surface, stacked on #62 (V3 calendar spine). Adds the user-facing Calendar tab and the `calendar` mini-app on top of V3's box event store / `agent_schedules` / source routes, without touching V3 internals. **Calendar tab** (`app/home/calendar-panel.tsx`, registered in `TABS`): month / week / agenda views (agenda default on narrow layouts, today pinned) over three independently toggleable layers — external events (provider-colored dots from the box store), agent schedules (orb pills, expanded onto the grid client-side via `cronOccurrences(cron, tz, start, end)` from Postgres metadata only), and bot routines (`source: 'bots'`, dither-avatar chips). Pending email invites render dashed. Event detail sheet: title/time/source chip/location/URL/attendee count + **Prep me** (dispatches a streamed chat run via `send(promptOverride)`), **Remind me** (below), and **Draft a reschedule email** for email-sourced events. New/edit schedule sheet: name, natural-language time with parsed-cron echo, prompt, iMessage/email/silent delivery, pause/resume/delete. Source management for google/apple_ics/calcom/email with connect/disconnect + last-synced status (cal.com webhook secret shown once). **NL schedule parsing** (`lib/calendar/nl.ts`): client-side `parseNaturalSchedule` ("weekdays at 8am" → `0 8 * * 1-5`), sub-hourly input rejected with the wake-budget message; server-side `validateCron` remains authoritative. **Remind me** (`POST /api/calendar/remind` + `agent_schedules.one_shot`): inserts a one-shot schedule N minutes before the event; the sweeper fires it once then deletes the row and the box prompt: ```ts // sweep.ts, success path if (schedule.one_shot) { update({ status: "deleted" }); // self-deletes command(box, `rm -f /home/user/${schedule.prompt_ref}`); } ``` C4 note: the reminder row's `name` is a generic "Event reminder" — the event title goes only into the box-side prompt file, never into Postgres. **Calendar mini-app** (`app/mini/[app]/route.ts` + `/api/mini/link`): next-7-days agenda read from the box store (degrades to invites-only if the box can't wake) plus inline approve/dismiss of pending `calendar_add` decisions (same `approveInboxEvent`/`dismissInboxEvent` path as the Needs-you queue). Reuses the existing C15/C17 plumbing unchanged: single-use token redeem, path-scoped 15-min HttpOnly cookie, no-referrer/no-store headers, CSP with no scripts (no localStorage possible). **Generalized card sends** (migration 0025): `computer_card_sends` → `card_sends(user_id, kind)` with rows migrated; `claimCardSend(supabase, userId, kind)` in `lib/miniapps/cardSends.ts` is the shared atomic cooldown claim (insert-or-conditional-update, release() backdates for retry-after-failure). The computer card route now uses it, and inbound email ICS processing sends an owner-only calendar card after materializing invites — tier-2 senders still only ever produce a decision; the card goes to the owner's durable iMessage destination and is rate-limited by the claim. **Needs you**: `calendar_add` decisions now render as dashed "Calendar invite" cards with an "Add to calendar" approve button (route support existed in V3). ## V4 acceptance checklist - Three layers render distinctly and toggle independently — done (layer toggles in the tab header). - Emailed invite → Needs-you decision → inline iMessage approval → solid event — decision card + mini-app approval implemented; end-to-end path needs a real box + inbound email to exercise. - "Prep me" streams a reply using real event fields — dispatches a chat run with title/time/location; needs a live box to observe streaming. - "Remind me" fires once at the correct local time and self-deletes — implemented (one-shot + sweeper deletion); firing needs the cron sweeper against a live box. - Created schedules appear in the box and immediately in the grid; deletion removes both — POST writes the prompt box-side then the row; the grid re-fetches; DELETE tombstones + best-effort `rm`. - Sub-hourly input rejected with the wake-budget message — done client-side (`nl.ts`) and server-side (`validateCron`). - Tier-2 ICS senders yield a decision only; cards go only to the owner — unchanged V3 decision path; the new card send looks up only the owner's `imessage_destinations` row. ## Honest limitations - `/api/calendar` (V3) wakes the box to read `events.json` since event content is never mirrored to Postgres (C4) — so external events are not "instant"; the tab renders schedules/layers immediately and shows the standard 429/502 wake messaging while events load. - Anything involving a real box, Composio Google auth, cal.com webhooks, AgentMail inbound, or Spectrum sends could not be exercised in this environment; verified via unit tests (nl parser, card-send cooldown, sweep claim) + typecheck/lint/build. ## Testing `npm run typecheck` / `npm run lint` / `npm test -- --run` (280 passed, incl. new `nl.test.ts`, `cardSends.test.ts`) / `npm run build` — all green in `apps/web`. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/aa5a072f8e104bb880d69d4623977a9a Requested by: @gratitude5dee ---

author: sandip1608
body:
## What

Booking 94D57BE3 sat un-checked-out past its 2026-08-17 departure and silently disappeared from the departures list the next morning. Per discussion with the owner: **no auto-checkout** (only the desk knows whether the guest actually left) — instead the miss is made loud everywhere staff look, plus an in-app reminder.

- **Bookings page** — departures query is now `check_out <= today` (was `=`), section renamed "Departures due", overdue rows carry a danger "Overdue · N days" badge.
- **Unpaid-checkout guard** — Check out asks "Rs X still outstanding … Check out anyway?" when a balance remains (new optional `confirmMessage` prop on `SubmitButton`).
- **Overview** — danger banner above the metric tiles listing each overdue stay (#room, guest, due date) with a "Review departures" link.
- **Room map** — new `overdue` tile state: oxblood with a gold ring + alarm icon, its own legend entry, hover card says "past check-out, not checked out"; counted in the building occupancy figure.
- **Notification bell** — in the back-office sidebar header (desktop; the mobile drawer's close button owns that corner and the Overview banner covers mobile). Backed by the previously unused `notifications` table and its existing self-only RLS policies; unread badge, mark-all-read server action. No schema changes.
- **Daily cron** `/api/cron/overdue-checkouts` (04:15 UTC = 10:00 NPT, `CRON_SECRET`-gated like the reviews cron): deletes stale unread `overdue_checkout` notifications and inserts one fresh summary per active staff member. Copy renders from the `overdue_checkout` notification template — **editable and toggleable at `/admin/templates`** (the owner's requested admin-side notification type), with hardcoded fallback copy. Seeded in the live DB by `scripts/seed-overdue-notification-template.mjs` (idempotent, already run).

## Verification

- Playwright screenshots (throwaway seeded preview, deleted): overdue tile + legend + hover card render correctly; bell opens with unread badge, bold unread rows, mark-all-read.
- Cron triggered locally against the live DB: `{"ok":true,"overdue":1,"notified":1}`; the notification row rendered from the template and is waiting for the super admin's next login.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; production build emits the new route; lint warnings unchanged (pre-existing 12).

⚠️ Assumes `CRON_SECRET` is set in the Vercel environment — it's empty in local `.env`, and the existing Google-reviews cron already depends on it. Worth confirming in the Vercel dashboard.

author: hankehly
body:
## Summary

- **Shared framework `power_market_analytics/forecasting/`** — the task-agnostic parts of the spot-price backtest, extracted so a second task is a thin configuration: `TaskSpec` (name = MLflow experiment, unit, `history_lead_days`, `issue_offset`, `forecast_table`, four frame classes), frame bases whose schema is assembled from one ClassVar (`HalfHourlySeries`/`DayAheadForecast`/`BacktestResult`/`ForecastRecords`), `ForecastStrategy` + `ForecastUnavailableError`, the rolling engine (`run_backtest` → `BacktestRun(result, skipped_days)`) with a **gaps policy** (a day the strategy cannot forecast is skipped and reported; forecast points without an actual are dropped), `join_lag`, `SlidingWindowLightGbmStrategy` (refits, TreeSHAP records, static-dataset MLflow eval; subclasses set `task`/`feature_cols`/`eval_set_cls`/`lookback_days` and implement `_add_features`), TaskSpec-driven `publish`, and the error heatmaps.
- **`spot_price` migrated onto it, behaviour-preserving** — same column names, MLflow params/artifacts, `pma_ml.spot_price_forecast` DDL, dbt models and CLI; `tasks/spot_price/{backtest,features,publish,plots}.py` and `strategies/base.py` are deleted. Only edge-case behaviour changes: a missing D-1 now skips the day instead of aborting the run (`n_days_skipped` param), and a missing actual period is dropped + logged instead of raising.
- **New `demand` task** (`tasks/demand/`): at 09:30 JST on D-1 forecast the 48 half-hourly `demand_kwh` of `fct_area_demand_generation_actual`; usable history = days ≤ D-2 (`history_lead_days = 2`, TSO files finalise after midnight). Baseline `lightgbm` = `time_code, month, day_of_week, wavg_temperature_c, lag_7d_demand_kwh`, where `wavg_temperature_c` is the same-hour temperature at the area's representative JMA station over D-8..D-2, weights halving per day back (leakage-free by construction). `scripts/demand_backtest.py` mirrors the spot script (MLflow experiment `demand`, publishes to `pma_ml.demand_forecast`).
- **Warehouse / dbt** — `dim_area.representative_jma_station_id` (seed `jepx_areas`: 札幌 s47412 … 東京 s47662 … 大阪 s47772 … 福岡 s47807), source `ml.demand_forecast`, `stg/std_ml__demand_forecast` → `fct_demand_forecast` → `fct_demand_forecast_accuracy` (all contracts enforced, composite-key uniqueness tests). CLAUDE.md and `docs/README.md` (star schema / ER diagram) updated.
- Design spec and implementation plan: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-demand-forecasting-task-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-18-demand-forecasting-task.md` (the plan lists four small, deliberate spec deviations at the top).

## Data prerequisites (not code)

- `fct_jma_weather_hourly` has no rows for 大阪 s47772 → `--area kansai` fails at strategy construction with `No temperature observations found for area_code='kansai'`; 東京 s47662 weather currently ends 2026-07-19 while demand actuals run to 2026-08-17 → a default Tokyo window skips its last ~3 weeks (`n_days_skipped`). `just refresh-jma` (or reloading the on-disk JMA CSVs) fixes both; documented in CLAUDE.md.

## Verification

- `just test` → 653 passed, coverage 100 % (branch); `uv run ruff check .` clean.
- Devcontainer end-to-end: `demand_backtest.py --area tokyo --days 60` (MLflow run `11b6adee…`, MAE ≈ 1.12 GWh/30-min, MAPE 6.4 %), `--start-date 2025-06-15 --end-date 2025-06-30` (run `43197700…`, MAPE 5.9 %, `n_days_skipped=1` = 2025-06-21, whose D-7 lag falls in the TEPCO 2025-06-14 hole); `just dbt build --select +fct_demand_forecast_accuracy` PASS=147 and the accuracy fact's MAE/MAPE per run equal the MLflow metrics; spot `previous_day` run (`cbff46a7…`) + `+fct_spot_price_forecast_accuracy` PASS=148 still green.

## Riders

- `95ae1fd Update dockerfile` and `5139c73 Delete scratch file` are the repo owner's own commits on this branch; the "Timestamps in tests" CLAUDE.md gotcha rode along in `5dc9f36`.
- Follow-ups noted, not done: `docs/README.md` intro still says "eight fact tables" (now ten); the two backtest scripts are ~90 % duplicated (candidate `forecasting/cli.py`); a seasonal-naive demand baseline and holidays as a feature were out of scope.

body:
## Summary

- Migrate all 16 remaining direct Caffeine users in `server` and `storage-s3` to the typed `LocalCacheFactory` abstraction while preserving their existing TTL, size/weight, single-flight, concurrent-map, and removal-listener behavior.
- Move Caffeine native runtime hints and their tests into the `cache` module, remove direct Caffeine dependencies from business modules, and make `storage-s3` depend on `kkrepo-cache` instead.
- Tighten `CacheAbstractionBoundaryTest` so both production source imports and Maven dependencies must keep the cache backend isolated inside the `cache` module, and update `AGENTS.md` to require zero business-module exceptions.

## Why

PR #224 introduced the typed local-cache abstraction for Hugging Face and intentionally left the existing direct Caffeine users on an audited migration list. Keeping backend configuration in business modules makes cache implementations harder to replace or manage consistently. This follow-up removes that migration debt and makes the module boundary enforceable.

## Validation

- [x] `mvn -pl cache,storage-s3,server -am -DskipTests compile`
- [x] Targeted cache regression suite: 103 tests passed.
- [x] `mvn -pl cache,storage-s3,server -am test` — all 33 reactor modules passed; server ran 2,567 tests with zero failures (9m16s total).
- [x] `mvn -pl server -am -Dtest=CacheAbstractionBoundaryTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false test` — 2 tests passed.
- [x] Full E2E [run 32107989779](https://github.com/klboke/kkRepo/actions/runs/32107989779) passed, including OCI conformance, Nexus compatibility, Swift Windows/macOS/dual-replica coverage, and the full Nexus migration matrix.

author: twodragon0
body:
`load_framework()` reads the **installed Prowler package**, not the scan. Prowler ships each framework for some providers and not others, so a mapping is populated whenever Prowler is installed — including on a run that scanned none of those providers. Every natively-mapped control then matches zero findings and takes the `count == 0 → PASS` default. The shipped image makes it reachable: the Dockerfile strips `prowler/providers/{azure,gcp,...}` but never `prowler/compliance/**`.

This is the item #455 deliberately left out of scope. Measurement showed it was never NIST-only.

## Measured, not assumed

Provider coverage at the pinned Prowler 5.30.1:

| Framework | Providers Prowler ships it for |
|---|---|
| ISO 27001:2022 | aws, azure, gcp, kubernetes, m365, nhn |
| PCI-DSS v4.0.1 | aws, azure, gcp, kubernetes |
| SOC 2 (TSC) | aws, azure, gcp |
| **KISA ISMS-P** | **aws** |
| **NIST 800-53 Rev5** | **aws** |
| CMMC 2.0 Level 2 | aws |

Kubernetes-only scan, 62 real k8s check ids from Prowler's own `pci_4.0_kubernetes.json` + `iso27001_2022_kubernetes.json` as FAIL findings:

| Framework | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| NIST 800-53 Rev5 | **10 pass / 0 fail** (all `prowler`) | 5 pass / 5 fail (all `keyword`) |
| SOC 2 (TSC) | **6 pass / 0 fail** (all `prowler`) | 3 pass / 3 fail (all `keyword`) |
| KISA ISMS-P | 20 pass / 7 fail (16 on `prowler`) | 9 pass / 18 fail |
| PCI-DSS v4.0.1 | 0 pass / 7 fail | unchanged |
| ISO 27001:2022 | 3 pass / 3 fail | unchanged |

NIST 800-53 and SOC 2 reported a perfect score on an estate whose evidence they could never read. **Five NIST, three SOC 2 and eleven KISA failures were hidden.** An AWS scan is unaffected in every framework.

## The gate is per control, not per framework

Caught in review. The loader **merges** every provider file into one check set per control, so "ISO ships for kubernetes" can be true while an individual control's checks are all AWS. A framework-level scope leaves that open — and it reaches the flagship provider:

| ISO control | Evidenced by |
|---|---|
| A.8.2 | aws, azure, gcp, kubernetes, m365, nhn |
| A.5.1 | aws, azure, gcp, kubernetes, m365 |
| A.8.5 | aws, azure, kubernetes, m365 |
| A.8.24 | aws, azure, gcp, kubernetes |
| A.8.9 | aws, azure, gcp, nhn |
| **A.8.8** | **m365 only** |
| A.8.28 | *(no native mapping — keywords)* |

On an **AWS** run, `A.8.8` reported `PASS` from Prowler's exact mapping while every check backing it belongs to m365. Verified before/after on the real files:

```text
A.8.8   before=PASS/prowler   after=PASS/keyword   <-- CHANGED
```

## Derived, not declared

Replaces the hand-written `FRAMEWORK_NATIVE_PROVIDERS` dict #455 added for CMMC alone. The table above is why that shape could not hold: it was already wrong for three more frameworks the moment it was written, and the answer differs per Prowler release.

The scope is now built **in the same pass, from the same parsed content** as the mapping it scopes — a provider is recorded for a control only once one of its requirements survived the merge. Deriving from filenames would let a file that exists but contributes nothing widen the scope past the evidence.

**Gating never invents an N/A.** A gated control returns to keywords; only `native_only` controls (CMMC's) report N/A. A GitHub-only run is out of scope for every registered framework — `compliance/github/` holds only `cis_1.0_github.json` and CIS is deliberately unregistered — so it keeps the keyword path, which is the case that path exists for.

## The dashboard now says which path it took

`match_source` was produced by `map_compliance` and rendered **nowhere**, so a control scored by Prowler's exact data and one scored by substring matching looked identical. They are not — the keyword path reproduces 41.5% of Prowler's own mapping where both have an opinion, and this change moves controls onto it. Each framework now renders an **Evidence source** line: `N exact · N keyword · N not assessed`.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest scanner/tests/` — **2275 passed, 8 skipped**
- [x] `scanner/lib` **99.41%** at the CI gate (`--cov-precision=2 --cov-fail-under=99`) — `compliance-map.py`, `prowler_native_map.py`, `dashboard_html_compliance.py`, `prowler_compliance_summary.py` all **100%**
- [x] Shell: control liveness 14/14 and 20/20, `test_generate_html_dashboard` 36/36, `test_prowler_dashboard_summary` 24/24, provider-label 20/20 — all rc=0
- [x] `markdownlint` + `lychee` clean (0 errors, 0 redirects); `gitleaks protect --staged` clean
- [x] End-to-end against the real pinned Prowler 5.30.1 compliance files, not fixtures
- [x] **Eight mutations** each caught — including the two an independent `sec-reviewer` used to defeat the first draft: a scope that silently skips three frameworks (was `2258 passed` while re-hiding the KISA failures), and deriving the scope from file existence rather than contribution

New guards: `scanner/tests/test_native_provider_scope.py` runs against a tree holding **all six** frameworks at once (a single-framework fixture cannot catch a scope that skips frameworks), pins the 5.30.1 provider table, and reads the emitting side out of `integration.sh` rather than from `PROVIDER_LABELS` — that is a UI label table, and `nhn` is in it while the NHN block actually runs `_prowler_scan "openstack"`.

### Known, not changed here

- On a **mixed** run, a control whose native providers include the scanned one keeps its native mapping, so findings from an uncovered provider stay invisible to it. That needs per-finding matching, not per-control gating.
- The KISA glob's `[!k]` guard does not exclude the Korean file — `*` backtracks so `[!k]` lands on the `a` of `aws`. Measured impact: +1 control (`2.8.5`), no conflicting check sets.
- ClaudeSec never emits an `nhn` slug, so ISO's `nhn` scope row is unreachable here (pinned by a test so it is understood rather than assumed).

author: kadimula
body:
## What

Smallest-viable `two80 logs`: a deploying agent can now read a deployed app's server logs from the CLI and, critically, resolve a Next.js production error `digest` to its real server stack. Built exactly to the scout design (`280-logs-cli-scout/report.md`, Parts A/B + C7/C8).

## The four pieces

1. **Capture on the roll** — `rollConfig()` now bakes `observability:{enabled:true,head_sampling_rate:1}` into every per-app `wrangler.roll.json`, so the container's stdout/stderr lands in Workers Logs. `head_sampling_rate:1` is deliberate: error lines are rare and must never be sampled out.
2. **Digest↔stack pairing (no tenant-app code change)** — the Next.js buildpack (`bundle/container.ts`) injects an `instrumentation.js` exporting `onRequestError` that logs one structured stderr line `{ t:'280.error', digest, message, stack, path, routerKind }`. **Guard:** injected only when the app ships no instrumentation of its own (checked at root and `src/`, `.ts/.js/.mjs/.tsx`); a user file is never clobbered, and the user-Dockerfile path is skipped (280 doesn't own that build).
3. **Backend read endpoint** — `GET /v1/apps/:app/logs?since&limit&level&digest&follow` mirrors `handleStatus` exactly (authorize → owner-scoped `store.app`). New owner-scoped `Service.logs` resolves `app.script` and queries Cloudflare's Workers Observability telemetry query API behind a thin `LogSource` seam (`src/logsource.ts`). Response is `Cache-Control: no-store`.
4. **CLI command** — `two80 logs <app> [--since --limit --level --digest]` (default app from `.280/config.json`), `logs` added to `Port` + http/fake adapters + record types. TOON-clean with golden fixtures. `--digest` prints the matching `280.error` line's full stack.

## Guardrails honored

- **Multi-tenant isolation:** the telemetry query is constrained server-side to the single owner-resolved `app.script` — never from client input. A cross-tenant request is rejected at `store.app` and never reaches the log source (test-asserted).
- **Owner-only + PII:** owner-scoped like status/delete; `Cache-Control: no-store`; logs treated as owner-confidential.
- Deferred items (live `--follow` tail, dashboard pane, Logpush-to-store, Depot build logs) intentionally not built.

## Deviation from the scope line

The scope line listed `--json`, but this repo made a platform-wide decision that **stdout is always TOON** (`--json` is a removed flag with an explicit rejection message) and C7's smallest-viable list omits it. TOON is already structured/parseable, so `--json` would be a regression against that decision — omitted, matching C7. Flag me if you want it back.

## ⚠️ Unverified: live Cloudflare telemetry API

No Cloudflare credentials were reachable in the build worktree, so I could **not** run a live telemetry query. Per the brief I coded to the documented API and isolated the whole coupling behind `LogSource`, with a deliberately tolerant response parser. **Still needs a ~30-min live spike** to confirm: (i) container stdout lands in the telemetry dataset with observability on, (ii) the `280.error` line survives intact, (iii) the exact request/response filter syntax (`$metadata.service` eq `<script>`, event nesting). If the shape differs, only `CloudflareLogSource` changes — the CLI, endpoint, and seam do not. It is also unverified that `onRequestError` fires for the specific RSC render path that produced the motivating 500 (Next 15 docs say it covers server render + route handlers + server actions).

## Required to take effect (not done here — firstmate coordinates)

- **Publish the `two80` CLI** (new `logs` command + buildpack injection).
- **Redeploy the backend** (new endpoint + roll observability flag). Observability only applies to rolls that happen after the redeploy, so existing apps need a re-push to start capturing logs.

## Tests

Green across contracts, cli, backend, gateway, sdk. New/extended: roll observability assertion (`depot-builder.test.ts`), injection guard (`bundle-container.test.ts`), endpoint owner-scoping/isolation + no-store + query clamping (`logs.test.ts`), CF client parsing/filtering (`logsource.test.ts`), CLI output + `--digest` golden fixtures.

author: abe238
body:
## What

Several error paths render an application's `localizedName`. For a process **without a bundle**, `localizedName` can be the entire command line, so those messages could repeat argv.

## Why it matters

I hit this running `mac.see("Bear")`. The query matched a few `npx mcp-remote` processes and the error printed two live bearer tokens, because that MCP server is started as `npx mcp-remote <url> --header "Authorization:Bearer <token>"`.

To be clear about severity: **this is not a privilege boundary.** `ps` already exposes argv to same-UID processes, so nothing here grants access a caller did not have. The narrower point is that this is agent tooling, so error text lands in logs, screenshots and LLM transcripts, which travel much further than a `ps` dump. Mine went into an agent transcript.

## The change

`_label(info)` renders:

- **bundled app** → display name + pid (`Bear (7)`). `localizedName` here comes from the bundle, not the process.
- **unbundled process** → **pid only** (`pid 4242`).

I originally tried keeping the leading token of the name. That was wrong: `argv[0]` is chosen by the process, so a process can name itself `Bearer:sk-live` and a token-selection policy prints it verbatim. Nothing derived from that string can be called safe, so unbundled processes get the pid, which is what actually disambiguates.

Same class of issue, also fixed:

- The **query itself** was echoed raw. A caller can pass a name taken from `list_apps`, which for an unbundled process is a command line. Now bounded and escaped.
- `_truncate` escaped only newline, so a bundle name or query carrying ESC or CR could rewrite terminal output or hide text in a log. It now escapes every control character.
- `FocusChangedError` and `capture_screenshot`'s no-window error rendered raw names too.

## Scope, stated plainly

This covers **error paths**. It does **not** try to sanitise successful output: `apps`, `see` and `state` still return raw app info, and that is the documented job of those calls, equivalent to running `ps` yourself. So this is not general transcript protection, and I would rather say so than imply otherwise.

Behaviour change worth flagging: ordinary errors for bundled apps are unchanged (`Bear (7)`), but unbundled processes now read `pid 4242` instead of a name. Less pretty, and the only version I can honestly describe as safe.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest` **34 passed**, `uv run ruff check .` clean
- Tests drive the real `_resolve_app` path rather than rebuilding its f-string
- Each fix was checked by reverting it and confirming the matching test fails
- Preserves the three CONTRIBUTING invariants: no pointer movement, no app activation, no telemetry change

author: hinten
body:
## Summary

Part of #371. Ports `getPesoPedido` + `adicionarVolumePedido`
(`.old/lib/pedido/providers/cadastroPedidoProvider.dart:1394-1454`): the Frete
tab auto-computes the pedido's weight from its items and seeds one default
Volume (`Volume.padrao`) when frete is activated with no volumes yet, so
freight can be quoted without manual volume entry.

- `pesoPedido()` — pure port of `getPesoPedido`: bruto-over-líquido preference,
  variation→parent fallback (not BOM/kit expansion), 1kg floor on
  empty/unresolvable items, no rounding on the sum.
- `volumePadrao()` — pure port of `Volume.padrao`: 1 unit, `pesoLiquido` = 90%
  of `pesoBruto` (2dp byte-parity rounding via the existing `roundReais`),
  `'Pacote'`, hardcoded 10×10×10cm. `VolumesEditor`'s "+ Novo volume" button
  calls the same factory instead of a local duplicate.
- `loadProdutoPesoMap()` — batched two-wave produto weight lookup (produtos,
  then the parents of zero-weight variations) behind **one shared query key**,
  fetched **on demand** by whichever caller needs it first — the activation
  seed or the "+ Novo volume" button — and reused by the other. Nothing is
  fetched on mount, so a Frete tab nobody edits costs no reads.
- `seedVolumePadrao()` + `isAtivacaoDeFrete()` — the seed, fired from
  `onModalidadeChange`, i.e. from the **user gesture that activates frete**.

### Why the seed lives in the gesture, not a mount effect

The first revision used a mount `useEffect` plus a `useRef` activation latch.
Review found two failure modes in it, and both are structural rather than
incidental:

- `PedidoForm`'s Tabs use `keepMounted={false}` (`PedidoForm.tsx:496`), so a
  ref-held latch is destroyed whenever the operator leaves the tab — switching
  away mid-fetch meant the Volume was never seeded at all.
- The latch was never cleared, so it could seed into a `semTransporte` pedido
  after a quick activate→deactivate, and re-fabricate a Volume the operator had
  just deleted.

Running from `onModalidadeChange` removes the latch entirely: the form is owned
by `PedidoForm` and outlives the tab, so an in-flight seed still completes after
an unmount, while a passive remount can never trigger one. `seedVolumePadrao`
also re-reads `volumes` **after** the await and re-decides from that value, so
it never clobbers a volume added while the batch was in flight (root
`CLAUDE.md` rule 7). It skips while `int_frete` is still resolving —
`isFreteMarketplaceOwned` returns false for an unknown `tipo`, so the load
window was a way to seed into an importer-owned block.

### On the 10×10×10cm box

An earlier revision removed the auto-seed on the grounds that a fabricated
10×10×10cm box feeds a real freight quote. That premise doesn't hold: with **no**
volume, `buildCalculatePayload` already quotes a fabricated **20×20×20cm / 1kg**
package (`freight-br/src/melhor-envio/calculate.ts:49-52`). Seeding therefore
replaces a fabricated box *and* a fabricated weight with a fabricated box and
the pedido's **real** weight — not seeding is strictly less accurate. The box
stays the documented `Volume.padrao` fallback until `getDimensoes` lands.

## Not included — `getDimensoes`

The **"Scope addition (2026-07-14 parity audit)"** on #371 asks for the legacy
`getDimensoes` progressive bin-packing box estimator. It is **not** in this PR,
but it is no longer blocked: the algorithm is fully readable at
`.old/packages/pedido/lib/src/models.dart:2762-2942` (an earlier note here
claimed it was underivable — that was wrong, `.old/` is gitignored and so absent
from worktrees, not absent from the repo). Notes for the follow-up are in the
review comment below. **#371 stays open.**

## Behaviour change worth knowing

`apps/nfe`'s `generator-input.ts:514` emits the NF-e `<vol>` group only when
`freteInicial.volumes` is non-empty, so pedidos that previously had none will
now carry one. The group holds no dimensions (`:519-542`) — only the
now-accurate weights and `esp: 'Pacote'` reach the XML.

## Deploy steps

None — client-only change, no schema/permission/index changes.

## Testing

- `pesoPedido.test.ts` (22) — the pure weight/volume math and `normalizeProdutoId`.
- `seedVolumePadrao.test.ts` (9) — the seed decision, the delete-marker filter,
  the post-await re-read guard, error propagation, and the activation rule.
- `FreteTab.autoVolume.test.tsx` (4) — drives the real component inside
  `<Tabs keepMounted={false}>`, unmounting the panel mid-fetch.
- Both new files verified **red-on-mutation**.
- `pnpm --filter @delfrance/web test` — 1662/1662, 0 unhandled errors.
  `vitest.setup.ts` gains a `scrollIntoView` shim (Mantine's Combobox calls it
  from a timer; without it the TypeError surfaced as an unhandled error
  attributed to an unrelated test).
- lint 0 errors, typecheck clean.

Refs #371

author: jinwoo-h
body:
Fixes STA-1756 (#8585).

## What was broken

`launchRelay` probes for an existing relay socket and, when `--connect` to it fails, it removed the socket and launched a fresh detached relay over the same path:

```ts
// Why: stale socket from a crashed relay — remove it so the fresh launch can bind at the same path.
await execCommand(conn, `rm -f ${shellEscape(sockFile)}`, { signal })
```

That comment states an inference the code never checked. A refused `--connect` is loss of contact, not proof of death. On Unix, unlinking a socket path does not close a listening socket its owner already holds, so when the old relay was alive it kept running, kept its PTYs and every shell/agent inside them, and became permanently unreachable. With the shipped `--grace-time 0`, a relay still holding a PTY takes the `configured` grace branch with `timeoutMs=0`, which arms no timer — so nothing ever reaped it.

The relay already refuses this displacement on its own: a fresh daemon that hits `EADDRINUSE` probe-connects the path and declines to steal it from a live owner (`src/relay/relay.ts`, `onInitialError`). The unconditional `rm -f` destroyed exactly the evidence that interlock runs on.

## Reproduction (real processes, not mocks)

Two live-daemon files, both in the new `relay socket ownership` CI job:

`ssh-relay-launch-ownership.integration.test.ts` drives the **production** `launchRelay` against a real detached relay holding a real PTY, over an `SshConnection` whose exec runs the same command strings through a local shell. The reconnect is made to fail the way it fails in the field — by rotating the endpoint credential the daemon read at startup, which is what an interrupted deploy does. It asserts the incumbent keeps its socket and its shell and that nothing was started over it. **That test fails when the guard is reverted.** A second case proves the other direction: a killed relay's leftover socket is taken over normally.

`ssh-relay-socket-owner.integration.test.ts` isolates the decision, including a control arm that performs the old raw unlink and observes the orphan appear: the socket path answers for a daemon owning `ptys: 0` while the incumbent is still alive with the user's shell, its log ending at `Grace started (socket client closed): timeoutMs=0, branch=configured, ptys=1` and never saying anything again.

## The fix

One new boundary, `src/main/ssh/ssh-relay-socket-owner.ts`: the socket's own owner decides. No pidfile, no process scavenger.

`relaySocketOwnerProbeCommand` asks the host who owns the path, and answers `exited` only on positive evidence that nothing does:

- **`lsof -t -a -U`**, when present, both ways: a match proves an owner is there, and a clean run that matches nothing is absence evidence.
- **A connect probe**, retried three times — `ECONNREFUSED` is not by itself absence, since a live listener with a full accept backlog refuses too (measured: 199 of 200 simultaneous connects to a live listener with `backlog: 1`).
- **`/proc/net/unix`**, the authority where it exists: an owner inventory that ran and did not list the path, compared on the pathname column exactly. A refused connect alone never proves absence; with no inventory at all the verdict is `unverifiable` and nothing is launched. (`ENOENT` is the one direct answer — the path is simply not there.)

Outcomes are `live` / `exited` / `unverifiable`, following `src/shared/pty-liveness-verdict.ts`. `requireUnownedRelaySocket` throws `RelaySocketOwnerLiveError` for anything but `exited`; `launchRelay` calls it in place of the raw `rm -f` and rethrows the typed error from the outer catch so it cannot fall through to a fresh launch.

Verified on a real Linux host with no `lsof`: a saturated live listener reports `LIVE` and keeps its socket; a genuinely stale inode is taken over. Verified across `sh`/`dash`/`bash`/`zsh`, and for socket paths containing spaces, apostrophes and backslashes.

Behaviour deliberately preserved: ordinary stale sockets are still cleaned up and the fresh launch proceeds; relays intentionally surviving with live PTYs are never displaced; empty husks are already handled on main by the `idle-no-ptys` grace branch.

## Reset, the recovery path this change points at

`forceStopRelayForTarget` removed the socket even when it found no owner to kill or the kill was refused — on a host where the lookup came back silent that stranded exactly the relay the user asked it to stop. It now stops the owner, checks an inventory to confirm it is gone, and reports an actionable failure otherwise. It no longer unlinks anything: a relay that stops cleanly removes its own path, one that had to be killed leaves an inode the deploy path releases under its identity guard, and unlinking here would need that same guard and still race a relay binding the path in between.

## Trade-off

A relay that is alive but permanently unreachable now fails the deploy instead of silently connecting. That is the honest outcome: the alternative is what this PR removes — a connection that appears to work while a full process tree leaks forever. A generic owner-live failure stays retryable, so `ssh.ts`'s bounded relay-lost backoff still gives a transiently busy relay six chances to recover *with the user's sessions*, which the old path destroyed. A wrapped `RelayVersionMismatchError` stays terminal, since no amount of backoff changes a version. If a relay stays unreachable, **Reset remote relay** stops it deliberately.

## Scope notes

- **Not fixed here, different mechanism:** the one-relay-per-build accumulation in the issue's later comments is upgrade churn (STA-3832) — version-scoped install dirs mean the new relay binds a different path, so nothing is stolen and nothing is unlinked; the old relay is simply abandoned.
- **Windows is untouched by this branch**, but review surfaced two pre-existing Windows analogues worth their own tickets: `launchWindowsRelay` moves to a fallback pipe on a failed reconnect and rotates the shared credential, abandoning the incumbent; and Windows GC reads an inconclusive pipe probe (`WAITING`) as safe-to-delete.
- **Residual, stated plainly:** on a host with neither `/proc/net/unix` nor a working `lsof`, a stale socket is never taken over and the deploy asks the user to reset. That is the safe direction, and no such host is known to run the relay. All three reviewers examined this residual and agreed not to re-file it.
- **No reuse of `hasLiveRelaySocket`**: that probe is deliberately `test -S`-only because its job is to *never authorize* deleting a version dir. This one must prove absence to authorize an unlink.
- **Remote wire compatibility**: no RPC params, stream opcodes, or host-published content change — only which shell command the client runs on the host.

## Tests

- `ssh-relay-socket-owner.test.ts` — command shape (lsof proven functional before it counts, inventory requirement, exact pathname column, removes nothing, retry budget), verdict parsing, every refusal path including abort, and the terminal-cause unwrap.
- `ssh-relay-socket-displacement.test.ts` — the shipping wiring: no `--detached` launch and no credential rotation on `live` or `unverifiable`; both still happen on `released`.
- `ssh-relay-launch-ownership.integration.test.ts` / `ssh-relay-socket-owner.integration.test.ts` — the live journeys above.
- `ssh-relay-reset.test.ts` — the real reset script against a sandboxed host with a real killable socket owner: kill works, kill refused, and a host that cannot name the owner.

Reverting the guard fails the live journey and four wiring tests. `src/main/ssh` (1621 tests), `src/main/ipc`, typecheck, and the changed-code quality gate all pass. Two `pty-handler-spawn-environment` Windows/WSL failures reproduce on clean `origin/main` on macOS and are unrelated.

Reviewed across four rounds by three independent GPT-5.6 reviewers, all three now SHIP. Every finding above the nit line was reproduced before it was fixed — including two that only appear on Linux (

author: melodyyyyin
body:
## Summary

PR4 is the Qwen3-Omni-specific adapter and observable text-result layer on top of PR3's generic runtime. Its production changes are limited to:

- `sglang_omni/models/qwen3_omni/bootstrap.py`
- `sglang_omni/models/qwen3_omni/request_builders.py`
- `sglang_omni/models/qwen3_omni/stages.py`

Generic resume hooks, continuation ownership, KV transfer, and admission remain in PR3.

## Qwen resume and result state

The adapter provides `QWEN_THINKER_PD_RESUME_SCHEMA` plus Qwen state builder/restorer hooks. It projects only msgpack-safe state needed by Decode:

- original prompt token IDs and request parameters;
- streaming/result metadata;
- first-token and output-logprob continuity;
- Qwen mRoPE position delta when present;
- stage payload needed by the existing Qwen result path.

Consumed Prefill tensors, projected embeddings, and media tensors are not copied because transferred KV represents their effect. The tokenizer is rebound from the Decode-local scheduler rather than serialized.

Validated behavior covers terminal `max_new_tokens=1`, deterministic text, EOS, stop string/token, streaming and non-streaming, token IDs, numeric logprobs, usage, finish reason, weight version, image input, and mRoPE restoration.

## Supported scope

- `Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct` at revision `26291f793822fb6be9555850f06dfe95f2d7e695`
- BF16, TP=1, page size=1
- same-node CUDA IPC
- RadixCache and CUDA graph disabled
- thinker text output
- text and image prompts

This PR does not claim general audio/video support. TP>1, cross-node transfer, RadixCache ownership, speculative decoding, grammar/custom-logit resume, and talker/code2wav PD splitting remain outside scope.

## Correctness and lifecycle reliability

With `temperature=0` and `seed=17`, PD and non-PD matched exactly for `max_new_tokens=1/2/3/16/64`, EOS, stop string/token, streaming, and image/mRoPE. Output token IDs, decoded text, usage, finish reason, weight version, and all numeric output logprobs matched.

The rebuilt stack then completed 1,000 persistent requests:

| Phase | Concurrency | Completed | Errors | Time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mixed sequential | 1 | 500/500 | 0 | 186.08 s |
| mixed concurrent | 16 | 500/500 | 0 | 46.87 s |

The mix included streaming `max_new_tokens=1/2/3/16` and 25 long 8128-token prompts in each half. Final health was 0 active / 0 pending, with no crash, cleanup assertion, incomplete stream, or monotonic leak.

## Final clean repeated benchmark

Configuration: H200, NV18-connected, BF16, TP=1, page size=1, same-node CUDA IPC, RadixCache/CUDA graph disabled, `max_running_requests=4`. Core cells use 5 warmups + 20 measured requests; mixed cells use 10 warmups + 100 measured requests. Client streaming records TTFT, TPOT, E2E, errors, timeouts, and incomplete streams.

Accepted clean repetitions were PD r1/r3/r6 and non-PD r1/r5/r6. Full-run telemetry covered startup, warmup, measurement, and shutdown. Every accepted measured request completed; errors, timeouts, and incomplete streams were all zero.

Values below are medians across three repetitions; latency is client-observed p50/p95 seconds.

| Workload | Mode | req/s | TTFT | TPOT | E2E |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128/128 c8 | PD | 0.5327 | 0.113/0.243 | 0.117/0.118 | 15.060/15.100 |
| 128/128 c8 | non-PD | 0.5302 | 7.607/7.710 | 0.059/0.059 | 15.097/15.189 |
| 8128/32 c8 | PD | 1.9371 | 0.202/1.192 | 0.117/0.120 | 3.881/4.462 |
| 8128/32 c8 | non-PD | 1.7014 | 2.634/2.828 | 0.065/0.068 | 4.648/4.850 |
| 8128/32 c16 | PD | 1.9300 | 1.113/2.537 | 0.147/0.227 | 6.344/8.363 |
| 8128/32 c16 | non-PD | 1.7051 | 5.061/7.465 | 0.065/0.068 | 7.063/9.465 |
| mixed c8 | PD | 0.8302 | 0.180/0.365 | 0.103/0.231 | 7.905/13.107 |
| mixed c8 | non-PD | 0.7946 | 4.390/5.965 | 0.060/0.061 | 8.754/13.623 |
| mixed c16 | PD | 0.8315 | 0.182/1.124 | 0.176/0.530 | 16.669/22.379 |
| mixed c16 | non-PD | 0.7937 | 14.216/15.935 | 0.059/0.061 | 17.639/23.504 |

Against one non-PD thinker, PD improves median throughput by 0.5–13.9% and greatly reduces TTFT queueing, but median TPOT is worse by 74–196% depending on workload.

## Equal-hardware comparison

Two non-PD thinker replicas ran on the same physical thinker GPUs used by PD (GPU0/GPU2), with equivalent shared-stage placement on GPU1 and round-robin routing. Each of three clean repetitions used identical requests and warmups.

| Workload | PD median req/s | 2× non-PD median req/s | 2× Δ | PD total GPU-s | 2× non-PD total GPU-s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8128/32 c8 | 1.9371 | 2.8516 | +47.2% | 93.064 | 63.257 |
| mixed c8 | 0.8302 | 1.0120 | +21.9% | 1084.085 | 890.355 |

GPU-seconds are measurement wall time × three physical GPUs, totaled across the three repetitions for the fixed request counts.

Two non-PD replicas outperform PD in throughput and fixed-work GPU-seconds. PD retains much lower mixed-workload TTFT p95 (0.365 s versus 7.710 s), but this is an isolation/tail-latency tradeoff, not a resource-efficiency win. No PD resource-efficiency claim is made.

## Stack and validation

- **PR1 — #1517:** topology and launch identity
- **PR2 — #1538:** continuation/handoff lifecycle
- **PR3 — #1596:** generic runtime/KV/admission seams
- **PR4 — #1599 (this PR):** base `pd_runtime`; Qwen-only adapter and focused tests

Final validation on `pd_result@c20f4a2f3b3419b2f103191a10fe42cc8feae100`:

- `pytest -q tests/unit_test/pipeline tests/unit_test/scheduling` — **769 passed**
- `pre-commit run --all-files` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
- tracked worktree clean

author: liberatingscripture
body:
Follow-up to #127. That PR fixed a stale embed by re-pinning it to the **1 Corinthians** playlist — which would itself have gone stale the moment the show moved to the next book. This makes the slot self-maintaining instead.

## The change

The "Latest Episodes" YouTube iframe now frames the channel's curated show-wide **"Found in Translation"** playlist (`PLZJ2_GOQPBSqVAh8S7AFqmpcK_I7eEz6H`), which the show owner keeps current — it already leads with the newest episode.

That makes all three embeds in the block **show-level**, matching the Apple and Spotify ones beside it, so none of them need touching when an episode ships. The embed has now been re-pinned twice for the same underlying reason (first a single video, then a per-book playlist), which is the thing this fixes.

The `?si=` token is dropped — it was tied to the old 1 Corinthians share link, and YouTube's canonical playlist embed omits it anyway.

## The option not taken

The auto-uploads playlist (`UU` + the channel id minus its `UC` prefix — here `UUYRSxbodu4NIzsHYRavuR4g`) is the other self-maintaining choice and is *guaranteed* newest-first. It was rejected because it carries the channel's ~11 Shorts as well, so a newly posted Short would take the lead spot in the embed. The curated playlist trades that ordering guarantee for episodes-only content; the tradeoff is recorded in `CLAUDE.md` so it doesn't get re-litigated from scratch.

## Docs

The `CLAUDE.md` row for this page is rewritten: it now says these embeds are deliberately show-level, and explicitly says **not** to re-pin the YouTube one to a single video or a per-book playlist.

## Verification

- `npm run check` → 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `npm run build` → clean; `npm run check:links` → 349 pages, 32,028 internal links, no breaks
- Confirmed in the browser that the iframe `src` is the show playlist and that it renders a real player leading with "1 Corinthians 1 & 2 in the LIT Bible with Dr. Miguel A. De La Torre"; Apple and Spotify embeds still render
- `src/data/podcast-feed.xml` churn from `fetch:podcast` (a `<generator>` timestamp only) reverted rather than swept in

## Summary

CubeMaster's integration test package panics at TestMain on current master: pkg/base/db.Init is now a thin wrapper over dao.Default(), which panics with "dao: Open has not been called yet" until the shared handle is established by dao.Open at app startup. Mechanical sweep to align source comments with rule 17: self-documenting code, comments earn their line only when they carry information the code cannot show.

## Scope

100 files, 426 insertions / 648 deletions (net -222 lines). Comments and JSDoc only — zero code changes.

## Categories of removals

- **PR / issue references in comments** (`(#NNN)`, `PR #NNN`, `Closes #NNN`, `see #NNN`, `regression for #NNN`) — dropped from source; those refs belong in commit messages and PR bodies, not the tree.
- **Attribution by name** (`Hoie 2026-XX-XX`, `per Hoie`, `reviewoie R1 caught`, `Reviewoie #624`) — state the constraint, drop the source.
- **Change-history narrative** (`before this PR`, `pre-fix`, `pre-PR`, `previous implementation`, `used to`) — the git log tells that story.
- **Multi-paragraph walkthroughs** in `sync.ts`, `transfers.ts` (repo), `auto-suggest.ts`, `holdings.ts` (repo), `budgets.ts` (calculation) trimmed from 10–20-line design narratives to 3–7-line intent + WHY.
- **Describe/test titles** with trailing `(#NNN)` / `(#NNN case)` / `(regression for #NNN)` trimmed to the behavior name only.

## Preservation policy

- JSDoc on public / abstraction surfaces (`extractCashFlowsBySecurity`, `MwrResult`, module-level constants like `RECONNECT_MAX_FATAL_ATTEMPTS`) kept as intent + short usage.
- One-line WHY on non-obvious constraints kept where the code alone doesn't derive the reason: advisory-lock ordering vs. `deleteTransactions`, cash-shape detector's two-channel rationale, cold-sync rollover suppression, `<Fragment>`-vs-wrapper CSS dependency, direct-children combinators, and similar.
- `TODO` markers, `// eslint-disable-*` hints, and license headers untouched.

## Gates

- `bun run typecheck` — clean
- `bun run lint` — clean
- `bun test` — 1305 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail (unchanged from `upstream/main` baseline)

## Reviewer alignment

The comment-hygiene rule is now encoded in `~/claude/CLAUDE.md` rule 17, backing memory at `~/claude/memory/feedback_comment_hygiene.md`, and the `budget-reviewer` agent's §F was updated in workspace commit `1e1013e` so a fresh reviewer session flags these violations proactively going forward.

## Judgment calls worth a second look

- **`useServerEvents.ts` module-level JSDocs left intact.** Each of `RECONNECT_MAX_FATAL_ATTEMPTS`, `RECONNECT_FATAL_SLOW_MS`, `RESYNC_JITTER_MS`, `RESYNC_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` carries a long WHY paragraph justifying the value against alternatives. They're on module-level named constants (IDE tooltip earns space) and the WHY is not derivable from the identifier alone. Kept.
- **`extractCashFlowsBySecurity` header preserved.** The 15-line JSDoc on this public API documents the cash-exclusion invariant and Plaid `type` mapping — a fresh reader hitting the function without it would guess wrong about which txns are counted. Kept.
- **`transfers.ts` (repo) advisory-lock comments trimmed but not deleted.** The WHY of the row-level `FOR SHARE` vs. the `pg_advisory_xact_lock` interaction is a genuine constraint that reviewers who've been bitten by READ-COMMITTED write-skew will want documented. Kept in tighter form.

author: bennetleff
body:
Diagnostic only. `pcb/temper.kicad_pcb` never opened for writing — sha256 `26981fea2d…` verified identical before and after.

## The question

`pad_connectivity_audit` partitions 139 nets into **60 connected / 70 broken / 9 `zone_dependent_unmeasured`**. The audit is deliberately zone-blind: it answers "does the segment/via graph join these pads", and refuses to classify a net whose unjoined pads all have zones declared. **Nobody had ever resolved those 9.** If pours connected them, the real figure was 69/139.

## Verdict: zero rescued. 60/139 stands, and the gap is 79 nets.

The non-flattering answer, and the measured one.

## The 9

`+170V_BUS`, `DC_BUS_RTN`, `PWR_RTN`, `SW_NODE`, `ac_n`, `power_in.ntc-no`, `tank.c_tank1-p2`, `w1_1`, `w1_2`

**That set is the board's primary power distribution** — the DC bus and its return, the switch node, a mains line, the bypass-relay contacts, and the tank capacitor. `DC_BUS_RTN` was established earlier to sit at ~−170V relative to signal ground. **The nets that do not connect are the power path.**

Re-measured live rather than inherited from the 2026-08-17 doc, which was taken against a different board — the set is identical despite the board changing underneath, and the 60/70/9 split is unchanged.

## Method, and its validation

`kicad-cli pcb drc --refill-zones --save-board` on a scratch copy, using KiCad's own connectivity engine (`unconnected_items`) — the honest-fill path PR #1298 established.

**Validated against the full known-answer population, not a sample**: 0/60 `connected` nets false-positive, and 70/70 `broken` nets still correctly flagged after refill. That second one is a real positive control — a rescue *could* have appeared there and did not. Deterministic across 3 independent runs: 815 violations, 265 unconnected items, byte-identical net sets each time.

## Why they fail — the zones fill, then fragment

The zones do produce real copper. `+170V_BUS` fills **19 separate polygon islands across 4 layers**. They simply never touch each other — the pour fragments into disjoint per-pad-local islands.

**This is the same mechanism as the `isolated_copper` characterization in handoff §13**, not a missing-fill artifact. The zone generator is producing pours that do not connect what they are pouring over.

## The committed board carries no fill data at all

**151 zone outlines declared, 0 with `filled_polygon` data.** (The handoff's "96" predates further zone generation; the zero-fill finding holds.)

So the board as committed cannot connect anything through pours — and when filled honestly, the pours fragment. Both halves of that need fixing before zone-dependent connectivity means anything.

## What this changes

- The headline **60/139 is correct**; no upward revision.
- The routing gap is **79 nets, not 70**.
- **9 of those 79 are the power distribution, and their failure mode is zone fragmentation rather than routing** — a different problem from the other 70, needing zone-generator work rather than router work.

Evidence: `docs/evidence/2026-08-18-zone-dependent-unmeasured-connectivity-resolution.md`.

author: asrbekshokirovich-bot
body:
Re-parsing the 21 stuck documents runs **~12 hours** end to end on the subscription backend. Three knobs to shorten that. None changes the default behaviour of anything.

## The measurement that matters

Field groups are nowhere near equal, and the timeouts already in the code say so — they were set from measured healthy tails:

| group | timeout | why |
|---|---|---|
| `calendar`, `tuition` | 240s | default; tails are outliers |
| `requirements` | 900s | healthy runs reach 1121s |
| `scholarships` | 900s | healthy runs reach 716s |
| `documents_required` | 1800s | healthy runs reach 1381s |

An earlier estimate in this session averaged a single per-call figure across all five and came out at ~5h. That was wrong: the average hides that two groups dominate.

## 1. `reparse --skip-groups`

`scholarships` is one of the two heavy groups **and** no screen in the app renders it. `retry-failed` has skipped it by default for exactly that reason; `reparse` had no way to. Dropping it takes roughly a **quarter** off the run — not the fifth a flat per-group average would suggest.

## 2. `reparse --shard I/N`

Splits one selection across N processes with no coordination: each takes the ids whose hash falls in its bucket, so two runs never pick the same document and never need a claim table.

`abs()` matters here. `hashtext` is signed and Postgres keeps the sign through `%`, so a bare `hashtext(id::text) % 2 = 1` would leave the entire negative half of the hash space belonging to **no shard at all** — roughly half the documents silently skipped, with both processes reporting success. A test pins that the shards are disjoint *and* cover everything.

## 3. `UNI_DB_CLI_CONCURRENCY`

The CLI backend's "at most one `claude` subprocess anywhere on the host" becomes a counting semaphore:

- in-process: `BoundedSemaphore`
- across processes: a **pool** of flock files, each tried non-blocking, so a caller takes the first free slot instead of queueing behind one file while another sits idle

Slot 0 deliberately keeps the original filename. If it were renamed, a concurrency-1 run would sit *beside* a process that predates this setting rather than contend with it — two `claude` calls where the guarantee says one, and neither side internally inconsistent enough for a test to notice.

**Default stays 1.** That is the original guarantee and the right value for the nightly crawl, which shares the subscription with whoever is using it interactively.

The honest caveat, also written into the config comment: N slots consume the subscription's usage window N times as fast, so wall clock does not simply divide by N. Hitting a limit is not fatal — the backend waits the window out and resumes — but the speed-up is a hope, not arithmetic.

## Combined effect

| | wall clock |
|---|---|
| today | ~12h |
| `--skip-groups scholarships` | ~9h |
| + 2 shards at concurrency 2 | **~4.5h** |

## Verification

- 747 unit tests pass (`test_llm_anthropic.py` deselected — it fails in this sandbox for unrelated environment reasons and passes in CI)
- 10 new tests, including: six callers against three slots never produce a fourth; every caller still gets through (a leaked slot would deadlock the run); shards are disjoint and total; skipping every group is rejected rather than silently doing nothing and reporting `ok=0`

## A false alarm worth recording

An 8-minute `claude` subprocess looked like the 240s timeout being ignored. It was not — `documents_required` carries a deliberate 1800s ceiling. No bug; checked before reporting.

---

author: gondalaimafia
body:
## Why

`scripts/` was outside the workspace globs and had no tsconfig, so `npm run typecheck` never saw it. That was not cosmetic: the gap was hiding real compile errors in shipped operator, release, and governance tooling (including the gate scripts themselves). Two scripts called `runGraphQuery(db, q)` with two arguments against a mandatory three-argument signature that throws `graph_tenant_scope_required`, so they failed at runtime immediately.

## Config approach (and why)

I followed the existing `evals/` precedent exactly. `evals/` is a non-workspace directory run via `tsx` that gets typechecked through a dedicated `evals/tsconfig.json` (extends `tsconfig.base.json`) plus a minimal `evals/package.json` with `"type": "module"`.

- Added `scripts/tsconfig.json` extending `tsconfig.base.json` (identical strictness to the rest of the repo — `strict: true`, NodeNext, etc.). No laxer settings.
- Added `scripts/package.json` (`"type": "module"`, `private`, not in the workspace globs). Without it, NodeNext resolves `scripts/*.ts` as CommonJS and every `import.meta` becomes a spurious `TS1470` error; the module marker makes the compiler see them as the ESM that `tsx` already runs them as. This mirrors `evals/package.json` and does **not** make `scripts/` a workspace (globs remain `packages/*`, `apps/*`).
- Root `typecheck` script now runs `... && tsc -p scripts/tsconfig.json --noEmit`.

I did not widen the workspace globs: `scripts/` is a scripts directory, not a package, and adding it as a workspace would pull it into install/build/dependency resolution.

## CI coverage

CI's existing **Typecheck** step (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the `release-gates` job) runs `npm run typecheck`. Because the root script now appends the `scripts/` compile, that same step covers `scripts/` with no workflow change needed.

## Errors the new coverage surfaced, and the fix for each

| File:line | Error | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `git-temporal.ts:41,45` | `TS2554` runGraphQuery got 2 args, needs 3 | Scope the read-back to the repo just backfilled (`result.repoId`); every ingested node carries that `repo_id`, so the tenant view counts exactly what was written. |
| `slo-report.ts:21-28` | `TS2554` (x4) same | Added a dedicated named operator scope `{ tenantId: "slo-report" }`, mirroring the graph benchmark's own `BENCH_SCOPE`. The SLO gate measures query latency, not customer data. |

body:
## Summary

Audited the live site (playsabotage.com) and found the homepage was silently broken: the Railway multiplayer backend was unreachable, and the resulting unguarded `ReferenceError` in `connectSocket()` aborted every script statement queued after it on page load — including the drifting-pawns background animation, which had **never rendered on the live site** since it was added (two commits ago).

Railway has since been renewed by @AZ-sort and is back online (verified), but this PR also makes the page resilient so this class of failure can't blank the homepage again, regardless of backend uptime.

- Guard `connectSocket()` so a missing/failed socket.io load shows a clear "multiplayer server offline — try Local Game" state instead of throwing.
- Fix the same unguarded-`socket` assumption in `handleUrlRouting()` (room-code URL links), which hit the identical failure mode.
- Move the background-canvas init ahead of the network/auth init so it's structurally independent of backend failures, not just guarded.
- `checkAuth()` was calling `showAuthModal()` for any anonymous visitor — a forced login wall on load. This had never actually run in production (the ReferenceError above prevented it from ever being scheduled), so it was untested. Now defaults anonymous visitors to guest mode, consistent with the existing "Continue as guest" flow and the opt-in nav "Log In" button.
- Consolidated the socket.io server origin into one `PS_SERVER_URL` constant instead of three hardcoded copies.

**Small, high-leverage fixes from the same audit:**
- Deleted a duplicate `twitter:card` meta tag that was silently downgrading shared-link previews from a large banner to a small thumbnail.
- Added `preconnect` hints for Google Fonts.
- Aligned canonical/`og:url`/JSON-LD/sitemap/robots.txt to the actually-served host (`www.playsabotage.com` — apex 308-redirects there).
- Demoted the redundant `<h1>` on the hidden local-game setup panel to `<h2>`.

## Test plan
- [x] Verified in a real browser against the live Railway backend (now restored) — socket connects, live "N players online" counter populates, background canvas paints ~50k pixels, no forced login modal.
- [x] Verified against a simulated backend outage (broken socket.io script src) — no uncaught errors, background still renders, homepage shows "multiplayer server offline — try Local Game below" instead of a silently-empty lobby.
- [x] `node -c`-equivalent syntax check on all three inline `<script>` blocks — all parse cleanly.
- [ ] Manual pass on the Vercel preview deploy for this branch before merging (not yet done by me — recommend checking it live before merge).

author: ericgriffin
body:
Fixes #828.

## The reported problem, and what actually caused it

A diver logged a 12 L cylinder, 150 bar used, 44 min, 13.2 m average depth.
By hand that is 17.6 L/min; the app showed 16.5. The issue attributed the gap
to the app adding three minutes (a safety stop) to the dive time.

It does not. The runtime is used verbatim, and there is now a test that proves
it by comparing a 44-minute dive against a 47-minute one. The gap was entirely
on the volume side of the calculation:

| Calculation | Gas used | SAC |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hand arithmetic (ideal gas) | 1800 L | 17.63 L/min |
| App before this change | 1689 L | 16.55 L/min |
| App after this change, real gas | 1712 L | 16.77 L/min |
| App after this change, ideal gas | 1800 L | 17.63 L/min |

`gasVolume()` applied a virial compressibility correction (Z), so a "12 L at
200 bar" cylinder was treated as holding ~2287 free liters rather than the
ideal-gas 2400. That correction is physically right and matches Subsurface,
but it is not what divers compute by hand, and it accounted for ~4.9% of the
difference.

## The genuine bug

The remaining ~1.3% was a unit inconsistency. `gasVolume()` returned liters at
**1 atm** (it divided by 1.01325), while every caller then divided by an
ambient pressure ratio written as `depth / 10 + 1`, which is in **bar**.
Dividing atm-liters by a bar-referenced ratio understated every volumetric SAC
rate by 1.32%.

The volumetric and pressure lanes therefore disagreed with each other:
`Dive.sacPressure` (bar/min) and `_zCorrectedSacRate` converted back to bar and
were correct, while `Dive.sac` (L/min), the statistics SAC, and the segment
SAC were not.

`gasVolume()` is now referenced to **1 bar**, matching both the ambient ratio
and the convention divers use (a 12 L 200 bar cylinder holds 2400 L). Two
downstream conversions that existed only to patch over the mismatch are gone:

- `CylinderSac.sacVolume` no longer divides by the standard atmosphere
- `GasAnalysisService._zCorrectedSacRate` no longer multiplies by it

## The new preference

`Settings > Units > Gas calculations` selects **Real gas** (default, current
behavior) or **Ideal gas** (matches hand calculation and training-agency
tables). It applies everywhere the app converts between cylinder pressure and
gas volume, so numbers never round-trip through two different models:

- logged SAC, per-cylinder SAC, segment SAC
- gas statistics
- the plan engine, bailout solver, and plan calculator
- the rock-bottom and gas-consumption calculators, which were unconditionally
  ideal-gas before and now join the system

`gasVolume()` and `pressureAfterConsuming()` take the model as a **required**
parameter, so no call site can silently inherit an assumption. That flushed out
14 call sites across 6 files, including two in `plan_engine.dart` that a grep
for `gasVolume(` had missed.

Services take the model by constructor injection from `gasModelProvider`, so
flipping the preference rebuilds them and invalidates every dependent readout
with no manual cache busting. `Dive.sac` was a getter on a pure entity with no
container access, so it becomes `Dive.sacFor(GasModel)`, following the seam
`extractDiveFieldValue` already established for `sacUnit`.

## A correction worth flagging

Air's compressibility factor **dips below 1 up to about 121.5 bar** and only
rises above it at fill pressures. The two models therefore move numbers in
opposite directions depending on the pressure involved:

- a full 200 bar cylinder holds ~4% **less** than ideal (the reported symptom)
- a ~60 bar rock-bottom reserve holds slightly **more** than ideal, so the
  computed reserve pressure comes out ~0.9% **lower**

That is a safety-relevant number moving in the non-conservative direction. It
is under 1%, and it is now pinned by a test that states the reason. It is also
why the preference has to be global rather than per-screen.

## Schema

v154 adds `diver_settings.gas_model TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'real'`, with the
usual `beforeOpen` backstop so a database arriving by restore or sync-adopt
(which never runs `onUpgrade`) still gets the column. The sync serializer seeds
`gasModel` so a payload from a pre-v154 peer hydrates to the default.

## Behavior changes on upgrade

- **All existing users' volumetric SAC and gas statistics rise 1.3%** from the
  unit fix, independent of the preference. Bar/min SAC is unchanged.
- **The rock-bottom and consumption calculators change** for everyone, since
  they were ideal-gas and now default to real gas.

Both are worth a release note.

## Testing

New coverage:

- `test/core/utils/gas_model_test.dart` - both models, the 1 bar reference, the
  `pressureHoldingVolume` inverse, and the Z crossover
- `test/features/dive_log/domain/entities/dive_sac_gas_model_test.dart` - the
  issue's exact scenario under both models, plus the no-padding proof
- `test/features/dive_log/domain/entities/cylinder_sac_volume_test.dart`
- `test/core/constants/dive_field_extractor_gas_model_test.dart`
- `test/features/settings/gas_model_setting_test.dart`
- `test/core/database/migration_v154_gas_model_test.dart`
- pre-v154 sync payload cases in `sync_diver_settings_fallback_test.dart`
- a rock-bottom test asserting the model moves reserve *pressure* but not
  reserve *volume*
- `tank_spec_test.dart` now asserts the real model reproduces the AL80's rated
  77.4 cuft to within 1%, where ideal overshoots to 81

Updated expectations, each a deliberate consequence of the reference fix:
`dive_sac_fix_test`, `dive_field_extractor_test`, `gas_compressibility_test`,
`gas_consumption_test`, `rock_bottom_test` (hand-verified reference cases
pinned to `GasModel.ideal`, which is the arithmetic they were computed with),
`cylinders_card_test`, `dive_table_view_test`, `dive_list_tile_sac_test`.

Four `SettingsNotifier` test doubles gained `setGasModel`, and four provider
containers in statistics/dashboard tests now pin `gasModelProvider` rather than
standing up the whole settings stack.

`flutter analyze` is clean across the project.

## Known gap

There is no widget test for the new picker dialog. The existing suite has no
coverage of any unit picker, so a bespoke navigation test for this one would be
out of step with the codebase, but the dialog is untested UI.

- The Subnet scanners table listed every enrolled asset, producing an overly long list; admins should see only currently enabled scanners and have a single, discoverable control to add more.

- Split scanner data in the route handler by calling `network_devices_repo.list_scanners(company_id)` and deriving `enabled_scanners` and `available_scanners`, then render those to the template. (`app/features/assets/routes.py`)

- Updated the devices template to render only enabled scanners and, when the user can configure, include a persistent empty row with a dropdown of available assets, interval input, and an `Add scanner` button that submits to the new endpoint. (`app/templates/devices/index.html`)

author: kwoo24-oss
body:
## Summary

- add explicit `all`, `api`, and `worker` process roles while preserving the local all-in-one default
- run Kubernetes API serving and durable workers as separate containers in the same single-replica, RWO-backed Pod
- make worker shutdown bounded and observable with broadcast-first stop signals, a shared join deadline, loop heartbeat probes, and `/health` runner snapshots
- make durable queue claims crash-safe with attempt-at-claim accounting, explicit claim/abandon state, credit-back for unattempted batches, and an advisory-lock rescuer
- harden shared Bare-Git writes with storage-backed per-vault locking, exact-parent commits, ref CAS, same-name vault creation locking, and deterministic GitPython handle cleanup
- serialize migrations and role reconciliation for multi-process startup
- move known blocking filesystem, S3, hashing, grep, and response-encoding work off the serving event loop
- retry ambiguous MCP transport failures only for an explicit read-only allowlist; bump `akb-mcp` to 2.2.1
- add the reproducible 300-concurrency scenario and the accepted architecture record with supporting design analysis

## Deployment shape

The Kubernetes base remains deliberately conservative:

- `replicas: 1`
- `strategy: Recreate`
- one Pod and one RWO Git PVC
- `backend` container: `AKB_PROCESS_ROLE=api`
- `worker` sidecar: `AKB_PROCESS_ROLE=worker`

Local Docker Compose continues to use `AKB_PROCESS_ROLE=all`. This PR isolates the serving event loop, but does not yet authorize horizontal API scaling or removal of the API PVC mount.

## Validation

- changed Python files: Ruff passed
- focused backend regression suite: 227 passed
- MCP proxy contract/reconnect suite: 25 passed
- full endpoint-driven backend validation: 805 passed
- split-role MCP E2E: 88 passed
- asset backend/frontend/proxy suites: 45 / 35 / 15 passed
- Playwright smoke: 2 passed
- 300-concurrency scenario in all-in-one mode: PASS, 3,300 operations
- 300-concurrency scenario in split API/worker mode: PASS, 3,300 operations
- split-role runtime inspection: API durable runners 0, worker loops 10, healthy heartbeat, pending queues 0, no leaked Git child processes

## Remaining gates

The follow-up topology still requires a networked single-writer gitd, API-side Git/PVC removal, split-aware operational health and repair drills, MCP multi-replica session ownership, and distributed audit/throttling authority before increasing replicas or switching to RollingUpdate.

### **User description** Closes #32 Closes #33 Closes #34 #14 백로그에서 분리한 주제 3건입니다. 주제가 6개 → **9개** 가 되고 카테고리 균형이 `math 3/cs 2/ai 1` → `math 5/cs 2/ai 2` 로 바뀝니다. 커밋을 주제별로 분리했으니 커밋 단위로 읽으시는 편이 편합니다. | 커밋 | 주제 | | --- | --- | | `e9b71a9` | #32 `ai/next-word` — 다음 단어 맞히기 | | `bd44b86` | #33 `math/monte-carlo-pi` — 점을 뿌려서 π 구하기 | | `5e5db58` | #34 `math/repeating-nines` — 0.999… 는 1인가 + 시리즈 개통 | ## 시리즈 라벨을 바꿨습니다 (#34) #12 는 `0.999…` 를 `float`(**부동소수점 2부작** — "컴퓨터가 소수를 다루는 방식과 그 틈") 2편으로 지목했습니다. 그대로 묶으면 **"무한소수는 다 오차가 있다"는 정반대 오해**를 줍니다. `0.999… = 1` 은 근사가 아니라 정확히 참이기 때문입니다. 두 주제의 진짜 공통점은 따로 있었습니다: - `0.1` 은 10진법에서 유한하지만 **2진법에서는 무한소수**라 컴퓨터가 잘라내야 합니다 - `0.999…` 는 10진법에서 무한하지만 값은 **정확히 1** 입니다 둘 다 "끝없이 이어지는 소수를 어떻게 다루는가" 입니다. ``` float → infinite-decimal "무한소수 2부작 — 끝없이 이어지는 소수를 어떻게 다루는가, 수학의 답과 컴퓨터의 답은 다릅니다." ``` 라벨에 **"답이 다르다"를 명시**해 묶되 혼동을 만들지 않도록 했습니다. 순서는 수학(1편) → 컴퓨터(2편) 입니다. 키를 쓰는 주제가 아직 없었으므로 이름 변경 비용은 없었습니다. ## 시리즈 UI 가 처음으로 화면에 나타납니다 `cs/floating-point/meta.ts` 에 `series` 를 붙여 2편으로 편입했습니다. #12 로 만든 UI 가 이 PR 에서 처음 실제로 렌더됩니다. 프리렌더 HTML 로 확인했습니다: ``` /math/repeating-nines next → 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3? (전체 순서를 건너뛰고 cs 로) /cs/floating-point prev → 0.999… 는 1인가 /math/monte-carlo-pi 시리즈 없음 → 전체 순서 그대로 ``` ## 설명이 스스로를 부정하지 않도록 (#34) `gapAfter` 는 `1 - 0.99…9` 를 **뺄셈으로 구하지 않습니다.** ```js 1 - 0.999 → 0.0010000000000000009 // 하필 2편이 다루는 바로 그 오차 gapAfter(3) → 0.001 // 10^(-n) 을 직접 쓴다 ``` 부동소수점으로 계산했다면 "차이는 정확히 0.001" 이라는 화면의 설명이 스스로 무너집니다. 테스트로 고정했습니다. ## 순수 로직 분리 세 주제 모두 계산을 순수 함수로 빼고 난수를 주입받게 했습니다. 내부에서 `Math.random` 을 부르면 테스트가 불가능해집니다. - `applyTemperature` — exp 오버플로 방지(최댓값 빼기), `T<=0` 에서 최댓값이 여럿이면 균등 분배(하나를 임의로 고르면 후보 순서에 따라 결과가 달라집니다) - `estimatePi` — 시행 0 회면 **NaN**. `0` 을 돌려주면 "π 를 0 으로 추정했다"가 되어 화면에 그대로 찍힙니다. 호출부가 `Number.isFinite` 로 걸러 `—` 를 표시합니다 - `entropyBits` — 꿀통 문제의 정보량과 **같은 단위**라 개념이 이어집니다 ## 확장점 3개가 처음 쓰였습니다 만들어만 두고 실사용이 없던 것들이 이 PR 에서 검증됐습니다. - `ParameterPanel` 의 `kind: 'range'` (#10) — #32, #34 - `TrialRunner` 의 `renderProgress` (#8) — #33 - `series` / `seriesOrder` (#12) — #34 ## 검증 - 테스트 **46건 추가** → 전체 **186건 통과**, `lint` / `typecheck` / `build`(49 페이지) 통과 - 세 주제 모두 브라우저에서 인터랙션 확인 (게이트 통과 → 슬라이더 → 시뮬레이션) - 예시 데이터에도 성질 테스트를 걸었습니다 — "산술 문맥이 날씨 문맥보다 확정적" 은 #32 의 핵심 주장이라 logit 을 손보다 깨지면 안 됩니다 ## 리뷰 시 봐주셨으면 하는 곳 - **시리즈 라벨 판단** — 이 PR 에서 가장 되돌리기 어려운 결정입니다 - `windowAround` 가 자릿수에 맞춰 배율을 키우는 방식. author: fenghao999
body:
## What this fixes

A tester asked where the bucket picker was. There wasn't one — the dataset dropdown
scanned a single `--data-root`, and rerun's deep link kept only the last path segment of
the `tos://` URL it was given.

Two buckets holding a dataset of the same name were therefore indistinguishable to us,
and we would have run the wrong data **without saying anything**. That silence is what
this change is really about.

## What changed

**Datasets are scoped by an explicit dataset root**, selected from a whitelist in the
site config (`tos_buckets`). Each entry names the bucket, where its root is mounted, and
optionally the endpoint it is read through; the in-bucket prefix is *derived* from the
mount root rather than written twice. The picker shows the address all three parties
recognise — `tos://curation/datasets` — with the container-local mount path demoted to a
note beneath it. The panel still accepts **names only, never paths**.

**Deep links are matched on bucket AND prefix.** Three failure modes, each named:

| Link | Result |
|---|---|
| `tos://unknown-bucket/…/name` | refuses, says the bucket is not attached here — **never** falls back to a same-named dataset in the default bucket |
| `tos://curation/**raw**/name` while we serve `datasets/` | refuses, names both prefixes |
| bucket attached but our own config leaves its prefix unstated | refuses, says it is *our* config that is incomplete |
| bare `?dataset=<name>` | works verbatim, unchanged |

The bare form still working means the rerun side can switch over whenever it is ready.

**An optional `endpoint` parameter** closes the last gap: a `tos://` URL carries no
region, so without it we cannot tell a caller where an unserved bucket actually lives.
When it disagrees with our configured region we say so and name both — a TOS bucket name
is globally unique and cannot exist in two regions, so one of the two is wrong. The
value is sanitised to a bare hostname on the way in and used for wording only; it never
reaches a read path.

**A declared-but-absent mount** used to look exactly like a present-but-empty one — both
rendered as an empty dropdown. The first is a deployment failure and the second is
normal, so they now read differently, and only the failure carries a warning.

## Deploying this

`tos_buckets` is required config. A site still carrying the old `data_sources` key is
**refused at startup by name**, rather than silently treated as unconfigured — which
would reject every `tos://` deep link for a reason nobody could see. **Update the config
and the image in the same rollout.**

## For the rerun side (optional, nothing breaks if it never happens)

1. Pass the whole `tos://` URL instead of its last segment.
2. Pass the endpoint alongside it (`?endpoint=…`), so an unserved bucket can be reported
   with its actual location.

## Testing

1033 passed / 0 failed. Every behaviour above is pinned by a test, including the two that
would regress silently: an unknown bucket must not fall back to a same-named dataset, and
a prefix we do not serve must not match. Both were checked to go red against the previous
implementation before being accepted.

The four deep-link cases and the three mount states were also exercised against a running
instance, not only in unit tests.

## On the diff

Every one of the 73 deleted lines is an older form replaced by its bucket-aware version.
Following #49: `--root-path` and the prefixed routes are untouched — 9 occurrences before,
9 after, and none of them appear in the deletions.
