author: bomly-guy
body:
Closes part of #380 (the origin half; supplier/description remain out of scope — see below).

Replaces #395, which derived package origin at the SBOM export layer by classifying `Dependency.ResolvedURL`. That approach did not converge over ~20 review rounds, and the reason generalizes: `ResolvedURL` is not one kind of value. npm writes a registry tarball there, but also a local directory for link entries; uv writes a repository, an archive, an index root, or an editable path; Bundler writes a gem server, a repository, or a directory. Recovering the meaning downstream is guesswork, and every rule had an ecosystem-specific counterexample — an archive-extension check misclassifies repositories ending in `.zip`, a URL fragment is a resolved commit in uv but a content checksum in Yarn Classic, and an opaque token is not distinguishable from a content hash at all.

This PR asserts origin where the meaning is known.

## What changed

**Each detector reports its own origin** from the field its lockfile records it in — an exact artifact URL, a repository plus resolved revision, or nothing. Twelve resolvers across npm/pnpm/yarn/bun, uv/poetry/pipenv/pip, cargo, Bundler, SwiftPM, and pub. `ResolvedURL` keeps its existing value everywhere, so scorecard repository resolution is untouched.

**Export projects it and decides nothing.** SPDX packages get a real `downloadLocation` (the artifact, or `git+<url>@<revision>`) instead of a constant `NOASSERTION`; CycloneDX components get a `distribution` or `vcs` external reference.

**One rule replaces the classifier** — `NormalizeOriginURL`: absolute http(s), host present, no userinfo, re-serialized from the parse. Local paths, `file:`, ssh remotes, and credentialed URLs fail the scheme, host, or userinfo check rather than a bespoke heuristic. No archive-extension table, no credential-prefix list, no secret-shape detection. It runs when a detector records a value **and again at export**, so plugin-supplied graphs are held to the same rule.

**Registry and index roots are never published.** `https://rubygems.org/`, `https://pub.dev`, and the crates.io index describe an ecosystem's fetch configuration, not a package's provenance — and once out of context, a private server URL with a path is indistinguishable from a repository.

## Deliberate behavior notes for review

- **CycloneDX `vcs` refs are plain URLs.** The format has no revision slot on external references, so a resolved commit survives an SPDX round trip and not a CycloneDX one. Documented.
- **Origin keys are filtered out of `scan`/`diff`/`explain` output** by prefix in `cloneRefMetadata`. They are transport between two pipeline stages; the SBOM is where users read them. The filter returns nil for an emptied map so `omitempty` still fires and no golden grows a `"metadata": {}` block.
- **Syft-detected and SBOM-ingested packages carry no origin**, since an external module cannot call an `internal/` helper.
- **This does not close the CRA supplier error on #380.** Per-package supplier and description need registry-native metadata (npm `author`, PyPI `author`, POM `<organization>`), which means new allowed network hosts — a separate decision.

## Verification

- `make test`, `make fuzz FUZZTIME=5s`, `make generate` (no drift, as expected — no schema surface changed).
- New `FuzzSetOrigin` ran 8.4M executions with no failures.
- Mutation-checked: every load-bearing rule (scheme, host, userinfo, fragment, query, empty-path, revision charset), the output filter and its empty-map guard, and each detector's branch condition were individually broken and confirmed to fail a test. Two test gaps were found and closed this way — the original registry-root examples had empty paths, so the ruby and pub branch conditions weren't actually covered.
- Real scans of an npm project and a cargo project with a git dependency: correct locations in both formats, zero leaks of the scan directory, `file://`, or userinfo.
- Validated against the official SPDX validator (`spdxlib.ValidateDocument`) and the CycloneDX 1.4/1.5/1.6 JSON schemas.
- New smoke case scans the pinned `example-javascript-npm` repo and asserts on exported bytes (137 packages); it fails if emission regresses. Registered in both slice matrices with the node toolchain so it cannot silently skip.

author: bigkatoan
body:
## Summary

A real 20M-step PPO run against JAVIS's mjlab balance task (`Javis-Payload-Rough`) peaked in `eval/score_mean` around step 3.5M (1.87) then declined continuously for the remaining 16.5M steps, ending at 1.06. `ppo/approx_kl` stayed inside a superficially healthy band the whole run -- healthy only because nothing was enforcing a target: `PPOConfig.target_kl` defaults to `None` (disabled), and even when set, it's only a same-epoch early stop (breaks out of *that* update's minibatch loop once KL runs high) -- it does nothing to bound the *next* update. mjlab's own reference PPO training path for this exact task (rsl_rl, via `javis_balance_ppo_runner_cfg` in JAVIS's `balance_task.py`) uses `schedule="adaptive", desired_kl=0.01` -- a continuous, every-minibatch, whole-run LR schedule keyed on measured KL. SRL's PPO had no equivalent mechanism at all.

`PPO._adapt_lr` ports rsl_rl's exact algorithm: every minibatch, shrink `lr` when `approx_kl > desired_kl * 2.0` (divide by `kl_lr_factor`, floored at `min_lr`), grow it when `approx_kl < desired_kl / 2.0` (multiply by `kl_lr_factor`, capped at `max_lr`). Gated behind `PPOConfig.lr_schedule="adaptive"` (default `"fixed"` -- off, byte-for-byte preserving every existing run's behavior). The adapted LR round-trips through `checkpoint_payload`/`load_checkpoint_payload` so `--resume` continues the schedule instead of resetting it.

## Real-GPU verification (honest results, not all positive)

All runs below are against the identical real task/config this bug was found on, `configs/srl/javis_mjlab_ppo.yaml`-derived variants, RTX 3090, `n_envs=4096`:

| Config | Peak (step) | Final (20M unless noted) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unmodified baseline | 1.87 (3.5M) | 1.06 | The original bug |
| `entropy_coef=0.02` (4x) | 2.04 (5.5M) | 0.89 | Entropy stayed healthy (2.79->2.91) the *whole* run yet score still declined just as badly -- proves entropy collapse is a downstream symptom, not the root cause |
| `log_std_min=-3.5` | 2.15 (6.6M) | ~1.4 (killed early, 3 consecutive declines confirmed) | Floor never actually bound (real std stayed >0.2 the whole baseline run) -- no real effect |
| `target_kl=0.01` (existing weak safeguard) | 2.17 (5.0M) | 1.13 | Real but partial improvement -- slows, doesn't stop, the decline |
| `lr_schedule=adaptive` (uncapped, `max_lr=1e-2` matching rsl_rl's raw constant) | 2.12 (4.0M) | 0.46 (killed at 14.5M) | **Actively worse than baseline at matched steps.** Root-caused: LR spent nearly the entire run pinned near `max_lr` (10x the tuned base `lr=1e-3`); KL was in fact held tightly at `desired_kl` (mean 0.0095) the whole time -- the *mechanism* was working exactly as designed, but rsl_rl's hardcoded `max_lr=1e-2` doesn't safely transfer to SRL's setup |
| `lr_schedule=adaptive`, `max_lr=1e-3` (capped at the already-tuned base lr) | 2.88 (8.5M) | 1.36 (20M) | Substantially better peak and delayed onset, but still declines -- entropy still erodes (real entropy ~2.75 -> ~0) over the run |
| Above + `state_dependent_std=false, log_std_init=0.0` (matches rsl_rl's `std_type="scalar", init_std=1.0` exactly) + 40M steps + `--save-best` | 3.18 (10M), still running/declining as of writing | -- | Highest peak of any config tried, still not a flat hold |

**Honest bottom line**: this fix is real and meaningfully better than doing nothing (peak height and time-to-peak both improve substantially, and the *mechanism itself* -- confirmed by direct inspection of the KL/LR trajectory -- works exactly as designed once capped sanely). But even combined with matching rsl_rl's actor std configuration almost exactly, no config tested achieves a genuinely flat, indefinitely-held plateau within a 20-40M step budget on this task. Two things worth flagging for whoever picks this up:
1. mjlab's actual rsl_rl reference config for this task (`javis_balance_ppo_runner_cfg`) trains for `max_iterations=3000 * num_steps_per_env=24 * num_envs=4096` ~= **295M steps** -- ~15x the budget tested here. It's not established whether rsl_rl's own curve is flat that whole time or has a similar-shaped peak-then-recover cycle that just needs far more runway; the comparison in the original bug report assumed rsl_rl "just converges and holds" without confirming against a matched step budget.
2. SRL's `PPO.__init__` declares `self._obs_normalizer`/`self._ret_normalizer` (`RunningNormalizer`, already implemented in `srl/utils/normalizer.py`) but never actually uses them anywhere -- dead scaffolding. rsl_rl's reference config for this task sets `obs_normalization=True` on both actor and critic. This is a real, untested gap -- not implemented or verified as part of this PR, flagged here for follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] New `tests/test_ppo_adaptive_kl_lr.py` (12 tests): `_adapt_lr` unit tests (shrink/grow/dead-zone/clamps, matches rsl_rl's exact thresholds), wired-into-`update()` tests (fixed schedule never touches lr; adaptive schedule does, across real gradient steps), config-default backward-compat, checkpoint round-trip (including a stale-checkpoint-without-the-new-key compat test).
- [x] Full suite: 159 passed/1 skipped on `main` HEAD -> 171 passed/1 skipped on this branch (net +12, zero regressions).
- [x] `ruff check srl tests` / `black --check srl tests` clean.
- [x] Docs: `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/source/algorithms.md` (PPO config + note), `docs/source/yaml/training_block.md` (field table).
- [x] Real GPU verification: see table above -- this is the part that actually matters for a training-dynamics claim, done on the real task that surfaced the bug, not just synthetic unit tests.

body:
Automated promotion by the release train (RFC-0008 D14). Head is the train-managed `release-train/to-main` branch (a mirror of `staging`), so it never collides with a human PR. Merged only when the fr-gate is green.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes affect authentication polling, cluster error messaging, doctor exit codes, and visible `client create`—security-adjacent and installer-critical paths—but behavior is heavily gated (three-valued residency, confirmed reach only, mint guards unchanged) and covered by extensive new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Release 0.10.9** promotes a batch of CLI fixes and UX changes from staging, centered on **wrong or stale active-client pointers** (#515), **device-login polling** (#517), and **guided ingest prompts** (#504).
> 
> **Stale / wrong active client (#515)** makes `client create` user-visible again as the supported way to **adopt** a client already on the cluster (repoint without minting). `client list` separates **selection** from **residency** via a three-valued `cluster_id` comparison and only suggests `client create` when a client is provably on this cluster. Exit-4 / §7.3 paths **survey the reached cluster** before advising: local single-client clusters get `client create`; remote/shared clusters get `--namespace` only. **Doctor** and the **home screen** re-probe the kubeconfig namespace on local clusters when the bound pointer misses, use `reachConfirmedOK` (not `!= ReachNoEnv`) before trusting a re-probe, and treat stale pointers as **not ready** (exit 2) instead of “everything looks good.”
> 
> **Login (#517)** retries transient `PollToken` failures (DNS, 5xx, etc.) with a consecutive-failure cap, names the sign-in code TTL in expiry copy, and suppresses `tracebloc login` follow-up advice when `TRACEBLOC_INSTALLER` is set.
> 
> **Guided `data ingest` (#504)** drops bare `?` prompts: survey labels are short nouns (`Path:`, `Task:`, `Label:` / `Target:`) with questions in step headers; tests enforce the label contract.
> 
> **`sanitizeClientName`** also strips SS3 cursor-mode escapes (#516) and rejects escape-only residue before slugging namespaces. Copy-catalog harvesting folds string-literal concatenations so split `fmt.Errorf` messages stay inventoried.
> 
> Docs (`STYLE.md`, `cli-navigation.md`, `BUGBOT.md`) and version bump align with the above.

body: A missing bounds check in Dragonball's vsock and balloon device emulation allows a compromised guest kernel to make the host containerd-shim-kata-v2 process (root)read/write operations against its own memory outside the guest-RAM mapping. This yields guest-controlled out-of-bounds read and write in the host shim, leading to guest-to-host VM escape with code execution as root on the node.

author: siyuqian
body:
## Description

Makes `devpilot:pr-creator` fire on its own the moment a task is finished, instead of waiting to be asked.

The obvious fix — adding "use PROACTIVELY when a task is finished" to the skill's `description` frontmatter — **does not work**, and this PR includes the probe that proves it. A skill description is consulted when matching *what the user asked for*; nothing re-reads it at the moment the model decides to stop. So the trigger has to live in the harness, not in skill prose.

`scripts/pr-on-finish.sh` is a `Stop` hook, registered in `hooks/hooks.json` alongside the existing `SessionStart` one. It emits `{"decision":"block", "reason": ...}` to send the session back into `pr-creator`, and stays silent unless **all** of these hold:

- inside a git repo, on a resolvable non-default branch
- at least one commit ahead of `origin/<default>` (uncommitted-only work is mid-edit, not finished)
- no open PR for the branch already
- `stop_hook_active` is not set — without this guard, blocking loops until the turn limit

Two findings that shaped the implementation, both from the probe rather than from reading:

1. **The model refuses a bare nudge.** First version was declined with *"opening a PR is outward-facing, I won't do it unannounced."* That is the model correctly applying its confirm-before-outward-facing rule. The reason text now states the standing authorization explicitly — the owner installed the hook precisely to pre-authorize this — which satisfies that rule instead of fighting it.
2. **An explicit user scope-close still wins.** If the user says "that is the whole task, do nothing beyond that," the hook loses and the model stops. That is correct behavior and is now pinned by a test arm so nobody "fixes" it into an override.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S["session stops"] --> H["pr-on-finish.sh **new**"]
    H -->|"stop_hook_active"| Q["exit 0, silent"]
    H -->|"on default branch / 0 commits ahead / PR exists"| Q
    H -->|"finished branch, no PR"| B["decision: block + standing authorization"]
    B --> P["devpilot:pr-creator"]
    P --> C["gh pr create"]
```

## Review Guide

**Start here:** `scripts/pr-on-finish.sh` — 40 lines, and the whole feature. Read the gating conditions top to bottom; every one of them is an "exit 0 silently" path, because a Stop hook that talks when it shouldn't is worse than one that never talks.

Then, in order:

1. `tests/pr-on-finish_test.sh` — 8 assertions on that gating, no API cost. Stubs `gh` on `PATH` so the tests don't depend on network or auth state.
2. `hooks/hooks.json` — three lines, mirrors the existing `SessionStart` entry.
3. `.claude/skills/run-devpilot-plugin/driver.sh` — the new `cmd_select` probe (the bulk of the diff).
4. `.claude/skills/run-devpilot-plugin/SKILL.md` — docs for the above.

**Worth watching in `cmd_select`, because both traps produce a confident wrong answer:**

- **The `claude -p` call deliberately has no CLI flags.** Verified on this build: `--output-format`, `--allowedTools`, and `--permission-mode` *each* silently suppress hooks passed via `--settings`. Adding any of them turns the probe into a no-hook run that always fails and looks like a broken skill. Permissions therefore ride inside the settings file as `permissions.defaultMode`. The `explicit` arm is the canary — re-run it first if you touch that invocation.
- **The assertion reads a `PreToolUse` tool log, not the output stream.** An earlier version grepped the stream for `pr-creator` and reported a false PASS: the session's init event lists every available skill, so that string matches on every run.

The four arms are a matched set — `explicit` proves the probe can see an invocation at all, so a `finished` failure means something; `bare` and `scoped` prove the trigger is scoped rather than always-on.

## Verification

- [x] `driver.sh smoke` passes — 21 checks (was 20; the new hook test is wired into `cmd_hook`)
- [x] `driver.sh validate` passes — 28 skills, manifests, agents, commands, cross-refs, README
- [x] `tests/pr-on-finish_test.sh` — `1..8`
- [x] `bash -n` clean on both new/changed shell files
- [x] All four `select` arms run against a real `claude -p`: `explicit` PASS, `finished` PASS, `bare` PASS, `scoped` PASS
- [x] Attribution check: `finished` re-run after reverting the frontmatter edit, still PASS — the hook alone carries it

## Additional Notes

- The `select` arms cost API tokens (~4 sessions). They are in `smoke-full`, not in the default `smoke`.
- The frontmatter edit that started this was reverted once measured ineffective, so `skills/pr-creator/SKILL.md` is unchanged in this diff — the skill body was already "automatic by default" with no approval gate.
- `gh` is only shelled out to after the cheap local checks pass, so the common case costs no network call.

## For Reviewers (human)

- [x] Self-review of the code
- [x] Checked for security implications

## Summary

- preserve a Django model field's `verbose_name` and `help_text` when a
  `ModelSchema` overrides that field with Pydantic `Field` constraints
- keep an explicitly configured custom title or description authoritative

## Root cause

`SchemaFactory.create_schema()` replaced the model-derived `FieldInfo` with the
custom field's `FieldInfo`. This correctly kept custom validation constraints,
but discarded the title and description already derived from the Django model.

The two metadata values are now merged into the custom `FieldInfo` before the
schema is created. Pydantic's merge semantics ensure explicitly provided custom
values still win.

author: adexdsamson
body:
## Summary

The per-PM **Manage Access** dialog (Vendor Management → vendor → Project Managers → row → *Manage Access*) always showed a **single** `Vendor-PM (CLM)` chip, even when the project manager also holds **Vendor (Solicitation)** access. Both roles should pre-select.

## Root cause

`VendorDetailPage` passed:

```ts
currentRole={(accessTarget as { role?: string } | null)?.role}
```

But a PM row has **no top-level `role` string**. The vendor-detail payload carries a populated **`roles`** array, and `user.roles` holds both roles (`project_manager` + `vendor`) as `{_id, name}` objects. So `currentRole` was always `undefined`, and the dialog's `toOptions(undefined)` fell back to its hardcoded `Vendor-PM` default → one chip.

## Fix

- Extend `VendorProjectManager` with the real `roles` / `user.roles` shape.
- Add `pmRoleNames()` to extract role **names**, preferring `user.roles` (authoritative — carries both) and falling back to row-level `roles`.
- Pass those names to `currentRole`. The dialog's `toOptions` already dedupes and maps an array, so both chips now pre-select.

This mirrors the vendor-account Manage Access fix (seed from the already-loaded detail payload rather than a role string that isn't there).

## Testing
- New `manage-project-manager-access-dialog.test.tsx`: both roles pre-select when present; a single role pre-selects when only one is held. **2 passed.**
- `tsc -b` passes clean.

author: rushow111
body:
## Goal

Fix the real user-page defect where clicking **Personal** hides untouched knowledge balls but leaves their relation lines visible, and add regression guards proving the two recently introduced layout algorithms are actually wired into the live user page.

## Root cause

`setHideUntouched()` only updated node-group and label visibility. `edgeMap` had no endpoint-aware visibility update, so relation lines remained rendered after one or both endpoint balls disappeared.

## Fix

- Every premise/logic/twin rendered edge now retains its endpoint node IDs.
- Personal-mode visibility builds one canonical visible-node set.
- A line is render-visible only when both of its endpoints are currently visible.
- Leaving Personal mode first resynchronizes the real edge geometry, then reapplies endpoint visibility, so the original line set is restored exactly.
- Personal visibility does not mutate `pos`, `homePos`, fixed slots, layer assignment, or relation-length optimization.

## Live layout wiring audit

Regression guards now enforce the production chain:

`GraphProjection all nodes -> layoutNodes -> applyUniformLayerLayout(layoutNodes) -> optimizeRelationLengthLayout(nodes) -> renderNodes visibility filter -> KnowledgeScene`

This proves:
- uniform fixed-slot distribution runs on the live user page;
- hidden/falsified/superseded nodes participate before render filtering;
- the complete historical relation-length optimizer is invoked from the same live layout entry point;
- Personal mode is a render-only filter and cannot create a separate personal layout.

## Final validation

Final validation: **Validate run #614**, HEAD `eee4ab70de4780c8936a87421e383f539c581de4` — all jobs passed.

- TypeScript + Vite production build: passed.
- Complete `npm test`: passed.
- `PersonalVisibilityRegression`: passed.
- `LayoutRuntimeWiringRegression`: passed, proving both recent layout algorithms are in the live user-page path.
- Existing uniform-layout and complete historical relation-length regressions: passed.
- 390×844 Chromium/WebGL user-page regression: passed with 8 finite raycast targets.
- The real `#btnPersonal` control was clicked in Chromium; visible relation-line count decreased when a connected untouched endpoint was hidden, and returned to exactly the prior count when Personal mode was disabled.
- Issue #51 production-scale interaction regression: passed; measured tap wall time was ~56.8 ms.
- Clean merge preflight against current `main`: passed.
- Android tests + debug APK build: passed.
- iOS sync + unsigned simulator build: passed.

`npm ci` still reports the repository's existing 3 dependency advisories (1 moderate, 2 high). This PR does not change dependencies or the lockfile.

## Scope guard

No Supabase migration or data mutation, no vote/energy changes, no layer-policy changes, no uniform/relation-layout algorithm changes, no visual-theme changes, no Android/iOS native-source changes, and no dependency/lockfile changes.

## Diff guard

Current `main` remains `032952705ebdd53eeeecf2c65378cfb8f9e61a35`. The branch is 5 commits ahead / 0 behind with the same merge base. Runtime product code changes are limited to the endpoint-aware Personal visibility fix in `KnowledgeScene.ts`; the remaining changes are regression coverage and the scene-test script entry.

author: bkpepe
body:
cmake/Makefile.am maintains the EXTRA_DIST list manually, and five
CMake modules are missing from it even though they are tracked in git.

Two of them break CMake builds from the 4.12.0 release tarball:
CMakeLists.txt unconditionally includes enable_jemalloc, but
enable_jemalloc.cmake and find_jemalloc.cmake are not shipped.

FindLIBBPF.cmake, FindLIBUNWIND.cmake and Finduring.cmake are
missing as well, so the corresponding optional features cannot be
built from a tarball.

This was found while packaging 4.12.0 for OpenWrt, where the tarball
is the only input. Git builds are unaffected.

After the change, the tracked cmake/*.cmake files and the EXTRA_DIST
list match.

- Innholdet PII-vaskes FØR embedding, og **KS-funn: spørringen vaskes OGSÅ** (#81-regelen — samme datatype behandles aldri ulikt per kodevei). Vask-svikt er fail-closed: `sok()` returnerer None og ord-søket tar over.
- **KS: backfillen leser indeksen i BATCH** (`indekserte_rev`, `.in_()`-bolker à 200 — N+1-vernet fra fagrolle-/miljøsert-rundene), og 20k-taket i registerlesningen rapporteres ærlig (`register_kappet`) i stedet for å telle en kappet lesning som full dekning.
- **KS (selv-verifisert etter feilet verifiserings-agent): RLS på `rom_indeks`** — husmønsteret fra `rom_data`/`styre_data`: `enable row level security` uten policies = kun service-rollen; RPC-en er security invoker så RLS gjelder gjennom den.

## B3 — Hjelmkamera-økten (`rom/hms_agent.py`)

- Økt-intake (flere klipp → ÉN absolutt tidslinje), drøftingsplikt-gate (AML § 9-2, målt på datoene — en planlagt drøfting åpner aldri gaten) og beslutningsgrunnlag per runde.
- **KS-funn: kamera-feltene `av`/`at` er persondata** (aktør-e-post — tilgangslogg-regelen) og PL-gates nå i `api_hms` (`_hms_kamera_felt`-feltplukk); datoene består for alle som ser gaten.

## F6 — AR-grunnmuren (`rom/ar_modell.py`)

IFC→GLB per revisjon (ifcopenshell server-side, innholds-hashet cache i Storage) + Scene Viewer-inngang. KS-herding i fire lag:

1. **En død byggetråd ER en feilet bygging** — `_jobb` i try/except; statusen blir `error:` med årsaken, aldri et evig «bygger».
2. **Signerte URL-er mintes ALDRI blindt** — en signert URL kan mintes for en sti som ikke finnes. `_speilet` bærer kun prosess-bekreftede Storage-objekter; `_klar_svar` selv-healer speilingen per lesning og skiller ærlig mellom «Storage mangler i miljøet» og «forbigående — prøv igjen om litt».
3. **Polling laster aldri IFC-en på nytt** — `_sha_cache` nøklet på `dok:rev:sti:size` (innholdet bak en revisjons sti er stabilt).
4. **Nedlasting beviser eksistens** — gren 2 merker sha-en som speilet etter GLB-nedlasting fra Storage, aldri en re-opplasting av det som nettopp ble lastet ned.

## Refutert i KS (bevisste valg, ikke fikset)

- DATASIKKERHET-tekstene — dokumenterte produktbeslutninger, ikke defekter.
- «Blind minting»-varianten som påsto at signering ER en eksistenssjekk — fiksen over er korrekt under BEGGE storage-py-adferder.

## Tester

`test_rom_gjenfinning` (15 — inkl. spørrings-vask + batch-kontrakt m/ spion), `test_rom_hms_okt` (4 — inkl. PL-gaten m/ gjeste-tildeling), `test_rom_ar` (7 + 1 skip — tråd-død, sha-cache m/ `hent_fil`-spion, aldri-blind-minting m/ re-speiling), `test_rom_hms` (27+1). Samlet 36 passed / 1 skipped etter rebase på main.

## Ærlige grenser

- ifcopenshell finnes ikke i sandboxen — den ekte konverteringen dekkes av en `importorskip`-test; resten av kjeden er målt med syntetisk GLB.
- Scene Viewer på fysisk Android kan ikke måles herfra; intent-URL-en er kontraktstestet.
- iOS krever USDZ (Quick Look) — bygges ikke ennå, grensen SIES i flaten (`IOS_GRENSE`).
- Pre-eksisterende: `test_rom_anbud_api::test_sammenstill_og_tilbud_fil_bak_pl_gaten` feiler identisk med og uten runden (verifisert med git stash).

Søster-PR i view-builtly bærer flatene (Byggeplass-økt-intake, Datarom AR-blokk, mock-paritet).

author: filip-pajalic
body:
Follow-up to the Claude Fable 5 (max effort) review filed as #6. v5 recorded the review; **v6 implements the follow-ups, closes every `sorry` in the Lean project, and extends the evidence base in both directions** — while *not* accepting the two objections that misread the argument.

## Objections addressed

| # | Objection | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | AGI Definition unsatisfiable by diagonalization — main theorem vacuous (**blocking**) | **Accepted and proved.** Proposition 1.10 proves the unrestricted criterion unsatisfiable; Definition 1.12 relativizes it to a fixed, model-independent family with resource bounds; Proposition 1.13 proves the target is occupiable |
| 2 | MI formalism lacks a Bayesian joint; unproven DPI strictness; no link to accuracy | **Accepted; strictness restored under the correct criterion.** Definition 2.1 fixes the joint; Lemma 2.3 proves the exact identity `I_k − I_{k+1} = I(Θ; θ_k \| θ_{k+1})`, so strictness holds iff the update is not a sufficient statistic, and Proposition 2.4 proves finite-sample self-distillation meets that condition; Lemma 2.7 + Corollary 2.8 add the Fano link to an accuracy ceiling |
| 3 | Support contraction vacuous for softmax models | **Accepted.** Restated over ε-effective support: Definition 3.1, Lemma 3.2 (total-variation transfer), Theorem 3.3 |
| 4 | Error-divergence universality fails in the accumulation regime | **Not accepted.** v4 stated verbatim that without its hypotheses the theorem "should be read as a recurrence analysis rather than a universal claim", so accumulation is not a counterexample. Section 9.1 shows the regime is outside Definition 1.9 on principle — it works by permanently retaining `D_train`, i.e. grounding re-supplied every step. The theorem is kept and proved in Lean |
| 5 | Context theorems attack a scenario the formal loop does not require | **Not accepted.** Remark 8.1 states the dichotomy: blind self-modification is bounded by the fixed-point trap and the information ceiling; directed self-modification by these resource inequalities. The objection lands in the blind horn, which other barriers already close. The RoPE correction (parameter count does not grow with context) *is* accepted |
| 6 | `barriers_hold` refutable; two axioms vacuous; docstring overstated | **Accepted.** The loop is now a composition of training channels, so `barriers_hold` and the main theorem are proved; Gödel I proved in computability form; Gödel II is a bridge axiom that asserts something; docstring corrected |
| 7 | "human influence" should be "external grounding" | **Accepted as a generalization, not a replacement.** Every category of Definition 1.7 is a grounding signal, including item (4)'s human-designed *environments*, which covers the embodied-agent case as ordinarily realized. The residual case — non-human-designed sensing apparatus — is outside the paradigm, not a counterexample inside it |
| 8 | Evidence audit; time-index the 2023-era props | **Accepted.** 29 new references, each verified against arXiv listings before citation; Section 12.5 time-indexes the older evidence |

## Lean: no `sorry` in the project

`info_ceiling`, `StepLoss.after_lt` (strict decrease), the Fano accuracy link, entropy and ε-effective-support contraction, the error results (`error_diverges`, `error_grows_linearly`, `error_nondecreasing`, `stagnation_at_fixed_point`, `accumulation_no_divergence`), `training_time_divergence`, `barriers_hold`, and `impossibility_of_autonomous_agi` are all proved. Contentless placeholders removed: the two Gödel axioms whose content was `True`, the tautological `data_processing_inequality`, `axiom P_ne_NP : True`, the `True`-valued barrier fields, and the Kolmogorov placeholder that made its own theorem *false*. `autonomous_no_human_influence` is a theorem now. New `Impossibility/Audit.lean` prints axiom dependencies on every build — every load-bearing result depends only on `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.

## New supporting evidence (Section 12)

Six results found for v6, each verified against arXiv:

- **SlopCodeBench** (2603.24755) — 15 agents, 196 checkpoints: structural erosion rises in 77% of trajectories, agent code is 2.3× more verbose and 2.0× more eroded than 473 human repositories, and quality prompting lowers the initial level *"without affecting degradation rates"*.
- **When Good Verifiers Go Bad** (2606.14629) — sub-threshold verifiers regress the student 3.4–10.9 points *while training loss keeps falling*; confident wrong verifiers do the most damage. A direct measurement of undetected degradation.
- **TTRL correct-answer extinction window** (2605.19444) — in majority-vote self-training, gains are mostly sharpening of already-solvable problems and corrupted problems outnumber genuinely learned ones. This is the closest instrumented measurement of a label-free loop.
- **Self-consistency backfires** (2608.11403) — majority vote lowers per-problem accuracy on 56.6% / 65.7% of GPQA Diamond problems for two small models, with wrong answers confidently held.
- **Solver–verifier gap** (2507.00075) — improvement is available only while discriminative capability exceeds generative capability, and stops when the gap closes.
- **Information-theoretic limits of safety verification** (2603.28650) — classifier-based self-assessment cannot combine bounded cumulative risk with unbounded utility; a genuine decision procedure can.

Section 12 also separates results that fall **outside the definitions** (accumulation, verifier-driven systems: DGM, SEAL, AZR, Self-Harness, AlphaEvolve) from the three in **genuine tension** (ProRL vs Yue et al.; the self-correction illusion; synthetic-data scaling), adds a grounding audit naming each system's external signal in advance, and states four pre-registered falsification criteria.

## Consensus assessment (Section 13)

Synthesis of the five adversarial LLM reviews plus the independent literature: converged, contested, withdrawn, examined-and-not-accepted, and the residual claim stated at the width the mathematics supports.

## Artifacts

- `papers/llm_self_improvement_proof.pdf` regenerated: 40 pages (was 22), 0 undefined references.
- `lake build` passes clean under Lean v4.16.0 — no `sorry`, no warnings.
- `docs/verification_plan.md` marks resolved items and names the main remaining formal gap: the data-processing property is a channel hypothesis, not yet derived from a measure-theoretic model of sampling and training.

author: trankhacvinh
body:
## Mục tiêu

Thêm **Custom Pages / Page Builder** dùng chung hệ thống Section, Inline Editing và Row Builder hiện tại để tạo các trang như Giới thiệu, Liên hệ, Chính sách, Dịch vụ hoặc landing page — không tạo editor thứ hai.

## Admin → Website → Trang nội dung

- Có mục `Trang nội dung` trong sidebar Website.
- Admin quản lý được `Trang chung` và từng cơ sở; Manager chỉ quản lý cơ sở có quyền.
- Tạo / sửa / xóa / nhân bản trang.
- Draft / Published.
- Ẩn khỏi danh sách điều hướng nhưng vẫn có URL public khi Published.
- Slug tự sinh từ tiếng Việt, kiểm tra trùng và chặn route hệ thống như `rooms`, `booking`, `blog`, `admin`…
- SEO title, meta description, OG image.
- Template khởi tạo: Trang trống / Giới thiệu / Liên hệ / Landing ưu đãi.
- Modal tạo/sửa trang đã được làm lại: section rõ ràng, switch đẹp hơn, header/footer cố định và X/Hủy/click backdrop/Esc đều đóng đúng.

## Public page

- Global: `/{slug}`.
- Property: `/h/{siteSlug}/{slug}`.
- Draft chỉ Admin/Manager có quyền preview; guest nhận 404 và preview draft có `noindex,nofollow`.
- Published page được đưa vào sitemap đúng scope.
- Kế thừa Header / Sticky Header / Footer Builder hiện tại.

## Visual Editor dùng lại toàn bộ stack hiện tại

- Nút `Thiết kế` mở trang với `?edit=1` và tự bật chỉnh sửa.
- Thêm / sửa / kéo sắp xếp / duplicate / hide / delete các Section chuẩn.
- Inline edit Hero, text, CTA, FAQ, Policy, Feature…
- Row / Column Builder hoạt động trên Custom Page.
- Row Inline Editing, Undo/Redo, Copy/Paste, Responsive Desktop/Tablet/Mobile.
- Advanced Elements tiếp tục dùng được qua Row Builder hiện tại.
- Row Template Library dùng chung như Homepage.
- Upload ảnh vẫn đi qua site asset / Media Library pipeline hiện tại.

## Element Style trực tiếp trên Custom Page

- Khi click text/heading/button trong inline editor có thêm `↔ Kiểu`.
- Chỉnh được `Căn`: tự động / trái / giữa / phải.
- Chỉnh được `Cỡ chữ`: mặc định → rất nhỏ / nhỏ / vừa / lớn / rất lớn / Hero.
- Chỉnh được `Độ rộng`: mặc định / gọn / vừa / rộng / Full.
- Ảnh Hero/Feature có thêm `↔ Kiểu ảnh`: căn trái/giữa/phải + kích thước gọn/vừa/rộng/Full khối.
- `Full` cho Hero text/image có thể chuyển layout sang một hàng rộng để không bị khóa trong cột hẹp.
- Style được lưu trong `_visual` của chính section ContentJson; guest render đúng style sau khi publish.
- Khi bấm `Kiểu` trong lúc đang sửa text, editor lưu text trước rồi mới mở panel style để tránh mất nội dung hoặc ghi đè snapshot cũ.

## Smart Link Picker

- Nhóm mới `Trang` trong picker.
- Tự liệt kê Custom Page Published và không bị `Ẩn khỏi danh sách điều hướng`.
- Dùng được cho Menu, Header CTA, Footer và các link picker hiện tại.

## Storage / compatibility

- **Không migration DB mới.**
- Custom Page được lưu trong HomeSection metadata type `__CustomPage`; mỗi metadata chứa cấu hình trang + section list của riêng trang.
- `__CustomPage` bị loại khỏi Homepage section GET/reorder/default generation để không làm nhiễu Homepage.
- Media URL nằm trong metadata nên usage scanner hiện tại vẫn có thể phát hiện asset đang được tham chiếu.
- Header/Footer vẫn là shell theo scope, không bị copy riêng cho mỗi trang.

## UAT

- `docs/PUBLIC-CUSTOM-PAGES-UAT.md`
- `docs/PUBLIC-CUSTOM-PAGE-ELEMENT-STYLE-UAT.md`

Ưu tiên test: tạo `Giới thiệu` → `Thiết kế` → click Hero title → sửa text → `Kiểu` → căn giữa + Hero + Full → lưu → chỉnh ảnh Hero `Full khối` → thêm Row/Advanced Element → publish → mở tab ẩn danh → kiểm tra Smart Link Picker / Header / Footer / Media safe-delete.

author: artokun
body:
Reported in #886 — `panel_open_workflow` keeps reporting UNCONFIRMED on opens whose only differences are per-node `properties` / `widgets_values`, and the thread's blocker for two months has been that nobody can say WHICH keys moved.

## Where the issue stands on current main

Most of #886 is already fixed and released, and this PR does not re-litigate any of it:

- a `definitions` difference that is pure link renumbering is accounted for (#1125, 0.14.20)
- an open where only presentation moved reports applied, with the fields disclosed (#1274, 0.14.44)
- an accounted `definitions` surface no longer blocks the reassurance (#1252/#1291, 0.14.44)

The two most recent recurrences (2026-08-15, panel 0.14.42 and 0.14.43) both predate those releases, but each names a difference set that still refuses on main **deliberately**: per-node `properties` (with `size`/`order`) in one, `size` + `widgets_values` in the other. `properties` and `widgets_values` are outside every allowlist for the reason recorded in `resolveOpenRebindVerdict` — a mid-`configure()` partial load drops exactly those fields, and nothing the panel can see separates that from the frontend normalizing them.

## Root cause of the remaining cost

The refusal names the differing **fields** (`properties, size, order`) but `properties` is one field name standing in for a whole bag of keys. A rewritten pack-version stamp (`ver`) and an extension's stored settings read identically at the field level, so the reader cannot judge the refusal, and the automated reports pasted onto #886 cannot answer the question the thread keeps asking: *which keys inside `properties` does the frontend normalize?* I checked the obvious candidate before writing this — in comfyui_frontend_package 1.48.7 the only generic `properties` transform (zod validation's `ver` leading-`v` strip) is gated behind `Comfy.Validation.Workflows`, which **defaults to false** — so on default installs these differences come from node-pack constructors and `loadedGraphNode` hooks, which cannot be allowlisted blind. The maintainers' measured-key requirement stands, and this change exists to produce exactly that measurement.

## The change — disclosure only, verdict untouched

`classifyNodeDifference` now also returns `propertyFields`: when `properties` is among the differing per-node fields and both sides are readable objects, the keys INSIDE `properties` that differ, computed with the same discipline as the field comparison (presence before value, `undefined` is absent, anything unreadable names no keys). `nodeSurfaceClause` appends them to the refusal:

> what differs is per-node (order, properties, size)**; within properties, the keys that differ are: ver**. A widget value is real content, so read it (panel_graph_outline) before assuming either way

The list is capped at 10 keys with the trim disclosed (", and N more"), so a hostile properties bag cannot grow the clause without bound.

Nothing else moves: `CONTENT_UNVERIFIED` still throws, the fence is still withheld, `widgets_values` stays outside both allowlists, and an unreadable `properties` shape names the field but no keys — fail closed, same as an unreadable node set.

## What this deliberately does NOT do

- It does not admit `properties` or `widgets_values` into `COSMETIC_NODE_FIELDS` or `RECOMPUTED_NODE_FIELDS`. Without a per-key measurement that would be the fabricated all-clear this guard exists to avoid — and my source check above shows the reporters' differences are not the one transform the frontend documents.
- It does not change the reassurance tiers: a non-cosmetic difference still gets "no node was lost" and never "no missing work to redo".

## Verification

- `npm run test:unit` — **4949 tests, 4948 pass, 0 fail, 1 pre-existing todo**; i18n, i18n-render, tool-vocabulary and panel-scope gates all OK.
- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- 9 new tests in `open-node-difference.test.mjs` (this file's style), including: the key union across nodes, `undefined`-is-absent one level down, unreadable/absent `properties` naming no keys, the refusal sentence carrying the keys, the cap disclosing its trim, and the full pipeline (`describeGraphStateDifference` → `describeOpenRebindOutcome`) rather than a hand-built shape. One existing whole-shape assertion in `open-rebind-proof.test.mjs` gained `propertyFields: []` for the additive field.
- Not done: no live-rig reproduction (no ComfyUI instance was available where this was built) — the change is disclosure-only, so nothing it ships can soften a verdict untested.

Closes #886

author: perincheckad
body:
## Syfte
Reparera det röda fyndet från Steg 3.1: direkt Supabase Data API-access som ligger vid sidan av det redan säkrade `/api`-lagret.

## Baseline
- `main`: `d1bbf5f318405028113f12c5dd162662b7065464`
- Production-schema live-verifierat 2026-08-18
- Ingen Production-DDL eller DML har körts i denna PR

## Diff
Exakt **3 migrationsfiler**:
- `migrations/20260818_lock_down_supabase_data_api.sql`
- `migrations/20260818_lock_down_supabase_data_api_defaults.sql`
- `migrations/20260818_preserve_status_read_contracts.sql`

Ingen appkod, affärslogik, dependency eller UI-förändring.

## Reparation
- återkallar browser/Data API-tabellrättigheter generellt från `PUBLIC`, `anon` och `authenticated`
- återkallar legacy-sekvensrättigheter från samma roller
- återger endast verifierade browser-kontrakt till `authenticated`
- kräver intern DB-side `whitelist OR employees.is_active` för RLS
- stänger själv-eskalering via `employees` INSERT/UPDATE
- återkallar `EXECUTE` på public-schemafunktioner från `PUBLIC`, `anon` och `authenticated`
- bevarar service-role RPC-behörighet explicit
- konverterar de tre verifierade browser-RPC:erna till `SECURITY INVOKER`: `get_all_allowed_plates`, `get_vehicle_by_trimmed_regnr`, `get_damages_by_trimmed_regnr`
- stänger legacy anon-policyer på `checkins`, `checkin_damages` och `checkin_damage_photos`
- hårdnar `postgres` default privileges för tabeller, funktioner och sekvenser

## Verifierade browser-kontrakt som bevaras
- `employees`: SELECT egen rad
- `vehicles`: SELECT
- `nybil_inventering`: SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE
- `damages`: SELECT/INSERT
- `damage_media`: SELECT
- `vehicle_edits`: SELECT
- `arrivals`: SELECT för Status
- `damage_comments`: SELECT för Status
- `damages_external`: SELECT endast som underliggande RLS-källa för BUHS-RPC
- `checkin_drafts`: SELECT egen användares drafts
- `checkins`: SELECT för Status och `get_all_allowed_plates`
- tre ovan nämnda RPC:er: EXECUTE för authenticated, nu som invoker

`checkin_damages` fortsätter via skyddat server-API i Status och får ingen browsergrant.

## Plattformsspecifik residual
Live-default ACL visar även Supabase-ägda defaults under rollen `supabase_admin`. Migrationsrollen `postgres` är inte medlem i `supabase_admin`, så PR:n försöker inte ändra dessa plattformsägda defaults och riskerar därmed inte en transaktionsrollback. Alla **befintliga** public-objekt stängs explicit. Efter Production-migration körs Security Advisor igen.

## Viktigt
Migrationerna är ännu **inte körda mot Production**. De ska först gå igenom repo-CI och därefter appliceras kontrollerat med negativa accesskontroller och read-only funktionella smoke checks. Inga write probes ska göras i Production.

**Behålla → reparera → ta bort → addera.**

| `getStereotype(project, "SAF_LogicalUser", prf)` | `getStereotype(project, "SAF_ConceptualUser", prf)` |
| `getStereotype(project, "SAF_LogicalEnvironment", prf)` | `getStereotype(project, "SAF_ConceptualEnvironment", prf)` |
| errorMessage "… SAF Logical Context Elements." | "… SAF Conceptual Context Elements." |

Plus a `changes.md` entry.

**Verification.** Cameo 2024x R3 with this profile mounted (also applies to 2026x — same mdzip): a model with 22 associations between `SAF_SystemUseCase`s and `SAF_ConceptualUser`/`SAF_ConceptualSystem`/`SAF_ConceptualEnvironment` blocks and no UML Actor reported 22 × `WUCASSCTX` on `main`'s profile; after swapping in this file and reopening the project the same model reports 0, and the rule body reads back with the new names via `Constraint.getSpecification()`.

The mdzip was patched with a small script rather than in Cameo so that nothing else in the profile moves — if you would rather apply the three-name edit in the profile project yourself and regenerate, the issue has everything needed; happy to close this PR in that case.

Note for reviewers (see #8): with `SAF_ConceptualSystem` covering both the SoI and external systems, the patched rule also accepts an association to the SoI block; if that should remain a violation, the rule needs the `SAF_ConceptualContextRole_SoI` role to distinguish them.

author: foxly-it
body:
Two independent, unrelated issues found investigating "why does RootGuard Unbound have errors on GitHub, and the site looks stale again."

## 1. Unbound CI failing (`Unbound CI` scheduled run)
`rootguard-unbound`'s Dockerfile pins exact Debian package versions for reproducibility. Debian shipped a security patch to `libexpat1`/`libexpat1-dev` (2.8.2 -> 2.8.3) and dropped the old version from the mirror entirely - Debian repos only ever serve the latest point release. Checked every other pinned package in both build stages (`build-essential`, `ca-certificates`, `curl`, `libevent-dev`/`libevent-2.1-7t64`, `libssl-dev`/`libssl3t64`, `pkg-config`, `bind9-dnsutils`, `dns-root-data`) against the real `debian:13-slim` base image - only expat had drifted. Bumped both references.

## 2. Site stale again
Same root cause as before beta.3: the release pipeline updates `compose.alpha.yaml`/`.env.alpha.example` automatically but never touches the hardcoded site version strings. Cutting `v0.1.0-beta.3` without a manual site pass left it a release behind within two days. Updated `index.html`/`docs.html`/`wiki.html`/`roadmap.html`.

## Test plan
- [x] Rebuilt `rootguard-unbound` on the `.7` test host with the fix: build succeeds, `unbound -V` reports `1.25.2`, `unbound-checkconf` reports no errors.

author: xiaofeicao
body:
## Scope

Adds Azure Core support for consuming a single generic server-sent event response. The implementation parses one established `Response<BinaryData>` and does not reconnect, replay requests, or send `Last-Event-Id`.

- Adds `ServerSentEvent<T>`, `ServerSentEventListener<T>`, `ServerSentEventStreams`, incremental parsing, and optional typed terminal-event predicates.
- Preserves live SSE response bodies through REST proxies and prevents response logging from consuming them.
- Keeps `Response<BinaryData>` as an ordinary REST response while closing stream-backed bodies or cancelling reactive body publishers when consumption ends.
- Preserves synchronous OkHttp and JDK `BinaryData` stream behavior, and closes Vert.x response sockets when reactive body consumption is cancelled.

## Contract

Non-204 responses require exactly one `text/event-stream` content type. Declared character sets are decoded incrementally, with an initial byte-order mark taking precedence. Response streams support one subscription.

Existing overloads complete on EOF or HTTP 204. Predicate overloads deliver the matching typed terminal event and complete; EOF before a match is reported as an incomplete stream. Reactive cancellation, terminal events, processing failures, and blocking listener interruption terminate the body subscription so the HTTP transport can release its resources.

`Accept: text/event-stream` preserves a live body only when its `q` value is syntactically valid and greater than zero.

## Validation

- Focused SSE parser, media-type, REST proxy, and response logging tests
- Stream-backed and reactive-body cancellation tests, plus a Vert.x socket cancellation test
- Azure Core and Vert.x HTTP transport package builds
- Checkstyle and SpotBugs

author: vineeththomasalex
body:
## What
Adds a bounded retry (5s budget, 50ms poll interval) around `OpenEventW` in the two PackageManager
test apps (`PackageManager.Test.M.Black.msix`, `PackageManager.Test.M.Blacker.msix`) before falling
back to the existing failure behavior (`RETURN_LAST_ERROR_IF_NULL`, immediate exit).

## Why
Follow-up to the investigation into the residual `PackageDeploymentManagerTests_IsPackageRegistrationPending`
failures (`IsPackageRegistrationPending_Pending` / `IsPackageRegistrationPendingForUser_Pending`),
which fail deterministically on every CI config where `InteractiveExperiences` is built from source
in the monobuild (they pass on stub IXP builds).

**Exhaustive local investigation ruled out every code-level and timing-level hypothesis:**
- The raw `PackageManagement_IsPackageRegistrationPending` FrameworkUdk export — correct in both
  stub and source-built DLL variants (direct P/Invoke, single-call and same-process-ordering tests).
- The compiled `Microsoft.WindowsAppRuntime.dll` WinRT wrapper — correct (direct
  `DllGetActivationFactory` harness, both DLL variants).
- A timing race between `ActivateApplication` and the deferred install — correct with zero
  artificial delay, tested via both PowerShell and a fully-native C++ harness replicating the real
  test's exact call sequence.
- `PackageDeploymentManagerTests_Register`'s ClassSetup cascade polluting this class — ruled out:
  the failure occurs on `Windows.10.Enterprise.LTSC.2021` (a config with **zero** `_Register`
  cascade failures), and `_IsPackageRegistrationPending`'s tests run and complete before any
  `_Register` test starts.
- **The real, completely unmodified TAEF test itself** — built the actual `PackageManagerTests.dll`
  + its full dependency chain (Framework/DataStore/LifetimeManager/Singleton MSIX packages) from
  source and ran it via real `te.exe` on an IXPTools VM. **Passed 4/4 consecutive runs**, zero
  modifications to any test file.

The one concrete fragility found: this app's `WinMain` parses its activation argument as an event
name and calls `OpenEventW` exactly once. If that ever transiently fails to see the caller's
`CreateEventW`-created event (e.g. a broker/activation-scheduling timing variance specific to some
CI execution contexts, not reproduced in this investigation's VM), the app exits almost instantly
instead of holding the package "in use" — producing exactly the observed symptom: no exception, no
error, `IsPackageRegistrationPending()` correctly (from the OS's perspective) reports nothing
pending because the deferred upgrade already silently completed.

## Honest scope of this change
This is **defensive hardening for an identified robustness gap**, not a proven fix for a fully
confirmed root cause. The CI-specific trigger mechanism could not be force-reproduced locally
despite exhausting every constructible hypothesis. If a CI run with this change still fails the
same way, that's meaningful evidence the real cause lies elsewhere (e.g. a CloudTest-infrastructure
scheduling/session issue outside this app's control) — this change should still stand on its own
merits as a legitimate improvement to test-app robustness.

## Test-infrastructure only
Only the two MSIX test app `winmain.cpp` files change (identical diff in both, 15 lines added each).
No product code changes.

## Local verification
- Rebuilt both hardened MSIX packages — compiles cleanly.
- Ran the full `PackageDeploymentManagerTests_IsPackageRegistrationPending` class (8 methods,
  including both `_Pending` variants) via real `te.exe` against the real, unmodified test binary and
  real MSIX/Framework/Bootstrap infrastructure on an IXPTools VM: **8/8 Passed, 0 Failed**, no
  regression from the added retry loop in the already-passing case.

Separate from #6693 (the cascading `ERROR_PACKAGES_IN_USE` fix, out of scope here per that PR's own
"no need to fix it in this PR" guidance for these residual tests).

## Summary

Fixes audit finding **R2**: `AdvancedAnalytics.tsx`'s `fetchAiInsights` (professor Advanced Analytics page) called `POST /api/ai/analytics-insights`, and on any failure (the backend raises a 500 on internal failure — `backend/api/v1/ai_content.py:149-157`) the `catch` block wrote a hardcoded, plausible-sounding fake "AI Summary" + 3 fake suggestions into the exact same `aiInsights` state used for genuine AI responses. author: heiko-w
body:
Alerts were switched on yesterday and produced **18 findings**. Triaged rather than bulk-bumped, because only one of them reaches a user.

## The one that ships

**DOMPurify 3.4.11 → 3.4.13.** The only flagged package in the browser bundle, and it is the sanitizer, so it got looked at properly.

| | needs | 
|---|---|
| `GHSA-55q2-fjhq-7xh7` (medium) | `IN_PLACE` **plus** a hook that *removes* an element — a detached subtree keeps its queued `onload` and fires after `sanitize()` returns |
| `GHSA-c2j3-45gr-mqc4` (low) | `CUSTOM_ELEMENT_HANDLING` **plus** reliance on `afterSanitizeElements` as a policy layer |

Waxwing sets neither `IN_PLACE` nor `CUSTOM_ELEMENT_HANDLING`, uses no `afterSanitizeElements`, and its only hook — in `sanitize.ts` and `squire-adapter.ts` — is `uponSanitizeAttribute`, which removes no elements. **This build was not exposed to either.** Bumped anyway: that analysis holds only for today's configuration, and the sanitizer is the wrong place to run a version behind.

## The other 15 never leave the build

GitHub's scope labels are actively misleading here — `undici` and `fast-uri` are tagged **runtime** while their real paths are `jsdom` (test environment) and `workbox-build` (build tooling). Nothing flagged besides DOMPurify appears in the shipped bundle.

Resolved with `overrides` in **`pnpm-workspace.yaml`**. Every target sits *inside* the range its parent already declares, so these force a patch pnpm would otherwise leave alone rather than overriding a contract:

```
undici           jsdom@29.1.1     wants ^7.25.0   -> 7.29.0
fast-uri         ajv@8.20.0       wants ^3.0.1    -> 3.1.5
nanoid           postcss@8.5.16   wants ^3.3.12   -> 3.3.18
postcss          vite@8.1.3       wants ^8.5.16   -> 8.5.26
brace-expansion  minimatch@5.1.9  wants ^2.0.1    -> 2.1.4
brace-expansion  minimatch@10.2.5 wants ^5.0.5    -> 5.0.9
```

They are in the workspace file and **not** in `pnpm.overrides` in `package.json`, which is where the docs put them: pnpm 11 reads its settings from the workspace file and ignores the `package.json` block without a word. Tried it first, watched `overrides:` fail to appear in `pnpm-lock.yaml`, moved it. Same trap the `allowBuilds` comment two lines above already documents.

## One is deliberately left open

**esbuild, `GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr`.** The fix is 0.28.1; `tsup@8.5.1` — the latest — declares `^0.27.0`, so an override would break a semver contract in the build toolchain. The advisory is a path traversal in esbuild's *own* dev server, on **Windows only**; this repo serves through vite and CI is `ubuntu-latest`.

Not dismissed in GitHub either. It should stay visible until tsup moves.

## Verification

Full gate green (6m 7s), including the 211 sanitizer tests against 3.4.13. Bundle 254.8 kB gz against the 300 kB budget (was 254.5).

author: ru-se
body:
[plan-h33](docs/plan-honsen/plan-h33_sim人間モデルの精緻化.md) の実装です。

## 何が問題だったか

バランス判断はすべて sim の数字を根拠に決めています。その sim が **速度とミス率を独立の乱数2本**で振っていたため、「130ms/打鍵なのにミス率9%」「300ms/打鍵なのにミス率1%」という**実在しない個体**が混ざっていました。難度が上がっても速度が落ちない点も、終盤を楽観的に見積もる原因でした。

## 何をしたか

`skill ∈ [0,1]` **1本**から速度・ミス率・難度追従を導く形にしました。

| プロファイル | 相関（変更前 → 後） |
|---|---|
| normal | +0.016 → **+1.000** |
| wide | +0.020 → **+1.000** |
| duel | 凍結（意図的に不変） |

難度追従は `skill` に反比例します（上手い人ほど崩れない）。

| skill | heat 0 → 17 | 倍率 |
|---|---|---|
| 0.00 | 350 → 588 ms/打鍵 | ×1.68 |
| 0.50 | 200 → 285 | ×1.43 |
| 1.00 | 50 → 58 | ×1.17 |

**`--profile match`（Bot 96体＋人間3名）を追加**しました。本 plan の実用目的です。

```
人間の平均順位: 46〜48 / 99（目安 40〜60 に収まる）
人間が1位     : 11%（偶然なら3%）
tier 配分      : 24 / 48 / 23（h31 の 25/50/25 と一致）
```

## モデルは h31 と共有しています

`internal/typist` に `SkillCurve` / `At(skill)` を足しただけで、**新しいパッケージは作っていません**。`Serve` / `Individual` は無変更です。共有できていないのは「重み付き抽選」の数行だけ（depguard が `sim → app` を禁じているため）。

## 🔴 h26 の再測定で重大な発見（値は変えていません）

`weightMiss` の拮抗点が **30 → 22** に動いていました。**原因は h33 ではなく h32** です。

| W_MISS | h30まで | **h32後** | 現 main |
|---|---|---|---|
| 22 | −23.8 | **−4.0** | **−0.4** |
| **30** | **−1.6** ← h26 §2.2 はここ | +25.4 | +25.8 |

h32（難度カーブの時間主軸化）で序盤から語が伸び、ミスの絶対数が増えて罰が再び重くなった、という向きです。**h32 の後に duel スイープを回し直していませんでした。**

本番は `weightMiss = 30` のままで、**この PR では値を変えていません**（設計判断は所有者が決めるため）。測定結果は [plan-h26 §2.4](docs/plan-honsen/plan-h26_バランス検証.md) に記録しています。

## plan の誤りを3件見つけました

1. **🔴 §1.1「duel を凍結」と §5「h26 を測り直す」が噛み合っていない。** `weightMiss` を測る道具は duel スイープただ1つなので、duel を凍結する限り §5 は**定義上ゼロ変化**になります。§5 を「今の main で 30 は成立しているか」と読み替えたことで上の発見が出ました
2. §5 の表が古い（25 → 30 が反映されていない）
3. §1.1 が `skill` の**両端の値**を書いていない（下記）

## 検証

`make check` 緑。決定性維持（同一シードで完全一致・6プロファイルで確認）。`duel` が乱数を1つも引かないことをテストで固定したので、h26 のスイープは今後も動きません。

| normal・20 runs | 変更前 | 変更後 |
|---|---|---|
| 決着時間 | 120.0s | 120.0s |
| 負スコア / 早期切り事故 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| 分離度 | 4600 | 4521 |
| **実力相関** | 0.92 | **0.95** |

実力が1本のスカラーになったぶん、順位が実力を素直に反映するようになりました。

## 判断待ちが2件あります

**① `weightMiss`**（上記）。**② `skill` の両端**を 350〜50ms（中央200ms）にしています。中央が旧モデルの中心かつ h31 の中 tier と一致するので、今回の変更を「相関と難度追従の効果」だけに切り分けて読めます。別案（h31 の 400/150 に合わせる）だと母集団の中心が 275ms へ動き、モデル変更と母集団変更が混ざります。

どちらも所有者に確認中です。

author: kaiwenyao
body:
## Bug
The miniprogram only connected to the `/room` Socket.IO namespace (derived from `config.socketUrl`). The client's `handleSocketPacket` dropped every `/avalon`-framed packet, and every `avalon:*` emit was framed for `/room`, where the backend has **no** handler (the AvalonGateway lives on `/avalon`).

Consequence: the entire Avalon game — `avalon:state`, proposals, `avalon:team-vote`, quests, assassination, `avalon:game-finished` — could not run through the miniprogram. Verified two ways:
1. Static: exact client parser logic drops `/avalon` packets and frames emits for `/room`.
2. Live: a real socket.io server with `/room` + `/avalon` namespaces — the old client receives no `avalon:state`, no `avalon:vote-updated`, and its `avalon:team-vote` is never handled; the fixed client receives all of them and the vote is handled.

## Fix
Subscribe to the `/avalon` namespace on the **same** Engine.IO connection (Socket.IO namespace multiplexing):
- After engine-open, send a CONNECT for `/avalon` with the same `{ token }` auth payload.
- Dispatch incoming packets by namespace (route `/avalon` events to listeners, keep `/room` as before).
- Route `avalon:*` emits to `/avalon`.
- Expose a local `avalon:connect` event so the page (re)sends `avalon:join` once the namespace ack arrives (the main `connect` fires on the `/room` ack, before `/avalon` is ready).
- Clean teardown: send `/avalon` namespace disconnect on manual disconnect; reset `avalonConnected` on close/reconnect/connect.

The avalon page emits `avalon:join` on both `connect` and the new `avalon:connect`; `avalon:join` is idempotent so the duplicate is harmless, and it covers the race where the page loads/connects before the `/avalon` ack.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- End-to-end raw-protocol test (real socket.io server, both namespaces): fixed client receives `avalon:state` + `avalon:vote-updated`, and its `avalon:team-vote` is handled by the `/avalon` gateway. Negative control with the old single-namespace behavior fails exactly as expected.

author: rjayasin
body:
The knockout-panel fix landed in #31, so this is the notes half of it, rebased onto `main` and reduced to the one file #31 did not carry.

## What it adds

A **"When a line leaves its drawing"** section, placed before the hand-tuned tables — because those tables are the fix menu and only answer one of the four causes. It gives the diagnostic order:

1. **See both courses at once** — the stored path over the artwork, and a raw tile crop for the drawing on its own, since a path drawn over its line hides the line.
2. **Ask the feed where the route goes** — stop names in order through `to_px`, which separates the drawn corridor from the decoy running parallel before any pixel work starts.
3. **Score against the strokes, not the mask** — `pdf_ink([LEGEND_INK[feed]])` is the drawing itself, complete under every label, and the one yardstick a mask change cannot move.
4. **Ask whether the mask holds the line** — query `mask_tree` with the ink points; a run of ink several px from any mask pixel is a hole, and a hole is what a snap falls into.

Then what each answer means: a hole under a place name is `unfade`'s business and its gates are measurable per pixel, so print them and let the gate that rejects them name the fix; an intact mask with a wandering path is an anchor question; a mask holding lettering or a neighbour's casing is a colour question; and a stretch the sheet never drew is already right however a metric scores it. It closes on pricing the general fix — a change inside the mask machinery moves every colour-masked feed at once, so diff per system and look at the largest movers, because an improving total can hide a route that got worse.

It also records the trap behind that investigation: a build without pymupdf falls back to no badges, no strokes and no panels, writes the empty stroke set into `scratch/mask-cache/` under a key that says nothing about which libraries were installed, and the next build reads it back and comes out wrong in silence.

Documentation only — no code, no rebuild, `schedule.json` untouched.

author: shriya678
body:
## Summary

Closes the last P1/P2 gap — @mentions in comments now actually deliver. Bell icon in the top bar with a live unread badge; click a notification to jump to the mentioned task.

**Ships:**
- Backend `NotificationsModule` (list / unread-count / mark-read / mark-all-read) + `MENTION` emission inside the comment-create transaction
- Frontend bell in TopBar with 30s polling for unread count + on-demand full-list fetch
- Shared `@mention` regex between backend parser and frontend renderer — one source of truth for what counts as a mention

## Design decisions

- **Poll, not WebSocket.** Simpler infra, no gateway to manage. 30s cadence matches "notification" expectations without pounding the server. Trade-off: latency for the recipient. Fine for a first cut.
- **Two separate queries: cheap count + on-demand list.** The bell badge polls a single indexed COUNT every 30s. The full list only fetches when the popover opens. Most users have zero unread — no reason to pull 50 rows every poll.
- **Mention emission inside the comment transaction.** A comment insert + activity append + notification insert either all commit or all roll back. Prevents split-brain where notifications reference a comment that failed to insert.
- **Silent skip for typos + self-mentions + seeded users.** `@nonexistent-user` doesn't 400 the comment — it just doesn't notify anyone. `@yourself` is a no-op. Seeded fake teammates (Alex/Jamie/Sam) never get notifications because they'll never log in to see them.
- **404 for other users' notification ids.** `PATCH /notifications/foo/read` where `foo` belongs to another user returns 404 — indistinguishable from "doesn't exist" — so we don't leak the existence of other users' notifications.
- **Bell outside the scrollable actions strip.** On narrow viewports the page's own actions can overflow; the bell stays pinned to the right so it's always reachable.
- **`refetchIntervalInBackground: false`** — hidden tabs don't poll. Saves server load; the count catches up when the tab becomes visible.

## How to test

**Multi-user smoke path** (needs two accounts):

1. Sign in as User A. Invite User B (guest or Google) as MEMBER of their workspace.
2. Sign in as User B in another window. Switch to User A's workspace, open any task.
3. Add a comment: `@userA-username hey take a look`.
4. Within 30s, User A's bell shows badge `1`. Click → popover shows the notification → click it → jumps to the mentioned task, badge clears.
5. Self-mention (`@yourself`) → no notification.
6. Typo (`@nonexistent-user`) → no notification.
7. "Mark all read" clears every unread at once.

**Postman folder 14** — 4 endpoint tests pass.

## Also: @-typeahead picker in the composer

Discovered while smoke-testing this feature: users can't guess teammate usernames from display names. A user named "Shriya Gupta" has username "guptashriya" — typing `@shriya-gupta` silently delivers no notification.

The fix is a Slack-style typeahead: type `@` in the comment composer → dropdown of workspace members filtered by username OR full name → arrow/Enter or click to insert the exact `@username` token. The picker is workspaceSlug-aware and appears in every composer (top-level, reply, edit).

Bonus: teaches users what usernames look like, so mentions typed from memory later stand a chance too.


## Prod checklist

- [x] Typecheck green (api + web)
- [x] Lint green — 0 errors (api 190 warnings all pre-existing, web 8 warnings all pre-existing hard-navs)
- [x] Tests green (158/158)
- [x] `next build` green — 14 routes compile
- [x] Schema unchanged — `Notification` model already existed with `MENTION` enum
- [x] `(userId, readAt)` index is already in the schema — hot path (unread count) stays constant-time
- [x] Postman: 15 folders (was 14), notifications inserted as 14, Logout renumbered to 15

## Related

- **This is the last P0/P1/P2 item from the original plan.** Every deferred feature now ships.

author: somanshreddy
body:
## Description

Stacked on #296. That PR bumped the Go toolchain by hand-editing the same version string in six
workflow spots; this one removes the need to ever do that again.

The version was written in **seven** places: the `go` directive in `go.mod`, four `setup-go` pins in
`ci.yml`, and one each in `release-stable.yml` and `dev-release.yml`. Nothing kept them in agreement
except remembering to grep.

That drift is not cosmetic, and the reason is worth knowing because it is not obvious from reading the
workflows. `setup-go` exports `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` itself:

```js
// actions/setup-go src/main.ts — "so any `go` commands run as child-process
// don't cause toolchain downloads"
core.exportVariable(installer.GOTOOLCHAIN_ENV_VAR, installer.GOTOOLCHAIN_LOCAL_VAL)
```

With `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, the installed toolchain cannot upgrade itself to satisfy `go.mod`. So a pin
that falls **behind** the `go` directive fails the build outright, and one that runs **ahead** of it
builds against a newer stdlib than the module declares. Every `setup-go` step now uses
`go-version-file: go.mod`, leaving the directive as the only place the version exists.

## How it works

`setup-go` reads the version out of `go.mod` itself. Its parser prefers a `toolchain` directive, but
only when `GOTOOLCHAIN` is not `local`, then falls back to the `go` directive:

```js
// installer.ts parseGoVersionFile
const matchGo = contents.match(/^go (\d+(\.\d+)*)/m);
```

Our `go.mod` has no `toolchain` line, so both paths land on the `go` directive and resolve `1.25.13`.

One property to understand before editing `go.mod`, because it is silent: `setup-go` matches its input
with `semver.satisfies`, so **whether the toolchain is pinned or floating depends on how many
components the directive has.**

| directive | installs | behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `go 1.25.13` | exactly 1.25.13 | pinned (1.25.14 does not satisfy) |
| `go 1.26` | latest 1.26.x | floats |

Today the directive is patchful, so resolution is exact and behaviour is **identical** to the literal
pins this replaces. If someone later writes a two-component directive, every job silently starts
taking the latest patch. That trade is real in both directions: floating picks up stdlib security
fixes without a workflow edit (and would have pre-empted #296 entirely), while pinning keeps release
builds reproducible. This PR does not decide it, and deliberately changes no behaviour; it is recorded
here so the choice is made knowingly rather than discovered.

## Design decisions

**`go-version-file` rather than a workflow-level env var or a reusable workflow.** An env var would
still be a second copy of the number, just a better-organised one. Reading `go.mod` makes the module's
declared minimum and the installed toolchain the same value by construction, so they cannot disagree.

**A test, not just a convention.** The entire benefit evaporates the first time someone re-pins a
literal version by hand, and a reviewer would have to notice. `cmd/heygen/go_version_pin_test.go`
asserts the invariant instead. It follows the precedent of `generated_example_flags_test.go`, which
similarly reads a repo file outside its own package to guard a cross-file invariant.

**The test reads both `.yml` and `.yaml`.** This repo already spells one config `.goreleaser.yaml`, so
a `.yaml` workflow was a live way to land outside the sweep. Its documented boundary is direct
`setup-go` steps in top-level workflow files; a reusable workflow or composite action could install Go
without a step it sees. Nothing uses either today, and the comment says so rather than leaving it
implied.

## Testing

- Every assertion was mutation-tested: each break was observed failing with a distinct message, then
  reverted.
  - Reintroduced `go-version: "1.25.14"` in `ci.yml` → fails, naming file and job.
  - Pointed `go-version-file` at `.go-version` → fails on the mismatch.
  - Widened the search dir so no `setup-go` steps matched → trips the explicit `steps == 0` guard,
    which exists because an empty match set would otherwise pass while checking nothing.

author: honglu2875
body:
…ndex

The pointer trie could not do what this library is for. Each TrieNode carried an unordered_map, an atomic counter and an omp_lock_t -- 150-250 bytes, up to five nodes per token, so roughly 1 KB of RAM per corpus token. It also fixed n at construction, capped the vocabulary at 65535, and never touched disk. It had real bugs besides: `get()` used `operator[]`, which inserts on miss and so mutated the children map inside lock-free readers; `insert()` raced and lost counts; `put()` re-entered a non-recursive lock; serialize/deserialize recursed per node; and the destructor leaked every child.

This implements Infini-gram (arXiv:2401.17377) instead: a memory-mapped suffix array over the token stream, ~6 bytes per token on disk, arbitrary n, and the longest-matching-suffix queries the paper is named for.

Index format (docs/format.md): per shard a `tokenized` token array, a `table` suffix array of packed token indices, an `offset` document table, and a `bucket` search accelerator. Shards are independent and counts add, so a corpus larger than RAM is indexed one in-memory shard at a time with no merge step.

Three things make queries fast:

- A two-level in-RAM jump table. Level one maps a token id straight to its rank range and falls out of suffix-array construction for free; level two samples the first 8 tokens of every 512th suffix (N/32 bytes) so the top of every binary search runs in RAM. 2.4x faster warm, 3.6x cold, and it is provably answer-neutral -- the tests assert identical results with it disabled.
- Range reuse. Extending an n-gram searches inside its prefix's range; infgram_batch exploits the fact that the matching suffix grows by at most one per position, making per-token scoring amortised O(1) searches.
- One persistent thread pool, so no thread is created on the query path. Throughput scales close to linearly with cores.

Construction uses libsais on the uint16 array directly, so suffixes sort in numeric token order and no byte-level encoding trick is needed. Shards build in separate processes rather than threads: libsais' own OpenMP scaling is ~1.25x at 30 threads, while independent shards scale nearly linearly.

Verified against brute force at both scales -- exhaustive Counter oracles on small corpora, and on a 7.9B-token FineWeb-edu index all 50100 distinct token counts against a bincount plus exact full-corpus n-gram counts. That index builds in 6.2 minutes and answers 2.09M queries/s warm.

body:
This PR upgrades the otelcollector to the latest version available for the opentelemetry-collector and opentelemetry-operator.

It was automatically generated by the GitHub Actions workflow.

The summary of the OSS changelog is below:
# Prometheusreceiver Changes
## v0.156.0 to v0.158.0

Generated on: 2026-08-18 07:17:20

---

No changes found for prometheusreceiver between v0.156.0 and v0.158.0

# Target-allocator Changes
## v0.156.0 to v0.158.0

Generated on: 2026-08-18 07:17:37

---

### 0.158.0
- [**FEATURE**] `operator, collector, target allocator`: Enable operator, collector, target allocator network policies by default. ([#5394](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-operator/pull/5394)) Feature gate `operator.networkpolicy` and `operand.networkpolicy` are promoted to beta, and enabled by default. These feature gates create network policies for the operator and operand components.
### 0.157.0
- [**FEATURE**] `target allocator`: Allow enabling mTLS between the target allocator and the collector using user-provided certificate Secrets, without requiring cert-manager. ([#3982](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-operator/pull/3982)) When `spec.targetAllocator.mtls.useCertManager` is set to `false`, the new `mtls.tls` block references user-provided certificates. The CA certificate may be sourced from either a Secret or a ConfigMap (`certificateAuthorityCertificate.secret` / `.configMap`). The target allocator's server certificate and the collector's client certificate each reference their certificate and private key independently, so the certificate and key may live in different Secrets. Data keys default to `tls.crt`, `tls.key` and `ca.crt` and can be overridden per reference. The CA reference is required in this mode. 
- [**BUG FIX**] `target allocator`: Seed Prometheus's scrape labels (`job`, `__scheme__`, `__metrics_path__`, `__scrape_interval__`, `__scrape_timeout__`, `__param_*`) before relabel filtering, so keep/drop rules referencing them make the same decisions as Prometheus instead of silently dropping or over-allocating targets ([#5246](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-operator/pull/5246)) The seeded labels also feed the target identity hash, matching Prometheus's post-relabel label partition more closely. With the `relabel-config` filter strategy enabled, existing targets are re-allocated once on upgrade because their hashes change. The served (pre-relabel) target labels are unchanged. 
### 0.157.0
- [**FEATURE**] `target allocator`: Support exporting the TargetAllocator's self-telemetry metrics via OTLP, in addition to the Prometheus /metrics endpoint. ([#5047](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-operator/pull/5047)) Configure it under `spec.targetAllocator.telemetry.metrics.otlp` (OpenTelemetryCollector CR) or `spec.telemetry.metrics.otlp` (TargetAllocator CR), with endpoint, protocol (grpc/http), temporality, headers, TLS and export interval/timeout. Metrics registered directly on the Prometheus registry (Prometheus service discovery, Go runtime and process collectors) are bridged into the OTLP export so the Prometheus endpoint and OTLP expose the same metric set. 
- [**BUG FIX**] `target allocator`: Fix collector mtls with a TargetAllocator CR ([#4297](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-operator/pull/4297)) This only affected collectors associated with a TargetAllocator CR whose name differs from the collector's, e.g. via the `opentelemetry.io/target-allocator` label, causing them to address the wrong hostname (and TLS certificate) once mTLS was enabled. 
- [**BUG FIX**] `target allocator`: Refresh stale Prometheus meta labels (e.g. `__meta_kubernetes_pod_name`) on rediscovered targets whose address is unchanged ([#4839](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-operator/pull/4839)) Target identity is deliberately hashed without meta labels, since Prometheus discards them after relabeling. But because the allocator's target map is keyed by that same hash, a rediscovered target whose address is unchanged (e.g. a hostNetwork DaemonSet pod after a restart) was never recognized as changed, so its stale meta labels persisted until target-allocator itself restarted. 
- [**BUG FIX**] `target allocator`: Propagate the TargetAllocator CR's metadata annotations to all resources created for it, and restrict `podAnnotations` to the pod template ([#4393](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-operator/pull/4393)) This aligns the TargetAllocator with the OpenTelemetryCollector behavior: CR metadata annotations now land (respecting the annotations filter) on the Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, ServiceAccount, ServiceMonitor, PodDisruptionBudget and NetworkPolicy, while `podAnnotations` is no longer copied to the NetworkPolicy and PodDisruptionBudget.
