author: leandrorojas
body:
Dependabot has **never opened a PR** on this repo. Investigation found two unrelated failures, only one of which needed a fix.

## `github_actions` — not a config problem, already resolved

```
Error during file fetching; aborting: /action.yml or /.github/workflows/<anything>.yml not found
```

On 2026-07-20 the repo had no workflow files. `ci.yml` landed 2026-08-11, `codeql.yml` 2026-08-14, so this job was correctly reporting there was nothing to scan. It needs no change.

The two ecosystems run as **independent jobs** (separate update IDs), so this was never blocked by the pyfangs problem.

## `uv` — the real failure

```
dependency_file_not_resolvable
  × Failed to download and build `pyfangs @ git+ssh://git@github.com/leandrorojas/pyfangs@v0.7.3`
  ╰─▶ process didn't exit successfully: git fetch ssh://git@github.com/leandrorojas/pyfangs
```

Dependabot's container has no SSH key, so resolving the lockfile fails and the job aborts **before updating anything** — including packages unrelated to pyfangs.

This PR adds a `git` registry supplying HTTPS credentials for github.com.

## What you need to do

Create a **`DEPENDABOT_PAT`** secret with read access to `leandrorojas/pyfangs`:

**Settings → Secrets and variables → Dependabot → New repository secret**

Note that's the *Dependabot* tab — Actions secrets are not visible to Dependabot, which is why the existing `PYFANGS_DEPLOY_KEY` doesn't help here.

A fine-grained PAT with `Contents: Read` on that one repo is enough.

## Honest uncertainty

`pyproject.toml` declares the dependency as `ssh://`, while Dependabot's credential injection is HTTPS-based. Whether its proxy rewrites the scheme isn't something I can confirm without a live run — the next scheduled job will tell us. If it still fails, the fallback is switching `pyproject.toml` to an HTTPS git URL, which also means giving CI a token instead of its current SSH deploy key.

## Separate findings, not fixed here

- **Dependabot alerts are disabled** (`vulnerability-alerts` → 404, `dependabot_security_updates: disabled`). That's the vulnerability-driven feature, distinct from these version updates — so you currently get no notification when a dependency has a known CVE.
- **No run since 2026-07-20** — four scheduled Mondays missed. The pause reason isn't exposed via API; the Dependabot page under Insights → Dependency graph should show it.

Both are repo-settings changes rather than config, so I've left them to you.

Config only — 336 tests, 100% coverage, unchanged.

Configure Dependabot to authenticate against the private pyfangs repository so scheduled uv dependency updates can proceed.

Bug Fixes:
- Enable Dependabot to resolve private Git dependencies for the uv ecosystem by supplying HTTPS registry credentials.

Enhancements:
- Associate the private pyfangs registry with uv dependency updates while keeping GitHub Actions updates independent.

author: weisiang329-eng
body:
## In plain language

The notification bell and the pop-up banner at the top of the screen were
re-reading the **entire** announcements table about once a minute, on every open
desktop, for every signed-in person — measured 2026-08-18 at roughly **0.9-1.4
seconds every minute**, on both.

This PR makes them reuse a short-lived saved copy so the database is not asked
the same heavy question every minute. Two rounds of work:

1. The bell was not using the cache at all. (First fix.)
2. Then a live capture showed the pop-up was *also* slow every minute even
   though it *was* "cached" — because the saved copy expired at the exact moment
   the next check arrived, so it was thrown away before it could ever be reused.
   (Second fix — this is the important one.)

Nothing about what the user sees changes: same bell, same banner, same contents.

## Round 1 — the bell was never cached

`GET /api/announcements/banner?scope=system` (the bell) bypassed the per-user
cache and ran the full-table build on every 60s poll. Fixed by caching it like
the pop-up, with the cache key carrying the **scope** so the two per-user
payloads (human / system) can never answer each other.

## Round 2 — the cache was configured but never HITTING

A live capture showed the already-cached **human** slice still at ~874-984ms on
**every** 60s poll. A cache that truly hits is not slow every poll. Two causes:

1. **TTL == poll.** `CONFIG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS.banner` was 60s and the frontend
   polls at 60s (`useAnnouncementBanner.ts` `POLL_MS`), so the KV entry expired
   exactly as the next poll arrived → near-100% miss. (The neighbouring
   `presence` note in `configCache.ts` already recorded the same KV-consistency
   failure at 15s.) Raised to **300s** (5 polls, matching `branding`), with a
   MUST-exceed-poll invariant comment citing the live evidence.

2. **Serial DB reads.** The announcements read and the acks read were two
   sequential awaits, so a MISS paid ~2 round-trips (~900ms). They are
   independent reads of the same user → `Promise.all`, so a MISS is ~1
   round-trip. Behaviour-identical.

### The catch a longer TTL buys, and how it is closed

The 60s TTL was deliberately chosen to match the targeting freshness window: the
banner filters by `department_id` / `position_id` / company grants, so a 300s
TTL would serve up to 5 minutes of STALE TARGETING unless those edits bust the
cache. **The session bust did NOT cover this** — it fires only on disable / role
change, while a dept-only / position-only / company-only edit changes targeting
without touching the session.

So `bustBannerForUser` (both scopes) is wired into every per-user targeting-edit
route, and a department DELETE bumps the banner family version (a bulk,
unknown-subset un-assign):

```enumeration
$ git grep -n "bustBannerForUser(" -- backend/src
backend/src/routes/announcements.ts:1262:  await bustBannerForUser(c.env, user.id);
backend/src/routes/users.ts:807:  await bustBannerForUser(c.env, id);
backend/src/routes/users.ts:1826:    await bustBannerForUser(c.env, id);
backend/src/routes/users.ts:1907:  await bustBannerForUser(c.env, id);
backend/src/services/configCache.ts:235:export async function bustBannerForUser(
backend/src/services/personalNotice.ts:118:      await bustBannerForUser(env, uid);
```

- `users.ts:807` — PUT `/:id/companies` (company-grant change)
- `users.ts:1826` — PATCH `/:id`, gated by a `bannerTargetingChanged` predicate
  over department_id / position_id / role_id / status / department_ids /
  company_ids
- `users.ts:1907` — DELETE `/:id` (disable / delete removes the audience member)
- `announcements.ts:1262` — the ack endpoint (unchanged; own ack)
- `personalNotice.ts:118` — a private notice targeted at a user (unchanged)

```enumeration
$ git grep -n "bumpConfigVersion(c.env, \"banner\")" -- backend/src
backend/src/routes/announcements.ts:948:  await bumpConfigVersion(c.env, "banner");
backend/src/routes/announcements.ts:1129:  await bumpConfigVersion(c.env, "banner");
backend/src/routes/announcements.ts:1195:  await bumpConfigVersion(c.env, "banner");
backend/src/routes/announcements.ts:1225:  await bumpConfigVersion(c.env, "banner");
backend/src/routes/departments.ts:189:  await bumpConfigVersion(c.env, "banner");
```

`departments.ts:189` is the new one — a department DELETE un-assigns every member
(`UPDATE users SET department_id = NULL`), so the whole banner family version is
bumped after it. Positions DELETE is blocked (409) while any user holds the
position, so it never bulk-changes targeting. Roles do not affect the banner
filter. The invite path sets company grants for a brand-new placeholder user
that has no cached banner yet, so it is intentionally not busted.

## Tests

- `configCache.test.ts`
  - Scope keys never collide (`human` != `system` for the same user/version);
    `bustBannerForUser` clears BOTH scopes and leaves other users untouched.
  - Router flow: a 2nd `scope=system` read HITS its own entry, and the human
    read still returns the human payload.
  - **TTL invariant**: `CONFIG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS.banner` stays comfortably above
    the 60s poll (never == poll).
  - **Bust wiring** pinned by a source-structure test (see the honesty note
    below): the PATCH predicate covers every targeting field and gates the bust;
    PUT `/:id/companies` and DELETE `/:id` call it; department DELETE bumps the
    banner version after un-assigning members.
- `announcementsBannerFilter.test.ts` — the system slice is now `miss`→`hit`; a
  system entry never answers the human read (this exercises the parallelized
  reads and asserts the exact payload is unchanged).

## Measurement

- **Before (live):** human + system ~874-1393ms every ~60s, desktop,
  2026-08-18, `[perf]` console.
- **Structural after:** both slices take the cached path; the TTL (300s) now
  comfortably exceeds the 60s poll so a poll lands inside a valid entry; a MISS
  is halved by the parallel reads. Proven by the miss→hit and TTL-invariant
  tests.
- A production before/after stopwatch needs an owner-run probe (a worktree has
  no prod KV), so it is **DEFERRED, not fabricated**.

## Honesty note — why the route wiring is a source-structure test

The users / departments handlers use `getDb` (drizzle → Postgres). This vitest
harness has **no** Postgres binding — `getDb` throws `DATABASE_URL /
HYPERDRIVE.connectionString is empty` (observed while writing the test), so those
handlers cannot be executed here. The behavioural "both scopes cleared" is proven
directly against KV by the `bustBannerForUser` test; the route wiring is pinned
by reading the handler source, the same pattern `mailAliasRevocation.test.ts`
already uses for the users PATCH.

## Gates run locally

- `npm --prefix backend run typecheck` — clean.
- `configCache` + `announcementsBannerFilter` + `personalNotice` vitest — 26 passed.
- `npm --prefix backend run audit:swallowed-reads` — at the ceiling, no new swallowed read.
- `npm --prefix backend run audit:bug-index` — generates cleanly.
- Working-agreement gate — OK (guides updated: announcements + team-members).

Still a DRAFT — a human reviews; not auto-merged.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: jzy1688
body:
Fixes #4458

### Description

Both slot-stat comparators return a `uint64_t` difference as `int`:

```c
return entry_a.stat - entry_b.stat;
```

The subtraction is done in `uint64_t` arithmetic and then truncated to `int`, so `ORDERBY` sorts incorrectly once two slots' counters differ by more than `INT_MAX` — and a difference of exactly 2³² truncates to zero, making two very different slots compare equal.

This affects the cumulative counters `cpu-usec`, `network-bytes-in` and `network-bytes-out`, which grow without bound until `CONFIG RESETSTAT` or a slot ownership change.

Replaced with an explicit three-way comparison, keeping the existing tie-break on slot number (safe, since slots are bounded at 16383):

```c
return (entry_a.stat > entry_b.stat) - (entry_a.stat < entry_b.stat);
```

The values are only compared, never subtracted, so nothing can overflow. This idiom is already used at `src/vset.c:869`.

Surfaced by the review of #4455, which adds a fourth cumulative byte counter that would inherit this.

### Testing

Added a test to `tests/unit/cluster/slot-stats.tcl` that drives one slot's `network-bytes-in` past `INT_MAX` (repeatedly overwriting one large key, so memory stays flat) and asserts the ordering in both directions. It fails without the fix — the heavy slot lands last in a `DESC` sort — and passes with it.

Tagged `slow`: the test moves ~2.2 GB and takes ~150s.

author: jesperdramsch
body:
Follow-up to #41 — Copilot's review comment arrived after the merge, so this picks it up. Good catch, and it turned out to be wrong in a second way too.

## The comment

> `family in H` is computed via `hundos.includes(mon.families[0])`, but both the hundo list and the typed family can be in different locales […] Canonicalize both sides.

Correct. `buildFilters` already solved exactly this for the H∩L set math (`canonKey`, `src/App.jsx:1414`) — the panel was the odd one out.

## The second way it was wrong

`+name` selects the whole **candy family**, so a hundo Pikachu covers a Raichu. A raw string compare misses that regardless of locale. So rather than canonicalising names, `hundoFamilyMatch()` resolves both sides through `resolveSpeciesInfo` and compares **line roots** — the same identity `+name` itself uses. Same idea as `canonKey`, one level up from names to families.

```js
hundoFamilyMatch(["glurak"], "charizard")   // true  — cross-locale
hundoFamilyMatch(["リザードン"], "charizard")  // true  — cross-script
hundoFamilyMatch(["pikachu"], "raichu")     // true  — candy family
hundoFamilyMatch(["pikachu"], "magikarp")   // false — still says no when it means no
```

## Scope

**Display-only.** The trash/trade verdicts were already correct: `buildFilters` renders hundos through `speciesForOutput`, and `VerifyPanel` expands the candy family in the same locale, so both sides of the *evaluation* already agreed. Only the "family in H" line lied — it told you a species wasn't protected while the filter was protecting it.

## Verification

14 new assertions in `check-verify.mjs` (51 total): both directions of the evolution line, cross-script input, the over-reporting guards (unrelated line, empty/undefined/unresolvable input), and a cross-check that a DE-stored hundo really does emit a `+charizard` clause that the EN mon matches — so the display and the filter can't drift apart again.

All 8 suites pass; build clean; fixtures unchanged.

## What changed

- documented the target production architecture for a private Gate.io copy-trading platform
- added a target-state copy engine that calculates follower exposure from master position/equity
- added member risk decisions for emergency stop, daily loss, drawdown, leverage, position caps, reduce-only mode and hard halt
- split long/short flips into a confirmed reduce-only close followed by a conditional open
- added deterministic Gate order text for duplicate suppression
- added an environment-aware Gate Futures client with Testnet default and explicit live-order guards
- added AES-256-GCM credential envelopes with account-specific authenticated data
- added a protected dry-run preview endpoint; it is disabled unless explicit environment variables and an admin token are configured
- added the initial Supabase schema, RLS boundaries, audit/error tables and a `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` durable queue lease function
- documented required environment variables and production release blockers

## Why

The current repository is a single-account, read-only Vercel dashboard. A multi-member trading system needs authenticated tenant isolation, encrypted per-member credentials, durable order state, fixed-IP worker execution, idempotency and position reconciliation before any order API is enabled.

This foundation deliberately uses the master account’s actual position as the desired state rather than blindly replaying individual master orders. That allows recovery after missed WebSocket events, partial fills and worker restarts.

## Safety boundary

- no live trading is enabled
- order placement is disabled by default
- Testnet is the default Gate environment
- live orders require two independent runtime opt-ins
- the database system control starts in `halted` with copying disabled
- the preview API returns 404 unless explicitly enabled and authenticated
- the migration has not been applied to any Supabase environment
- no Vercel production deployment is included in this PR

## Validation

```text
node --test
12 tests passed, 0 failed
```

Covered behavior includes proportional copying, maximum exposure caps, a 0% cap that flattens an existing position, the 200% copy ceiling, emergency-stop reductions, direction flips, drift tolerance, deterministic Gate order text, quantity quantization, credential encryption/AAD, request signing and live-order blocking.

## Next phase

1. protect the legacy public account-data endpoint
2. add Supabase Auth, invitation/approval and member/admin authorization
3. implement write-only Gate API credential onboarding and verification
4. build the fixed-egress-IP Testnet worker and master WebSocket/REST reconciler
5. add durable Testnet execution, fill reconciliation and operational monitoring

author: mishrasanjeev
body:
Closes **DATA-GOV-05** for IPLF-028B (M2).

## Three clauses, two of which had nowhere to live

Dual approval was **already enforced in the database** — `ck_legal_hold_activation_approval` and `ck_legal_hold_approver_distinct` refuse an active hold without a distinct, company-scoped approver. That constraint remains the guarantee, because it survives a service bug.

The other two couldn't live there:

- **step-up** is a property of the *session*, not the row — no CHECK constraint can express it
- **"release never deletes immediately without a new dry-run"** is a relationship between two records and a clock

There was no hold activation or release path at all, so neither clause had anywhere to attach.

## Release is the clause with teeth

Releasing a hold deletes nothing by itself — it removes the thing that was **blocking** deletion. So the operator must have seen a *current* manifest of what becomes eligible the moment the hold lifts.

| condition | result |
|---|---|
| no dry run | refused |
| dry run **predating** the hold | refused — otherwise the control is satisfied by a manifest generated before the preserved data existed |
| dry run from another company | refused |
| requester approves their own release | refused |
| current dry run + distinct approver | **releases** |

Step-up uses named purposes (`legal_hold_change`, `retention_policy_activation`) rather than the existing `destructive_action`, so an audit trail says which control was satisfied.

## Three corrections that came from the schema and tests, not from me

1. **The immutability trigger rejected activation** — `created_by_membership_id` and companions are immutable. That's the schema encoding dual approval end-to-end: the requester is recorded when the hold is *drafted*, so activation cannot retroactively nominate one. It now refuses a draft with no recorded requester rather than installing itself as the first party.
2. **naive/aware datetime `TypeError`** — SQLite returns naive timestamps while the app writes aware ones. A real bug, normalised at the comparison.
3. **The cross-tenant test fabricated a company id** and hit a foreign key — proving nothing about cross-tenant behaviour. It now creates a real second company.

## Verification

- 10 new tests covering each refusal **and** the legitimate path — a control that blocks the correct workflow is an outage
- **352 passed** across governance, hold, audit, purge, export and security suites
- change gate, migration preflight, ruff — clean

author: egorkhmelev
body:
`git status` exits 128 in an LFS repo for a read-only agent. Fixed by symlinking git-lfs's scratch dir out of the read-only clone.

## The bug

From a prod log (`task-20260817-1854-1ahc24`):

```
Error cleaning Git LFS object: open .../.git/lfs/tmp/3829252116: read-only file system
fatal: e2e/snapshots/.../allBadges-badgeCategory-special.png: clean filter 'lfs' failed
```

git-lfs writes a temp object into `.git/lfs/tmp` whenever its clean filter runs, and `git status` triggers that filter on an LFS file whose index stat data is stale. On a read-only clone the write fails and takes git down with it.

Both conditions are needed, which is why it looked intermittent. Confirmed in a synthetic LFS repo:

| tmp dir | index stat | `git status` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| writable | stale | exit 0 |
| **unwritable** | **stale** | **exit 128**, `clean filter 'lfs' failed` |

Affects `sweatcoin-mobile` and `sweatcoin-backend`. Worse than a failed command: the workaround seen in prod was to bypass the LFS filters, which then reported **279 unmodified PNGs as modified**, since git compares the smudged binary against the stored pointer.

## The fix

```
link:   <clone>/.git/lfs/tmp                   ← read-only mount
target: <workspace>/.lfs-tmp/<repo>            ← writable mount
rm(link); symlink(target, link)
```

`.git/lfs/tmp` becomes a symlink pointing out of the clone. git-lfs opens the same path as always; the kernel resolves the symlink and the write lands in the agent workspace, which is already in `allowWritePaths`. The read-only mount is never written to.

Two things make it work: the symlink is created in the unsandboxed app process during spawn, so it needs no write permission inside the sandbox; and bwrap restricts *mounts*, so a write through a symlink is evaluated against the workspace mount.

**Adding `<clone>/.git/lfs/tmp` to `allowWritePaths` was tried first and verified not to work** — a read-only agent still got `TOUCH_EXIT=1`. The clone must stay in `allowReadPaths`, and that ro-bind shadows any rw bind beneath it.

Config can't do this either: `git lfs env` shows `TempDir` and `LfsStorageDir` both derived from `lfs.storage`, with no separate tmp knob. Repointing `lfs.storage` would move the objects too, and those are hardlinked to the base cache (same inode, 65 links) — trading this bug for real disk duplication.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` clean; suite **1121 passed, 5 skipped**.

Live via `archie-e2e`, read-only agent on `sweatco/sweatcoin-mobile`:

| Probe | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `touch .git/lfs/tmp/probe` | **`TOUCH_EXIT=0`** |
| `git lfs env` | `TempDir` resolves through the symlink |
| `touch ./package.json` | **exit 1** — `Read-only file system` |
| `echo x >> ./package.json` | **exit 1** — `Read-only file system` |

Scratch writable, write boundary intact. Baseline on `main` gives `TOUCH_EXIT=1`.

**Not covered:** I could not induce the natural stale-stat condition inside a read-only agent (it cannot touch its own working tree; prod's staleness came from clone/resume timing). Mechanism proven in isolation and precondition proven fixed live, but a read-only agent hitting the original 128 and then succeeding is not directly demonstrated.

author: balbasty
body:
Regression test for the defect fixed in fastfields-kernels#81 (issue fastfields-kernels#48). Test-only: +230 lines across the two test drivers, **no production code touched**.

## The oracle — no reference implementation needed

The boundary-corrected diagonal expanded each corner weight as `(fx0*fy0 + fx1*fy0 + fx1*fy0 + fx1*fy1)`, double-counting `fx1*fy0` and dropping `fx0*fy1`.

On a square/cubic domain with the **same boundary condition and voxel size on every axis**, relabelling two spatial axes maps the operator onto itself, so its diagonal must be invariant under that relabelling:

| case | invariant |
|---|---|
| field, 2D and 3D | `diag(x,y,c) == diag(y,x,c)` |
| flow, bending-only (`shears == div == 0`) | `diag(x,y,c) == diag(y,x,c)` — channels uncoupled, isotropic voxel size |
| flow, `diag_all` | `diag(x,y,c) == diag(y,x,1-c)` — the Lamé terms couple the channels, so the axis swap carries a channel swap; `shears == div` keeps the Lamé part symmetric under that simultaneous relabelling |

The buggy corner sum is not symmetric under the `fx <-> fy` relabelling wherever the two axes' one-sided boundary signs differ. It cancels exactly where they agree (`fx0==fx1` and `fy0==fy1` make both forms `4*fx0*fy0`) — which is precisely why the pre-existing interior-only diagonal checks never caught it.

## What this covers beyond the minimum

- **3D as well as 2D.** The 3D diagonal carries three independent corner cross-terms (`w110`/`w101`/`w011`) rather than one; the xy and yz swaps exercise two directly and the third by composition. 9 of the 12 fixed terms live in 3D, so 2D-only coverage would leave most of the fix untested.
- **Whole-domain sweep** rather than a single row/column.
- **Three boundary conditions** — Zero, DCT2, DST2. DCT2 is a deliberate **control**: it does not flip signs, so it passes with or without the fix.

## Verification — it demonstrably bites

Same tests, same build flags, same binaries; the *only* thing changed between the two runs is the kernels headers:

| kernels | `test_reg_field` | `test_reg_flow` |
|---|---|---|
| pre-fix (buggy corner term) | 19250 checks, **328 failures** → FAILED (exit 1) | 16347 checks, **1696 failures** → FAILED (exit 1) |
| `1df9fd3` (the fix) | 19250 checks, **0 failures** → PASSED | 16347 checks, **0 failures** → PASSED |

Check counts are identical in both directions, so the only difference is pass/fail. Every one of the 2024 failures is in the new checks — no pre-existing test changes value:

```
  68  field2d_diag_bending.axis_symmetry
 130  field3d_diag_bending.axis_symmetry_xy
 130  field3d_diag_bending.axis_symmetry_yz
  68  flow2d_diag_bending.axis_symmetry
  68  flow2d_diag_all.axis_symmetry
 390  flow3d_diag_bending.axis_symmetry_xy   390  flow3d_diag_bending.axis_symmetry_yz
 390  flow3d_diag_all.axis_symmetry_xy       390  flow3d_diag_all.axis_symmetry_yz
```

Discrepancies are large and unambiguous (e.g. `got 17 expected 21`, `got 32.3 expected 36.3`) against a `1e-5` tolerance — not a marginal-tolerance test.

## Ordering

This depends on the pin chain already reaching the fix, which it now does on `main`:

```
cpu-lib bdbe80d  ->  cpu-impl 5e2c78e  ->  kernels 1df9fd3
```

(kernels#81 → cpu-impl#72 → cpu-lib#88, all merged.)

## Provenance

An equivalent 2D-only test exists on the `teeny` branch in `8afcab4`. `fastfields-cpu-lib#53` was an attempt to port it to `main`, but it was filed from the `claude-fastfields-to-teeny` workstream, whose PRs must always target `teeny` — so it was mis-filed, not wrong. Its oracle is sound and was useful prior art; credit to it. This PR lands equivalent (and broader — 3D, whole-domain, multi-bound) coverage on `main` properly, re-derived and re-verified from scratch.

author: pawaca
body:
## What changed

- expose the Worker-managed `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` through the upstream credentials service and resolve it per operation for both chat and search
- mount the upstream Web runtime, official DeepSeek Web Search provider, and search-only `web_search` tool in each Edge session
- validate and project the separate Anthropic-compatible `DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_BASE_URL`, while keeping `web_fetch` disabled until Edge network policy exists
- preserve no-follow redirect behavior on Cloudflare Workers by using manual redirect handling in the shared DeepSeek search provider
- add unit, integration, browser snapshot, deployment metadata, bilingual docs, and Agent Note coverage

## Why

The previous Edge-only key binding worked for chat but bypassed the credential seam used by upstream plugins. Web Search should consume the same Worker secret without copying it into Durable Object state, session events, settings, or request headers supplied by the browser. Reusing the upstream composition keeps the Edge delta narrow and makes future upstream syncs easier.

## User impact

Edge sessions can now invoke native DeepSeek Web Search and render the existing upstream tool/result UI. Chat and search share one deployment secret. Operators may optionally set `DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_BASE_URL`; `web_fetch` remains unavailable by design.

This is a pre-release breaking cleanup: `x-deepseek-api-key` and request-scoped BYOK handling are removed rather than carried as compatibility paths.

body:
## Summary

The "+" quick-actions sheet showed six action tiles **and** a labelled list of the More pages (Coach, Friends, Settings, Signups, Log out) stacked underneath. That pushed it past its 88%-height cap, so it scrolled on short phones and the top rows were the first thing to go off-screen.

It now holds two panes and mounts only one at a time.

**The sheet**
- Five action tiles: Scan a meal, Analyze a lift, Log today's weight, Scan barcode, Challenges. **Log a workout** is gone — the bottom bar already has a Workouts tab, so it was the one action with a shorter path elsewhere.
- Challenges takes the wide fifth slot as a centered row rather than a stretched square, which saves ~36px and is what keeps the pane clear of the height cap.
- **More options** is a deliberately quiet text row, not a tile, so it never competes with the five colours. Its chevron points right because it opens a page rather than expanding in place. 44px minimum target.
- Tapping it slides a second pane in over the tiles, with `.qa-panes` animating its own height so the sheet morphs (521px → 393px) instead of jumping. Back arrow returns. **Neither pane scrolls, in either state.**
- The `What do you want to do?` subtitle is deleted; its i18n key is retired and replaced by `mobile.moreOptions` (EN + TH).

**No glow**
- Dropped the `.qa-tile:hover` box-shadow — hover moves the border instead. A drop shadow under a tile reads as a halo on the dark theme.
- Writing the test for that turned up dead CSS: `.qa-tile` still listed `box-shadow` in its `transition` after the shadow was removed. Dropped.

**Bug found in review**
- `go()` scheduled its cleanup 300ms out, and that cleanup hides whichever pane the slide moved *away* from. Nothing cancelled it. Tap More options and dismiss the sheet inside that window — easy to hit with Cancel, the backdrop, or a handle drag — and the cleanup still landed, hiding the actions pane `reset()` had just restored. Both panes then read hidden, `reset()`'s early-return guard saw a clean sheet and bailed, and the next open showed an **empty sheet**: handle, Cancel, nothing else. Only a reload cleared it. Fixed by cancelling the pending timer and letting `reset()` always normalize both panes.

**Docs**
- DESIGN.md documented a tinted icon-badge shadow and a hover elevation on interactive tiles. The glow has now been stripped on three separate branches, so the doc was actively teaching the pattern that keeps getting removed. Recorded the exception next to both rules rather than deleting them — the elevation still holds for cards and rows outside this sheet.

## Test Coverage

```
CODE PATHS (templates/base.html inline block)        USER FLOWS
[+] quick-actions pane controller                    [+] Reaching an action
```

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## What
Ramp sandbox apps only work against `https://demo-api.ramp.com`, but source-ramp hardcoded `https://api.ramp.com`, making it impossible to test the connector with sandbox credentials. This adds a configurable API base URL so the sandbox can be used for testing, and enables the acceptance test suite using sandbox credentials from GSM. Since all production Ramp accounts use the same URL, the option is hidden from users.

Requested by Danylo Jablonski.

## How
1. `manifest.yaml` — new optional `api_url` spec property, default `https://api.ramp.com`, marked `airbyte_hidden: true` so it never shows in the UI. All 4 requester URLs (token, cards, transactions, reimbursements) now use:
```yaml
url: "{{ config.get('api_url', 'https://api.ramp.com').rstrip('/') }}/developer/v1/..."
```
(`rstrip('/')` normalizes a trailing slash in the configured base URL.)

2. `metadata.yaml` — added `demo-api.ramp.com` to `allowedHosts`, bumped `dockerImageTag` to 0.0.4, and enabled the acceptance test suite (same pattern as source-reddit-ads in #84348):
```yaml
connectorTestSuitesOptions:
  - suite: acceptanceTests
    testSecrets:
      - name: SECRET_SOURCE-RAMP-SANDBOX__CREDS
        fileName: config.json
        secretStore:
          type: GSM
          alias: airbyte-connector-testing-secret-store
```
The GSM secret contains the sandbox connector config JSON (including `api_url: https://demo-api.ramp.com`); CI materializes it at `secrets/config.json`.

3. `acceptance-test-config.yml` — replaces the builder-contribution bypasses with real test configs for `connection` (succeed + invalid-config failed), `discovery`, `basic_read`, `incremental` (with future/abnormal state), and `full_refresh` covering all 3 streams.

4. Adds `integration_tests/configured_catalog.json` (cards full_refresh; transactions and reimbursements incremental), `integration_tests/invalid_config.json`, and `integration_tests/abnormal_state.json` with far-future `updated_at` cursors (per-partition state for `reimbursements`, which is partitioned by `direction`).

5. Changelog entry in `docs/integrations/sources/ramp.md`.

## Review guide
1. `airbyte-integrations/connectors/source-ramp/manifest.yaml`
2. `airbyte-integrations/connectors/source-ramp/metadata.yaml`
3. `airbyte-integrations/connectors/source-ramp/acceptance-test-config.yml`
4. `airbyte-integrations/connectors/source-ramp/integration_tests/`
5. `docs/integrations/sources/ramp.md`

## User Impact
None for existing users — the default is unchanged and the new field is hidden. Enables sandbox testing by setting `api_url: https://demo-api.ramp.com` in the config (API/Terraform).

Verified locally with `source-declarative-manifest`:
- default config (no `api_url`) still targets `api.ramp.com`
- sandbox config with `api_url: https://demo-api.ramp.com` (with and without trailing slash) passes check and reads all 3 streams (cards: 63, transactions: 560, reimbursements: 23 records)
- incremental read with `abnormal_state.json` returns 0 records and preserves the future cursors (state format captured from actual connector STATE output)
- unit tests pass (6 passed)

## Can this PR be safely reverted and rolled back?
- [x] YES 💚
- [ ] NO ❌

author: alpcaner
body:
## Summary

Closes #846.

The dispatched parity suite went red against alp-sdk `94378a056549c7377d714a7f2b68878aca8fea01` with `3 failed, 765 passed, 8 skipped` — `tests/parity/test_planner_emit_parity.py::test_the_scaffold_mode_agrees_on_stdout_through_argv[minimal|peripheral|sensor]`. The entire byte divergence was the git ref inside scaffolded README links: alp-sdk emitting `.../tree/main/examples/...`, tan emitting `.../tree/v0.16.0/examples/...`.

**tan was the wrong side, and not for the reason it first looks.** This is not "pin to the version you built against" versus "link to a moving `main`". alp-sdk at that ref has `v0.16.0-rc1` tagged but **not** `v0.16.0` — so tan was emitting links to a tag that does not exist, which GitHub 404s. alp-sdk already guards this: `_docs_ref()` at `scripts/alp_template.py:1250` is gated by `_tag_resolves()` at `scripts/alp_template.py:1228`, added by `94378a05` itself (`fix(metadata): require the docs ref tag to resolve before a scaffold pins to it`, alp-sdk#1535). tan carried the un-ported copy, which pinned unconditionally on `status: released` + `version:`.

This ports that guard verbatim.

## The issue's own remedy was wrong — do not follow it

#846 is auto-filed by `parity.yml`'s `notify-planner-drift` and instructs the reader to diff `scripts/alp_orchestrate/` and re-pin `PINNED_HASHES`/`PINNED_SDK_COMMIT`. Measured: `scripts/alp_orchestrate/` is byte-identical (21 files) across the pinned commit `88318e759958529fbbd8fe9d481373681c0fa78d`, the dispatched ref `94378a056549c7377d714a7f2b68878aca8fea01`, and `origin/dev`. `git log --oneline 88318e75..94378a05 -- scripts/alp_orchestrate/` is empty. Following that remedy would have re-pinned the hashes, closed the issue, and shipped the 404 links.

**No pin is moved by this PR.**

## Why the drift was invisible

The gate's *surface* is not the gap — `scripts/alp_template.py` **is** watched, at `python/tests/gates/test_planner_relocation_freshness.py:667` in `HAND_PORT_HASHES`. Binding `ALP_SDK_HAND_PORT_ROOT` to the dispatched ref proves it fires: `scripts/alp_template.py: sha256 5d453c5d… != pinned 9321c7e3…`.

The gap is which **ref** the blocking steps compare against:

1. `parity.yml:904-906` — the always-run `tests/gates` step binds all three audit roots to **frozen** checkouts at the pins, so it can only catch table self-inconsistency.
2. `parity.yml:1982` — `python-tests`, the one job bound to the **dispatched** ref, runs `pytest --ignore=tests/gates`. `tests/gates` therefore never runs against the dispatched ref.
3. `parity.yml:1038-1058` — the one live-vs-dispatched hand-port comparison exists but is `if: repository_dispatch` + `continue-on-error: true` + `::warning::`. Its own text already anticipates this state: *"tan's copy may be AHEAD of the pin rather than behind"*. It names #509 as the make-it-blocking issue.

The first commit's docstring and message stated this as "`alp_template.py` is not watched", which is false; `96a06fd` corrects it.

## The pin stays put, deliberately

`scripts/alp_template.py` is now ported **ahead** of `HAND_PORT_PINNED_SDK_COMMIT`, and the pin must not move to match. `scripts/alp_cli/doctor.py` changed in the same `88318e75..94378a05` range (alp-sdk `efeaf65c`, #1471 — pinned `f2faa07c…` vs the ref's `fe109d98…`) and is genuinely un-ported on the tan side. Moving the pin would silently re-freeze that as "audited". A `#:` note now records this so `python/scripts/planner_resync.py` does not re-propose #1535 as unported work.

## Test plan

The port is AST-identical to upstream (docstrings stripped): `_docs_ref` IDENTICAL, `_tag_resolves` IDENTICAL. Mechanism is `git -C <base> rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/tags/<tag>` — local refs only, no network, no `shell=`, tag value cannot become a flag. One subprocess per scaffold, not per link: `_docs_ref(base)` has exactly one call site at `python/tan/planner/template.py:1393`.

Bound at a checkout of `94378a05` (`metadata/sdk_version.yaml` reads `version: 0.16.0` / `status: released`; `git tag -l` gives `v0.15.0`, `v0.15.0-rc1`, `v0.16.0-rc1`; `rev-parse refs/tags/v0.16.0` -> rc=1 — the exact #846 shape):

```
tests/parity/test_planner_emit_parity.py -k test_the_scaffold_mode_agrees_on_stdout_through_argv
  with fix:     4 passed, 771 deselected in 2.36s    (rc=0)
  fix reverted: 3 failed, 1 passed, 771 deselected   (minimal|peripheral|sensor)
```

Unit-level mutation proof reproduces verbatim: `AssertionError: assert 'v0.16.0' == 'main'` and `AttributeError: module 'tan.planner.template' has no attribute '_tag_resolves'`.

Full suite, clean venv (`pip install -e ./python pytest`), both rc=0:

| binding | result |
|---|---|
| unbound | `4379 passed, 311 skipped, 1 xfailed in 301.04s` |
| bound at `94378a05` | `5317 passed, 66 skipped, 1 xfailed in 866.68s` |

Degradation measured directly: outside a git checkout `_docs_ref` -> `main`, `_tag_resolves` -> `False`; missing dir -> `main`.

## Module-size ratchet

`python/tests/gates/module_size_budget.generated.json` moves 1436 -> 1470 for `tan/planner/template.py` (the diff's net +34). Regenerated with the repo's own tool — `regen_module_size_budget.py --check` reports `module_size_budget.generated.json already matches the measured tree.` `function_count_budget` and `function_worst_budget` unchanged.

Splitting `_tag_resolves` into `tan/core/` would break the relocation-audit model: `HAND_PORT_SOURCES` maps `template.py` -> `scripts/alp_template.py` 1:1, and `planner_resync.py` three-way-merges against it. Verbatim placement is what keeps that audit honest, so the bump is the right trade here.

## Known: this does NOT turn run 32063286933 green on its own

That run had two independent failures. `python-tests` (the three scaffold parity tests) is fixed here. `seam1 -- plan-shape parity` failed separately on its `scaffold byte-parity (vendored tree vs. pinned alp-sdk --emit scaffold)` step with 7 × `README.md: content differs` — `python/tan/templates/vendored/**/README.md` is captured at `v0.15.0` and `tests/parity/scaffold_byte_parity.py:110-114` hardcodes that normalisation, while the live emit now renders `main`. Pre-existing and recurring: the same step is the sole seam1 failure in dispatch runs `32067489629` and `32125707219`, and it is blocking.

Worth acting on next: `changelog.d/756.fixed.md` deferred that re-vendor because *"re-vendoring to match would ship a scaffold whose links 404 until v0.16.0 is actually released"*. With alp-sdk#1535 and this port the emit renders `main`, so that objection no longer holds and the re-vendor is safe.

author: seejiaokai
body:
## What

On the Inputs page, picking a **multi-day** range wrote a `till 15 Jul` tail into Remarks, but a **one-day** input wrote nothing. The owner wants a one-day input to still read **`till <that date>`**, showing the selected day.

## Why it was empty before

The tail helper's `'none'` mode returned an empty string for a single day. That mode existed to stop an `on 13 Jul` from flashing on the first click of a two-click range — but `till 13 Jul` showing and then updating to `till 18 Jul` reads consistently, so that reason no longer holds.

## Change

- Added a `'till'` mode to `remarksDateTail` / `withRemarksTail` (single day → `till <that day>`, guarded so an empty form yields nothing, never `till <blank>`), and pointed the Inputs calendar at it.
- Leave War sync keeps its `'on'` mode; `'none'` stays for the direct tests.
- Because the token is now rewritten **in place** rather than stripped and re-appended, a kept note stays where the typist put it: `till 13 Jul Bangkok` → `till 18 Jul Bangkok` — the owner's own 18 Aug example.
- Folded the two contradictory comments above `withTill` (one said the token was anchored at the end, the next said it floated) into one accurate comment.

## Tests / verification

- `leave.test.ts` gains a `'till'`-mode block; the three Inputs tests that pinned "single day → no tail" now pin `till <that day>`.
- Gates green first-hand: `npm test` **2534/139**, build clean, reference **728/0**, e2e **272 passed / 6 skips**, probes **6/6**, perf **4/4** (week 3743 / board 844, unmoved — text only).
- Live-driven on the built bundle: one-day pick → `till 13 Jul`, span → `till 16 Jul`, typed note → `LL till 20 Jul`; zero console/page/network errors.

author: carlosdaniel092015-crypto
body:
En Redis no vive sólo cache: vive la **config de negocio** (precios, mínimos, mensajes, los dos canales), los **prompts** editados desde el panel, las **reglas aprendidas**, la cola de revisión y el **índice de conversaciones del CRM**. Apuntar el bot a un Redis vacío no explota: arranca con los defaults del código y el panel aparece sin conversaciones, como si el negocio empezara de cero. Es la falla más silenciosa de la mudanza.

## Qué se agrega

- **`scripts/migrar_redis.py`**: copia las keys `pastoriza:*` de un Redis a otro con DUMP/RESTORE (respeta el tipo y el TTL). Sin `--si` sólo muestra lo que haría; el origen se **lee** y nunca se escribe; se puede correr dos veces (`replace=True`). No copia las efímeras (buffer, locks) a propósito, pero **sí la sesión**: perderla hace que el bot le pregunte de nuevo al cliente lo que ya había dicho.
- **`DESPLIEGUE_VPS.md`**: la mudanza en orden, con el interruptor (el webhook de YCloud) al **final** y la verificación antes. Incluye la vuelta atrás: Railway queda andando hasta que se decida apagarlo.
- **`.env.example`**: faltaba **`PUBLIC_BASE_URL`**, que en Railway salía sola (`RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN`) y en un VPS hay que poner a mano. Sin ella **no sale la foto del comprobante** al supervisor y las fotos de producto caen al proxy externo. También faltaban `TEMPLATE_APROBACION_*` y `REDIS_MAX_CONEXIONES`.
- Redis nuevo con **`--maxmemory-policy noeviction`**: con la política por defecto, al llenarse la memoria borra keys al azar — y algunas de esas keys son los precios.

## Verificación

El script se probó contra **dos Redis reales**: copia la config (string), el hash del CRM, el prompt editado y la lista de sesión **con su TTL**; saltea la key efímera; es idempotente; y una URL mal escrita da un mensaje legible en vez de un traceback. Los 474 tests siguen pasando (no se tocó código de la app).

author: ghashtag
body:
Verilog is the target that actually goes to silicon, and it was the **least** verified of the four: `verify_emit_bitexact.py` checks it by sample, while model/C/Rust are now exhaustive (#2200).

This adds Verilog as a fourth arm, under `iverilog`, folding the same FNV-1a digest over the same domain.

**Result:**

```
full_adder   model == C == Rust on ALL 16,777,216 inputs   digest d50715c5
             Verilog == model on a SLICE of 65,536 (0.4% of the domain)
maj3         model == C == Rust on ALL 16,777,216 inputs   digest 80f1d1c5
             Verilog == model on a SLICE of 524,288 (3.1% of the domain)
tmul         model == C == Rust == Verilog on ALL 65,536 inputs   digest 91a68892
negate       model == C == Rust == Verilog on ALL    256 inputs   digest eeede76b
pack2        model == C == Rust on ALL 65,536 inputs [3-way: no Verilog arm]
```

`tmul` and `negate` now have **four independent implementations agreeing on every input**.

**Why the others are slices, measured rather than assumed.** iverilog is an interpreter and the cost per input is not uniform:

| function | inputs/s | whole domain |
|---|---:|---:|
| `tmul` | ~330,000 | 0.2 s |
| `maj3` | 21,061 | **13 min** |
| `full_adder` | 2,972 | **94 min** |

`full_adder` calls `dot27` nine times per input at 27 lanes each. So the Verilog arm gets a budget and reports a **labelled slice** where the whole domain does not fit. A slice is never printed as exhaustive, and `--verilog-full` runs the long version.

**Three mistakes of mine in this PR, all caught before it opened.**

1. I measured `tmul`'s Verilog rate and extrapolated to `full_adder` — which does nine times the work per input. The run timed out at ten minutes. Measuring one thing and extrapolating to another is the error this whole line of work exists to catch.
2. I then set the budget in **inputs**, a unit whose cost varies 100× across these functions, so one number was seconds for `tmul` and eleven minutes for `full_adder`. The budget is now in **seconds**, converted per function from the measured rates.
3. The summary line read `ALL 5 PRIMITIVES AGREE EXHAUSTIVELY across every arm (no sampling)` — **false for three of the five**, while the per-line detail above it was correct. A summary that overstates its own detail is the exact failure this session has been finding elsewhere.

`pack2` returns `u64`; the C and Rust folds take the low 32 bits and a matching Verilog fold needs a wider accumulator. Left three-way and labelled rather than quietly given a Verilog arm that compares something else.

Refs #2200

---

Two things the previous PRs left open, plus the theory that says why they matter.

**1. `--verilog-full` as a nightly job.** #2202 gates on a labelled Verilog *slice* because iverilog needs 13 minutes for `maj3` and 94 for `full_adder` at its measured rates (21,061 and 2,972 inputs/s). Unacceptable per push; fine once a day. The slice keeps gating; this closes it, giving **four independent implementations agreeing on all 16,777,216 inputs** rather than on 0.4 % of them.

**2. `docs/EXHAUSTION_THEORY.md`** — why this line of work is worth the wall-clock, stated precisely.

---

### The point, in three steps

**Exhaustive agreement over a finite domain is a decision procedure, not a test.** For `f_A, f_B : D → R` with `D` finite, checking equality on every `x ∈ D` *decides* `f_A ≡ f_B`. No induction, no invariants, no trusted prover kernel. It is not a weaker substitute for formal EC — on a finite domain it is the strongest statement available, and it is what HECTOR and ACL2 approximate when `D` is too large to walk.

**`|D|` is set by the representation, not the semantics.** A trit carries three values; these specs declare it `u8`.

> **Claim.** For `k` trit arguments in a `w`-bit type, enumeration costs `(2^w / 3)^k` times more than the semantic domain requires.
> **Proof.** Semantic domain `3^k`; representational `(2^w)^k`; ratio `(2^w/3)^k`. ∎
> **Check.** `w=8, k=3` → `(256/3)³ = 621,378.4`. Measured here: `16,777,216 / 27 = 621,378.4`. ✓

Only **1.61 × 10⁻⁶** of `full_adder`'s enumerated space is a valid trit triple.

**Both readings of that are true.** It is waste — a 2-bit trit type would put `full_adder` at `4³ = 64` inputs, which iverilog finishes in **0.02 s** instead of 94 minutes, a four-million-fold change from a type declaration with no algorithmic change. And it is coverage — nothing stops a caller passing `200`, the spec has defined behaviour there (`pack2` does not mask, so values above 3 spill into the next lane), and enumerating the byte-wide domain verifies it. A 2-bit type would make those inputs *unrepresentable* rather than *verified*: better, but a different guarantee, not the same one made cheaper.

### Why this is a property of the number system

| domain | `\|D\|` | C, ~10⁷/s | iverilog, measured |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| trit primitive, 2-bit type, k=3 | 64 | instant | instant |
| trit primitive, `u8`, k=2 | 65,536 | instant | 0.2 s |
| trit primitive, `u8`, k=3 | 16,777,216 | ~1.5 s | 13–94 min |
| binary float add, 2 × 32-bit | 1.8 × 10¹⁹ | **58,561 years** | — |

The line between *enumerate* and *prove* is crossed by representation width, and small alphabets sit below it. **That is the one place choosing ternary buys a verification advantage rather than an area or energy claim** — and unlike the area claims in this project's history, which were withdrawn twice, this one follows from counting and can be rechecked by anyone in seconds.

Refs #2202, #2200

Closes #2202
Closes #2204

---

## Fix-forward 2026-08-19 (CI repair)

**What changed and why.** CI diagnosis showed the `quality-ratchet` check
FAILing: `modules_over_500_lines moved 207 -> 208`. This PR's own LG12
invocation-surface addition (`invoke`, `invoke_sync`, `stream`,
`stream_sync`, `SuperstepEmission`, `run_on_private_loop`, and their
private helpers `_reject_running_loop` / `_validate_stream_contract` /
`_stream_chunks` / `_update_chunks`) grew `dharma_swarm/graph/scheduler.py`
to 721 lines, one module over the ratchet ceiling. Split that block,
unchanged in behavior, into a new sibling module
`dharma_swarm/graph/invocation.py` — the idiom this repo already uses
for splitting a class's surface across files
(`mission_control_lifecycle.py`'s `MissionControlLifecycleMixin`
composed into `MissionControl`). `CompiledGraph` now inherits
`InvocationSurfacesMixin` from `invocation.py`; `scheduler.py` keeps only
the run lifecycle itself (`_run_supersteps`, `_validated_seed`) and
re-exports `SuperstepEmission` / `run_on_private_loop` so every existing
import path (`dharma_swarm/graph/__init__.py`, `dharma_swarm/graph/schema.py`,

author: smarlhens
body:
Makes the `riri-*` crates usable as libraries: publishable metadata, no CLI layer forced into a library build, no HTTP stack by default, and engine application that works on a `serde_json::Value` instead of a file on disk.

| # | Item | Commit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `description` on every publishable crate | `561f264` |
| 2 | `rust-version = 1.88.0` — measured floor, 1.87 fails on let-chains | `2d1ef5a` |
| 3 | README: pin a `rev`, not a per-crate tag | `df3ddf0` |
| 4 | Re-export consumer-facing types (nce, npd, ncd) | `70aba95` |
| 5 | Feature-gate `pub mod cli` (nce, npd, ncd) | `1f7d696` |
| 6 | `refresh` out of default features | `d449121` |
| 7 | `engines_iter()` yields bare package names | `7039173` |
| 8 | Pure engine application | `57aac6a` |
| 9 | `parse_lockfile(PackageManager, &str)` in a new `riri-lockfile` crate | `199dcfb` |
| 10 | API policy in the README + publish metadata | `fa37e59` |

## Breaking

- `apply_engines_update` takes `&mut serde_json::Value`, not `&mut PackageJsonFile`.
- `engines_iter()` yields `typescript`, not `node_modules/typescript`.
- `riri-nce`'s `refresh` is no longer default. Released binaries keep it via `[package.metadata.dist] features`; `cargo install --git` needs `--features refresh`.

## Verified

- Zero hand-rolled package-manager matches left in `src/` — was 5 (`riri-ncd` ×3, both napi shims).
- Napi shims import only from the facade: −4 direct deps in `riri-napi-nce`, −3 in `riri-napi-npd`.
- Lean builds drop clap, `clap_*`, comfy-table, console, anyhow, tracing-subscriber, task-runner, `sort-package-json`, ureq/rustls/webpki-roots; `riri-ncd --no-default-features` also drops indicatif.
- `riri-lockfile/tests/engines_names.rs` enforces the bare-name contract over the fixture corpus; reverting one impl to raw keys fails it.
- `tests/facade.rs` in nce and npd imports only its own crate root, incl. `check_engines_with_lifecycle`.
- 1.88.0 compiles `--lib --bins`, `--no-default-features`, `--all-features`, `--all-targets`.
- `check_engines: 500 deps` unchanged vs `main` (64.3 µs). pnpm snapshots byte-identical to `main`.
- CI builds both new configs (`--no-default-features`, `--features refresh`).

## Not done

- `riri-ncd`'s `ureq` stays unconditional: `check_deprecations_from_content` builds the registry client itself, so making it optional means pushing that out to `DeprecationSource`.
- `ParsedLockfile::engines()` returns `Option` because the entry point is pure; a `scan`-gated `open_engines` would remove the last yarn special case.
- Pre-existing, unrelated: `riri-semver-range` gives `false` for `<0.0.0-beta` vs `0.0.0-alpha` where nodejs-semver gives `true` (proptest seed `cc 6b24f37aae62dce4d5f6c097dbee74902b8a8a151a3a5c974b46b57b875fa8d1`); `nce/cli.rs` reads `package.json` twice; `riri_npm::version_for` allocates per lookup.
- No CI gate on the MSRV floor.

## What (logging only — no behavior change)

author: stashilin
body:
Делает `psp.Fake` пригодным для прогона сценариев контракта без внешнего стенда. До этого он отдавал
`payload: {"fake": true}` и сумму один в один — против такого стенда нельзя проверить ни один сценарий:
мастер маппит реквизиты в контрактный блок `requisites` **по белому списку имён** и всё чужое молча
выбрасывает, поэтому мерч получал пустой блок при формально выданных реквизитах.

## Что умеет теперь

- **Реквизиты контрактными именами** по каждому методу (`openapi.yaml`, схема `Requisites`):
  `sbp` — `phone`/`bank`/`bank_name`/`recipient_name`, `c2c` — `card_number`, `nspk` —
  `payment_url`/`qr_data`/`qr_image_url`, `transgran` — `payment_currency`/`instruction`.
- **Сумма — ровно запрошенная.** Уникализацию делает мастер: шаг 5 каскада сам просит другую сумму,
  а шаг 3 (`fanExact`) принимает реквизит **только при точном совпадении**.
- **Сценарии отказов по магическому хвосту суммы**, включаются явно через `FAKE_SCENARIOS=1`:
  `…13` — реквизитов нет (заявка уйдёт в `FAILED/UNROUTED`), `…66` — сбой провайдера,
  `…99` — реквизит выдан уже протухшим.
- **Мусор с шины отбивается**: непололожительная сумма больше не возвращается «платёжной».

Заголовки для выбора сценария не годятся принципиально: до PSP они не доезжают — в `FetchCall` их нет,
а воркер ставит в запрос только свои `x-api-key`/`x-signature`. Механика хвоста в системе уже принята:
у стенда `mock-psp` причина отказа так и называется `magic_tail`.

## Две ошибки, найденные аудитом и исправленные здесь

Ветку смотрела вторая модель другого провайдера (read-only аудит). Обе находки оказались верными:

1. **Недоплата.** Первая версия считала `amount - amount%100 + tail`, поэтому заявка на 700.85 при
   хвосте 37 давала к оплате **700.37** — меньше запрошенного. Теперь инвариант жёсткий: сумма никогда
   не меньше запрошенной и всегда в тех же рублях.
2. **Сломанный точный веер.** Уникализация на стороне стенда означала, что шаг 3 каскада не проходил
   **ни разу** — каждая заявка сваливалась на шаг 5 с random-суммой, а реквизит шага 3 уходил в буфер.
   Уникализация принадлежит мастеру; стенд обязан отвечать ровно на запрошенное.

Отклонено осознанно: аудитор пометил как высокую находку то, что сервис не блокирует недоплату
(`paid_amount` меньше `pay_amount` даёт `SUCCESS`). Контракт предписывает обратное — «расхождение
означает недоплату или переплату; отдельных статусов и этапов для этого нет, это арифметика»
(`openapi.yaml:1085-1088`): сверка на стороне мерча, дело сервиса — отдать `pay_amount`.

## Проверки

`go build ./...`, `go test ./...` — зелено. Тесты: точность суммы на четырёх границах, отказ на мусорной
сумме, контрактные имена по всем методам, сценарии под `opt-in` и — отдельно — что **без** `opt-in`
те же суммы обслуживаются как обычные платежи.

Живьём (cascade + этот воркер + Postgres/Redis/RabbitMQ): путь h2h проходит целиком —
`AWAITING_PAYMENT` с блоком `requisites` и без `pay_amount` (суммы совпали, как и обещает контракт),
затем по событию оплаты `SUCCESS/SETTLED`. Сценарии `…13` и `…66` дают `FAILED/UNROUTED`
с человекочитаемым `error.message`.

author: jonparis
body:
Follow-up to #199.

Pointing launchd at a shared checkout made the schedule depend on whichever branch that checkout was sitting on. Within an hour of merging #199 the primary checkout had moved from `feat/custom-status-without-lists` to `docs/deploys-are-manual` — neither contains the runner, so the Friday job would have died with `Cannot find module`.

The job now runs from a dedicated worktree (`astrid-web-hygiene`) that nobody works in, with `HYGIENE_SELF_UPDATE=1` hard-resetting it to `origin/main` at the start of every run. Prompt and runner changes take effect as soon as they land on main, with no reinstall.

Self-update **refuses to run when the checkout has local changes** and runs what is there instead — a hard reset must never be able to destroy someone's work if the variable is ever set on the wrong directory.

author: marius-kilocode
body: Agent Manager PR comments currently render GitHub hunks with a separate plain-text line renderer, so comments do not share the syntax highlighting, line layout, or theme behavior of the main review diff. This makes the same code look different depending on whether it is viewed in the PR comment list or the diff viewer. This change routes PR comment hunks through the existing Pierre-backed Kilo diff component. GitHub hunk-only payloads are normalized with synthetic file headers so Pierre preserves their actual line ranges, while malformed or incomplete hunks fail safely without hiding the comment. The shared normalization boundary is covered by a component-level regression fixture using a real GitHub-style hunk, including syntax-token output. Before: After:

author: rbuergi
body:
Closes #1834.

## The exact write

`src/MeshWeaver.Graph/Configuration/PrebuiltAssemblySeeder.cs:293-294` (pre-fix), inside the
`workspace.GetMeshNodeStream(nodeTypePath).Update(...)` lambda opened at line 267:

```csharp
CompiledSources = def.CurrentSourceVersions?.ToImmutableDictionary()
                  ?? def.CompiledSources,
```

That write is **cross-hub**. `MeshNodeStreamHandle.UpdateRemote`
(`src/MeshWeaver.Mesh.Contract/MeshNodeStreamExtensions.cs:1089-1190`) runs the lambda against the
**mirror's** first emission and RFC-7396-diffs the result, so the lambda reads a snapshot that
predates the first-activation write of `CurrentSourceVersions` — a write performed on the OWNER by
`NodeTypeCompilationHelpers.InstallSourcesWatcher`, on an activation **the seeder's own subscribe
causes**. `def.CurrentSourceVersions` is therefore `null`, the `??` falls through to `null`, the key
never enters the patch, and the owner merges the patch onto a state that already has the watcher's
snapshot. Committed result: `CurrentSourceVersions` non-empty over `CompiledSources = null`, which
`NodeTypeDefinition.IsDirty` reports as **dirty** ("one null + the other non-empty → dirty").

`InstallReleaseRequestWatcher`'s #1707-slice-3 branch requires `!def.IsDirty`, so the release request
`PackageInstaller` issues immediately after `SeedPrebuiltAssemblies` **compiles the type it just
adopted**. Not declined, not logged as a failure — thrown away one step later. For the sourceless
fixture the existing bundle tests use, both sides are empty and nothing shows; that is why the whole
suite stayed green.

## The approach, and why

The issue named two candidates. **Neither is sufficient on its own, and the reason is ordering.**

* **Owner-side stamp alone (option 1)** removes the mirror lag but not the race: on the owner, at
  adoption time, `CurrentSourceVersions` may still be unpublished. Stamping then gives
  `CompiledSources = CurrentSourceVersions = null` — momentarily clean, then dirty the instant the
  watcher publishes. Same defect, one hop later.
* **A source-set query per adopted type (option 2)** is authoritative but pays a fan-out per type on
  the boot path — the traffic `InstallSourcesWatcher`'s own comment calls out as dominant in prod —
  and two independent folds of a live collection can disagree, which is the "same outage with the
  opposite sign".

So the stamp moves to the owner **and is ordered against the publication** rather than racing it.
The adopter, which cannot know the value, writes a **request**
(`NodeTypeDefinition.RequestedSourceStampAt`, a new operational member); the owner, whose copy of
both fields is authoritative, applies the pure
`NodeTypeCompilationHelpers.ApplyAdoptedSourceStamp` — `CompiledSources := CurrentSourceVersions`,
request cleared. `IsDirty == false` is then true **by construction**, not by timing. No extra query,
no wait on the boot path, no new message type.

All three orderings converge:

| ordering | who fulfils the request |
|---|---|
| request written first | `InstallSourcesWatcher`'s publication, in the **same write** — no window at all, and no extra write on the boot path |
| snapshot published first | the new `InstallAdoptedSourceStampWatcher`, on the adoption's own emission (nothing re-emits the sources query) |
| a release request racing that second case | `InstallReleaseRequestWatcher`, in its own lambda, **before** it reads `IsDirty` |

**Storm safety (#223).** The new watcher writes the node it watches, so the trigger is one-shot: its
`Where` requires the request to be present and every fulfilment — including both terminal compile
stamps (`ApplyCompileSuccess`/`ApplyCompileFailure`) — clears it in the same write. A pass cannot
schedule another pass. Non-convergence is loud rather than retried: the commit advances a
process-local high-water mark, and an emission still carrying a trigger this hub already committed a
stamp for is logged as an **error** naming the type.

**No `MeshNode.Version` anywhere** — not in the fix and not in the tests. It is a counter the owner
mints for every writer, and this node has several (#1833 flaked on exactly that proxy). Every
assertion reads a field the code under test wrote.

## Non-vacuity

Control: the fix in place, with **only** the seeder's line reverted to main's, so the owner-side
machinery is inert because no request is ever written.

```
=== stamp half ===
Expected value not to be <null> because the adopted build's source snapshot is stamped by the OWNER,
whose copy of CurrentSourceVersions is authoritative — a cross-hub patch cannot see a field the
owner wrote after the mirror's snapshot.

=== consequence half (stamp assertions temporarily removed so the run reaches it) ===
Expected value to be Ok because the release request must be SATISFIED by the adopted build —
Pending here means the watcher dispatched a compile of the type it had just adopted (#1834),
but found Pending.
```

With the fix: `Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 2` (PluginCatalog) and `Passed: 7` (Graph).

`AdoptionAfterTheSnapshotIsAlreadyPublished_IsStillStamped` passes under the control too, and that
is deliberate: it is the ordering the issue's instrumentation caught as the *second* adoption
(`csv=0 cs=0`), which already worked because the mirror had caught up. It guards that the new
machinery does not regress it.

## Suites run (local, all green)

| suite | result |
|---|---|
| `MeshWeaver.Graph.Test` | 1292 passed, 0 failed |
| `MeshWeaver.PluginCatalog.Test` | 410 passed, 0 failed |
| `MeshWeaver.Hosting.Monolith.Test` | 750 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped |
| `MeshWeaver.Hosting.Test` | 193 passed |
| `MeshWeaver.PluginTester.Test` | 65 passed |

`-c Release -p:CIRun=true -warnaserror` clean for `MeshWeaver.Mesh.Contract`, `MeshWeaver.Graph`,
`MeshWeaver.Hosting`, `MeshWeaver.Documentation` and both touched test projects.

## 🚨 The deploy question: would a first pod now report `alreadyBaked=N compiled=0`?

**This fix does not change that number, and it was never the thing that could.** Naming it plainly
because a roll decision depends on it:

* The boot tally is decided by `NodeTypeBakeStatus.Classify` + the store probe, consumed by
  `DynamicTypePreWarmer` (`baked.Contains(p) → PreWarmStatus.AlreadyBaked`, without activating the
  hub). **Neither reads `IsDirty`**, and no kickoff in `InstallCompileWatcher` fires on a dirty type
  (`firstBuildKickoff` needs a null status, `recoveryKickoff` needs `Compiling`,
  `frameworkStaleKickoff` needs a stale framework stamp). A dirty-but-`Ok` type is not swept.
* So #1834's cost lands on the **release request** — a package install (`SeedForTypes` →
  `RequestReleases`), a git push, a static-repo import, a Compile click — not on the warm-up tally.

Therefore: **with the bake/portal identity mismatch (#1814 defect A) fixed, a first pod should report
`alreadyBaked=N compiled=0`, and this PR neither helps nor hinders that number.** What it does fix is
the step after: the release requests those installs issue are now answered by the adopted build
instead of recompiling it, so the adoption is not silently undone.

Two honest caveats, stated rather than softened:

1. I have **not** measured this on a real 269-type mesh; the evidence here is a deterministic
   in-process reproduction plus the code paths above. The claim "the sweep does not read IsDirty" is
   read directly off `NodeTypeBakeStatus.Classify` and `DynamicTypePreWarmer`, and is checkable.
2. Adjacent and **out of scope for this PR**: for a never-compiled type the seeder's own subscribe
   activates the hub, and `InstallCompileWatcher`'s `firstBuildKickoff` fires on a null
   `CompilationStatus` — i.e. a first-boot adoption of a fresh import races a kickoff compile
   independently of #1834. Worth its own issue; it is why this PR's fixture pre-settles
   `CompilationStatus` (documented at the fixture) rather than leaving that race in the test.

author: cristianperez06
body:
### 🎯 What does this PR do?

Gives the repo three issue templates — bug fix, feature and improvement — so an issue
arrives with its intent, its plan and how it will be verified already written down.
Each one sets a title prefix and a label, and prompts for the sections the repo
already expects a pull request to answer. It is the issue-side counterpart to the
pull request template adopted in #13.

### 🧩 Type of change

- [ ] 🐞 Bug fix
- [ ] 🧩 New feature
- [ ] ⚙️ Improvement / refactor
- [ ] 📄 Documentation
- [x] 🔧 Config / CI
- [ ] 🗂️ OpenSpec (proposing or archiving a change)

### 🧪 How to test it

1. With this branch checked out on GitHub, open **Issues → New issue**.
2. Three choices should appear: **🐞 Bug Fix**, **🧩 Feature** and **⚙️ Improvement**,
   each with its own description.
3. Pick one — the title should be pre-filled with its prefix (`[Bug]: `, `[Feature]: `,
   `[Improvement]: `), the matching label (`bug`, `feature`, `improvement`) applied, and
   the body pre-filled with that template's sections.
4. Note that `feature` and `improvement` are **not** repo labels yet (`gh label list`
   shows only `bug`), so GitHub will drop them on creation until they are added.

### ✅ Pre-merge checklist

#### Local validations (the same ones CI runs)

- [ ] Lint passes for web and mobile (`pnpm lint` + `pnpm lint:mobile`)
- [ ] Typecheck passes for web and mobile (`pnpm typecheck` + `pnpm typecheck:mobile`)
- [ ] Package tests pass (`pnpm test`)
- [ ] Web production build passes (`pnpm build`)
- [ ] `pnpm check:cycles`, `pnpm check:tokens`, `pnpm check:fonts` and `pnpm check:specs` pass
- [ ] If I touched dependencies: `pnpm-lock.yaml` is updated and committed
- [ ] If I touched dependencies: `react` and `react-native` are not duplicated in the
      workspace

#### Architecture and conventions

- [x] No product code at the repository root — automation lives in `.github/scripts/`

#### Branch hygiene

- [x] Branch named `<feature|bugfix|hotfix|chore>/<kebab-case>`, no IDs or random suffixes
- [x] Branch is up to date on `main` (`main` is linear — no merge commits)
- [x] Merging with **Squash and merge**, PR title in conventional-commit form
      (`type(scope): subject`), and **the body left empty**

### 💬 Notes for the reviewer

The diff is three markdown files under `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` — no product code, no
specs and no UI, so the OpenSpec and screenshot sections are dropped and the
architecture boxes have nothing to act on. I did not run the local validation suite;
nothing it checks is reachable from this diff, and CI will run it anyway.

Two things worth a look:

- Of the three labels the templates ask for, only `bug` exists in the repo. `feature`
  and `improvement` do not, and GitHub drops unknown labels silently when the issue is
  created. Either create them (`gh label create feature`, `gh label create improvement`)
  or point the templates at the existing `enhancement`. I left the templates as written
  rather than pick for you.
- The templates are classic `.md` templates rather than issue *forms* (`.yml`), which
  would let the sections be required fields. Fine as a first pass; worth revisiting if
  people skip sections.

author: gedaiu
body:
#1301, the accomplice-in-waiting from today's outage. The /agents editor's apply path did create-or-REPLACE with a body built from `lore.agent_definitions` — a row that knows nothing of `output.watch`, `format`/`schema`/`select`, or helm's labels and annotations. The 2026-08-13 save therefore amputated the feature-planning recipe's artifact declaration (the stale CRD of #1134 made it invisible even to helm), and with #1315's CRD hook restoring the schema, the very next UI save would have stripped it again.

The conflict path now runs a pure `preserveUnownedFields(current, desired)`: the editor wins every field it renders (prompt, model, sinks, labels it stamps), and everything else the live object carries — `metadata.labels`, `metadata.annotations`, and the members of `spec.output` beside `sinks` — survives the replace. Four tests cover the incident shape (watch survives, editor still wins its fields, helm annotations persist, fresh-create pass-through), linked from a new statement in `specs/floor-on-ai-subsystem`.

With #1315 (schema reaches the cluster) plus this (saves stop discarding it), the five-day artifact-delivery failure mode is closed at both ends.

Verified: lore-api 717/717, `tsc --noEmit` + eslint clean.

Closes #1301

author: yurii-levchenko
body:
## What & why

A read-through of the whole codebase against Go conventions, done as a learning exercise now that the feature work is complete. Six findings, all cosmetic or documentation — **no behavior changes**.

Stacked on #39; review that one first.

---

## 1. Django comparison in a comment

```go
email := c.Query("email") // Like request.GET.get('email') in Django
```

The only one in the project. Irrelevant to a Go reader.

## 2. Imports interleaved with the standard library — 4 files

```go
import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"github-release-notifier/internal/metrics"   // internal, mid-stdlib
	"log/slog"
	"time"
)
```

`gofmt` does not catch this — it sorts within a group but never regroups.

**Deliberately did NOT run `goimports -local`.** That tool orders groups `stdlib → external → local`, while this project consistently uses `stdlib → internal → external` (see `orchestrator.go`, `app.go`, `main.go`, `cmd/notifier/main.go`). Following the tool would have made these 4 files "correct" and inconsistent with the other 40. Fixed by hand to match the project's own convention instead.

Files: `scanner.go`, `handler.go`, `service.go`, `cached_client.go`.

## 3. Doc comments not starting with the identifier — 8 places

```go
// create a new Scanner                                    ← before
// New creates a Scanner that polls GitHub every ...       ← after
```

`godoc` extracts the comment verbatim and prepends nothing, so `// create a new Scanner` renders as a dangling fragment in the generated docs.

## 4. A doc comment split in half by a blank line

`middleware/logging.go`:

```go
// Each request gets an id (taken from the X-Request-ID header if the client
// sent one, otherwise generated), which is echoed back in the response header
// so a client/log reader can correlate a request across systems.
                                    ← blank line breaks the association
// The logged fields give the RED signals — rate, errors (via status),
// duration — at the log layer, complementing the Prometheus metrics
func RequestLogger() gin.HandlerFunc {
```

Only the block immediately above the declaration becomes documentation, so those first three lines documented nothing — they were dead text in the file. Merged into one block starting with the identifier name.

## 5. Exported identifiers with no doc comment — ~17 added

Worst offender was `subscription/store.go`: **all 8** public methods undocumented. Also `SMTPSender` and its two methods, `ReleaseRequest`, `BrokerPublisher.SendReleaseNotification`, `RepoSpec.String`, `DomainError.Error`, `Store.GetRepoTracking`, `NewConsumer`.

Methods on *unexported* types (`redisDeduper`, `channelReplier`) were left alone — the type is private, so godoc never surfaces them.

## 6. Comments that drifted since the move to RabbitMQ

```go
// ReleaseNotifier defines the email operations the scanner needs
```

It publishes a broker command; the notifier service sends the email. Nothing in `releasetracking` touches SMTP — the architecture test `TestArch_MonolithHasNoSMTP` enforces exactly that, so the comment contradicted a rule the build already checks. Also trimmed the `Scanner` type comment, which described its goroutine/ticker implementation in the type's own doc line.

---

## Checked and already clean

Worth recording as much as the findings:

| Convention | Result |
|---|---|
| Error strings lowercase | clean |
| Errors wrapped with `%w` | clean |
| `defer` inside a loop | none |
| Type assertions use two-value form | clean |
| Receiver names consistent per type | clean |

## Not in scope

The largest finding from the audit is **deferred to its own PR**: `context.Context` is not threaded through the store layer — 12 of 15 DB calls in production code use `s.db.Get(...)` instead of `s.db.GetContext(ctx, ...)`. That directly contradicts ADR-006 ("Прокидання context.Context через всю call chain"), which names creating a context inside a callee as an anti-pattern.

Practical effect: a canceled HTTP request stops the handler and service, but the SQL query keeps running. Fixing it changes method signatures across 4 interfaces and their test fakes, so it does not belong in a cosmetic PR.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`
- `go test ./...` — all packages pass
- `go vet -tags=integration ./internal/integration/...`
- `go vet -tags=e2e ./e2e/...`
- `gofmt -l .` clean
- `golangci-lint run ./...` clean

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/cliclanguage/agent-runs/6a84729758f904dd7a707735

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** la page est blanchee

✅ **Result:** # Fix for the blank page

## What was wrong

The live site was displaying a blank white page because Netlify was publishing the raw project source files as-is instead of building the React application. Checking the deployed page showed the browser receiving unprocessed source code — the HTML still contained unresolved template placeholders, and the main application file was being served as plain text rather than as compiled JavaScript. Since browsers cannot execute raw TypeScript/JSX, none of the site's content or styling could load, leaving visitors with an empty page.

## Why it happened

The project had no deployment configuration telling Netlify how to turn the source code into a deployable site (i.e. which command builds the app and which folder contains the finished output). Without that instruction, Netlify fell back to publishing the project directory directly, bypassing the build step entirely.

## What was fixed

Added the missing Netlify build configuration so that deployments now run the project's build process and publish the compiled output folder. This ensures the site is properly compiled into standard HTML/CSS/JavaScript before being served, so the page will render correctly for visitors on the next deploy.

author: tamnd
body:
The extension font of Topologie generale draws the bar of an absolute value at code 12 and the two bars of a norm at code 13, and this printing names them without a size on the end. Preparing the volume carried the four sized forms of each name and not the bare ones, so poppler had no character for the code and dropped it, and the pages have been printing x where the book reads the absolute value of x. Nothing reported it: the report of unknown TeX names only looks at names that carry a size or a piece of a delimiter on the end, and these carry neither.

There is a second half to it. A bar taller than one glyph is drawn as one piece repeated down the height of what it encloses, and every piece came back as a bar of its own, so a norm set around a display two lines tall read as three norms one inside another. The pieces of one bar stand at one left edge and are now read as the one bar they are.

Chapters 1 to 2 go from 18 pages flagged for a dropped glyph to 0 and from 21 flagged in all to 5. Chapters 3 to 5 go from 22 to 0 and from 31 to 10. 173 lines are rewritten across the two volumes, 4 of them still carrying a doubled bar where an absolute value sits inside a norm. The audit stays at 0 hard findings and 252 soft.

The reader is tamnd/bourbaki-solver#246.

author: tihmels
body:
Addresses both semantic findings from review, plus the package rename and repo tooling.

### fix: identical texts are not anagrams (P1)
`compare(listen, LISTEN!)` answered *yes*. An anagram rearranges the letters of a **different** text, and nothing was rearranged. This also contradicted feature 2, which already excludes the query from its own results.

`compareAndRecord` now returns a three-valued `ComparisonResult` (`ANAGRAMS` / `SAME_TEXT` / `NOT_ANAGRAMS`) so the same-text case stays distinguishable from a genuine mismatch and the CLI can say which it is.

### fix: combining marks were silently dropped (P2)
Filtering to `isLetterOrDigit` discarded every combining mark. Confirmed on the JVM: `क` (U+0915) and `का` (U+0915 U+093E) both normalized to `U+0915`, because U+093E is a spacing combining mark, not a letter. An accent with no precomposed form folded `ạ̈` onto `ạ`. Both contradicted the documented promise to preserve diacritics.

Marks (Mn, Mc, Me) are now significant, and NFC runs again after case mapping to recompose what case mapping decomposed. Trade-off, now pinned by a test: U+0130 keeps its combining dot, so `İ` is not equal to `i`.

### Also
- Package renamed to `io.github.tihmels.anagram`.
- `AGENTS.md` covering the contract's single home, the CLI/domain boundary, and the rule that Unicode in tests is written as `\\uXXXX` escapes (a literal-character test had silently become a tautology).
- `.githooks/pre-push` refusing a push while `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` is set, which overrides gh's stored account and would push under the wrong identity once this repo is public.

54 tests, all passing. Verified by the PR build.
