## Summary
This PR addresses styling inconsistencies in the events drink row swipe action buttons by normalizing button appearance across browsers and improving the visual presentation of the drink row container.

## Key Changes
- **Button appearance normalization**: Added `-webkit-appearance: none` and `appearance: none` to remove default browser button styling for cross-browser consistency
- **Button padding reset**: Set `padding: 0` on `.events-drink-row-swipe-action` to ensure consistent spacing
- **Drink row container styling**: Added `background: white` and `border-radius: 10px` to `.events-drink-row` for improved visual hierarchy and rounded corners

## Implementation Details

author: jlowapik
body:
Adds probation reporting to the PeopleForce connector and closes a silent correctness hole in the `listEmployees` status filter. Both changes come from probing a live 262-employee workspace on 2026-08-18 — every claim below is measured, not inferred from docs.

## Probation

`probation_ends_on` is a **first-class, HR-set date**, so it is reported, never derived. Observed spans run 3 to 17 months and are extendable, which rules out any `hired_on + 90 days` shortcut (one employee: hired 2025-05-01, probation ends 2026-10-01).

`probationStatus()` derives `on_probation` / `probation_passed` / `inactive` / `unknown`. `formatEmployee` and `formatEmployeeList` both render the date plus the derived state through one shared helper, so the two views cannot drift. **The list view previously showed no probation at all**, which made a `status=probation` query return rows you could not read.

Two deliberately conservative calls:

- **A departed employee reports `inactive`, never passed or failed.** The API exposes no termination or dismissal date, so terminated-during-probation cannot be distinguished from terminated-years-later. `probation_failed` is reserved in `PROBATION_STATUS_VALUES` but **never emitted**; because `probation_ends_on` survives offboarding, it becomes computable retroactively if a termination date ever surfaces.
- **A null date reports `unknown`, never "passed."** A null is ambiguous between no probation configured, cleared after passing, and simply unfilled — guessing would misreport contractors as having cleared a probation they never had.

## Status filter

`status` is now validated against `EMPLOYEE_STATUS_VALUES` (`active` | `probation` | `inactive`) instead of forwarding an arbitrary string. Measured behaviour of the values that misbehave:

| value | upstream result | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| _(omitted)_ | 110 rows, all active | default is **active-only**, not everyone |
| `active` | 110 rows | ✅ |
| `probation` | 4 rows, all active | ✅ real server-side segment, one call |
| `inactive` | 152 rows, all inactive | ✅ use for departed |
| `on_probation` | byte-identical to the default list | ❌ silently ignored — **fails open** |
| `terminated` | 156 rows spanning both statuses | ❌ a union, not a termination cohort |

Two consequences worth calling out for review:

- **The old tool description recommended `terminated` as an example**, actively steering callers to the value that returns a mixed active+inactive union. That was the more harmful of the two bugs, because it was the documented happy path.
- **`on_probation` failed open** — a typo returned a plausible-looking full directory instead of a 400. That is the specific failure mode the allowlist exists to prevent.

Also documented: omitting `status` returns active-only, so a full headcount needs two passes (`active` + `inactive`); there is no "all". And `status=probation` replaces paginating the whole directory.

## Tests

14 new tests covering the derived states, the never-emitted reserved slot, both rejected filter values, and the list-view rendering. Fixtures use the three real probation shapes observed live, including the 17-month span as a named regression against a `hired_on + 90d` heuristic.

- `peopleforce.test.ts`: 186/186
- Full suite: 1992/1992
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean

## Notes for the reviewer

Docs changes are two one-line diffs: the regenerated `listEmployees` row in `docs/MCP_TOOLS.md`, and one added findings bullet in `claude.md`.

The one open question is whether the termination date is genuinely absent upstream or merely unmapped in our hand-written `PeopleForceEmployee` type. A probe over two inactive records found nothing matching `terminat|dismiss|resign|offboard|contract|trial`. If it does turn up later, populating `probation_failed` is a small localized change — the type, tests, and docs already anticipate it.

author: brgkevin-arch
body:
Trois décisions du 2026-08-18, dans l'ordre où elles ont été prises. **Aucun code moteur n'est supprimé.**

## État final

| | Banque de calories | Hors plan |
|---|---|---|
| Pilier Kyroz+ | non — dégatée | jamais payant |
| Visible à l'écran | **non — éteinte** | **non — éteint** |
| Moteur lu | **non** (flag off) | — |
| Moteur intact | oui (`calorieBank.ts`, 23 tests) | oui (`offPlanJournal.ts`, `adaptDayOptions`…) |
| Interrupteur | `RYTHME_HEBDOMADAIRE_ACTIF` | `PARCOURS_HORS_PLAN_ACTIF` |

Les deux constantes vivent dans **un seul fichier**, `lib/featureFlags.ts` — point de vérité unique pour « qu'est-ce qui est éteint ? ». Volontairement **deux constantes et pas une** : les deux parcours ont été arbitrés séparément, à des jours différents ; un flag commun interdirait de rallumer l'un sans l'autre.

## Ce qui a été livré, dans l'ordre

1. **Dégatage + renommage** (`4038bcf`) — la banque sort de Kyroz+, devient « Jours plus copieux », les CGU sont recalées.
2. **Hors plan mis de côté** (`a0b8779`) — bouton et historique retirés, code intact, étape de visite guidée retirée avec sa cible (sinon écran bloqué sans sortie, cf. E50).
3. **Inventaire** (`8f69eea`) — chaque bloc classé VIVANT/DORMANT/MORT, TODO posé sur la dette de la clé jour-de-semaine.
4. **Bug corrigé** (`1322d67`) — un écart posé sur un jour retiré du plan restait affiché alors que le moteur l'ignorait. `servedWeekdays` devient la règle unique (affichage + moteur), `normalizeCalorieBank` referme la donnée au chargement.
5. **Extinction complète** (`d2bc231`) — la banque rejoint le hors plan derrière un flag. `planEngine::bankOf` est le seul point qui lit `calorie_bank` ; éteint, il rend `undefined` — **pas seulement l'écran, la lecture**. Sans ça, un compte portant déjà un réglage garderait une semaine déformée par une valeur qu'aucun écran ne montre plus.
6. **Docs recalées** (`ed0485a`) — CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/MONETISATION.md disaient encore « gratuite et visible ».

## Ce que le point 5 a exigé de plus

`profileSignature` lit `bankOf(p)`, pas `p.calorie_bank` : le plan **en cache** d'un compte qui portait déjà un réglage s'invalide et se refait sans lui, sans incrément d'`ENGINE_VERSION`.

Le contrat du moteur reste défendu : `planEngine.test.ts` force le flag à `true` (`vi.mock`) pour continuer de tester ce qu'il devra faire si on le rallume. Un second fichier, `rythmeEteint.test.ts` (4 cas), teste l'app **réelle**, flag éteint — sans lui la suite décrirait un produit qui n'existe plus.

**Vérifié par mutation, deux fois** : lire `profile.calorie_bank` brut dans `bankOf` fait rougir 3 des 4 cas ; le faire dans `profileSignature` en fait rougir 1 (le plan en cache).

**Vérifié dans le navigateur** avec un profil portant déjà « mercredi +500 » : écran Profil sans la ligne ni séparateur orphelin, écran Plan à 2 362 kcal plat sur toute la semaine (aucune trace de l'écart hérité).

## Mesures

`tsc` propre · **1 572 tests verts** (97 fichiers, +14 depuis le début du chantier).

author: georgepapagapitos
body:
## What

The refine pass already returned server-verified add/cut tweaks. The only thing you could do with one was accept it, singly, on a generated deck. This adds the management layer around it.

The governing constraint: **the AI proposes once; everything after that press runs on data already in the browser.** No lever here triggers another model call.

## Changes

**Ungate hand-built decks.** `use-commander-bracket-analysis.ts` runs for "generated and manual decks alike" — it gates on commander format and a commander being present, never on `deck.source`. So `gapAnalysis` / `hiddenGems` / `synergyAnalysis` were already populated on hand-built decks and `buildRefinePool` already had real input. Only the gate said otherwise.

**Wire the live owned-only toggle.** `refineOwnedOnly` derives solely from `deck.buildReport.collectionStrategy`, which a hand-built deck has no copy of, so it defaulted false. Meanwhile the Coach tab's own `ownedOnly` toggle went to `CoachFeed` but not to the AI panel beside it — you could turn on "owned only" and keep getting suggestions for cards you don't own. Now `refineOwnedOnly || ownedOnly` on the three mounts where it applies. The `variant="replace"` mount keeps `ownedOnly={false}`: the card being added there has already been chosen.

Note this correctly spends a reading — `ownedOnly` is in the server's refine cache hash, so a different constraint gets a different answer rather than a cached one.

**Apply all** reuses `handleApplyCostSwaps` (the existing budget/bracket bulk path), so a bulk accept lands as ONE undo entry. Hidden below 2 tweaks and on the `replace` variant, where a bulk control is meaningless.

**Dismiss**, reversibly — the row collapses to "Dismissed {name} · Undo" rather than vanishing. Persisted per deck, so a rejected card doesn't return on every cache replay.

**Re-roll** against the engine's own ranked pool. `buildAlternativeIndex` (new, pure, `roleOf` injected) maps each pool card to same-role siblings in pool order, which is lane priority: gaps → off-meta → owned substitutes → gems → lands. The AI names at most 5 cards; the pool holds up to 300.

## Two correctness rulings

**A re-rolled row drops the AI's reason.** The model never evaluated the replacement, so showing its sentence under that card would attribute a claim it didn't make. The row shows a neutral engine line instead, and the applied `Change.reason` is swapped too so the misattribution can't leak into undo history. Bulk apply respects the re-rolled pick, not the original.

**Every mount is keyed by deck id.** `/decks/:id` has no route key, so react-router reuses the editor element across decks and this panel never unmounted. Without the key, deck A's reading stays on screen while deck B is open — and "Apply all" would push A's swaps into B — while A's dismissal set stays in state and the next save writes it back under B's key. Two tests pin this; both fail without the key.

## Verification

Full CI-mirror gate on the frontend: typecheck / eslint / stylelint / format:check / test:coverage all green. **8925 tests pass**, no coverage breach. Backend and `packages/*` untouched.

The new behaviour tests were checked negatively — reverted against the un-fixed code, exactly the intended 2 fail and the other 17 pass.

UI eyeball is the user's, per repo convention.

author: andrei-hasna
body: ## Summary Successor of the terminated statusline-provisioner candidate (hasna/apps#272, 3x NO_GO, bounded policy). The open P1: the PATH-resolved statusline binary was persisted into fresh Claude profiles as `"" render` — double quotes do **not** neutralize `$()`, backticks, or embedded quotes, so a hostile PATH entry (e.g. `/tmp/a$(...)/statusline`) became a command executed at status refresh, auto-seeded for every fresh profile (profiles.ts:220, store.ts:241). This candidate keeps the provisioner's intent (fresh profiles born with the machine's installed statusline when shared settings omit it) and fixes the persistence defect: - `installedStatuslineCommand` resolves `statusline` from PATH and returns the resolved path **only when it contains no shell metacharacters** (`isSafeCommandPath`: strict charset, POSIX and win32 variants). A hostile/unusual entry (spaces, quotes, `$()`, backticks) is rejected, recorded on the result, and scanning continues to a later safe PATH entry. - The persisted command is plain words — `${binary} render` with no quoting, because quoting cannot make an unsafe path safe. - Birth-only: both `addProfile` paths (LocalStore `profiles.ts`, ApiStore `store.ts`) pass `{ freshProfile: true }`. Launch/switch/health passes (`env.ts`, `switch.ts`, `session-merge.ts`) stay source-driven and never sweep existing profiles. - The missing-shared-home case still gets the installed default at birth; the declared-no-statusLine negative control (no binary on PATH → nothing written) is preserved. TDD: red first (5 new/adapted tests failing on main), then green. Full accounts suite: 1716 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail (1717 tests). Typecheck clean. ## What / why

Rewrote docs/51 (the multi-agent audit playbook, deleted from a prior instance's version — recreated from scratch here, not restored, to avoid inheriting stale assumptions), then dogfooded it twice and did some related docs housekeeping. Six commits:

1. **`docs: rewrite docs/51 multi-agent audit playbook`** — adapted from a generic 17-agent/P0-P4 template into something sized for this repo's actual surface (no third-party integrations beyond Gmail SMTP/Neon, no file uploads, no test suite to grade coverage of). Kept: phase structure, evidence discipline, audit-first-modify-later. Dropped: the oversized agent roster and severity scale.
2. **`docs: run the docs/51 audit playbook, add docs/52 findings`** — first real run, 5 parallel lenses. 3 clean, 1 new Low a11y finding (left open), 1 lens (docs consistency) found + fixed 7 real staleness issues inline.
3. **`docs: import 3 playbooks from toolbox, archive 2 as superseded`** → **4. `docs: keep the 3 imported playbooks live, archive 3 superseded docs instead`** — imported 3 generalized playbooks from a separate `toolbox` repo (docs/53/54/55). author: dbenoit17
body:
Previously, our strictfipsruntime mode still rejected binaries built with -tags no_openssl when the host is in FIPS mode.  This commit adds strictfipsruntime support for binaries built with -tags no_openssl or CGO_ENABLED=0.  With this change, when the host is in FIPS mode, components built with strictfipsruntime and without openssl will allow operation in native fips140 mode.

This commit also propagates GODEBUG=fips140 through the internal/testenv clean environment, to ensure that subprocesses inherit the parent's fips mode configuration. Otherwise, binaries built with strictfipsruntime and executed in the clean environment would crash as a result of strictfipsruntime enforcement.

Lastly, the commit includes minor fixes to crypto_test.sh where the working directory was not restored after running some tests.  This issue actually never manifested itself, because we always set the test directory in relation to GOROOT.

author: giulioder
body:
Two commits on `docs/preregistrations/2026-08-16-sessionstart-hook-mcp-ordering.md`. **The prediction text is unedited throughout**; the only line removed in the whole PR is the status header, flipped from `predicted, not yet measured` to `MEASURED`.

## The result

The control never needed running by hand. It had already run itself, and session `e0aa68bb` is **both arms two hours apart in one approved checkout** — exactly the comparison the document asked for and could not previously construct.

| hook row | condition | recall tools in that session |
|---|---|---|
| `2026-08-18T09:21:43Z` (start) | `mcp_action: generated`, `existed_before: false` | **0** |
| `2026-08-18T12:08:56Z` (2nd SessionStart) | `mcp_action: already-present`, `existed_before: true` | **32**, two seconds later |

The first row is the treatment condition as specified, and that session did not get the tools. **The prediction is confirmed.** Because both rows share one project's approval state, confound 1 cannot explain the 09:21 absence — which is what made the first commit's run uninterpretable and this one readable.

## The two causes separate, and both are necessary

| condition | transcripts | tools |
|---|---|---|
| `.mcp.json` written by the session's own hook | `d8bded1a`, `30a93f4d`, `9b366ea4`, `e0aa68bb`(1st) | 0 |
| file present, project **not yet approved** | `b03972ae`, `2b8b37ba` | 0 |
| file present **and** approved | `e0aa68bb`(2nd) | **32** |

This retires "approval explains everything" (two sessions had the file present and still got nothing) and equally retires "ordering explains everything". Both are jointly necessary, and the tool inventory cannot say which is missing — which is why every earlier single-arm observation was unreadable.

## On the evidence type

The measurement is the harness's own `deferred_tools_delta` records, which are structural entries written by the client, **not model prose**. That distinction is load-bearing: a bare grep for `mcp__recall` also matches conversation text, and **four of these six transcripts contain the string while carrying zero tools**. An earlier draft of this analysis nearly reported those as positives.

## What is explicitly not established

1. **Approval is timestamped nowhere.** That the 09:21 arm was already approved is *inferred* from the same project being approved at 12:08 with no approval action between, not observed. **This is the check that would falsify the reading**, and it cannot be run retrospectively — a future run must snapshot `enabledMcpjsonServers` immediately before the session starts.
2. **What the 12:08 SessionStart was** — a resume, compaction or re-entry under the same session id. "A later SessionStart in the same checkout" is demonstrated; "a wholly new process" is not.
3. **`deferred_tools_delta` reports visibility, not connection.**
4. **`claude -p` is still 401**, re-checked today, and it **exits 0 while failing**, so a harness reading exit codes scores that as success. The original method stays unrunnable; this came from the deferred method.

## Consequence

A fresh worktree gets no recall tools in the session that creates it, and gets them on the next session **provided the project is also approved**. Since `scripts/session_mcp_approve.py` is absent from master (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 49ac9c5f origin/master` fails), a fresh worktree on master satisfies neither condition on its first session and only the ordering one on its second. Landing that commit is what makes the second session work.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: ma91n
body:
issue #2601。論点の **1（版の子をバージョン降順で先、続けて共起の絞り込みを記事数降順）** で実装しました。

## 変更

`scripts/related_tags.js` の detail 群の組み立て1行と、`versions` 群と共通化した2関数。

```js
- const detail = narrowing.concat(children).sort((a, b) => b.posts - a.posts || byName(a, b));
+ const detail = children.map(withVersion).sort(byVersionDesc).concat(narrowing);
```

`withVersion` / `byVersionDesc` は `versions` 群がインラインで持っていた処理をそのまま切り出したものです。同じ「新しい版が先」の規則を2箇所で持たないようにしています。`byVersionDesc` に名前順の同点処理を足したのは、`versionOf` で束ねたタグ（`version` が `Infinity` になる）が複数出たときに順序が決まらないためです。現状の該当は `Vue3` の1件だけで、いまの出力は変わりません。

## 実データでの前後（全697タグでヘルパーを直接叩いて突き合わせ）

**変わったのは6ページだけ**です。メンバーの増減、および detail 以外の群（隣接 / もっと広い / 他のバージョン / 他の年）の並びは1件も変化していません。

| ページ | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Go** | net/http(10) / Go1.22 / Go1.27 / GoCDK / Go1.16 / Go1.18 / Go1.20 / Go1.23 / Go1.17 / … 全24件 | **Go1.27 / Go1.26 / Go1.25 / Go1.24 / Go1.23 / Go1.22 / Go1.21 / Go1.20 / Go1.19 / Go1.18 / Go1.17 / Go1.16** / net/http / GoCDK / GoConference / … |
| **インターン** | インターン2022 / 2020 / 2021 / 2023 / 2024 / Dataflow / IoT / **インターン2026(1本)** | **インターン2026 / 2024 / 2023 / 2022 / 2021 / 2020** / Dataflow / IoTプラットフォーム |
| **Java** | SpringBoot / Java23 / JEP / Java24 / GraalVM / Java25 / Tomcat | **Java25 / Java24 / Java23** / SpringBoot / JEP / GraalVM / Tomcat |
| **NLP** | YANS(4) / NLP2024 / NLP2025 | **NLP2025 / NLP2024** / YANS |
| **Terraform** | tfstate(5) / Terraform1.4 / TerraformCloud / マルチリージョン | **Terraform1.4** / tfstate / TerraformCloud / マルチリージョン |
| **GoogleCloudNext** | 2025 / **2019** / 2024 | 2025 / **2024** / 2019 |

Go の24件が「版12件 → 共起12件」に自然に割れるため、issue の論点3（群を分けてラベルを付ける）は不要と判断しました。群を増やさずに版の列として流し読みできます。

### issue の記載との差分

- **PostgreSQL と Vue.js は変化なし**でした。PostgreSQL は既に 18 → 17 の降順、Vue.js は子が `Vue3` 1件で元から先頭だったためです
- かわりに issue に挙がっていなかった **NLP**（`NLP2025` / `NLP2024` ＋ 共起の `YANS`）が対象でした。語幹ページは7つではなく **8つ**です

## 検証

- 全697タグでヘルパーを before / after 実行し、差分が上記6ページの detail の並びだけであることを確認（メンバー集合の一致もアサート）
- 配信中の HTML（`localhost:4001`）で6ページすべての「もっと詳しいタグで探す」を抽出し、ヘルパーの出力と一致することを確認
- 版ページ（`/tags/Go1-27/`）の「他のバージョン」群が Go1.26 → Go1.16 の降順のままであることを確認
- `npx prettier --check scripts/related_tags.js` 通過

## 範囲外

- 群を分ける案（論点3）は採っていません
- 隣接群の並び（`co × log(1 + lift)`）には触れていません

body:
Follow-up to #29. That PR documented the TestFlight install failure; this one fixes the things in this repo that are actually broken and reachable from here.

## The real bug

`scripts/native/set-signing-secrets.sh` defaulted to `REPO=ay2m/FlyGACA`, but `git remote -v` on this repo is `ay2m/FlyGACA-ios` — the repo whose `ios-testflight` job reads these secrets. The script pushes a **distribution certificate, its p12 password, and an App Store Connect API key**, so a wrong default is a bad way to find out.

It now derives the target from the checkout's `origin` remote:

```bash
REPO="${REPO:-$(repo_from_origin || echo 'ay2m/FlyGACA-ios')}"
```

Verified: `https://github.com/ay2m/FlyGACA-ios` → `ay2m/FlyGACA-ios`; `git@github.com:ay2m/FlyGACA-ios.git` → same; a non-GitHub remote falls through to the literal. `bash -n` clean. `REPO=` still overrides.

## The unrunnable command

Runsheet §4.2 told you to pass **five** files (including `FlyGACA_PPL_AppStore.mobileprovision`), but the script has `[ "$#" -eq 4 ] || die "Expected 4 files: …"`. Following the runsheet as written aborts. PPL's module was removed in 2026-08 and `ios.yml`'s TestFlight matrix is `elpt · aip` (verified against the workflow — no `PROVISIONING_PROFILE_PPL_BASE64` reference anywhere in it). Fixed:

- §4.2 invocation → four files, `p12 · elpt · aip · p8`, with the count called out as hard-checked.
- §4 heading → "nine GitHub secrets", matching what the script actually sets.
- §4.3 → the PPL secret row marked ⏸ paused/orphaned rather than required.
- §5 → no longer claims the matrix uploads `ppl · elpt · aip`.
- `RUNBOOK-ios-signing-CHECKLIST.md` §C heading no longer names a specific repo.
- `CLAUDE.md` — it claimed the remote is `FlyGACA/FlyGACA-ios` and told you to always pass `REPO=`; both now match reality.

## Roadmap

"Create the signing secrets and the store records" was still listed as open work under **Now**, but run #69 exercised every artifact in it end to end. Marked done, and replaced with the genuine remaining blocker — the App Store Connect record gaps behind the install failure (Pricing and Availability, age rating), pointing at §5.1.

## Checked, healthy, unchanged

Ran these rather than assuming:

- **Content is in sync.** Regenerated via the monorepo's `build-ios-content.mjs` into a scratch dir and diffed: byte-identical for both apps. The only extra file is ELPT's hand-bundled `quiz-extra.json`, which the bundler doesn't generate — and `ContentKit/ContentLoader.swift:85` does load it, so it isn't dead weight.
- **Manifests are consistent.** ELPT 4 banks / 151 questions, AIP 3 banks / 113 questions; `module.bankIds` matches the quiz banks exactly in both, no empty banks, and `elpt-scenarios` doesn't clash with a `quiz.json` id.
- **`FG_MODULE_ID` matches `module.json`'s id** for both targets (`elp`, `aip`) — the pairing `CLAUDE.md` warns to verify.

## Not done, and why

- **The install failure itself is not fixable from here.** It needs App Store Connect (pricing/availability, age rating) and a check on the tester device's Media & Purchases account. No portal access in this environment.
- **No Swift build or test run.** There's no Swift toolchain or Xcode in this container, so `swift test` and `xcodebuild` could not be executed. Nothing in this PR touches Swift, so CI's `swift-test` is the first real check.
- **Left the `ay2m/FlyGACA` naming alone elsewhere** (README CI badge, `THE-BOOK-OF-FLY-GACA.md`, `MIGRATION.md` PR links). GitHub redirects renamed repos, so those may well work; shields.io is unreachable from this container, so I couldn't test the badge and didn't want to guess. Worth a look on a machine with network.

## Verification

Docs and one shell script. `ios.yml` carries `paths-ignore: ['**.md', 'docs/**']`, so only the `scripts/` change triggers jobs here.

Four checks that passed while holding nothing, and one bound with a real
consequence. Each fix has a test that fails when the fix is reverted.

- `Item.Self` could be deleted from `compactLocked` with the suite green:
  `journal_test.go` never mentioned it. The desktop's own queued messages came
  back unbadged after a restart, drawn like an app calling itself zde (#109).
- The smoke test's graphics assertion accepted `not known`, and #117 added a
  route to that word for a compositor with a screen for none of its outputs,
  which is the black screen the section exists to catch. The reason is checked
  now, pinned to doctor's sentence from both sides.
- `zde-report` (#103) was not a unit doctor asked about, so a failed snapshot
  unit was reported by nothing. The list is checked against `nix/home.nix`.
  Optional, because it is behind `zde.debug` and systemd says `inactive` for a
  unit that was never installed.
- `bootID` checked length where `reportName` checked hex, so a non-hex boot id
  produced a file rotation could never remove, at one per session start under
  `/var/log`. One expression is the shape now.
- Also pinned: `sort.Strings` in `askNiri`, without which the screens row moves
  between two readings of one machine.

Left alone: `cardsMax`, `inputsMax`, `screensMax`, `lineMax`, `cmdlineMax`,
`logLinesMax`, `fellMax`, `sawMax`, `reportBytesMax`. Each bounds a reading
whose only observable consequence is the file's 64 KiB ceiling, which
`TestASnapshotIsCappedAndSaysWhereItWasCut` already holds.

Also: the smoke test asks for its two snapshots a second apart. A snapshot is
named to the second and `O_EXCL` refuses the second one of any second, so its
two `zde report` calls failed whenever the boundary fell after both. That is a
pre-existing race; it surfaced on this branch.

`nix build .#zde-smoke` needs `/dev/kvm` and was not run locally; the changed
shell block was run over rendered snapshots for all five states, and CI's
`smoke` job is the real test.

author: adamenkoa1
body:
## Goal
Materialize the declared `receivables` register as a derived BAS-style read model over the existing immutable `patient_settlement_movements` ledger, without duplicating economic movements.

## Invariants
- `patient_settlement_movements` remains the single source of truth: charge increases patient debt, payment decreases it, refund increases it again.
- Receivables are computed as-of a selected date and scoped to one organization.
- Positive booking balance is debt; negative booking balance is patient credit and is reported separately, never netted invisibly against another booking.
- Aging starts when the current positive balance became outstanding after the last zero/non-positive running balance.
- Admin-only patient-level report; successful views emit only PHI-free audit metadata (`asOf`, row count).
- No schema migration and no production deploy.
- Add behavioral coverage for unpaid debt, payment settlement, refund reopening, credits, aging, tenant isolation, RBAC and audit.

author: bradymiller
body:
## Summary

Two related cleanups to how `data/announcements.yml` is managed:

### 1. Auto-source the "current release" banner from `data/releases.json`

- Retire the hardcoded `title` / `date` on the homepage banner's "Announcing OpenEMR Version X" entry; replace with a `kind: current-release` marker
- Teach `themes/openemr/layouts/partials/homepage-announcement-bar.html` to derive that title from `data/releases.json` — the highest `status: FINAL` entry, same logic as the `current-stable-version` shortcode used on the demo page — so the banner auto-updates when a new release lands in the manifest
- Version display rule: `"X.Y"` when `patch == 0` (e.g., `8.3.0` → **8.3**), `"X.Y.Z"` otherwise (e.g., `8.3.1` → **8.3.1**)

### 2. `disabled:` flag, hide AWS entry, drop unused dates

- Partial pre-filters entries into a `$visible` slice, skipping any with `disabled: true`. All downstream logic — first-item `active` class, `data-index`, dot count, carousel-controls gate on `len > 1` — operates on the filtered list, so hiding the first entry doesn't blank the initial slide or misalign the dots
- Hide the "OpenEMR 8.2 Express Plus AWS" entry via `disabled: true` (an 8.3-supporting AWS Express Plus build hasn't shipped yet; flip the flag back to re-enable)
- Drop the `date:` field from the remaining entries. No template consumes `.date` on announcement items (grep across `layouts/` and `themes/` returned zero hits) — the field was doc-metadata that drifted from any actual purpose

## Motivation

Every release cycle we've been bumping the banner by hand (see #202, #216). The demo page has already been auto-sourced from `data/releases.json` via the `current-stable-version` shortcode; this brings the banner onto the same single-source-of-truth pattern. The release-docs workflow keeps `releases.json` in sync with the conductor's branch state, so a new FINAL release ships → banner updates on the next site rebuild, no yaml touch required.

The `disabled:` flag closes the "how do I temporarily hide a banner" gap that would otherwise force a delete+restore cycle for time-limited announcements.

## Test plan

- [x] `hugo` renders "Announcing OpenEMR Version 8.3" (highest FINAL in current `data/releases.json` is 8.3.0, patch=0 → short form)
- [x] Synthetic `8.3.1` FINAL entry renders "Announcing OpenEMR Version 8.3.1" (patch>0 → full form)
- [x] AWS entry with `disabled: true` is skipped; dots and indices correct (`current-release` at index 0 with `active`, OpenCoreEMR at index 1, 2 dots)
- [x] With the first entry (current-release) also disabled, OpenCoreEMR renders at `data-index="0"` with `active` — no blank initial slide
- [ ] After merge, https://www.open-emr.org/ shows the auto-derived banner and no AWS entry
- [ ] Next release: `data/releases.json` gets the new FINAL entry via release-docs → banner updates without touching `data/announcements.yml`

author: seabbs-bot
body:
## Summary

`scaffold_inputs` defaults `org` to `DEFAULT_ORG` (`"EpiAware"`), so a
package hosted elsewhere got `EpiAware/<pkg>` URLs in its README badges,
`make.jl`'s `repo=`, `config.mts` and `try-this-pr.yaml`. The `org`
keyword already fixed that at scaffold time. What did not work was
keeping it: the scheduled template-sync ran `update(".")` with no `org`,
so every weekly run reset the owner back to `EpiAware`.

This makes the sync pass the argument. The generated
`.github/workflows/template-sync.yaml` now carries the scaffolded org in
its own `update` call, exactly as it already carries `ad`, `benchmarks`,
`downgrade_compat` and `unregistered_sources`:

```yaml
res = EpiAwarePackageTools.update("."; org = "epiforecasts", ad = false, ...)
```

The owner is stated once, at `scaffold`, and every later sync re-applies
the standard under it. Nothing is guessed.

The same substitution goes into the two other places the workflow prints
that call: the sync PR body, and the local re-apply command in the drift
tracking issue, so a maintainer following those steps by hand does not
revert the owner either.

`scaffold_inputs` and `update` are otherwise unchanged from `main`:
`org::AbstractString = DEFAULT_ORG`, no detection.

Closes #434.

## What was here before

The first two commits derived `org` from the local `origin` git remote,
then from committed README badges and `docs/make.jl` before the remote.
Both are removed. `_detect_org` and `_origin_org` no longer exist, and
with them go the two bugs found in that code: the `repo =` regex that
matched Documenter's URL form and captured the scheme, and
`setup_checklist` passing `DEFAULT_ORG` explicitly so detection never ran
from that path.

## Test plan

- [x] `a package outside EpiAware keeps its org on a sync` — scaffolds
  with `org = "epiforecasts"`, asserts the README carries
  `epiforecasts/Wombat.jl` and not `EpiAware/Wombat.jl`, that the
  generated workflow's `update` call and the drift-issue remediation both
  name `epiforecasts`, and that running exactly what the sync runs leaves
  the README byte-identical.
- [x] `scheduled sync is managed` extended: the emitted call is
  `update("."; org = "EpiAware", ad = false, ...)` and `{{ORG}}` is
  substituted.
- [x] `a failed sync opens one tracking issue` updated for the wrapped
  remediation command.
- [x] Filtered runs: `scaffold + update (logic)` 1784 pass; the remaining
  `test/scaffold.jl` testitems 303 pass.
- [x] `task format` and `task precommit` clean.
- [x] Self-drift: the kit's own `template-sync.yaml` regenerated by
  `update("."; ad = false)`, working tree otherwise clean.

## Interaction with #467

None. #467 rewrites the `uses: {{ORG}}/.github/...` callers to
`{{WORKFLOWS_ORG}}`, a separate ecosystem constant. This PR only adds
`{{ORG}}` to the `update` call inside the sync job. Either can land first.

This was opened by a bot. Please ping @seabbs for any questions.

**스택 PR — base 가 `feat/TRIP-357-region-catalog`(#228) 다.** 357 을 먼저 머지하고 이 PR 을 develop 으로 retarget 한다.

카탈로그를 화면이 쓸 수 있게 연다. 검증하는 쪽(C7)이 목록도 소유해야 "고를 수 있는 것"과 "받아주는 것"이 구조적으로 갈라지지 않는다.

## 계약
`GET /api/v1/regions?q=&level=` → `{regionCode, name, sidoName, level, selectable, poiCount}[]` · 인증 필요(/places 와 같은 정책)

## 티켓 대비 판단 2가지
| | 결정 | 왜 |
|---|---|---|
| `selectable` **추가** | 잘라 내지 않고 값으로 | 도(道)를 지우면 화면이 시도로 묶을 때 `수원시` 가 어디에도 안 붙는다. 규칙의 주인은 서버이고 이 필드가 그 규칙이다 |
| `sidoCode` **제외** | 안 내보냄 | 묶음 키는 `sidoName` 이면 충분 — 안 쓰는 칸을 계약에 실으면 못 뺀다 |

## 실 DB 가 아니었으면 못 봤을 결함
`:q is null or … concat('%', :q, '%')` 로 처음 썼더니 **검색어 없는 호출만 500** 이었다. Hibernate 가 null 파라미터 타입을 `concat` 안에서 추론 못 해 bytea 로 보낸다(`operator does not exist: character varying ~~ bytea`). 필터 있는 질의는 전부 통과해서, IT 가 없었으면 "검색은 되는데 목록만 안 나오는" 형태로 화면 붙일 때 나왔을 것이다. 빈 문자열 `%%` 로 분기 자체를 제거했다.

## 정본 이탈
AC 는 `level=SIDO` 가 **17행**이라 적었으나 **16행**이다 — 원본에서 광주광역시·전라남도가 폐지·통합돼 있다(357 실측). AC 의 17은 개편 전 숫자다.

body: Closes remediation task R10 in the Lattice 1.0 audit: three silent-gap findings about the boundary config, each with a silent-direction regression test (a test that goes red when the enforcement is removed). ## D-13 — `.mjs`/`.js` dialect tolerated extra top-level exports silently An unknown top-level export (`moduleBoundaryOption` for `moduleBoundaryOptions`) used to load exit-0 and disappear. The `.mjs` dialect now applies the same key law the `.json` dialect has: any export beyond `depConstraints`, `moduleBoundaryOptions`, `boundarySuppressions`, `fitness` is refused **by name**, through the shared `policyKeyViolations`. The language server's `.mjs` arm reads through the same two validators, so a config the CLI refuses cannot load clean in the editor. ## D-15 — `buildTargets` entries are exact-matched, and a non-exact value was silently inert Two guards: - **At load:** an entry carrying glob syntax (`"build:*"`) is refused — a pattern can never match an exact `===`-compared target name. - **At run (flag on, non-empty graph):** an entry that matches no target declared by any project throws from every evaluating command, naming the entry and the declared targets. Never silently read as selecting nothing. An empty graph skips the check (no claim to make on no projects). ## D-12b — `$schema` was a false-green trap `$schema` in the `.json` file dialect and a native `lattice.json` inline policy is now **accepted and checked**: it must be a non-empty string (whitespace counts as empty). The profile-registry `version` default now applies only to an *absent* version — a stated `version: null` is refused loudly, not silently defaulted. ## Validation - 124 test files / 2681 tests pass (including new silent-direction tests, each verified to fail when its fix is reverted) - `tsc` typecheck, ESLint zero-warnings, Prettier clean - Gate scripts: 133/133 `node --test`, `check-docs-links`, `check-skills`, `check-packages` all pass - Repo's own boundary check: `cli.mjs check` exit 0 - Adversarial review (independent) requested changes; all findings fixed and re-verified 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: chojona
body:
## Purpose [SCRUM-260](https://carpoolnu.atlassian.net/browse/SCRUM-260) — husky 9 warns about two constructs this repo still used, and both stop working in v10. The warnings printed on **every commit and every install**, which trains people to ignore husky output — the same channel a real hook failure would use. And with Dependabot now proposing majors individually (SCRUM-181), merging husky v10 would have silently disabled the pre-commit hook: formatting would just stop running, with no error. ## The change **`.husky/pre-commit`** — 4 lines to 1: ```diff -#!/usr/bin/env sh -. "$(dirname -- "$0")/_/husky.sh" - npx pretty-quick --staged ``` The sourcing line was redundant as well as deprecated: husky 9 already invokes this file through the generated `.husky/_/pre-commit` wrapper, which does that setup itself. **`package.json`**: ```diff -"prepare": "husky install", +"prepare": "husky", ``` **No dependency versions change** — husky stays at `9.1.7`. This only removes the deprecated *usage*, so the eventual v10 bump becomes a no-op. ## Verification — before and after Both acceptance criteria asked for confirmation rather than assertion, so here it is. **AC 4 — a fresh install still installs the hooks.** I deleted `node_modules` *and* the generated `.husky/_` first, so this was genuinely from scratch: | | output | |---|---| | before | `$ husky install`
`husky - install command is DEPRECATED` | | after | `$ husky` — no warning | After the fresh install, husky had regenerated `_/pre-commit`, `_/husky.sh` and `_/h`, and `core.hooksPath` was still `.husky/_` — unchanged, so no developer's git config shifts underneath them. **AC 3 — a commit still runs `pretty-quick --staged`, with no deprecation warning.** The commit on this branch is itself the test, and it printed no deprecation block (compare any recent commit, which emitted the 6-line `husky - DEPRECATED` notice). But "no warnings and a green checkmark" would not prove the hook still *does* anything, so I also staged a deliberately misformatted file and committed it: ``` 🔍 Finding changed files since f5850ad. 🎯 Found 1 changed file. ✍️ Fixing up src/__huskyprobe.ts. ✅ Everything is awesome! ``` The committed content came out properly formatted, confirming the hook still reformats and re-stages. That throwaway commit was then dropped with `git reset --hard`; the probe file is not in this PR. **Other checks**, in the same clean worktree: `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` (lockfile unmodified), `yarn lint`, `yarn tsc`, `yarn check:env`, `prisma generate`, `yarn build` — all pass. `yarn test --passWithNoTests` passes **vacuously**; the repo still has no test files, so that is not coverage (SCRUM-211). `prettier --check` clean on `package.json`. **File mode preserved:** `.husky/pre-commit` was already `100644` (not executable) and still is — the diff carries no mode change, so nothing depends on an exec bit that quietly disappeared. ## Acceptance criteria | AC | Status | |---|---| | Remove the shebang and `husky.sh` sourcing line, leaving the body | Done | | Change `prepare` from `husky install` to `husky` | Done | | Confirm a commit still runs `pretty-quick --staged`, no deprecation warning | Done — verified on a real commit, and separately proved it still reformats a misformatted file | | Confirm a fresh `yarn install` still installs the hooks | Done — with `node_modules` and `.husky/_` both deleted first | ## Note for reviewers After merging, your next `yarn install` regenerates `.husky/_` with the new wiring. Nothing needs doing by hand, and the deprecation noise on commits and installs should simply stop. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: mohsen1
body:
<!-- Describe what and why. For semantic fixes, state the structural rule:
     when <structural condition>, tsc does X; tsz does X through <owner layer>. -->

Fixes #17625.

An assignment RHS that calls an **import alias to a cross-file generic function**, inside an import cycle, produced a false `TS18048 "'x' is possibly 'undefined'"` — `tsc` is clean. Minimal two-file repro (oracle-clean on typescript 6.0.2 / 7.0.2):

```ts
// util.ts
import type { Row } from './consumer.js';           // the cycle
export function freeze<T>(value: T): Readonly<T> { return value; }

// consumer.ts
import { freeze } from './util.js';
export interface Row { readonly name: string; readonly cols: { readonly n: string }[]; }
interface Raw { readonly tn: string; readonly cn: string; }
export function gather(items: Raw[]): Row[] {
  return items.reduce<Row[]>((acc, it) => {
    let r = acc.find((c) => c.name === it.tn);
    if (!r) { r = freeze({ name: it.tn, cols: [] }); acc.push(r); }
    r.cols.push({ n: it.cn });          // tsz: false TS18048 on `r`
    return acc;
  }, []);
}
```

Removing the `import type` line (breaking the cycle) makes tsz clean — the cycle is the discriminator.

## Structural rule

When a flow assignment RHS is a call whose callee is an import alias to a cross-file generic function, the flow generic-call gate must resolve the callee through the alias target's stable **checked** signature, and when that signature is not yet computed (import cycles make "check the provider first" impossible) it must fail closed to the existing on-demand forcing retry. It must never accept the alias's own on-demand `Lazy(DefId)` — whose body, minted mid-cycle before the target is typed, collapses to a **non-callable object** — because that non-lazy-but-wrong callee type silently defeats the retry and leaves the conservative possibly-`undefined` union as a false positive.

Owner layer: the checker flow-analysis generic-call fallback gate (`crates/tsz-checker/src/flow/control_flow/assignment_fallback.rs`), reusing the existing `record_unresolved_import_callee` → `retry_flow_narrowing_after_forcing_import_callees` mechanism (`flow/flow_analysis/usage.rs`).

## Mechanism (traced)

`fallback_instantiated_generic_call_type` resolves the callee, then gates a generic call through the solver. The callee-resolution chain tries the callable-aware `fallback_cached_callable_reference_type` first (the path built for imported generic functions), but at flow time — inside the cycle — the alias target's real signature (`Function`) has not yet been published to the shared type-environment/def-store, so it returns `None`. It falls through to the general `fallback_type_for_reference`, which mints the alias's *own* on-demand `Lazy(DefId)`; resolving that mid-cycle yields a degraded non-callable `Object`. Because that result is non-lazy, it passes the `is_unresolved_lazy_type` filter and is treated as "resolved", so `record_unresolved_import_callee` never fires, the solver gate returns no return type, and the conservative TS18048 survives.

The forcing-retry mechanism already exists for exactly this import-cycle timing problem (record the alias, force `get_type_of_symbol` at the `&mut` boundary, re-run narrowing once). The fix broadens the "unresolved callee → record for retry" trigger to also cover "resolved to a non-callable type" for an import-alias callee: the retry then forces the alias's real `Function` signature, re-runs narrowing, and the accumulator narrows correctly. `record_unresolved_import_callee` now returns whether it recorded (alias-only), so a non-alias non-callable callee still falls through to the solver gate unchanged. The cheap `has_call_signatures` test short-circuits before the scope-walking alias lookup, so the common callable path pays nothing.

## Adjacent-case matrix (oracle = tsc 6.0.2, all match)

| case | shape | tsc | tsz before | tsz after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | `freeze<T>(v):Readonly<T>` import-cycle | clean | TS18048 | clean |
| renamed binder + arrow | `wrap = <U>(v):Readonly<U> =>` | clean | TS18048 | clean |
| concrete (non-generic) factory | `makeRow(name):Row` | clean | clean | clean |
| **negative control** | `maybe<T>(v):T\|undefined` | TS18048 | TS18048 | TS18048 |
| no cycle (control) | same, `import type` removed | clean | clean | clean |

The negative control proves the fix computes the **real** return type rather than blanket-suppressing: a genuinely nullable factory still keeps the accumulator possibly-`undefined`.

## Goal
Goal: green

## Verification
- New multi-arena (CLI-driver) regression test `import_cycle_alias_to_cross_file_generic_function_narrows_reduce_result` (`crates/tsz-cli/src/driver/check_tests/check_tests_part6.rs`) — covers the baseline, renamed-binder/arrow, negative-control rows and asserts full tsc-cleanliness for the non-null rows. Confirmed it **fails without the fix** and **passes with it**. The single-checker in-process harness shares binders and does not exercise the cross-arena delegation, so a checker-crate test would pass even unfixed — hence the CLI-driver test.
- `cargo nextest run -p tsz-checker --test generic_call_assignment_flow_tests` — 29/30 (the 1 failure is the pre-existing tracked known-failure #15983 `colliding_generic_terminals_...`, red on clean main too).
- `cargo nextest run -p tsz-cli --lib` — no checker-logic regressions; the only failures are pre-existing `tsc_compat_tests::*` (external-binary/parity harness tests, red on clean main).
- `cargo clippy -p tsz-checker --lib` clean; pre-commit hook (fmt + clippy + arch guard) passed.
- Emit parity (`./scripts/emit/run.sh --skip-build`) and conformance (`scripts/conformance/compare-to-parent.sh origin/main`) — running now on cloud; result will be added as a comment before this leaves draft.

Model: claude-opus-4-8[1m]
Effort: high

Adds the region-based semantic ops from ADR-0008: `swage.map`,
`swage.reduce` (kinds `sum`/`max`/`min`), `swage.map_store`, and
`swage.yield`.

- Regions are `IsolatedFromAbove`; outer values enter via `captures(...)`,
  appended to the block arguments after the element, in order.
- `swage.map_store` declares a write on its output; a canonicalization
  test locks the DCE contract (unused pure `map` folds, `map_store` stays).
- Verifiers: block-argument/capture agreement, yield-type agreement, kind
  validity; empty-segment semantics, reduction identities, and the
  aliasing obligation are documented in ADR-0008 and the op descriptions.
- Tests: 10 lit files — positive round trips including the segmented-
  softmax composite from ADR-0008, negatives via `--verify-diagnostics`
  (isolation violation, capture arity/type mismatches, yield-type
  mismatches, invalid kind), a canonicalization contract test, and
  f16/bf16 segment coverage.

Base is `foundation/mlir-m0` (#26); GitHub retargets this PR to `main`
when #26 merges. Nothing here executes on a GPU; these are semantic-level
ops only, per the roadmap's M1 gate.

Closes #1. Closes #2.

author: justaghost
body:
## What

The root vitest suite (`scripts/preflight-capacity.mjs` + its tests, plus `src/start/**`) has a `test:start` script but nothing ever calls it — `pnpm test`/`pnpm test:coverage` and CI's blocking "Test" job delegate straight to `.agentkit`, skipping the root suite entirely.

That gap let a real regression sit invisible: `scripts/preflight-capacity.mjs` was independently fixed on `dev` so page-file growth only counts disk headroom *above* the fixture floor (not raw free disk) — a good fix. But its own test file wasn't updated for the new semantics, so **`should not credit page-file growth the disk cannot absorb` has been failing on `dev` since that fix landed**, invisible because nothing runs it in CI.

## Changes

- **`package.json`**: `test` / `test:coverage` now run `test:start` / `test:start:coverage` before delegating to `.agentkit`.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: the blocking "Test" job's coverage step now also runs `pnpm test:start` (root suite) before `pnpm -C .agentkit coverage`.
- **`scripts/__tests__/preflight-capacity.test.mjs`**: fixed the stale fixture. `freeDiskGb: 3` predates the floor-aware fix, where `freeDiskGb` directly meant usable growth space. Under the corrected semantics, headroom is measured above `fullConfig.minFreeDiskGb` (30 GiB) — so `freeDiskGb: 3` now means *zero* headroom, a different (and already-covered-elsewhere) scenario than what this test's name/comment describe. Raised to `freeDiskGb: 33` (30 + 3) to restore the original intent — "3 GiB of disk is usable for growth" — verified against the fix's actual current output, not guessed.

## Deliberately scoped out

Root suite runs in CI **without** `--coverage`. `vitest.config.mjs`'s coverage thresholds (80%) apply jointly to `src/start/**` and `preflight-capacity.mjs`, and `src/start/index.ts` currently sits near 0% covered — for reasons unrelated to this suite. Wiring `test:start:coverage` into the required "Test" job would flip a currently-green required check red over that pre-existing, out-of-scope gap. `pnpm test:coverage` still runs the root suite with coverage locally, for whenever that gap gets closed on its own.

## Verification

- Fresh worktree off `origin/dev`'s tip, dependencies installed clean.
- `pnpm test:start`: 192/192 green, including the previously-failing case.
- `pnpm -C .agentkit coverage`: 2741 tests, thresholds met (branches 80.39%). One run hit a "Worker exited unexpectedly" flake — a class this repo's own `ci.yml` comments already document and handle via the reconcile step — reproduced clean on immediate retry, confirming it's not caused by this change.

author: dpavancini
body:
One-line fix. Unblocks the stalled prerelease channel.

## What broke

`787c3662` (in #288) needed to add `.cursor-plugin/` to `package.json:files`. It also rewrote the `description` line as collateral, because the JSON serializer I used defaulted to `ensure_ascii` and escaped the em-dash:

```diff
-  "description": "...Agentic Development Framework — installs adev..."
+  "description": "...Agentic Development Framework \\u2014 installs adev..."
```

That line sits directly beneath `version` — the one field that permanently differs between `main` (0.27.8) and `release/next` (0.28.0-next.2). Touching its neighbour turned a normally clean merge into a conflict.

## Consequence

`.github/workflows/propagate-to-next.yml` merges `main` → `release/next` on every push to main, and that push is what triggers release-please to update the prerelease PR. It **failed on all three merges to main today**:

```
16:45  failure  Merge pull request #291
16:45  failure  Merge pull request #290
16:44  failure  Merge pull request #288
23:30  success  Merge pull request #287   ← last good
```

```
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in package.json
```

So `release/next` fell 18 commits behind and release-please had nothing new to release there — no prerelease PR. The stable PR (#205) was unaffected because it runs on `main` directly, which is why this looked like "only one release branch is working".

## The fix

Restores the literal em-dash, keeping `.cursor-plugin/`. The description is now byte-identical to `release/next`'s, so the only difference in that region is `version` itself, which release-please owns per branch.

No behavioural change — npm reads both forms identically. This is purely about keeping the two release branches mergeable.

## Follow-up, not in this PR

`release/next` still needs its conflicted merge resolved manually to catch up; that is being done separately, taking `release/next`'s `version` and its `release-please-config.json` (the workflow's error message warns explicitly not to take main's config, or a stable version publishes to the `next` dist-tag).

Also worth confirming: the workflow header notes that if the propagation push uses the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, the cascade will not fire even on a successful merge, and `RELEASE_PLEASE_PAT` must be set. I cannot verify from outside whether that secret exists — if it does not, the prerelease PR will still need a manual nudge after this lands.

author: speccraft2025
body:
## Summary

Visual art direction pass for the Transcendence terrain renderer, replacing the neutral grey/alabaster palette with an EverSwap-inspired green mountain world.

### 1 — Palette
- Six-stop green height gradient: deep shadow green → dark forest → olive → saturated mid-green → pale green → near-white highlight
- Large coherent tonal regions via height zones, not random per-triangle color
- New `evergreen` palette entry (sun, sky, horizon, ground, fog) with green-tinted atmosphere

### 2 — Surface
- Broad tonal patches via low-frequency noise (`0.003`, `0.002×0.005`) create kilometre-scale material regions
- Geological strata banding on steep faces (`sin(height * 0.35 + fbm * 12)`) weighted by slope²
- Warmer olive ↔ cooler forest shifts across large regions via secondary macro noise
- Existing vein/streak/meso patterns preserved with adjusted intensity

### 3 — Lighting
- Tighter shadow wrap (`0.22` vs `0.42`) for stronger face-to-face variation
- Darker shadows (`shade * 0.09` vs `0.13`) with green shadow tint `(0.35, 0.52, 0.42)`
- Reduced translucency and specular for forest-like surfaces (higher roughness floor `0.34–0.94`)
- Reduced rim light and crest intensity to avoid excessive glow

### 4 — Atmosphere
- Green-tinted fog (near/far) replaces neutral grey
- Valley haze `(0.016, 0.026, 0.016)` replaces black void in trough
- Stronger low-lying fog (`0.38` vs `0.25`) with slower height falloff
- Clear foreground → midground → background tonal separation

### 5 — Ground
- Plinth floor shifted from near-black `(0.0175)` to dark earth green `(0.016, 0.024, 0.014)`
- Valley floor terrain gets deep shadow green from height gradient (not emptiness)
- Valley haze fills the trough depth instead of reading as black rectangle

### 6 — Geometry appearance
- Steep faces get smoothed normals (flat normal contribution reduced by `steepFade` factor)

body:
# Report empty metadata columns, stop the pan re-render storm, version in the README

v0.8.7 → **v0.8.8**

Three small things, plus a real hole found in one of my own tests while doing them. No new features; this is tidy-up of things flagged as known costs in the previous two PRs.

---

## 1. Columns that exist but hold nothing

`fov` and `transcript_count` are entirely null on the bundled MERSCOPE dataset, but colour-values reported them as a continuous `0.0–0.0` range. The UI then offered:

- a range slider spanning nothing,
- a legend with no span,
- and a filter that correctly matched zero cells while looking broken.

They now come back with **`empty: True`**, and the filter section says *"no values in this column"* instead of drawing a dead control.

`type` is still set, so nothing switching on categorical-vs-continuous needs a third case. The cross-panel merge calls a column empty only when it is empty in **every** panel — one panel having values is enough to keep the control worth showing.

## 2. The pan re-render storm

`usePanelSettings` subscribed to the whole store, so every sidebar section re-rendered on each OpenSeadragon viewport-change event. This was recorded as a known cost when the hook was introduced in v0.8.5.

It now ignores `viewports` and `viewportActual` — the only two continuously-rewritten keys, and ones **no consumer of that hook reads**: `ViewerPanel` takes `viewports[panelIndex]` through its own selector, and ⇔ Match zoom reads `viewportActual` via `getState()`. LayerPanel, CellInfoPanel and AnnotationToolbar reference neither.

Measured over one simulated pan of 120 viewport writes:

| | re-renders of every sidebar section |
|---|---|
| before | **121** |
| after | **0** |

…with ordinary settings changes still delivered (verified in the running app: the edge-width label repaints `6.0` → `9.0`).

Narrowing the rest would mean a selector per sidebar section — a real refactor with no component tests behind it, and not worth it once the pan storm is gone. There is a warning at `IGNORED_KEYS`: ignoring a key a consumer *does* read makes that consumer silently stale, which is much worse than a redundant render.

## 3. Version in the README

Added under the title. CLAUDE.md now records that the version lives in **three** places that must move together — `frontend/package.json` (read at build time via vite's `__APP_VERSION__`), `backend/app/main.py` (`APP_VERSION`, served by `/health`), and the README line — and that every other `v0.x.y` in the tree is a *historical* reference that must not be swept along by a bump.

Audited before changing anything: the two authoritative files already agreed, and all other mentions ("shipped in v0.8.4", "present since v0.2.0") were correctly historical.

---

## The hole this turned up

While chasing the empty-column behaviour I found that `tests/edge_pipeline_check.py` — the guard added in v0.8.6 to assert the #59 invariants — called:

```python
color_values("metadata", None, field)     # signature is (mode, field, genes, categorical)
```

The field went in as `genes`. The call returned the empty result, `spec_for` returned `None`, `ids` was `None`, and **the filtered-subset assertion was skipped on every dataset**. The check printed `OK` across 9 datasets while not exercising its own core property.

Fixed, and it now says so out loud when no filter resolves rather than passing over it in silence. With the assertion actually running, the property still holds — 9 datasets, 3 densities, with real cell counts now shown (24,033 on CosMx, 426 on Xenium, 790 on Visium kidney, …).

So the v0.8.6 claim that subset containment was verified across 9 datasets was weaker than stated. The property itself was sound — it had been checked by hand with explicit `MetadataFilter.build` calls at the time — but the automated guard was not the thing checking it.

## Testing

| | |
|---|---|
| Edge pipeline check | 9 datasets × 3 densities — **now actually running the subset assertion** |
| Golden snapshot | 249 probes / 8 datasets |
| Frontend (Vitest) | 56 tests |
| DuckDB config check | 4 `DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT` forms |

Plus, in the running app: the empty-column message appears for `fov` on MERSCOPE, settings changes still repaint the sidebar, and the console is clean.

## Note on tags

`v0.8.7` is merged upstream but its tag was never pushed, so the release history skips from `v0.8.6` to `v0.8.8`. Worth pushing that tag alongside this.

author: nddq
body:
# Description

`TestModule_Reconcile` builds four `Module` literals without `dirtyPods` — only `InitModule` initializes that field — and calls `Reconcile` on them. `Reconcile` calls `run`, which starts a ticker on the package constant `interval` (1 second, `metrics_module.go:38`) with a context that no test cancels. Each tick calls `applyDirtyPods`, and the first tick dereferences the nil `*DirtyCache`:

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x20 pc=0x21d3fe9]
github.com/microsoft/retina/pkg/common.(*DirtyCache).GetAddList(0x0)
        pkg/common/dirtycache.go:39
github.com/microsoft/retina/pkg/module/metrics.(*Module).applyDirtyPodsAdd(...)
        pkg/module/metrics/metrics_module.go:574
```

The SIGSEGV kills the whole test binary. Whether it fires is a race between the first tick and process exit: on a machine where the package takes longer than ~2 seconds, `go test -tags=unit ./pkg/module/metrics/` fails every run.

This PR sets `dirtyPods: common.NewDirtyCache()` in the four literals, matching the neighboring `TestPodCallBack` and `TestModule_NamespaceAndPodUpdates`. Ticks on an empty cache are no-ops (no filtermanager calls), so the leaked `run` goroutines stay harmless for the remainder of the process.

## Related Issue

N/A — found while validating #2628 locally.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [contributing documentation](https://retina.sh/docs/Contributing/overview).
- [x] I signed and signed-off the commits (`git commit -S -s ...`). See [this documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/about-commit-signature-verification) on signing commits.
- [x] I have correctly attributed the author(s) of the code.
- [x] I have tested the changes locally.
- [x] I have followed the project's style guidelines.
- [ ] I have updated the documentation, if necessary.
- [ ] I have added tests, if applicable. (N/A — fixes existing tests)

## Screenshots (if applicable) or Testing Completed

At `origin/main` (`792c9324`) the panic reproduces on every run of the package on a VM where the suite takes ~2.5 seconds. With this fix, `go test -tags=unit -count=10 ./pkg/module/metrics/` passes cleanly.

## Additional Notes

`go test -race` on this package still fails for an unrelated pre-existing reason: `TestBaseMetricObject`'s expire callback writes a test-local variable (`basemetricsobject_test.go:54`) that the test reads without synchronization (`:77`). It reproduces at `origin/main` with `-run TestBaseMetricObject` alone. CI does not run unit tests with `-race`, and that fix belongs in its own PR.

body:
## Central de Campanha sai do zero, e o indicador de atendidas para de inflar

A tela mostrava "sem dados" desde 15/08 esperando uma fonte de telemetria que nunca foi
construída. Esta PR constrói essa fonte e, no caminho, corrige um indicador que estava
publicando 2,5× o valor real. Tudo **somente leitura** — nenhuma escrita no Postgres,
no ClickUp ou no Wavoip.

### Por que
- **Atendidas estava errado em produção.** `ATENDEU` é drop_down (Sim/Não) e o painel
  contava "campo preenchido" como atendida, somando as **não** atendidas. Das 141
  ligações de 18/08: 17 Sim, 26 Não, 98 sem desfecho — a tela publicava **43**.
- **A Central nunca consultou nada.** O commit 93c0a31 (15/08) trocou a leitura de um
  `reais.json` estático por `const real = VAZIO`, com a nota "sem telemetria ao vivo".
  Era zero compilado no bundle, não cache velho.

### O que muda
- **Produção diária** — 6 dias de operação (12 a 18/08), ligações e contatos por dia.
- **Ranking de telefonistas** — 23 operadores, com rótulo legível (124 dos 144 valores
  do campo são e-mail; o domínio é cortado).
- **Taxa de atendimento** — 39%, calculada sobre as ligações **com desfecho**. Sobre o
  total daria 12% e mediria o registro, não o atendimento.
- `lerAtendeu` deixa de ser privado e passa a ser a única decodificação de `ATENDEU`.
- `duracaoEmSegundos` — o campo `DURAÇÃO` é texto (`"5min 32s"`); `Number()` nele dá NaN.
- `tempoMedio` usa **mediana**, não média: há outliers de até 12.217s (3h23) contra
  mediana de 50s, provavelmente ligação que nunca gravou `FIM`.

### Não muda
- Nenhuma escrita em lugar nenhum, e **nada no Wavoip** — nem API, nem configuração.
- Ligação sem operador fica fora do ranking (esse balde tinha 23 ligações e 21 dos 24
  contatos, e apareceria no topo como se fosse a melhor telefonista), mas **continua nos
  totais**: é dado real, só não é pessoa.
- Os demais cards seguem em "sem dados", corretamente: série de votos exigiria saber
  *quando* o voto foi confirmado (o ClickUp não guarda) e o comparativo semanal exige
  duas semanas — só existem 6 dias.

### Verificação
- `npm run build` verde na ponta **e no commit intermediário** (`67fb3ed` conferido por
  checkout, para não quebrar `bisect`); `npm run typecheck` verde em `romero-mobile`.
- Rota exercitada com Bearer: `200`, 6 dias na série, 23 telefonistas, taxa 39%.

### Sabido, e fora do escopo
Das 144 ligações feitas pelo app, só **3** registram atendida e **104** não têm desfecho
nenhum — o desfecho só é gravado quando o closer escolhe o motivo na tela. Por isso a
coluna de contatos do ranking fica quase zerada. `desfechoDeApp` é exposto na resposta
para a tela poder explicar o zero em vez de exibi-lo mudo. O conserto é no fluxo do
closer, em PR própria.

author: justinchuby
body:
## What

`ONNX_GENAI_MARLIN_M_GT_1` now defaults **ON**; `ONNX_GENAI_MARLIN_SPLITK` moves to opt-in (default **OFF**).

## Why

The M>1 `MatMulNBits` path had a tensor-core Marlin GEMM behind an env var that was off by default, so every default deployment paid a prefill tax. `.squad/decisions.md` recorded a NO-GO on flipping it, resting on two findings.

**Finding 1 — "the win is marginal" — does not generalize.** It was measured only on qwen2.5-14b/7b (0.976–1.013x). On an A100-SXM4-80GB (SM80) serving Muse-Glimmer-30B int4, measured end-to-end through the server with both arms on one binary:

| prompt_tokens | tiled (`=0`) | Marlin (default) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 287 | 6.0s | 3.6s | 1.67x |
| 647 | 9.4s | 4.7s | 2.00x |
| 1647 | 23.7s | 10.4s | 2.28x |
| 3247 | 37.5s | 16.1s | **2.33x** |

Prefill throughput 87 → 202 tok/s. Neutral on some models and 2.33x on others argues for a default plus an opt-out, not for hiding the win behind a variable nobody sets.

**Finding 2 — "full-vocab logprobs are not byte-identical" — stands.** An earlier draft of this PR claimed that divergence came from split-K and was therefore fixed by turning split-K off. **That was wrong**, and thanks to review it is corrected here: `choose_split_k` returns 1 for `m > SPLITK_MAX_M` (32), so prefill never elected a split. The measured Δ (0.017 qwen14, 0.168 qwen7 at M=128/512/2048) is the direct tensor-core kernel's accumulation order versus the tiled GEMM.

So this PR is an explicit, recorded **relaxation of the bar**, not a claim that the bar is met: the shipping default becomes *argmax-stable* rather than *bit-identical*. Greedy token streams match — `marlin_m_gt_1_e2e.rs` parity plus an 826-token spot check across the flip (identical answer; one sentence reworded at a near-tie, the nondeterminism that test already classifies). Consumers of the *distribution* rather than the selected token (logprobs API, beam search, spec-decode acceptance ratios) should set `ONNX_GENAI_MARLIN_M_GT_1=0`.

## Why split-K flips the other way

Flipping the parent ON while leaving split-K ON would newly ship a *second*, independent divergence source (its fixed-order fp32 partial reduction) to every default deployment. Split-K is inert for prefill by construction (M>32 never splits); the shapes it governs are M≤32 speculative verify, where it was the real lever (capture B\* 5.10x → 2.69x at M=8). Turning it off is acceptable only because that workload is separately shelved. Recover it with `ONNX_GENAI_MARLIN_SPLITK=1`.

## Safety

Every eligibility check still applies at all three call sites (SM80+, int4, no `g_idx`, no fused SwiGLU/RMSNorm epilogue where unsupported); ineligibility or launch error falls through to the tiled GEMM. Review confirmed the `Ok(Some)/Ok(None)/Err` fallback contract holds at `matmul_nbits.rs:7005`, `:7062`, `:8051`, and that no correctness path depends on split-K (all split entries route through `maybe_launch_marlin_splitk`, which falls back to the direct kernel for every shape when disabled).

## Test fallout

Tests that used an *unset* variable to mean "tiled" now set it to `0` explicitly. That includes the near-tie probe loop in the e2e parity test, which must re-run the **tiled reference** to expose its own nondeterminism — leaving it unset would have made those probes Marlin runs and inverted the test's meaning.

## Not addressed here

Marlin is no longer the prefill bottleneck. With it on, `MatMulNBits` is ~20% of a prefill forward (GEMMs at ~74 TFLOPS); attention and elementwise ops are the other ~80%. Separate investigation.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>go-task/task (aqua:go-task/task)</summary>

### [`v3.53.1`](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v3531---2026-08-18)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/compare/v3.53.0...v3.53.1)

##### 🚀 Features

- **Remote Taskfiles are now generally available!** This has been an
  experimental feature for 3 years, but is now enabled by default. Massive
  thanks to all those that contributed and gave feedback (too many to list
  here). We've also given the
  [Remote Taskfiles documentation](https://taskfile.dev/docs/remote-taskfiles) a
  bit of a polish ([#​1317](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/1317), [#​2906](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2906) by [@​pd93](https://redirect.github.com/pd93)).
- Added a per-command `timeout` that terminates a command once it exceeds the
  given duration (Go duration syntax). It covers shell commands, task calls,
  deferred commands, `deps` and the `if` condition, obeys `ignore_error`, and
  reports exit code `124`. Callers that join a `run: once` or `when_changed`
  task already running now honor their own `timeout`, and inherit that task's
  failure instead of being told it succeeded ([#​1569](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/1569), [#​2898](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2898) by [@​vmaerten](https://redirect.github.com/vmaerten)).
- Considerably improve performance of fingerprinting on large repositories
  (monorepos). Fingerprinting is up to 86% faster and make up to 70% fewer
  memory allocations on the more advanced scenarios. Benchmarks were added as
  well. We're basically skipping work when not needed. ([#​2853](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2853), [#​2883](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2883) by
  [@​Napolitain](https://redirect.github.com/Napolitain), [#​2884](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2884) by [@​Napolitain](https://redirect.github.com/Napolitain)).
- Further improved fingerprinting performance on large repositories: hashing
  source files now reuses a single buffer, reducing memory allocations by \~98%
  and wall-clock time by \~7% ([#​2925](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2925) by [@​vmaerten](https://redirect.github.com/vmaerten)).
- `includes.excludes` can now exclude a whole namespace: append `:*` to the
  namespace name, e.g. `excludes: ['debug:*']`. Bare entries still match a
  single task name exactly ([#​2300](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2300), [#​2959](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2959) by [@​xmxxc](https://redirect.github.com/xmxxc)).
- Added support for `enum.ref` in `--interactive` prompts. Required vars using
  `enum.ref` now show the selection list like static enums, instead of falling
  back to free-form input ([#​2817](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2817) by [@​vmaerten](https://redirect.github.com/vmaerten)).
- Added Nushell completions, available via `task --completion nu`. They complete
  task names and aliases, every flag with its description, and the values of
  `--completion`, `--output` and `--sort` ([#​2966](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2966) by [@​vmaerten](https://redirect.github.com/vmaerten)).
- Added a verbose log line for failed tasks. In `--verbose` mode, a task whose
  command exits non-zero now reports `task: "<name>" failed: <error>` instead of
  stopping without a trace ([#​2240](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2240) by [@​Drino](https://redirect.github.com/Drino)).

##### 🐛 Fixes

- Fixed a pinned `checksum:` not being verified when a remote Taskfile came from
  the cache ([#​2980](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2980) by [@​vmaerten](https://redirect.github.com/vmaerten)).
- Fixed the fingerprint variable (`{{.CHECKSUM}}`/`{{.TIMESTAMP}}`) ignoring a
  `method:` set at the Taskfile level: the variable now follows the same method
  resolution as the up-to-date check. Only the variable matching the effective
  method is injected, so a task inheriting a Taskfile-level `method: timestamp`
  gets `{{.TIMESTAMP}}` and no longer a `{{.CHECKSUM}}` (which now renders as an
  empty string), and neither variable is injected when the effective method is
  `none` ([#​2924](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2924) by [@​vmaerten](https://redirect.github.com/vmaerten)).
- Fixed `ref:` in `for: matrix:` and `enum:` only accepting literal lists. Refs
  computed with template functions like `keys` or `splitList` no longer fail
  with "must resolve to a list" ([#​2544](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2544), [#​2956](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2956) by [@​no-hup](https://redirect.github.com/no-hup)).
- Fixed pressing `Esc` at an interactive variable prompt not cancelling the run
  ([#​2942](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2942) by [@​anilnatha](https://redirect.github.com/anilnatha)).
- Fixed `joinUrl` collapsing the `//` in a URL scheme (e.g. producing
  `http:/localhost` instead of `http://localhost`) ([#​2915](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2915) by [@​vsaraikin](https://redirect.github.com/vsaraikin)).
- Fixed the JSON schema rejecting `ignore_error` on a command inside a `for`
  loop. Editors no longer flag a Taskfile that Task runs perfectly fine ([#​2044](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2044)
  by [@​gokeefe-atb](https://redirect.github.com/gokeefe-atb)).
- Fixed the JSON schema rejecting more keys the Taskfile parser accepts:

  inside a `for` loop ([#​2967](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2967) by [@​vmaerten](https://redirect.github.com/vmaerten)).

author: tystgodhet
body:
Four mastery-aligned mechanics borrowed from Duolingo, bent to the app's principles: reward speed + precision, never play time, no leagues, no hearts, no guilt.

## The path
The per-component multiplication ladder is redrawn as a winding Duolingo-style trail on the home screen: one node per "deltal" with ★★☆ level stars, 🔒 on locked nodes, a pulsing ring on the session focus, a dotted trail between nodes, and auto-scroll to the frontier. Pure presentation of existing mastery state — no new mechanics, nothing to buy or grind.

## Mästarprov (gold)
A component sitting open at its top level shows a bobbing 👑 on its node. Tapping it starts a voluntary challenge: **10 problems in a row, all correct, each under 3 s**. Passing gilds the node (confetti storm); failing ends kindly ("3 av 10 — nära! Ett försök kostar inget") with a retry button and **zero trace** in stats, weights or sessions. Gold is a live claim: if the accuracy band later lowers the component's level, the gold is revoked.

## Daily quests
Up to three goals per day generated from the player's actual weaknesses:
- "Kör ett träningspass" (needs ≥5 attempts — no quick-quit gaming)
- "5 snabba rätt i [weakest component]"
- "Klara av 3 gamla missar" — or "10 snabba rätt" on a clean slate

Progress ticks silently during drills; completions are cheered on the result screen. The reward is a checkmark and confetti — never XP, currency or shortcuts. Quests regenerate at local midnight and persist in profile state.

## Celebrations
Confetti, banner pop-ins and a count-up hero number — for mastery moments only: level up, unlock, personal best, completed quest, gold run. Honors `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Deliberately skipped
Leagues/leaderboards (compare profiles, reward volume), hearts/lives (punish errors the review mode is built to embrace), guilt notifications, and XP-as-currency.

## Implementation
- New pure module `js/quests.js` (generation, day rollover, progress events)
- Gold constants + eligibility + band revocation in `js/ladder.js`
- Path rendering, gold challenge flow, quest wiring, confetti/count-up/banner helpers in `js/app.js`
- 9 new unit tests (66 total, all green)
- Service worker bumped to v10 with `quests.js` precached

## Verification
Playwright e2e against a real Chromium: quest card renders 3 quests; path renders 15 nodes (locked/focus/dots correct); a real drill ticks quest progress and completes the session quest with banner; gold fail path shows the answer key + "Försök igen"; retry → 10 fast correct → node turns gold and persists across reload; no console errors.

author: cboettig
body:
The picker offered `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, which **this proxy cannot route** — clicking it fails.

The id is real: OpenRouter publishes it. The problem is the route. `open-llm-proxy`'s vendor-prefix allowlist has no `google/` entry, so `get_provider_for_model` matches nothing and falls back to the hard-coded NRP provider, which does not serve it. The proxy filters its own `GET /v1/models` through that same router, so only two Google ids show as routable — `~google/gemini-flash-latest` and `~google/gemini-pro-latest`, which survive because `~` **is** in the allowlist (added for OpenRouter floating aliases).

`layers-input.json` is deliberately **not** changed: its `llm.models` block is the BYO-key path, where the browser calls OpenRouter directly and the pinned id is valid.

Found by auditing every app's live `config.json` picker against its own deployment's `GET /api/llm/models`. 147 entries across 17 public apps, 2 unroutable — this one and the same entry in `geo-agent-template` ([PR #34](https://github.com/boettiger-lab/geo-agent-template/pull/34)). Context: [geo-agent-ops#133](https://github.com/boettiger-lab/geo-agent-ops/issues/133). This app was also only just added to the ops registry (it had been running unregistered and unmonitored since 2026-08-05).
