author: yyardi
body:
Morning-review wave, four items. **Stacked on #16** (which stacks on #15); GitHub retargets as each base merges.

## 1. QUOTE gets a page — `/quote` + `GET /api/quote`

The endpoint is the dispatch's read-only exception; everything else is frontend.

- **Engine status** from its own heartbeat row (beat age, cycle time, fills last cycle/total, DEAD/idle/ok verdict).
- **Current quotes** reconstructed from the same observations through the engine's own imported code (`ShadowQuoter._observations`, `Observation.is_quotable`) — the engine's memory is in another container, and the page *says* "reconstructed" rather than pretending to read it. One definition of quotable, imported not restated.
- **Recent simulated fills** with the static study's per-fill capture mark.
- **Per-regime capture vs the pre-registered floors** (500 settled fills + 10 games), progress meters, and an explicit `accruing — no verdict yet` chip. The verdict string is the server's verbatim; the page renders one only when the report's own `at_floor` is true. Verified live: ingame **927/500 fills but 1/10 games**, pregame 19/500 · 1/10 — both correctly `NO DATA`, and the capture CI is honestly absent with one game (clustered means need ≥2 clusters).
- **Explainer block**: posts both sides at the touch, earns spread, pays adverse selection (measured −2.74¢ in-game), exists to test whether 5s requoting flips the sign, and *nothing is sent*.
- League tabs filter the live tables only; the measurement stays global — it is registered **regime**-split, and re-slicing a registered analysis client-side would show a different measurement under the registered one's name.

## 2. Per-market-type split on /analytics

Shape agreed with Builder D (one message each; they crossed and converged — D's final consolidation is the contract). Renderer honors every load-bearing point:

- `null` renders as — and never as 0 (ROI 0 broke even; null is no data)
- `backtested: false` rows grey out with **"never backtested"** inline — without this, unvalidated moneyline ROI sits in the same column as validated totals ROI
- win rate renders **only** as one cell with its stake-weighted entry cost (`0.480 @ 0.47`) — the entry cost *is* the breakeven (C11)
- absent `by_market_type` key hides the section entirely, so D's producer lands in either order; empty rows → "no data yet"

Verified by splicing D's exact agreed shape into the live page: greying, flag, one-cell win@cost, dashes, and the in-game "model is pregame-only" note all render.

## 3. Header data-age labels

`PREGAME`/`LIVE` are now **"pregame data age" / "live data age"** with tooltips saying what the number is, when growth is expected (live, between games) and when it is a failure (pregame past 90 min). Both pages.

## 4. Game tape phase labels

- Every decision round's chip says **PREGAME** or **IN-PLAY** in words — the CHI-SEA confusion was 90 rounds of tables with no way to tell which side of tip any sat on.
- A pregame-only game says so in one plain line: *"The model was pregame-only for this game: all 530 shadow trades were decided before tip."* (verified on CHI-SEA itself).
- `ctxChip` is the one place a round's phase becomes words — left as the seam for Builder C's live PULSE tape: an in-play PULSE decision arrives as `is_live` with a real score and needs no new rendering.

## Notes

- One of my new tests initially banned the word "clustered" and tripped on a tooltip *describing* the CI — the findings.md proxy-check mistake, made the same day the doc merged. Rewritten to assert the property (card renders the server's numbers, contains no aggregation machinery); the mistake is recorded in the test's docstring.
- C's `test_no_page_hardcodes_the_league_in_its_header` caught the new page missing league tabs — the discovery-form test doing exactly what it was built for.

## Verification

**1060 pass** (9 new). `/api/quote` exercised live against the real fills table; QUOTE page screenshot-verified; analytics renderer exercised with the agreed shape; tape chips verified on CHI-SEA (90 PREGAME chips, pregame-only line). Zero POSTs; no container touched.

author: lushbits
body:
Closes #1.

A drag-a-rectangle picker stores the loot chat region; `Windows.Graphics.Capture` watches its monitor behind an `IFrameSource` seam (a GDI fallback could slot in without touching OCR); `Windows.Media.Ocr` reads the region and every line lands in the live log. **Deliberately no sending** — that needs (c)'s dedup.

Built to sit beside the game:
- Frame pool drained on a 2 fps timer — the compositor skips us between ticks instead of copying at refresh rate.
- Region cropped on the GPU; only the chat-sized rectangle is ever read back.
- OCR gated behind a pixel compare — it runs only when the region changed.
- Buffers allocated once; below-normal process priority; log window trims itself.
- Measured: ~0.8% of one core static, ~5.6% worst case while pixels change (that's OCR itself).

Liveness: the log announces the first successful frame (region size, OCR language, upscale) and heartbeats every 2 minutes when quiet — a silent log always means capture died. Win11 capture border turned off via `RequestAccessAsync(Borderless)`; on Win10 the border is unavoidable and the README says so. The app is now per-monitor DPI aware; Settings/Log forms got explicit DPI auto-scaling (layout verified at simulated 150%).

Tested live against a running BDO client: real UI text read end to end.

author: hereliesaz
body:
## Summary
Three separate bugs reported together from an on-device test.

**Bootstrap: `pkg`/`apt` hardcoded paths.** Bash itself now runs (confirming the earlier RUNPATH/hard-link fix worked), but `pkg`/`apt` still failed with two further hardcoded-path bugs from the same root cause - forking Termux's official bootstrap (built for its own package, `com.termux`) under a different `applicationId`:
- Every script Termux's bootstrap builder compiled - `pkg` among them - ships with a shebang line baked to `#!/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/bash`, which doesn't exist under this app's sandbox ("bad interpreter: Permission denied"). 102 of ~600 files in the bootstrap carry this. `extractBootstrap` now rewrites any hardcoded-to-`com.termux` shebang line to this app's real prefix as each script is extracted.
- apt's own `Dir::*` settings are compiled into `apt`/`libapt-pkg` as absolute-path string constants against Termux's own package too - unlike a shebang line, there's no single first-line fix, since apt reads these before consulting any config file. What apt does honor from the environment is `APT_CONFIG` - a path to a config file read before falling back to those compiled-in defaults. `extractBootstrap` now writes one (every `Dir::` `apt.conf(5)` documents, pointed at this app's real prefix), and `ShellSession` points `APT_CONFIG` at it.

**Mis-tap race.** Tapping a child pill (e.g. "apt") then quickly tapping the pill in its newly-opened band (e.g. "update") could register the second tap against the wrong target - as far back as `HostPill`, resetting the whole menu to Browsing. `ChildBand`'s own `selected == null` check only guards taps landing on its own sibling pills; it has no way to know about `HostPill`/`TrailRow`, which kept accepting taps for the whole hand-off delay before `trail` actually updates. A `pendingPick` flag now gates both.

**Band pill styling.** `ChildPill` rendered every pill in a band at one identical width and one shared hue, unlike `StackPill`'s root stack, which already varies both per pill. Now varies hue by the pill's own id and width by a cycling per-row step, matching the root stack's own pattern - every pill stack in the menu now varies the same way.

Both bootstrap fixes still can't be verified end-to-end without a physical device.

## Test plan
- [x] `:shared:compileKotlinMetadata`, `:shared:compileAndroidMain`, `:composeApp:detekt`, `:shared:detektMetadataMain`, `:shared:detektAndroidMain` - clean (detekt baseline regenerated for changed signatures)
- [x] `:composeApp:assembleDebug` - succeeds
- [ ] On-device: `pkg upgrade`/`apt update` actually work, the mis-tap sequence no longer resets to Browsing, band pills visibly vary in color/width (needs a physical device)


---

Correct bootstrap package paths, close the pill-menu transition race, and align child-pill styling with the root stack.

Bug Fixes:
- Fix bootstrap scripts and apt configuration so package-management commands resolve paths within the app's sandbox instead of Termux's hardcoded package path.
- Prevent taps during menu transitions from being applied to stale host or trail targets.

Enhancements:
- Make child-band pills vary in color and width consistently with root stack pills.

author: groeneai
body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115272
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115146
-->


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed wrong results from `if`, `multiIf` and `CASE` when one branch is a `Date` or `Date32` and the result type is `DateTime` or `DateTime64`. With `compile_expressions = 1` (the default) the compiled expression copied the date's day count into the timestamp column without converting days to seconds, so `if(cond, toDate32('1900-01-01'), toDateTime64('1970-01-01', 3))` returned `1969-12-31 23:59:34.433`. Closes #115272.


### Description

Reported by @ PedroTadim in [#115272](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115272), who asked me to fix it and have @Manerone review.

**Root cause.** `FunctionIfBase::isCompilableImpl` already intends to refuse these expressions -- its comment reads *"It's difficult to compare Date and DateTime - cannot use JIT compilation."* -- but it tested `WhichDataType::isDate()` and `isDateTime()`, which are exact `TypeIndex` equality, so it refused only `Date`+`DateTime` and admitted `Date32`+`DateTime64`, `Date`+`DateTime64` and `Date32`+`DateTime`. Those reach `nativeCast`, which correctly finds no scale for day-count types and falls through to a plain `CreateIntCast`: `-25567` days becomes `-25567` milliseconds. The predicates were never widened when `Date32` and `DateTime64` were added.

**The change** widens both predicates to `isDateOrDate32()` and `isDateTimeOrDateTime64()`, so the guard covers the whole family and the interpreted path runs. `if.cpp` and `multiIf.cpp` inherit this base, so one change covers all three. These expressions lose JIT, as the comment intended and as `Date`+`DateTime` always did. The commit message covers the rejected IR alternative.

**Validation.** New test `04930_jit_compiled_if_date_to_datetime` asserts the compiled result equals the `compile_expressions = 0` result over the reported matrix: scales 0/3/6/9, both date and both datetime types, both branch orders, constant and column dates, `if`/`multiIf`/`CASE`, `Nullable(Date32)`, pre/post-1970. 12 of its 14 comparison rows fail without the fix and all pass with it (50/50 runs). The 2 exceptions are controls green both ways: `Date`+`DateTime`, already refused, and same-unit `Date32`+`Date`, which must keep compiling.

Those rows are 1-vs-0 parity checks, so they would pass even if compilation stopped. Two further rows pin which shapes compile, via `ProfileEvents['CompiledFunctionExecute']`: it counts executions of an already-compiled node, so it needs no cache drop and the test stays parallel-safe. The mixed-unit row fails on an unpatched binary, so it tracks this change rather than asserting a constant. They are also why the test carries `no-fasttest, no-msan`: those builds have no embedded compiler.

author: pantani
body:
## O que estava errado

O administrador semeado entrava em `/acesso` e via **"Suas hospedagens"**, com quadro de estadias, cartaz de autocadastro e fila de hóspedes — como se operasse os lugares que apenas admitiu. Isso acontecia porque o administrador é membro (`core.memberships`) de toda hospedagem que cadastra ou que aprova pela fila da ADR-042, e `GET /accommodations` devolve exatamente o que a conta alcança por esse vínculo.

O vínculo em si está correto e continua existindo: entregar o acesso de uma hospedagem lê a linha (`GET /accommodations/{id}`, para o ETag) e escreve a ativação (`POST /accommodations/{id}/activation`), ambos exigindo membership. O problema era só a interface tratar esse vínculo como propriedade operacional.

## O que mudou

A API não tem uma coluna de papel — `accommodations:onboard` é o que faz esse papel hoje: gateia `POST /accommodations` e as três rotas de decisão da fila global da ADR-042. [`AuthenticatedPage`](apps/web/src/pages/AuthenticatedPage.tsx) passou a escolher a área por esse escopo:

- **Área da administração** (`AdminWorkspace`, novo): cadastra hospedagem, entrega o acesso da hospedagem escolhida (sem seleção automática — abrir o formulário de acesso de uma hospedagem que ninguém escolheu seria emitir credencial por engano) e decide a fila de pedidos. Sem quadro de estadias, sem cartaz, sem fila de hóspedes.
- **Área da hospedagem** (`OperatorWorkspace`): estadias, cartaz e aprovação de hóspede. Perdeu toda afordância de cadastro — inclusive para quem carrega `accommodations:onboard`, porque essa conta cai na outra tela agora.

O seed (`apps/api/internal/platform/seed/run.go`) deixou de conceder `stays:write` ao administrador: registrar estadia é ato do estabelecimento, não da administração. Nenhuma migration, nenhum escopo novo — só reorganização de escopos já existentes e de UI.

O carregamento de hospedagens virou um hook compartilhado (`use-accommodations.ts`) entre as duas áreas, já que a query é a mesma; o que muda é o que cada área faz com o resultado.

## Verificação

- `make post-task-quality` → `POST_TASK_QUALITY=PASS`
- `npm test` (web): 424 testes, 49 arquivos, incluindo 6 novos em `AdminWorkspace.test.tsx` que cobrem diretamente o relato (não abre quadro de estadias, não trata a lista como hospedagem própria)
- `go test ./internal/...`: verde
- `make local-demo-e2e` → `LOCAL_DEMO_BROWSER_E2E=PASS` (jornada completa em Chromium contra stack efêmera, cobrindo o cadastro pela administração e a operação pela hospedagem em abas separadas)

Não rodei `make self-service-full-stack` (script HTTP que exercita a fila da ADR-042 com a sessão do administrador) — os dois escopos que a entrega do acesso usa (`accommodations:manage`, `stays:read:own`) foram mantidos, então não deveria haver impacto, mas fica como próximo passo de verificação se o revisor quiser rodar.

author: rogalvil
body:
## La medición

Árbol real, 2,779 imágenes y 617 videos:

| | tiempo | aciertos |
|---|---|---|
| frío | **177.1 s** | 0 |
| caliente | **0.5 s** | 2,779 imágenes + 617 videos |

**354×, con la misma respuesta**: 4,771 pares las dos veces.

Y por eso no es una optimización: un video son **ocho decodes**, así que sin caché un segundo escaneo del mismo
árbol —lo que uno hace después de mover unos archivos— vuelve a pagar los tres minutos completos.

## Misma forma que la caché de digests

Archivo append-only de filas fijas en `~/Library/Caches`, nunca en el directorio de estado que comparte el CLI:
un documento de escaneo es interop que no se puede perder, esto es dato derivado que macOS puede purgar bajo
presión de disco. Misma clave —volumen, inodo, tamaño, mtime y **generation**— así que un archivo reescrito con
su fecha forzada hacia atrás falla el acierto, que es el caso `rsync -t`.

Y la misma historia de corrupción, en una oración: una cola truncada se detecta por aritmética sobre el largo del
archivo, una fila corrupta por su CRC-32C, y un header que no cuadra descarta el archivo entero.

## Dos cosas propias

**El salt se deriva de los parámetros, no de una constante a subir a mano.** Cambiar el decode de 256 a 512
invalida cada hash guardado, y *"acuérdate de subir la constante"* es una regla que se olvida exactamente una vez
y después la caché sirve números que significan otra cosa. Hay test para cada parámetro: decode, cuadros,
tolerancia de seek. La constante a mano **sigue existiendo** para lo que los parámetros no pueden ver —la fórmula
de grises, los pesos del resampler, qué esquina del transform se recorta— o sea que hacen falta las dos mitades.

**Filas de tamaño fijo con ocho huecos**, aunque una imagen use uno. Se desperdician 56 bytes por imagen, 156 KB
sobre 2,779 archivos, contra un escaneo de 177 segundos. Lo que compra: `(tamaño − header) % fila != 0` sigue
detectando una cola truncada, y eso solo funciona si las filas miden lo mismo. Medido: el archivo de 3,396
archivos pesa **exactamente** 32 + 3,396 × 112 = 380,384 bytes.

**Y verifica el tipo, no solo la clave.** Un inodo reusado por un archivo del otro tipo serviría ocho cuadros
como si fueran una imagen.

## Verificación

`make lint` limpio, **0 warnings**. Coverage **95.66%** (`PerceptualCache` 91.26%). `--mode all`: **30 modos, 0
fallas**.

17 tests nuevos: round-trip de las dos clases, byte volteado rechazado por CRC, fila de cero cuadros tratada como
corrupta, salt por parámetro, header ajeno rechazado, cola truncada que cuesta su propia fila y nada más, archivo
sin identidad no cacheado, escritura caliente que **no escribe nada**, y a nivel de sesión: segundo escaneo
servido completo, `usesCache: false` respetado, y **un archivo reescrito en su sitio que no se sirve de la
caché**.

El modo `similar-window` ahora corre un segundo escaneo y afirma los aciertos.

### Prueba de dientes

| roto | falla con |
|---|---|
| la sesión nunca crea la caché | `0 images came from the cache, wanted 3` |

## Lo que no se pudo verificar

- **Sin compactación.** `needsCompaction` existe y nadie lo consulta — la misma deuda que la caché de digests
  arrastra desde su PR. Un árbol que cambia seguido hace crecer el archivo con filas superadas.
- **Sin `flock`.** La caché de digests degrada a solo-lectura cuando otro proceso la tiene; esta no lo hace
  todavía, así que dos escaneos perceptuales simultáneos podrían intercalar appends. La app solo permite un
  escaneo a la vez, pero eso es una invariante de la UI, no del formato.
- **No medí memoria** ni el costo de cargar un archivo grande de golpe: 380 KB no dice nada sobre cómo se
  comporta con 100,000 archivos multimedia.
- **Limpié mi basura**: la medición dejó dos documentos de escaneo en tu directorio de estado y los borré. Quedan
  los 33 de antes, incluido el del 13 de agosto que sí pediste.

author: michaeldawson
body:
`isWhatsappEnabled` returned `true` for a missing field, so every user who had never heard of the setting was enrolled in proactive templates on the strength of having a `phoneNumber` — a number most of them gave in order to log in.

## Why now

That default has produced two complaints:

- **2026-07-28** — Sonya Ramsey. 116 users were mass-disabled by `disableWhatsappForUnengagedUsers.ts`, whose own header calls itself *"a stopgap until the consent gate is fixed"* and notes that new signups would default back to enabled.
- **2026-08-17** — Tonya Lockamy replied "Stop" after two templates in 14 hours.

Nobody fixed the gate, so it kept re-enrolling people: six users signed up after the sweep and were silently opted in again. This is that gate.

## Change

`whatsappEnabled` is now opt-in — only an explicit `true` permits a proactive send, and the yup default flips to `false`.

Consent is recorded in exactly two places: the Me-screen toggle, and `findOrCreateUser` for someone who messages the bot first (see the functions PR).

Callers must go through `isWhatsappEnabled()`. A direct `=== false` test treats absent as permitted and reopens the hole — one call site was doing exactly that, fixed in the functions PR with a test pinning the non-equivalence.

## Effect on existing data

| group | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 116 swept in July (`false`) | off | off |
| 2 explicit opt-ins (`true`) | on | on |
| 6 with no field | **on** | **off** |

Nobody who opted in loses anything; the six who never agreed stop being messaged.

## Testing

The helper's tests live in `walk2gether-functions` (this package has no test harness). Full functions suite on the studio: **9 failing / 385 passing** vs **10 / 381** on main — one pre-existing failure fixed, no regressions.

author: eygraber
body:
Consumers running tests on newer JDKs see warnings like:

```
WARNING: A terminally deprecated method in sun.misc.Unsafe has been called
WARNING: sun.misc.Unsafe::staticFieldOffset has been called by app.cash.paparazzi.ReflectionsKt
```

`Unsafe`'s memory-access methods are terminally deprecated (JEP 471) and will be disallowed by default in upcoming JDK releases, at which point Paparazzi would break outright.

## What changed

**`paparazzi`**: `setStaticValue` used `Unsafe` because plain reflection cannot write static final fields. A new `FinalFieldStripper` registers an ASM `ClassFileTransformer` through the existing self-attached agent that strips `ACC_FINAL` from static fields of `android.os.Build` and its nested classes as they are loaded (modifiers can only change at load time — the JVM rejects it during retransformation). It is registered at the top of `PaparazziSdk.setup()`, before the method interceptors cause any android classes to load. `setStaticValue` is now a plain `Field.set`, and the deprecated-for-removal `AccessController.doPrivileged` goes away with it. If a targeted class loads before setup (e.g. a test-class field initializer touching `Build`), the write fails with an error naming the cause.

**`paparazzi-gradle-plugin`**: instead of replacing the static final `SimpleHtmlWriter.VALID_HTML_TAGS`, mutate the set in place — `addAll` directly, falling back to the backing set of the `Collections.unmodifiableSet` wrapper Gradle 9.x uses. The Gradle daemon always runs with `--add-opens=java.base/java.util=ALL-UNNAMED` (see Gradle's `JpmsConfiguration`), so the reach-in is permitted. The plugin's copy of `Reflections.kt` is deleted.

## Testing

- New `FinalFieldStripperTest` verifies final is stripped at load and static fields (including nested classes) can be set via plain reflection
- `:paparazzi:test` passes — `PaparazziTest`/render-extension tests exercise `configureBuildProperties()` and `forcePlatformSdkVersion()` end-to-end through real rendering
- `PaparazziPluginTest.snapshotReport` (TestKit) passes — HTML report with `img`/`details`/`summary` tags generates in a real daemon

author: supevo
body:
Zwei Finanz-/Admin-Korrekturen.

## 1. SEPA-Export je Rechnungssteller
Der SEPA-Lastschrift-Export nutzte den **Standard-Gläubiger** der Org für **alle** offenen SEPA-Rechnungen. In Mehr-Firmen-Setups würden Kunden einer anderen Firma unter der falschen Gläubiger-ID/IBAN eingezogen (Korrektheits-/Rechtsproblem).

- Route `/api/billing/sepa?entity=<id>` (ohne Angabe: Standard-Firma): lädt die Gläubigerdaten **dieser** Firma und zieht nur deren Rechnungen (`billing_entity_id`). Die Standard-Firma zieht zusätzlich Rechnungen ohne zugeordnete Firma (Altbestand).
- `BillingPanel` bietet je Rechnungssteller einen eigenen SEPA-Download.

Kontext: Zuweisung, Rechnungserstellung (Absender + Nummernkreis je Firma), PDF und Buchhaltung waren bereits korrekt firmen-scoped – nur der SEPA-Export war es nicht.

## 2. Fix: Kunden-Purge scheiterte an xp_events
Beim endgültigen Löschen von „hedin": `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "xp_events_user_kind_idx"`.

Ursache: `xp_events.task_id` war `ON DELETE SET NULL`. Beim Löschen der Aufgaben eines Kunden wurden die XP-Events auf `task_id = NULL` gesetzt; zwei gleichartige Events (`kind`) eines Nutzers kollidieren dann mit dem partiellen Unique-Index `(user_id, kind) WHERE task_id IS NULL`. „hedin" hatte ≥2 solcher Events pro Nutzer.

Fix (**Migration 0139**): `task_id ON DELETE CASCADE` – ein aufgabenbezogenes XP-Event wird mit seiner Aufgabe gelöscht statt genullt.

## Test
- `tsc --noEmit`, `next build` grün.

## Nach dem Merge in Supabase
Migration `0139` ausführen (behebt den Purge-Fehler).

body:
## What changed

- prevent node merges that would introduce a repeated interior vertex in an area
- preserve valid merges of adjacent or consecutive area nodes
- keep repeated interior nodes supported for linear ways

## Why

Merging nonadjacent nodes belonging to the same area replaced both nodes with the survivor without checking the resulting area geometry. This could produce a closed way containing the survivor multiple times internally and allow invalid geometry to be uploaded without a warning.

The connect action now simulates replacements for affected parent areas and disables the merge with the existing `paths_intersect` reason when it introduces or increases a repeated interior node.

Closes #9328.

## Validation

- `npm test` (2,266 passed; 9 skipped; 6 todo)
- focused action suite (564 passed)
- `git diff --check`

author: teddmab
body:
## Summary

This PR brings two sets of fixes into main from `feature/sf-07-agro-advisory`.

### 1. Wire all admin pages to real Firestore data

- **AdminOpportunities** — replaced hardcoded mock array with real `getProductsAdmin` CF; shows live funding progress bars
- **AdminReports** — replaced fake static files with 5 real CSV export buttons (transactions, investments, farmers, financing, users)
- **AdminAlerts** — fixed `overdueFinancing` query using `status == "overdue"` (not a valid status — always returned 0); now counts `active` financing apps
- **AdminUsers UserDrawer** — fixed investment/transaction queries that fetched global top-20 then filtered client-side (silently empty); now uses `where("investorId","==",user.id)` and `where("userId","==",user.id)`
- **AdminFarmers STATUS_LABEL** — added `rejected → "Rejeté"` so rejected farmers don't show raw text in status pill
- **adminService.disburseTranche** — replaced invalid `getDocs(where("__name__","==",id))` with `getDoc()`
- **LoginScreen** — removed hardcoded credentials from default state and hint text

### 2. Fix 401 UNAUTHENTICATED on all httpsCallable (critical)

**Bug:** `AuthContext.tsx` had `if (user) return` guarding the `onAuthStateChanged` registration. If a demo session existed in `localStorage`, the Firebase auth listener was never registered. The user appeared logged in to the React UI, but `firebase/functions` had no real token → every `httpsCallable` returned 401 UNAUTHENTICATED.

**Fix:** `onAuthStateChanged` is now always registered on mount. When a real Firebase user is detected, the demo session is cleared and real credentials are used.

Also added `teddmabulay@gmail.com` to the frontend admin-email allowlist.

## ⚠️ Action required after deploy

1. **Clear `localStorage`** on the admin domain: DevTools → Application → Local Storage → delete `mombongo_admin_demo_session`, then log in again with your real Firebase credentials.
2. **Verify your Firestore `users` doc** has `role: "admin"` — the CF checks this after the auth token passes. Set it in Firebase Console if needed.

## Composite indexes needed (AdminUsers drawer)

- `investments`: `(investorId ASC, investedAt DESC)`
- `transactions`: `(userId ASC, createdAt DESC)`

Firestore will surface a direct link to create each index the first time those queries run.

author: strongt1me
body:
## Das Problem

Beim Programmstart stand rund eine Sekunde lang das **Standardsymbol von Tk** in der Taskleiste — die blaue Feder — bevor das richtige Symbol erschien.

Die Ursache ist die Reihenfolge im Start:

```python
root = tk.Tk()                    # Windows legt den Taskleisteneintrag an
root.attributes("-alpha", 0.0)    # macht das Fenster unsichtbar
app = PS5ConverterGUI(root)       # erst hier wird das Symbol gesetzt
```

Der Taskleisteneintrag entsteht schon mit `tk.Tk()`. Das Symbol wurde aber erst in `PS5ConverterGUI.__init__` gesetzt — also nach dem Laden von Hintergrundbildern, Cover und allen Bedienelementen.

Das `-alpha 0.0` half nicht dagegen: Es macht das **Fenster** durchsichtig, nicht den **Taskleisteneintrag** weg.

## Die Änderung

`_fenstersymbol_sofort_setzen()` läuft jetzt unmittelbar nach `tk.Tk()`, mit nur `root.title()` dazwischen. Drei Quellen der Reihe nach, damit auch ein unvollständiger Programmordner nie auf die Feder zurückfällt:

1. `app_icon.ico` neben dem Programm bzw. im entpackten Bundle — greift im Normalfall, mit allen sechs Auflösungen von 16 bis 256 px
2. das im Quelltext eingebettete `.ico`
3. das eingebettete 32×32-PNG über `iconphoto`

**Warum Stufe 3 ein PNG bleibt und keine `.ico` wird:** Das ist der Weg für Linux und macOS. Dort nimmt `iconbitmap()` gar keine `.ico` an, sondern braucht ein PhotoImage. Eine `.ico` daraus zu machen würde diesen Weg kaputtmachen.

## Was ein Prüfer wissen sollte

**Gemessen, welcher Weg greift:** Unter Windows im Skriptbetrieb Stufe 1 — die Debug-Protokollierung bleibt leer, also war kein Rückfall nötig. `wm_iconbitmap()` taugt dafür übrigens nicht als Kontrolle: Es gibt unter Windows auch dann einen leeren String zurück, wenn das Symbol gesetzt wurde.

**Drei Nebenbefunde, alle unauffällig:**

- Die Symbole in den gebauten EXE-Dateien (v1.8.38, v1.8.50, v1.8.51) sind korrekt und zeigen alle dasselbe, aktuelle Motiv.
- `_APP_ICON_ICO_B64` ist **byte-identisch** mit `app_icon.ico` — die eingebettete Rückfallebene ist also nicht veraltet.
- In der Taskleiste war nichts angeheftet; das alte Symbol erschien wirklich nur während des Starts, nicht dauerhaft.

## Tests

Sechs neue Prüfungen in `test_kleine_fixes.py` (34 gesamt grün):

- die Funktion existiert und setzt an einem echten Tk-Fenster wirklich ein Symbol
- der Aufruf steht **vor** dem Aufbau der Oberfläche
- zwischen `tk.Tk()` und dem Aufruf steht nur `root.title()` — alles Weitere verlängerte die Zeitspanne wieder
- die drei Quellen stehen in der richtigen Reihenfolge
- das eingebettete `.ico` gleicht der Datei — laufen sie auseinander, zeigt das Programm je nach Weg ein anderes Symbol

Dazu Release-Suite (`GO`).

Die Testdatei selbst liegt nicht im Repository — `.gitignore` hält den Testbestand lokal.

author: suorcd
body:
## What

Fixes a memory leak in the reconnect/endpoint-recycle path that OOM-kills low-RAM nodes within hours of every restart.

## Why (root cause)

The `iroh 0.97 → 1.0` upgrade (`945c3a3`) made `Gossip::shutdown()` hang — its actor awaits `Disconnect` sends to peers before replying. `618b8dd` then time-capped shutdown at 10s and *discarded the result*, abandoning the old gossip actor (and its receive buffers/connections) on every reconnect. Combined with a fire-and-forget endpoint close and a stale receive task that never exits, each reset leaks memory; under pressure the thrash slows shutdown further, the timeout fires more, and the leak accelerates until the kernel OOM-kills the process.

## Changes (all in `podping-gossipwatcher/src/main.rs`)

1. **`old_ep.close()` is now awaited** (was a detached `tokio::spawn` with a 5s timeout) so its QUIC state is actually freed. It's closed *before* the gossip shutdown, so the actor's `Disconnect` sends fail fast instead of hanging.
2. **`old_gossip.shutdown()` is awaited with a 30s cap** (was 10s + discarded result). On timeout it logs a warning instead of silently dropping; the handle is still replaced below, so the actor terminates once all handles are gone.
3. **Stale receive-task generation check moved to the top of the loop** (was skipped by `continue` on the 30s-timeout path), so an old task exits promptly instead of lingering forever holding the old `GossipReceiver`.

## Evidence

- `fa.ser.ink`: `memory allocation of 671088640 bytes failed` (640 MiB) immediately after `[ARCHIVE] Stored (new)`.
- `gw01`/`gw02`/`cur3direct02`: silent OOM-kill during the same archive store.
- `chrony00`: RSS climbed through repeated `Triggering endpoint reset` lines — the recycle leaked rather than freed.

## Verification

- Compiles: `cargo check` clean.
- **Not yet verified at runtime under memory pressure** — that needs deploying to a node or a `MemoryMax=`-capped container and confirming RSS drops after an endpoint reset.

## Tracking

Fixes #3.

- `ser.ink/gossip-ops` issue #17 (fleet-level OOM tracking).
- LLM wiki: `concepts/podping-gossipwatcher-oom-regression`.

author: casval0093
body:
## Summary

A `search` action whose `revealDestination` is `"hand"` was gated on open **Character** slots. With a
full Character area the engine refused every Character its own prompt had just reported as legal.

Opened as a **draft** per `CONTRIBUTING.md` ("Open an issue or draft PR for behavior changes with
broad impact") — happy to split, reshape, or reduce it to an issue if you'd prefer.

## The bug

`effectSearchSelection` in `packages/engine/src/effects/resolution.ts` rejects a selection when

```js
selectedIds.filter((id) => cardType(id) === "character").length > openCharacterSlots
```

and it applied that test to **every** search, regardless of `revealDestination`. Adding a card to
hand doesn't consume board space, so with 0 open slots the check rejects any Character selection.

**The two halves of the feature disagree.** Prompt creation in `effects/actions.ts` folds
`openCharacterSlots` into `destinationCapacity` *only* when `revealDestination === "character"`:

```js
const destinationCapacity =
  action.revealDestination === "character"
    ? playableEligibleIds.filter(/* stages */).length + openCharacterSlots
    : playableEligibleIds.length;
```

Resolution applied it unconditionally. So the prompt marks a card `enabled: true` **and** lists it in
`resolutionContext.eligibleIds`, and then resolution rejects that exact card with
`"Prompt resolution could not be applied."`

Filters are not involved — `eligibleIds` is correct throughout, and the rejected card is in it.

## Evidence — `OP12-086` Koala

`revealDestination: "hand"`, `remainderPosition: "trash"`. Four bodies down, Koala takes the fifth
slot, `[On Play]` looks at 3:

```
prompt options : Karasu enabled:true | Nico Robin enabled:true | Koala enabled:false
eligibleIds    : [Karasu, Nico Robin]
characterArea  : [c26, c27, c28, c29, c21]      <- full, 0 open slots
resolvePrompt  : selectedIds: [NicoRobin]       <- enabled:true, and in eligibleIds
result         : accepted: false, "Prompt resolution could not be applied."
```

## Scope

**171 of the 185 card definitions with a `search` action reveal to hand.** This fires whenever such
a search would add a Character to hand while the board is full — ordinary mid-game, and invisible to
the current tests because every existing search test starts from an empty board.

## The fix

Gate the slot test on the destination, mirroring `actions.ts`. The `playableEligibleIds` membership
check on the preceding line still constrains a hand reveal, so nothing is loosened for
`revealDestination === "character"`.

## Tests

Adds `packages/engine/tests/cards/OP12/086-koala.test.ts`. Fails without the fix
(`MoveFailedError: Move resolvePrompt failed`), passes with it.

Placed under `tests/cards/**` deliberately, because that is what `vite.config.ts` `test.include`
covers. Koala's existing test at `src/cards/OP12/characters/086-koala.test.ts` is **not** executed —
see the note below.

## Validation

- `pnpm run ci:one-piece:check` — **10/10 tasks successful** across all 5 packages
- `vp check` on both changed files — formatted, no lint or type errors, no new `any`/`unknown`
- engine suite **2631 → 2632** passing (confirmed by removing the new file and re-counting)

## Separate observation: per-card tests under `src/cards/` don't run

Filed separately as #217, with numbers measured on pristine `main`.

Short version: `vite.config.ts` `test.include` covers `tests/cards/**` but not `src/cards/**`, so
**1972** per-card test files never execute — including Koala's own `src/cards` test, which is exactly
why a full Character area was never exercised against a hand reveal. That is why the test in this PR
is a new file under `tests/cards/OP12/` rather than an addition to the existing one.

author: bashfulbits
body:
## The actual root cause, finally visible

PR #1259's error-logging fix paid off immediately — the next \`coordinator_error\` carried the real exception:

\`\`\`
TypeError: The receiving Durable Object does not support RPC, because its class was not declared
with \`extends DurableObject\`. In order to enable RPC, make sure your class extends the special
class \`DurableObject\`, which can be imported from the module "cloudflare:workers".
\`\`\`

\`index.js\`'s \`getCoordinator()\` calls \`env.LLM_SCHEDULER.getByName("global-v2")\` — the named-Durable-Object RPC binding style, which Cloudflare requires the class itself to support by extending the runtime's \`DurableObject\` base class. \`LLMSchedulerDO\` never did this, from Phase 1's very first deploy.

This is the actual explanation for the entire day: the DO's own RPC-transport trace reports \`outcome: "ok"\` for every one of these calls — the exception fires processing the response on the *calling* Worker's side, not inside the DO. **PR #1256 (RoutingStorage/\`cas_capable\` payload fix), #1257 (stale-backlog reconcile fix), and #1258 (\`dispatch_v2_url\` wiring fix) were all real, independently-necessary fixes** — but none of them could matter until a request actually reached a working RPC call, and none of them ever did, because this was broken underneath all of them the entire time.

It was invisible until now because this repo's test suite calls \`new LLMSchedulerDO(...)\` directly and calls its methods directly too — bypassing the real binding/RPC layer entirely. A local repro against the exact deployed source with realistic data "succeeded" for the exact same reason (see my earlier comment on the incident thread).

## Fix

Import \`DurableObject\` from \`\"cloudflare:workers\"\` and extend it, calling \`super(ctx, env)\` first. That module only exists under the real Workers runtime, so the import is dynamic with a plain-class fallback for this repo's Node-based test suite (\`node --test\`, using \`node:sqlite\`) — the fallback is never reached in production.

## Testing

- New regression test in \`coordinator.test.js\` asserting \`LLMSchedulerDO\`'s prototype chain extends something other than plain \`Object\`. Verified it fails with the exact symptom when the \`extends\` clause is reverted.
- Can't exercise the real \`\"cloudflare:workers\"\` \`DurableObject\` class under plain Node — this guards against a future accidental regression to the same failure mode, not the platform requirement itself.
- \`npm test\` — 25 passed (24 existing + 1 new).
- \`wrangler deploy --dry-run\` — clean, confirms the dynamic \`cloudflare:workers\` import bundles fine for the real runtime.

## After this merges

This should be the one that actually lands real dispatch traffic on \`citypods-llm-dispatch-v2\`'s DO. Worth re-running chapter-agenda/chapter-locator once deployed to confirm \`enqueue-batch\` finally returns \`200\`s.

body:
🟡 **Live preview: [pr-16265.preview.langfuse.com](https://pr-16265.preview.langfuse.com)** ## What does this PR do? Points the two Langfuse services in `docker-compose.yml` at `docker.langfuse.com`, a pull-through alias for Docker Hub, so self-host image pulls can be attributed: - `langfuse-worker`: `docker.io/langfuse/langfuse-worker:4` → `docker.langfuse.com/langfuse/langfuse-worker:4` - `langfuse-web`: `docker.io/langfuse/langfuse:4` → `docker.langfuse.com/langfuse/langfuse:4` This matches the equivalent change already made to `charts/langfuse/values.yaml` in `langfuse-k8s`. The Terraform modules (`-aws`, `-gcp`, `-azure`) install the chart via `helm_release` without overriding `image.repository`, so they inherit it with no change needed. Blob requests through the alias redirect to Docker Hub's CDN, so bandwidth and the public pull counter stay with Docker Hub — the README's "Docker Pulls" badge keeps working unchanged. ## Type of change - [x] Chore (tooling, dependencies, CI, workflows, repo upkeep, or other maintenance work) ## Mandatory Tasks - [x] Make sure you have self-reviewed the code. ## Notes for reviewers **Third-party images deliberately stay put.** The proxy is a generic Hub pass-through, so `clickhouse/clickhouse-server` and `redis` would also resolve through it — but routing other vendors' images through our vanity host adds a failure point for zero benefit. ClickHouse, Postgres, Redis and MinIO are unchanged. **Escape hatch is documented in the file.** Self-hosters whose registry allowlists are scoped to `*.docker.io`, who run pull-through mirrors, or whose `docker login` credentials are keyed on `index.docker.io` would otherwise hit a confusing failure. The header comment names the alias and points back to `docker.io/langfuse/...`. `docker login docker.langfuse.com` does work — the auth challenge advertises `realm="https://auth.docker.io/token"` — but existing logins don't carry over. **One follow-up in other repos, not fixed here.** `langfuse-js/.github/workflows/ci.yml:81` and `langfuse-python/.github/workflows/ci.yml:161` both `curl` this file by SHA and don't pin images in their compose overrides, so their CI runs will start pulling through the alias and count our own traffic as self-host pulls. That needs either a `sed` back to `docker.io` in those two workflows or confirmation that Actions egress is filtered out. Also unchanged and worth noting: `pipeline.yml` still publishes every image to `ghcr.io/langfuse/*`, and those pulls are never attributed. The `snyk-web.yml` / `snyk-worker.yml` scans stay on Docker Hub on purpose — they're our own security CI, not user pulls. ## Verification - `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml config` parses; rendered output confirms only the two Langfuse images moved. - Manifest digests through the alias match Docker Hub exactly at tag `:4` — `sha256:a68afa29…` (web) and `sha256:f431ca2b…` (worker). - `docker manifest inspect` resolves both through the new host using Docker's own auth flow. - Real `docker pull docker.langfuse.com/langfuse/langfuse-worker:4` succeeded in 23s with a matching digest, exercising the full blob path rather than just the manifest handshake. - `pnpm run format:check` clean; `pnpm run lint` → `Tasks: 7 successful, 7 total`.

Greptile Summary

 The PR redirects the default Langfuse web and worker images in Docker Compose through `docker.langfuse.com`, a Docker Hub pull-through alias, and documents how restricted environments can restore the original registry. - Changes only the two first-party Langfuse image references. - Leaves all third-party service images unchanged. - Adds an inline compatibility note for registry-restricted installations.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 The PR appears safe to merge because the registry migration is narrowly scoped and its known compatibility constraint is explicitly documented with a fallback. The two changed image references preserve their repositories and tags, while existing source-building automation does not depend on pulling them and self-hosters with registry restrictions receive clear replacement guidance.

### [`v3.53.1`](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v3531---2026-08-18)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/compare/v3.53.0...v3.53.1)

##### 🚀 Features

- **Remote Taskfiles are now generally available!** This has been an
  experimental feature for 3 years, but is now enabled by default. Massive
  thanks to all those that contributed and gave feedback (too many to list
  here). We've also given the
  [Remote Taskfiles documentation](https://taskfile.dev/docs/remote-taskfiles) a
  bit of a polish ([#​1317](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/1317), [#​2906](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2906) by [@​pd93](https://redirect.github.com/pd93)).
- Added a per-command `timeout` that terminates a command once it exceeds the
  given duration (Go duration syntax). It covers shell commands, task calls,
  deferred commands, `deps` and the `if` condition, obeys `ignore_error`, and
  reports exit code `124`. Callers that join a `run: once` or `when_changed`
  task already running now honor their own `timeout`, and inherit that task's
  failure instead of being told it succeeded ([#​1569](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/1569), [#​2898](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2898) by [@​vmaerten](https://redirect.github.com/vmaerten)).
- Considerably improve performance of fingerprinting on large repositories
  (monorepos). Fingerprinting is up to 86% faster and make up to 70% fewer
  memory allocations on the more advanced scenarios. Benchmarks were added as
  well. We're basically skipping work when not needed. ([#​2853](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2853), [#​2883](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2883) by
  [@​Napolitain](https://redirect.github.com/Napolitain), [#​2884](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2884) by [@​Napolitain](https://redirect.github.com/Napolitain)).
- Further improved fingerprinting performance on large repositories: hashing
  source files now reuses a single buffer, reducing memory allocations by \~98%
  and wall-clock time by \~7% ([#​2925](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2925) by [@​vmaerten](https://redirect.github.com/vmaerten)).
- `includes.excludes` can now exclude a whole namespace: append `:*` to the
  namespace name, e.g. `excludes: ['debug:*']`. Bare entries still match a
  single task name exactly ([#​2300](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2300), [#​2959](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2959) by [@​xmxxc](https://redirect.github.com/xmxxc)).
- Added support for `enum.ref` in `--interactive` prompts. Required vars using
  `enum.ref` now show the selection list like static enums, instead of falling
  back to free-form input ([#​2817](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2817) by [@​vmaerten](https://redirect.github.com/vmaerten)).
- Added Nushell completions, available via `task --completion nu`. They complete
  task names and aliases, every flag with its description, and the values of
  `--completion`, `--output` and `--sort` ([#​2966](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2966) by [@​vmaerten](https://redirect.github.com/vmaerten)).
- Added a verbose log line for failed tasks. In `--verbose` mode, a task whose
  command exits non-zero now reports `task: "<name>" failed: <error>` instead of
  stopping without a trace ([#​2240](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2240) by [@​Drino](https://redirect.github.com/Drino)).

##### 🐛 Fixes

- Fixed a pinned `checksum:` not being verified when a remote Taskfile came from
  the cache ([#​2980](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2980) by [@​vmaerten](https://redirect.github.com/vmaerten)).
- Fixed the fingerprint variable (`{{.CHECKSUM}}`/`{{.TIMESTAMP}}`) ignoring a
  `method:` set at the Taskfile level: the variable now follows the same method
  resolution as the up-to-date check. Only the variable matching the effective
  method is injected, so a task inheriting a Taskfile-level `method: timestamp`
  gets `{{.TIMESTAMP}}` and no longer a `{{.CHECKSUM}}` (which now renders as an
  empty string), and neither variable is injected when the effective method is
  `none` ([#​2924](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2924) by [@​vmaerten](https://redirect.github.com/vmaerten)).
- Fixed `ref:` in `for: matrix:` and `enum:` only accepting literal lists. Refs
  computed with template functions like `keys` or `splitList` no longer fail
  with "must resolve to a list" ([#​2544](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2544), [#​2956](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2956) by [@​no-hup](https://redirect.github.com/no-hup)).
- Fixed pressing `Esc` at an interactive variable prompt not cancelling the run
  ([#​2942](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2942) by [@​anilnatha](https://redirect.github.com/anilnatha)).
- Fixed `joinUrl` collapsing the `//` in a URL scheme (e.g. producing

- Fixed the JSON schema rejecting `ignore_error` on a command inside a `for`

  by [@​gokeefe-atb](https://redirect.github.com/gokeefe-atb)).
- Fixed the JSON schema rejecting more keys the Taskfile parser accepts:

  inside a `for` loop ([#​2967](https://redirect.github.com/go-task/task/issues/2967) by [@​vmaerten](https://redirect.github.com/vmaerten)).

- Updated taskfile versions doc to mention when version checks were introduced

author: thibautmelen
body:
## Defect

On the nine-key engine, a file written for 0.108.0 (every file that exists outside this repo today) is refused on its first retired key with `unknown field `workflow` in the workflow envelope` followed by the set listing. Only `config:` had a teaching. The set listing says what is valid NOW and nothing about the past; the Damerau-Levenshtein guess treats a key that shipped last week exactly like `zzz:`.

Measured 2026-08-18 with the two binaries side by side: the shipped 0.108.0 passes 0/40 of main's pack examples and main refuses 40/40 of 0.108.0's. This refusal is the FIRST line every existing file meets on 0.109.0, and it taught nothing.

## Mechanism

`retired_key_teaching` gains its two scopes, symmetric and sealed:

- **envelope arm** · `workflow` · `description` · `types` · `policy` · `assert` (beside the existing `config`)
- **task arm** · `on_finally` · `output` · `declassify` · `inert` · `max_parallel` · `fail_fast` (outside `for_each:`)

Each teaching is the engine's own words, never guessed: the identity moved onto `nika: <id>` and the prose becomes a `#` comment (nika-migrate's own note); cleanup is a task on an unwind edge (`after: {parent: unwind}` · graph_format 3); `output` is `extract`; `declassify`/`inert` are `lift`; the two knobs live inside `for_each:`; a shape rides `schema:` or `returns:`; `permits:` + `secrets:` survived `policy:`; obligations are proven by `nika trace verify`. An envelope arm never fires in a task and a task arm never fires in the envelope (`output` is a plausible name in both; one scope retired it).

The arms and their tests descend into `parser/retired.rs` (ADR-023 · mod.rs sat 15 lines under the 1,500 wall with them inline · the lift.rs / for_each.rs precedent) · mod.rs 1485 → 1329.

## Evidence

- 3 tests RED first (each key asserts its destination word and the absence of `did you mean`), then GREEN · nika-schema lib 209/209 · clippy `-D warnings` clean
- no snapshot or golden pinned the generic text (grep over crates/ · tests/)
- no spec code minted · the error stays the unknown-field one, only the suggestion clause leads with the migration (the SPEC's tombstone registry is the spec's to declare)

## Deliberately unchanged

`depends_on` (already typed · W2) · `fail_workflow` inside `on_error:` (already refused typed) · `vars`/`env` (their own NIKA-VALUES tombstones) · the task set stays silent for genuinely unknown keys.

Rides 0.109.0 · the release whose first contact with every existing file is exactly this refusal.

author: cygenix
body:
## What

Each file row in **Connections → Azure Blob Source** gains two copy actions, and backup files gain a shortcut into the Restore database tab.

## Copy: two values, full URL primary

- **⧉ Copy URL** — `https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/<container>/<encoded path>`. Primary, because it's what the Restore tab and the Azure tooling want, and the one nobody retypes from memory.
- **⧉ Path** — the unencoded path inside the container (`AdventureWorks2025 (2).bak`, `Staging/KY/foo.bak`), for azcopy and for reading.

Encoding splits on `/`, runs `encodeURIComponent` per segment and rejoins — spaces become `%20`, virtual-directory slashes survive. `encodeURI` is not usable here: it leaves `?` and `#` intact, and a filename containing either would truncate the URL at the query or fragment boundary, handing back a link to the wrong blob or to none.

**Neither copied value carries the SAS token.** The Restore tab expects a bare URL with the credential held server-side, and a SAS on the clipboard is a live credential that leaks into tickets, chat and screen shares. The azcopy button stays the single exception — it authenticates with nothing else — and its Clipboard-API-plus-textarea fallback is now shared with the new buttons, so all three behave identically on insecure origins. Confirmation is a transient `✓ Copied` on the clicked button itself.

## Use in restore →

Offered on `.bak` / `.trn` / `.dif` rows. Switches to the Restore database tab, selects the **Azure Blob URL** radio, fills `#rst-path` with the encoded URL, and calls `rstModeChanged()` so the SAS-credential helper appears.

**Prefill only** — Inspect reads the backup header and Run restore writes to the server; both stay the user's decision. A test asserts the function body never mentions `rstInspect`/`rstValidate`/`rstRun`, and the smoke confirms Inspect didn't fire and Run stayed disabled.

Deliberately **not** gated on the 100MB proxy cap that Download honours: nothing transfers through us here — SQL Server pulls the blob itself — so this is the only route that works for the multi-GB `.bak` files the tab exists for.

## Pre-existing bug fixed

`encodeURIComponent` doesn't escape apostrophes, and these values sit inside single-quoted JS strings in an `onclick` attribute. One file named `it's.bak` broke **every** button on its row — Import and Download included. One `.replace(/'/g, '%27')` fixes all of them.

## Tests

- 90 assertions in `blob-upload.test.js`: encoding against `?`, `#`, `+` and spaces; no-SAS; nested paths; backup detection; prefill-only; the apostrophe fix.
- Headless smoke **39/39** on the real UI — including a 5GB `.bak` (restore + copy offered, download correctly not) and a nested path with an apostrophe.
- Full suite: **1556 assertions, 0 failures**.

Frontend only — no Azure Function change, so this is a Netlify-only deploy.

author: sharon-fdm
body:
**Related issue:** Resolves https://github.com/fleetdm/fleet/issues/50720

## Problem

When Fleet server pushes a fleetd upgrade built without `--osquery-flagfile`, the packager writes an empty `osquery.flags` into the payload, which the installer extracts over the existing file on disk, silently wiping the admin's custom flags.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Admin
    participant Host as macOS host

    Admin->>Host: Install fleetd.pkg with custom osquery flags
    Note over Host: ✅ /opt/orbit/osquery.flags has flags, extensions load

    Admin->>Host: Fleet pushes fleetd upgrade (no --osquery-flagfile)
    Note over Host: ❌ osquery.flags overwritten with empty file, extensions gone
```

## Fix

Skip writing `osquery.flags` entirely when no flagfile is supplied, so the existing file on disk is preserved. Mirrors the guard `writeMacOSSecret` already uses for the same problem. Safe because Orbit handles a missing `osquery.flags` gracefully.

# Checklist for submitter

- [x] Changes file added for user-visible changes in `orbit/changes/`.
- [x] Input data is properly validated, `SELECT *` is avoided, SQL injection is prevented (using placeholders for values in statements), JS inline code is prevented especially for url redirects, and untrusted data interpolated into shell scripts/commands is validated against shell metacharacters.
- [x] Timeouts are implemented and retries are limited to avoid infinite loops

## Testing

- [x] Added/updated automated tests
- [ ] QA'd all new/changed functionality manually

## fleetd/orbit/Fleet Desktop

- [x] Verified compatibility with the latest released version of Fleet (see [Must rule](https://github.com/fleetdm/fleet/blob/main/docs/Contributing/workflows/fleetd-development-and-release-strategy.md))
- [x] If the change applies to only one platform, confirmed that `runtime.GOOS` is used as needed to isolate changes
- [ ] Verified that fleetd runs on macOS, Linux and Windows
- [ ] Verified auto-update works from the released version of component to the new version (see [tools/tuf/test](../tools/tuf/test/README.md))

Ticket: VTO-277

## Qué y por qué
Faltaba la posibilidad de que el administrador ordene el historial de combustibles por fecha de carga o de creación. Se incluyeron los query params `sortBy` y `sortDir` en `findAll` y `findAllByChofer` para soportar la ordenación visual solicitada en el listado de cargas de combustible. Se resolvió usando un `orderBy` dinámico en Prisma, lo que delega a la base de datos la estabilización de la paginación (mediante el uso de un tiebreaker por `id` descendente luego del criterio de fecha).

## Qué puede romper
El cambio está encapsulado en métodos read-only (listados). No debería romper nada.

author: mrpollo
body:
## Summary

Installs `Tools/setup/optional-requirements.txt` into the `px4-dev` container image so CI jobs stop fetching those packages from PyPI on every run.

## Problem

`Tools/setup/Dockerfile` copies `requirements.txt` and runs `ubuntu.sh`, which installs only that file. `optional-requirements.txt` sits in the same directory and is inside the build context, but was never copied or installed, so nothing in the image provides `pyelftools`.

That left `itcm_check.yml` running `pip3 install -r Tools/setup/optional-requirements.txt` on every job, reaching out to PyPI each time. Over the last 30 days, PyPI 502s from `files.pythonhosted.org` killed 29 CI runs across 5 workflows, 6 of them in the ITCM check. On Aug 15 and Aug 18 that was roughly 60% of all CI failures for the day. None of it was covered by a declared incident on status.python.org, so there was no upstream signal to wait on.

Baking it in also drops `symforce` from the ITCM job, which never needed it. `Tools/itcm_check.py` imports only `elftools`; `symforce` is used exclusively by the derivation scripts under `src/lib/wind_estimator/`, `src/modules/vision_target_estimator/`, and `src/modules/fw_att_control/`, none of which run in CI.

## Solution

Copy `optional-requirements.txt` into the image and pip install it after `ubuntu.sh`.

`symforce` publishes no Linux aarch64 wheel and no sdist, in any version ever released, so installing the file unguarded fails hard on the `linux/arm64` leg of the container matrix. It is gated behind a PEP 508 environment marker so aarch64 installs `pyelftools` only, while x86_64 and macOS keep the current behaviour.

`optional-requirements.txt` is now a container build input, so it is added to the `pull_request` paths filter in `dev_container.yml`.

Draft because it can't do anything on its own. It needs a new `px4-dev` tag cut, then a follow-up bumping the pins (currently `v1.17.0-rc2` across eight workflow files, with `sitl_tests.yml` and `fuzzing.yml` still on older `px4io/px4-dev` v1.16 tags) and deleting `itcm_check.yml:69`. If that step survives the bump, pip still reaches PyPI for the `symforce` line every run.

Verified the dependency resolution on both target architectures in clean `python:3.12-slim` containers: `linux/amd64` resolves `pyelftools` plus `symforce` and its 14 transitive deps; `linux/arm64` resolves `pyelftools` alone and exits 0, where the unmarked requirement fails with `No matching distribution found for symforce>=0.9.0`. The container workflow on this PR then built both arches green.

Two things worth a reviewer's eye.

Image growth, measured against `v1.17.0-rc2` rather than estimated. amd64 goes from 6.12GB to 6.37GB on disk (+253MB, +4.1%) and the registry pull goes from 2.01GB to roughly 2.13GB (+120MB compressed, ~+6%), across 4524 added files: `scipy`, `ruff`, `skymarshal`, `symforce-sym`, `sympy`, and a pip-installed `clang-format`. Every px4-dev-based job pays that pull. arm64 is unaffected beyond `pyelftools` itself, since the marker skips symforce there, so its 1.72GB pull is essentially unchanged.

The pip `clang-format` (21.1.2) may shadow the apt one from `ubuntu.sh:139`. `check_format` uses astyle so it should be inert, but it is a new binary on PATH.

author: trencho
body:
**One missing import explains the broken display.** The Vuetify 2 → 4 migration (`c449ac8`) never added `import 'vuetify/styles'`, so the app has been running on per-component CSS only since 2026-07-29. `vite-plugin-vuetify`'s `autoImport` does not cover it — the plugin registers a styles plugin only when its `styles` option is set.

Measured on **production** before the fix:

| Probe | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `--v-theme-overlay-multiplier` | **undefined** | `1` |
| `body` margin | **8px** (UA default) | `0px` |
| `.text-center` → `text-align` | **start** (no-op) | `center` |

Each maps to a defect I reproduced in a browser:

1. **Nav labels unreadable on hover.** Every hover rule is `opacity: calc(var(--v-hover-opacity) * var(--v-theme-overlay-multiplier))`. With the variable undefined the declaration is invalid at computed-value time, so `opacity` falls back to its initial `1` — and `.v-btn__overlay` is `currentColor`, i.e. white over white text. The active tab had the same problem permanently.
2. **A white strip down the left edge.** No reset meant `body` kept the UA's 8px margin, insetting the app while the fixed app bar and drawer sat at true `left: 0`.
3. **Layouts silently not applying.** Every utility class resolved to nothing, which is why "About me" rendered with its heading hard left and an empty column beside the text.

Also **pins `defaultTheme: 'dark'`**. Vuetify defaults to `'system'`, and this app's own stylesheet hard-codes white text on dark backgrounds — so a light-mode visitor got white text on Vuetify's light surfaces. The design has always been dark.

**Verified in a real browser** against `yarn mock-api` + `yarn dev:mock`: hover now legible, left strip gone, About section centred, hero and map unaffected. `yarn test` 303/303, `yarn lint` clean, `yarn build` green.

author: matheusviuge
jollyhrothgar
body:
An earlier commit had `bootstrap` clear `.env` and `analytics/.env` as soon as `op whoami` succeeded. That's the wrong signal twice over: a 1Password session is per-shell and short-lived, so signing in from one terminal deletes the fallback for every other one — and `whoami` says nothing about whether the `op://` references actually resolve.

It fired for real within minutes of shipping. A sync run in one shell deleted both files; another shell still had `op` locked, so `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` became unavailable with no fallback left.

Bootstrap now reports that the file is redundant and prints how to remove or restore it. Deleting somebody's only working credential isn't a thing to do on a weak signal.

Restore with: `op inject -i .env.tpl -o .env`

author: aroviqen
body:
Resolves #64.

Follow-up to #46 and the PR #63 review rounds, which exposed a structural
source of security-contract drift: collection, representation
normalization, provenance checks, and D.1a admission all lived in one
module, and the same contract was restated across the collector, the
schema, the independent validator, the static source validator, the
tests, and the documentation. A test could exercise one layer without
proving that its accepted representation crosses the declared evidence
boundary.

This is behaviour-preserving. Admission results are unchanged: 20822
pinned decisions over the reviewed fixture and systematic mutations
produce identical output before and after the refactor.

## Layer boundaries

`scripts/ci-cloud/collect-workload-evidence.py` keeps its path, CLI, and
artifact shape. It must stay one self-contained file because the runner
streams it to the target over `python3 -I -` on standard input, so it may
not import repository modules at target runtime. It now holds three
documented layers: the workload contract, representation normalization,
and side-effecting collection.

Every D.1a admission decision moved to the new
`scripts/ci-cloud/workload-admission.py`. It runs on the controller only,
binds the contract surface the collector declares in
`WORKLOAD_CONTRACT_EXPORTS`, and refuses to load when the two
declarations differ by name, order, or presence. No D.1a invariant name
remains in the streamed file, so a target can never grade itself.
`assemble-evidence.py` and `validate-evidence.py` consume the new module;
the evidence artifact is unchanged.

## One named home per contract

The canonical systemd unit-name rule was a nested predicate inside
`user_work_facts` restating `$defs/canonicalSystemdUnitName` — the exact
concept that broke in #63. It is now the named
`canonical_systemd_unit_name`, tied to the schema definition by an
agreement test over a corpus of accepted and rejected names.

The Quadlet unit file-name pattern was inline in `unitFact.name`. It is
now `$defs/quadletUnitFileName`, shared with the post-cleanup
`owned_units`, which previously used the generic `stringArray`. Passing
runs are unaffected because `owned_units` is empty there; a leftover the
installer could never have written now fails at the schema instead of
being described as a merely failed cleanup.

## Cross-layer proofs

`tests/ci-cloud-workload-layers.py` replays reviewed representations
through the collection layer, requires them to reproduce the reviewed
evidence exactly, and then carries them through assembly, the JSON
Schema, the independent validator, and admission:

- Podman 5.4 container inspect payloads for all ten roles;
- transient Podman health timer and service units, including the
  `podman healthcheck run` provenance probe for each timer;
- collector-admitted canonical systemd unit and job names;
- installed Quadlet units, generated services, the process census, and
  the resource inventory.

Negative coverage proves malformed, absent, duplicate, over-limit, and
provenance-free facts fail closed at the earliest boundary and stay
rejected by independent revalidation, and that health timers and process
census entries cannot be admitted from names alone.

Two boundaries that cannot become separate files are enforced rather
than documented: the functions declared in
`REPRESENTATION_NORMALIZATION_EXPORTS` are proven unable to reach a
command, the filesystem, or the clock through any callee, and admission
is proven to decide under an audit hook that rejects process, file, and
socket access. The streamed collector is additionally executed from
standard input in an empty working directory to prove it is
self-contained.

## Static checks

The static trust-boundary assertions in `scripts/validate-ci-cloud.py`
now point at the layer that owns each rule, plus a new rule for the layer
boundary itself. Five validator mutation tests in
`tests/ci-cloud-contract.py` prove that rule actually fires, so the
static checks cannot silently diverge from executable behaviour.

## Validation

- `./scripts/preflight.sh` passes, including `git diff --check`, REUSE
  lint, prettier, markdownlint, and every test suite.
- `tests/ci-cloud-workload-layers.py`: 22 tests.
- `tests/ci-cloud-contract.py`: 208 tests.
- The real CLI pipeline `assemble-evidence.py` into
  `validate-evidence.py --require-passed` produces a passing result and
  summary from the reviewed observations.

No production, provider, credential/IAM, workflow-dispatch, target
runtime, or Phase D.2 behaviour is changed. A cloud run is not required
for a behaviour-preserving refactor.

author: abhiaiyer91
body:
## Summary

Fourth slice of the factory fast-session-starts split (after #21795, #21796, #21798, #21800). This one covers the rules engine and run dispatch — no sandbox/perf code.

**Review feedback loop**
- Submitted PR reviews and PR comments now reach the rules engine on both the polling and webhook paths (they were previously dropped), waking the agent that authored the pull request.
- Feedback follows the linked Review card's `parentWorkItemId` back to the authoring work item instead of looping on the PR's own card.
- Factory verdict lines ("Verdict: request changes") are matched exactly — negated text like "do not request changes" no longer triggers a wake.
- `pull_request.opened` is ingested so a new PR mints its Review card; a push during Reviewing triggers a re-review.
- Reporters are credited as co-authors on work their issue caused (real GitHub accounts only).

**Run dispatch reliability**
- Autonomy arming is now atomic with whatever grants it: deferred-decision approval, board-drag transition commit, and run prep all arm inside the same storage transaction, so a revision conflict can't leave an item spuriously armed (or approved-but-unarmed).
- The dispatcher confirms a kickoff signal actually landed in the thread and observes the run's end reason — kickoffs queued onto an ending run are retried instead of reported as success.
- Aborted runs are retried like interrupted work (bounded by the attempt cap) instead of failing terminally.
- Same-stage reentry no longer runs `onExit`; entering Building auto-starts the implementation run; parked proposals are dismissed/superseded when their item reaches a terminal stage or the run starts anyway.
- Kickoff skill resolution moved off the sandbox so board actions don't block on provisioning.

## Scope
`src/rules/*`, work-items routes + storage, github/linear rules, `skills/service.ts`, review/rereview skill docs, 19 scoped changesets. The remaining slice (lazy sandbox materialization, base checkpoints, factory-ui session UX) follows as PR 5.

## Test plan
- factory typecheck clean
- 362 tests passing across rules, work-items routes/storage, and github rules suites

This PR helps Factory respond to pull request activity and recover from failed runs. It also keeps approvals, reviews, work items, proposals, and cleanup actions in the correct state.

## Summary

- Ingest newly opened pull requests and follow linked Review cards to their authoring work items.
- Match review verdict lines exactly and prevent Factory-authored comments from causing self-wakeup loops.
- Trigger a fresh review when a pull request receives new commits during Reviewing.

- Start implementation automatically when a work item enters Building.

- Verify kickoff delivery and retry signals dropped while runs end.
- Retry aborted runs within the existing attempt limit.
- Avoid `onExit` rules during same-stage reentry.
- Dismiss parked proposals when work reaches a terminal stage or starts running.
- Revoke stale bindings and clean up terminal work items, proposals, and sandboxes.
- Wire terminal-stage cleanup into production transition-service composition.
