## 概要

チャット・AIアシスタント・ワークフロー・RAG/GraphRAG・Deep Research・OpenCode/OMo の LLM 接続先を、llama.cpp の個別ポートから ControlDeck ゲートウェイ（`/api/v1/llm/v1`）1本へ集約する。あわせて、転送先の既定解決を「起動中優先」に変え、起動失敗の再試行ループを読み込み中と区別して表示する。

### 背景

8091 が稼働中でも、OpenCode がゲートウェイへ投げたリクエストの model 解決が「登録順の先頭」に落ちて 8090 を追加起動し、VRAM 91% / swap 2.4GB まで逼迫して双方が不安定になっていた（実測で SIGKILL に至った）。接続先がクライアントごとに違うため、モデル解決も受け入れ制御もばらついていたのが根本。

## 変更点

### 接続先の集約
- `/workflows/llm-endpoints` はゲートウェイを selected で返し、llama.cpp 系の個別エンドポイントはそこへ集約する。モデル管理の一覧には出さない（モデルを保有するのは llama.cpp 側）ため `list_providers(include_gateway=...)` で用途を分ける
- 内部の生成は自分の HTTP へ戻らず、`runtime_provider.resolve_target()` で実エンドポイント + 実 alias へ解決してから叩く。ホップを増やさずに thinking 解決・キャンセル・KV 受け入れ制御・Deep Research の ctx 拡張をそのまま効かせる

### 転送先の解決
- 未指定 / `auto` / 未登録名のときは**起動中の LLM を優先**し、いなければ登録順の先頭。停止中の別モデルを起こして GPU へ二重ロードするのを避ける（明示指定時は従来どおりそのモデルを起動）
- 仮想モデル `auto` を追加。クライアント側でモデルを固定せずに済む。OpenCode 導入時の自動設定の既定も `auto`
- OMo の並列数同期も同じ解決規則で転送先 instance を引く

### 起動失敗の可視化
- systemd の `sub_state=auto-restart`（起動失敗の再試行待ち）を `STARTING` のまま扱っていたため、モデル読込中と区別が付かず UI が延々と「起動中…（読み込み待ち）」を出していた。`FAILED` へ落とし、失敗時だけログ末尾を `last_error` に添える
- `/models/llama/capacity` が失敗中のモデルを `failed` として返し、ホームの LLM 利用状況が理由付きで表示する
- `_revive_endpoint_for_opencode()` が未定義の `base_url` を参照していた（例外を握って復活しない状態）ので解決済み port から組み立てるよう修正。ゲートウェイ経由の設定では復活処理自体をスキップする（リクエスト時にオンデマンド起動されるため）

## 検証

- backend 578件成功（新規9件）、frontend production build 成功
- 実機: ゲートウェイ経由で `model:"auto"` が起動中のモデルへ解決されること、3本同時投入で 3本とも正常応答すること、停止中の別モデルを起こさないことを確認

author: bennetleff
body:
Board sha256 `26981fea2dbc425f…` unchanged throughout. Gate goes from **7 violations to 1** on PROPERTY 1 / BLOCKING PROPERTY 3 — the remainder is `input` (PR #1360).

## All 6 are the same defect as `input`

Every one is **affirmatively declared HV** in `elec/domain_manifest.yaml` (lines 285, 306, 313, 335, 345, 359) yet absent from **both** enforced surfaces → resolved to `Default`: 0.2 mm clearance, **zero creepage**.

`DISCHARGE_CTRL` (the SELV declaration at line 457) is **not** in this family and was never flagged — the three manifest states are distinguishable and were checked per net.

Topology re-traced from `elec/src/modules.ato` and the board pad→net map, not the manifest summary:

| net | pads | circuit | reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `r_dis1a-p2` | R6.2+R7.1 | half-bus-1 bleed mid-node, `:1378-1381` | ~+85 V wrt PWR_RTN |
| `r_dis2a-p2` | R8.2+R9.1 | half-bus-2 bleed mid-node, `:1384-1387` | ~−85 V wrt PWR_RTN |
| `r_snub1-p2` | C7.1+R14.2 | K2 NC-COM RC snubber, `:1392-1394` | DC-blocked, both ends HV |
| `r_snub2-p2` | C8.1+R15.2 | K3 NC-COM RC snubber, `:1395-1397` | DC-blocked, both ends HV |
| `k_dis1-no` | K2.3 | relay NO contact | bonded to COM = PWR_RTN |
| `k_dis2-no` | K3.3 | relay NO contact | bonded to COM = DC_BUS_RTN |

**Correction to the manifest's own reasoning:** it defends the NO contacts as merely "the same physical contact bank." That understates it. `modules.ato:1388-1389` records the coils are held **energized** in normal operation, holding each pole *on* its NO contact — so NO is **galvanically bonded to COM the entire time the unit runs.** These are live HV pads whenever the product is powered, not mechanically-adjacent unconnected ones.

## Class: `HighVoltageSignal`

Matching their own directly-connected siblings `k_dis1-nc` / `k_dis2-nc`.

**The `GateDriveHV` trap was checked explicitly**: `HighVoltageSignal` is the A-side of a real generated rule ("HighVoltageSignal to LV", RULE 4d) carrying 2.0 mm clearance **and 12.6 mm creepage**. `GateDriveHV` by contrast has `creepage: None`. Nothing was reclassified to escape a clearance it owes.

## Measured delta — 3 runs per variant, sets intersected

**379 → 395 errors.** The rise is the point.

- **−18 creepage, every one a same-domain HV↔HV false positive.** Includes K2.3↔K2.4 and K3.3↔K3.4 (adjacent pads of one relay contact block) and **R14.1↔R14.2, R15.1↔R15.2 — the two pads of a single 2512 resistor, unsatisfiable at any placement** (the analogue of `input`'s 0.6700 mm SOIC pads). Byte-identical across two independent 3-run intersections.
- **+17 creepage against genuinely LV/SELV nets** — `+3V3`, `gnd`, `safety-line/-1/-2`, `RTD_SDI/SDO`, `V_BUS_SENSE`, `OCP2_VREF_2V5`, `rtd_force_n`, `rtd_pan.r_high_top-inp`, `safety.coil_thermal-*`. Real reinforced-barrier exposure, previously invisible.

## New finding for the board owner

**+15 `track_width` violations, all on `discharge.r_snub1-p2`** — the only one of the six with routed copper, carried at **0.2 mm on In3.Cu against the 0.5 mm floor, on a net that swings to the full half-bus.**

That is a genuine undersized-trace exposure, not an artifact. Fixing it means moving copper. **A weaker class was deliberately not chosen to make it disappear.**

## Pre-existing, confirmed not from this change

Verified by content-diffing `origin/main` and running against a pristine worktree: the oracle differential (already red from `hb-gnd` alone — **not** re-pinned, registry still 171/171), 6 `test_tank_creepage` failures, 3 `check_net_classification` violations, the `sync_kicad_netclass_assignments` protected-net refusal on `PWR_RTN`/`CGND` (which is why only these 6 were hand-edited), and `ci_check_drc`'s four categories — byte-identical on main.

Affected categories sit far under ceiling: creepage 105 ≤ 272, track_width 15 ≤ 393.

author: thevillanelle
body:
## What changed

Stacked on #3 (which is stacked on #2) — needs both merged first.

- **`matching.ts`** — added `findBestMatch` for on-demand single-candidate discovery, refactored the hard-constraint logic (blocked pairs, dating compatibility, domain soft-block) into shared helpers used by both the new on-demand path and the existing batch `runMatching`.
- **`actions/discover.ts`** — `findMatch(vertical)`: builds a real candidate pool (active enrollments, excluding blocked pairs and anyone already matched with this user in the vertical — a permanent re-match exclusion for now, not yet a time-based cooldown), creates a real `matches` + `game_sessions` row.
- **`actions/match.ts`** — match detail (partner shown only safe fields: first name, avatar, bio, vibe — no location/age/last name), This or That answer submission, external-game self-report, play-again signaling (creates a `connections` row once both sides opt in), and `getLiveSession` (only returns the realtime token once both players have mutually signaled play-again).
- **`(app)/discover`**, **`(app)/play/[matchId]`**, **`(app)/live/[matchId]`** — the actual pages/components for the above.
- **This or That** (`lib/this-or-that.ts`) — the one native mini-game built end to end this pass, both async (self-paced, compare after) and live (real-time synced) modes. The other three native games (Wavelength, Hot Take, Story Chain) aren't built yet — if the matching engine suggests one of them, the match page substitutes This or That rather than dead-ending, with a note explaining the swap.
- **`005_realtime_token.sql`** — `game_sessions.realtime_token`, an unguessable per-session UUID used as the live Realtime broadcast channel name. Same constraint as the RLS work in #2: the browser Realtime client only has the anon key, no Supabase-issued JWT, so there's no `auth.uid()`-based way to restrict channel subscribers. The token itself is the access control — a capability handed only to the two participants by `getLiveSession`, never exposed in any list/public query.

## How it works

Discover is on-demand (ask for a match right now), not a scheduled batch drop — matches the "Field Day matches you..." framing already on the landing page. Live is gated behind mutual play-again, matching the landing page's own "if you both want a second round, we unlock a live session" copy — so this PR also includes the minimal play-again-signal plumbing needed to make that gate real, even though the full field notes thread is still Phase 3.

## Known limitations (flagging, not hiding)

- Live session progress isn't persisted anywhere — a page refresh mid-round loses your place. No reconnect/replay logic. Acceptable for this pass since it's an ephemeral real-time experience, not a system of record.
- Re-match exclusion is permanent (never re-suggest someone you've matched before in this vertical), not a time-based cooldown — simplest correct thing for now.
- `games` table still isn't seeded; game metadata comes from `GAMES_SEED` in code, same as the matching engine already did.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` — clean, no type errors
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean (including two real React hook rule violations in the live component, fixed: a ref mutated during render, and synchronous setState inside an effect body — both moved into event-handler-triggered code instead)
- [x] `005_realtime_token.sql` applied, security advisors checked — same expected posture, no new issues
- [ ] Manual: two accounts, both join Dating (or Friends), both hit Discover, confirm they match each other and land on the same match
- [ ] Manual: play This or That async as both players, confirm completion states and the play-again unlock flow
- [ ] Manual: both play-again → both open `/live/[matchId]` → confirm real-time sync (answers appear live, match tally updates)
- [ ] Manual: confirm a match page for a native-but-unbuilt suggested game (e.g. force `suggested_game: "wavelength"`) shows the This or That substitution message instead of a dead end

author: trillymatt
body:
## The bug

The build and deploy both succeeded, every stage in the Railway dashboard was green, and every request still returned **"Application failed to respond."** Nothing was listening in the container.

Next's generated `server.js` binds to:

```js
const hostname = process.env.HOSTNAME || '0.0.0.0'
```

Container runtimes — Docker, and therefore Railway — set `HOSTNAME` to the container's ID. So the server tried to bind to a name DNS has never heard of and died during startup:

```
⨯ Failed to start server
Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND a3f9c2b1d4e5
```

This never reproduces locally, where `HOSTNAME` is typically unset and the `0.0.0.0` fallback applies. That's exactly why the deploy looked healthy: the failure only exists inside a container.

## The fix

`npm start` now runs [`scripts/start.mjs`](scripts/start.mjs), which forces `HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0` before launching the server and leaves `HOST` as a deliberate override for binding somewhere specific.

Written as a Node script rather than an inline env assignment in the npm script so it behaves identically on Windows, and so the explanation lives next to the workaround — this is the kind of line that gets "tidied up" and silently breaks production again. The README says so too.

### Verification

| | `node .next/standalone/server.js` | `npm start` (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| `HOSTNAME` unset | ✅ binds `0.0.0.0` | ✅ binds `0.0.0.0` |
| `HOSTNAME=<container id>` | ❌ `ENOTFOUND`, crashes | ✅ binds `0.0.0.0` |

Reproduced the crash, applied the fix, then confirmed with a production-only install (`NODE_ENV=production npm ci`, matching Railway) and a container-style `HOSTNAME`: server reports `Network: http://0.0.0.0:<port>`, and `/api/health`, all pages, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, and static assets all return 200.

## Also included

The earlier commit on this branch: the missing-domain build log was printing five multi-line `WARNING` blocks, which reads like a failure in a deploy log when it's the expected state before a domain is attached. It's now one informational line, emitted from `robots.ts` (generated once) rather than at module scope in `site-url.ts` (imported by every static-generation worker). It disappears entirely once a domain exists.

The README's environment section was also rewritten — the previous wording implied `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` had to be set. It doesn't: Railway injects `RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN` as soon as a domain is generated, and the site derives its URLs and indexing from that on its own.

`npm run lint` and `tsc --noEmit` both clean.

body:
[#309](https://github.com/LinzeColin/KMOS/pull/309) 的索引只覆盖 `tools`。实测四个大目录全列的代价：

| 目录 | 条目 | 成本 |
|---|---|---|
| `KMFA/tools` | 854 | ≈ 16,546 tokens |
| `KMFA/tests` | 470 | ≈ 9,041 tokens |
| **`KMFA/metadata/quality`** | **953** | **≈ 28,371 tokens** ← 比 tools 还贵 |
| `KMFA/stage_artifacts` | 567 | ≈ 10,412 tokens |
| **合计** | | **≈ 64,370 tokens** |

**索引 3,092 tokens 覆盖全部四个 —— 省 95%。**

## 两类目录区别对待

- `tools` / `tests`：逐个列出**活跃**文件（168 + 120 个），冻结的只给规模和「别看」的理由
- `metadata/quality`、`stage_artifacts`：**不枚举** —— 枚举它们等于把省下的 token 还回去。只给规模、用途、样例和检索方式

## 为什么这些文件一个都不动（本次核实，不是推测）

1. `KMFA/tests` 里的测试**真的 import 那些脚本**：`from KMFA.tools.check_v013_s00_app_entry import ...` —— 移动断 import

```python
_require(summary.get("full_suite_test_count", 0) >= 1502, "full suite inventory shrank", errors)
```

当前 **1,515**，删掉 43 个 v013 测试 → **1,472 < 1,502** → **正在跑的 v014 总复审直接红**。余量只剩 13 个测试。

**那 40.9 万行是被机器守卫锁住的，不是没人清理。** 测试删不得，脚本被测试 import 也删不得。所以一个文件不动，只让 agent 不必列目录。

- `--check` **PASS**；**负控**：`touch` 一个新测试后立即 FAIL
- `check_dual_plane_ci --require-projects` **PASS**
- `check_kit_drift` **PASS**｜kit 第 1 代
- 零文件移动、零删除

body:
## Summary

OpenCode `POST /session` rejects `{ modelID }`. This maps the selected model to `{ providerID, id }` so a new workspace session starts.

Opening a file or a per-turn diff now adds a tab in the center pane. **Chat** stays first and stays open. The **Files** inspector is a nested explorer with name search (Cmd+F / Ctrl+F) and include/exclude globs.

The tree route stays paths-only (`{ paths, query }`). File text is a separate `GET /code/workspaces/{id}/blob` that Monaco 0.56.0 (`@monaco-editor/react` 4.7.0) reads. Third-party notices are regenerated.

## Also in this change

- The new-workspace repo picker stays enabled when you already have a repo.
- You can search the model list.
- The composer stays at the bottom. Reasoning effort sits next to the model.
- Image attach is in the composer; images stay local until a harness declares `image_input`.
- Package-cache warmup runs after bind so startup is shorter.

## Test plan

- [ ] Create an OpenCode workspace session. It should not 400 on `POST /session`.
- [ ] Open a file from **Files**. It should open as a center tab in Monaco.
- [ ] Open a turn diff. It should open as a center tab.

author: cryptobal
body: ## Objetivo Que quien llega a ternio.cl sepa en un segundo si entra como comprador o como proveedor; que el proveedor pueda entrar con correo y contraseña; y que un mismo teléfono con cotizaciones y perfil de proveedor deje de mandar a la persona al lugar equivocado. ## Qué cambia - Cabecera: `Entrar` → `/entrar`, `Soy proveedor` → `/proveedores` (sin «Ya coticé»). - `/entrar` pregunta primero la puerta; el lado proveedor tiene pestañas correo/contraseña y código SMS. - Destino post-login por **capacidades** (`tieneCotizaciones` × `tienePerfilProveedor`), no por el escalar `rol`. Pantalla `/elegir` cuando hay ambas. - Credentials Auth.js `proveedor` (correo + contraseña, rate limit, rechaza `ADMIN` / `SUSPENDIDO` / `RECHAZADO`). - Alta de proveedor: campo contraseña; si el teléfono ya es de un comprador, **reutiliza** el `User`, eleva `rol` a `PROVEEDOR` y no vuelve a pedir OTP si ya estaba verificado. Pack de arranque sigue idempotente (`alta:{proveedorId}`). - Enlaces cruzados entre `/panel` y `/mis-cotizaciones`; aviso/formulario para crear contraseña en el panel. - `requerirProveedor` exige perfil `Proveedor` (no solo rol) y responde 404 sin perfil / `RECHAZADO`. ## Antifraude (riesgo §19) Antes no existía validación «proveedor compra lead de su propio RUT». Se agregó en `puedeTomarLead` / listado del panel / `tomarLeadAction`, con tests. Sin eso no se habría eliminado el bloqueo comprador→proveedor. ## Validación ``` pnpm typecheck ✅ pnpm lint ✅ pnpm test ✅ (274 passed) pnpm build ✅ ``` ## Pendiente / riesgos - No hay `DATABASE_URL` de producción en este entorno: no se pudo contar correos duplicados entre proveedores ni `User PROVEEDOR` sin fila `Proveedor` antes del deploy. - Prueba manual de alta comprador→proveedor + ledger (pack una sola vez) queda para el dueño con datos reales. - Recuperación de contraseña por correo queda fuera (V1: SMS).

author: alvarodiez20
body:
Titanic is in the README, the docs quick start and the linked example report, and it has no datetime column and no numeric pair correlating above 0.5. So the datetime card, its four temporal panels, and both populated correlation views never appeared in the one example anybody looks at — three of four card kinds, one of three correlation views.

`docs/assets/bike_sharing.csv` replaces it: two calendar years of hourly bike rentals from UCI, 17,379 rows, vendored so no CI job fetches anything.

## Acceptance

- [x] The example report renders all four card kinds — 7 numeric, 2 categorical, 2 boolean, 1 datetime
- [x] It renders a populated correlation view — `temp` ↔ `feels_like` at r = 0.99
- [x] The quick-start dataset still loads instantly — 0.16 s to profile
- [x] No CI job depends on a network fetch — vendored, and the build script is never run by CI

Plus all four temporal panels, which is what two years buys.

## Two years rather than one, deliberately

The renderer drops the year panel inside a single year — one bar reading "all of it" — so a trimmed dataset would quietly lose a panel this dataset was chosen to demonstrate.

That is what costs the size. The floor for two years of hourly rows is ~1,150 KB even at minute precision with two-decimal floats, so the large-file hook goes from 500 KB to 1500 KB **for this one file**, with the reasoning written beside it. The guard exists to catch a large file added by *accident*; this is not one.

## Two changes to the source, both recorded

`scripts/build_demo_dataset.py` is the reproducible record, and `bike_sharing.NOTICE` carries the citation the source asks for.

- the date and hour columns are recombined into one timestamp — without this every value is midnight and the hour-of-day panel is a single bar. This is the change that makes the dataset worth vendoring at all.
- `season` and `weathersit` are decoded from small integers to labels, because a bar chart of `1, 2, 3, 4` is a chart of nothing.

Nothing is sampled, filtered or reordered: all 17,379 observations, in source order.

## What stays

**Titanic remains the fixture for `tests/test_report_layout.py`.** Its byte and height ratchets are pinned to it, and repinning them would throw away their history for no gain. `docs/examples.md` also keeps it, legitimately — it is a page of several example datasets and Titanic is a good one for missing values.

The generated example becomes `example_report.html` rather than `titanic_report.html`: a dataset-neutral name, so the next swap does not break the link again. The old published URL is superseded; README and docs are updated in this PR.

## How the [0,1] bug was found

The first screenshot of this report showed `temp`, `feels_like` and `humidity` at **100% missing** — that is #349, merged separately, and this PR sits on top of it. The current screenshot reads `0.0% missing, 12 of 12 columns are complete`.

`tests/test_demo_dataset.py` asserts the four acceptance lines rather than trusting them, plus the four properties the dataset was picked for: two calendar years, all 24 hours present, the strong pair still strong, both booleans two-valued. A documentation fixture that quietly stops demonstrating the thing it was chosen for is the failure worth guarding against.

Full suite green: 3,334 passed, 0 failed.

author: radodge
body:
Implements `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-decoupled-finalize-design.md` (spec and implementation plan are the first two commits).

## What changed

- **flac_writer reserves a 4 KiB trailing PADDING block** at encode time, and the new `flac_writer_embed_tags()` writes vorbis tags in place via the metadata chain API. Previously, embedding ~200 bytes of duration tags forced libFLAC to rewrite the entire RF file (~10-20 min on a full-tape capture, via a `.metadata_edit` temp). Applies to both the GUI and `misrc_capture`. Legacy unpadded files still fall back to the full rewrite, now with a WARN in the capture log.
- **All per-recording state moved into `gui_record_session_t`** (writers, files, paths, session log, spill/write-error state, byte accumulators, stat snapshots). Stop hands the session to the finalize thread and immediately frees the module for a new capture. Buffer-stat counters snapshot at stop; byte totals accumulate per-session, so a new recording can no longer corrupt a finalizing session's summary.
- **A new capture can be configured and started while the previous one finalizes.** Start is refused only while the previous session's writer threads still drain the shared record ring buffers (design addendum: `BUF_RECORD_A/B` and the reference-video encoder are single instances, so two consumers would corrupt both recordings — the `drained` flag gates exactly that window), or when output paths collide with the finalizing session's files.
- **Closing the app can no longer truncate a finalize** (root cause of the 2026-08-18 interrupted capture): `gui_record_cleanup()` — which joins the finalize thread but previously had no caller — is wired into `main()` teardown, and a window-close during an in-flight finalize holds the app open with a status message until it completes.
- **CI guard harness extended**: padding presence, in-place embed (no tempfile), tag round-trip, legacy-fallback reporting. Also realigned the vendored-hsdaoh guard with the probing `meson.build` from the Fedora merge — it had been failing on every run since that merge (pre-existing; unrelated to this change).

## Verification

- `ci_guard_tests.py`: 25/25 PASS (includes the extended FLAC runtime harness).
- `meson compile -C build-fedora misrc_gui misrc_capture misrc_extract`: clean.
- GUI launch smoke-tested after each refactor stage.
- **Outstanding (operator, MISRC hardware attached):** short capture → stop → immediately start a second capture (expect instant start, no refusal once drained); close the app during a finalize (expect it holds open briefly, file comes out fully tagged); `metaflac --list` on a new capture shows STREAMINFO, VORBIS_COMMENT (5 duration tags), SEEKTABLE, PADDING (~3.9 KB remaining) and no `.metadata_edit` leftover.

author: beingkk
body:
## What this change does

This pull request reorganizes the app around one task and one lifecycle, and adds a named grouping above tasks.

Before this change, a project is one research question, and its six pages sit flat in the top navigation. After this change:

- You start work by choosing a capability, then typing a question.
- Inside a task, navigation follows a fixed lifecycle: **Plan · Results · Sources · Share · History**. A stage that can't work yet is locked rather than empty.
- Tasks can belong to a project, and a project page lists its tasks.

The change closes gaps G1 through G15 in the contract. It also includes a hand-driven UX pass (17–18 August) that landed on top of the contracted build.

Task: `docs/tasks/032-task-lifecycle-ia/` · ADR: `docs/adr/0031-portfolio-layer-above-the-project.md` · UX pass: `docs/tasks/032-task-lifecycle-ia/live-polish-2026-08-18.md`

### Terminology

The screen words and the code words differ on purpose:

| Screen word | Code word | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Task | `project` table row | One research question with its own plan, run, and report. Nothing is re-parented. |
| Project | `portfolio` table row (new) | A named group of related tasks. It holds no plan, run, or evidence. |

## Contracted scope (G1–G15)

- **New task entry.** A capability list, then a question-first page. Only Evidence search runs. The other three capabilities appear greyed out and aren't runnable — this is deliberate product surface, not dead UI.
- **Lifecycle bar.** Five task-level tabs with per-stage locking, plus redirects from the retired flat routes.
- **Plan document.** The plan opens as a document. Each part can be sent back to the chat with **Change this**.
- **Results.** An answer callout, a metadata strip, a scannable contents list that uses the new `nav_label` field, and a top-sources list.
- **Sources.** One page with four views: Themes, Landscape, All sources, and Findings.
- **History.** Replaces the decision log and starts at the question rather than at plan approval.
- **Tasks list and projects.** A new `portfolio` table, its routes, and a nullable `project.portfolio_id` column.
- **Planning conversations in the chats overlay,** so you can still read an earlier plan lineage.
- **Type scale.** Reading surfaces now sit at the app's own 16px floor, plus one new `text-display` token.

## Hand-driven UX pass (17–18 August)

This pass is roughly half the diff (commit `5fc10cc`, 110 files). It adds no new contract, and it reopens one gate. Full record in `live-polish-2026-08-18.md`.

**Search plan panel.** Saving a field used to post a planner turn, which made the planner rewrite the whole plan and drop fields. Edits now stay in local React state (`planOverlay.ts`) until you press Start.

**New endpoint: `PATCH /api/v1/projects/{id}/plan`.** This is the extra public interface in this pass, and it needs security review. It performs a typed merge of `backend_scope`, question, dates, geography, screening, effort, depth, and check-ins, then re-validates and persists a new approved plan version. It calls no model. Start now patches first, then posts the run. This fixes a real bug: setting Sources to OpenAlex-only still ran against Overton, because `backend_scope` never reached acquire.

**Plan vocabulary.** Wire identifiers are unchanged; the screen words are new: Search scope (Focused / Broad / Broadest), Analysis level, and Thoroughness presets. Caps read as "per database", not "per library". The planner prompt moves to `planner_v8`, with `prompt_hashes.json` updated in step.

**Running card.** The old "Analysing the evidence" side panel is no longer the live run surface. A running card in the planning thread (`RunningCard.tsx`, `runProgress.ts`) shows progress, and finished steps expand.

**Download.** `ArtefactDownload.tsx` produces PDF through `window.print()` using the existing print CSS, and Markdown through a client-side flatten. Word is skipped on purpose, because it would need a new library. Markdown now inserts `[n]` citation markers, which the earlier export omitted.

**Sources layout.** All four Sources tabs share one 1180px column on a white card, with the tab bar spanning the card. Plan, Results, History, and Share stay on the 780px reading measure.

**Chat.** The bottom-left **Open chat** bubble opens your latest follow-up chat, or creates one if none exist. The `+` control creates a new chat. A bug where a created chat had no tab is fixed by seeding the list cache, deriving the tab during render, showing a placeholder tab, and fencing the composer on error.

**Other additions.** A footer on every view with the AI-mistake notice and legal links, updated Terms and Privacy pages, and a sensitive-information banner.

## How this was verified

Evidence: `docs/tasks/032-task-lifecycle-ia/verification.md`.

- **`make verify`:** passes. `EXIT=0`, backend 2160 tests, mypy clean over 266 files, ruff clean, frontend 330 tests over 54 files.
- **End-to-end:** `pnpm exec playwright test` passes 11 tests. This includes a rewritten mock journey (`e2e/journey.spec.ts`) covering plan → run → check-in → report, and `e2e/eye-check.spec.ts`, which asserts that no rendered sentence falls below 16px and that primary buttons render white on blue.

## Risk tier

Tier 3. A new table and new public routes are a hard gate.

## AI role

The agent wrote the contract, rubric, plan, ADR, and all code across 13 phases. The owner approved the contract and the plan (with two reductions), approved all three gates (schema, public interface, and prompt surface), directed the Phase 7 onward gate deviation (code first, tests at the exit), waived adversarial review, and drove the 17–18 August UX pass directly.

## What to review

- **`PATCH /plan`.** A new public write that this slice's original gate approval didn't cover. Check the typed merge, re-validation, and the geography compilation path in `_geography_constraints`, which returns 422 on unknown tokens rather than persisting them.
- **Tenancy on the portfolio routes.** Owner scoping, and equality between unknown-resource and cross-owner 404 responses.
- **The additive-only claim** on `ProjectOut` (`portfolio_id`, `source_count`), `SectionOut.nav_label`, and `PATCH /projects/{id}`. Compare against the OpenAPI diff.
- **The locking and redirect table.** A locked stage must never render an empty page or leak a route.
- **Chat create.** Four mechanisms now cover one race. The polish record proposes keeping the cache seed and the composer fence, then dropping the other two once the seed is trusted.
- **Scope creep and over-abstraction** across a diff of roughly 14,000 lines.

## Reviews run

Findings go in `verification.md`. 

- [ ] Contract verifier
- [ ] `/code-review`
- [ ] `/security-review`
- [ ] `/simplify`
- **Adversarial review: not run.** The owner waived it on 17 August. It was also unavailable as specified, because the Codex CLI isn't on PATH — the same gap as task 031. No non-Claude reviewer read this slice. The tier stays at 3.

## Public safety

- [x] The diff and the evidence contain no secrets, credentials, or real source text.
- [x] Logs, traces, and screenshots are safe to publish.
- [x] No approval-gated change went in unapproved, with one exception stated above: `PATCH /plan` is a new public write added during the UX pass and needs `/security-review`.

author: bredebjorhovd
body:
Follow-up to #500 (gh#499) — a leftover I missed in that removal.

gh#499 deleted the `checkout_prep` module, but `ci.yml` kept its smoke step:

```yaml
- name: bubblewrap checkout-prep smoke
  run: >-
    cargo test -p comet-engine --lib
    checkout_prep::tests::bubblewrap_starts_through_the_production_runner
    -- --exact --nocapture
```

`cargo test --exact` against a filter matching nothing selects zero tests and **exits 0**. So this step has been reporting green while verifying nothing since #500 merged — the worst kind of check, because it looks like coverage.

## What stays

The `bubblewrap` apt package and the `allow bubblewrap user namespaces` AppArmor grant are **kept deliberately**. They look dead alongside the removed sandbox, but the `pinned Codex CLI for push-policy regression` step installs a real Codex and the suite runs under `COMET_REQUIRE_REAL_CODEX=1`; Codex sandboxes through `bwrap` on Linux, and `crates/harness/src/codex/normalize.rs` parses its `bwrap:` failures. Dropping them could turn a real sandbox regression into a confusing harness error.

Only the step that references a deleted symbol goes.

author: rhyssullivan
body:
Elimination so far, all measured in the same requests that took 3-11s wall: `preWorkMs` 0-4ms, `cacheProbeMs` 2-21ms, `timerProbeMs` 1ms, `fetchProbeMs` median 1ms, cpu 18-323ms.

Everything generic is fast. But two app operations are genuinely slow, and both read a response body:

- `http.client GET` to `executor.mintlify.dev` — p50 **3001ms** from the Worker, while the same URL is 0.063-0.196s from a laptop (`x-vercel-cache: HIT`, 179KB) and a probe fetch to cloudflare.com from inside the same request is 1ms.
- `workos.session.jwt_verify` — p50 **2895ms**, whose only I/O is a Cache API hit plus `hit.json()`, while a Cache API *miss* probe is 4ms.

The earlier `fetchProbeMs` never read a body, which is why it looked fast. This times headers and body separately. Gated to `/robots.txt`.

author: hooleeun
body:
### Motivation
- Evitar el segundo desplazamiento que en iOS devolvía la vista a la card anterior tras alcanzar el objetivo, preservando la lógica de cálculo de destino que ya funciona en Android.
- Ocultar el "barrido" visible en móvil al navegar desde notificaciones cambiando solo la presentación del scroll y sin tocar la coordenada final usada en Android.
- Garantizar que la animación de reacción se ejecute solo después de que la tarjeta objetivo quede posicionada y que el scroll manual permanezca siempre libre.

### Description
- Cambié la presentación del desplazamiento: la variable `behavior` ahora usa `desktop && !reducedMotion ? "smooth" : "auto"`, de modo que desktop sigue animado y móvil posiciona instantáneamente usando exactamente la misma coordenada final (`finalScrollTop`).
- Eliminé la segunda corrección iOS (la re-medición y el `scrollBy` exclusivo para `iosWebKit`) y removí el helper de estabilización asociado, de modo que no haya una segunda autoridad que vuelva a modificar el scroll tras el posicionamiento inicial.
- Reemplacé la espera de finalización de animación móvil por un `requestAnimationFrame` mínimo tras el `scrollTo` para asegurar un frame de pintura antes de continuar, manteniendo la comprobación de visibilidad y la posible corrección única ya existente (correctionApplied).
- Mantuve intacto el cálculo de `finalScrollTop`, offsets y selección de target (no se modificó la lógica que determina la card objetivo en Android), y la animación de reacción se activa después del posicionamiento y dura ~2,2s según la lógica previa.
- Archivos modificados: `app/movies/[id]/page.tsx` y `tests/notification-detail-targets.test.mjs` (se actualizaron pruebas para verificar ausencia de la rama iOS, el cambio de `behavior` y el orden posicionamiento→animación).

### Testing
- `npm test` — Ejecutadas 69 pruebas automatizadas; resultado: todas pasadas (69/69). 
- `npm run lint` — Ejecutado (sin errores críticos reportados en el flujo de pruebas aquí).
- `npm run build` — Falló en la fase de `next build` por problemas de entorno al descargar fuentes remotas (Geist / Geist Mono desde Google Fonts), por lo que la compilación completa no terminó por una dependencia externa de red; los cambios de código no introducen errores de compilación reportados localmente.
- Validaciones de código: `git diff --check` y commit local realizados; commit resultante: `Corregir navegación móvil a videos desde notificaciones`.

body:
Primer PR real del repo: `main` solo tenía el commit inicial y todo el proyecto estaba sin versionar. Este PR trae el scaffold completo, con un ejemplo funcional de punta a punta (tipos de cambio del BCE vía frankfurter.dev) modelado en un esquema estrella de Kimball.

## Qué entra

**Ingesta (dlt)** — un pipeline **por recurso** (`frankfurter_rates`, `frankfurter_currencies`), cada uno con su estado y su cursor, para que se programen distinto y fallen por separado. Incremental con `lag` + `range_start="closed"` y merge por clave natural. Troceado adaptativo (AIMD) de la ventana de fechas y circuit breaker sobre la API. Raw se guarda crudo, con los nombres del origen (`naming = direct`).

**Dos cadencias de overlap** sobre el mismo pipeline y cursor: la corrida diaria usa `INGEST_OVERLAP_DAYS` (7d) y la de reconciliación `INGEST_RECONCILE_OVERLAP_DAYS` (365d). Sin la segunda, una corrección que el origen publica dos meses tarde no entra nunca; con el overlap largo en la diaria, se re-piden 365 días todos los días al pedo.

**Transformación (dbt)** — medallón raw → staging → intermediate → marts, con snapshots SCD Type 2. De staging en adelante, modelos y columnas en español.

**Orquestación (Prefect)** — un deployment por *schedule*, no por forma de correr un flow: la carga histórica (`full_refresh=true`) y el backfill (`date_from`/`date_to`) son custom runs desde la UI. Los flows no cortan en el primer error; `finalize_flow` aplica la política grave/leve.

**Infra y calidad** — Docker multi-stage con compose por entorno, GitHub Actions, runner self-hosted, `ruff`/`sqlfluff`/`commitlint`/`gitleaks`, y las reglas de rama `feature/* → dev → main`.

## Una decisión que vale mirar

`/currencies` **no tiene eje temporal**: verificado contra la API el 2026-08-18, ignora `?date=` y devuelve el payload idéntico byte a byte. Por eso su ETL no expone `date_from`/`date_to`/`overlap` y **no tiene reconciliación** — sería el mismo request otra vez. Las monedas que el BCE ya no publica (dracma, tolar, lira turca vieja) se recuperan de las cotizaciones, no del catálogo. Está documentado en `docs/fuentes/frankfurter.md` y fijado con un test.

## Verificación

- 92 tests pasan (unitarios sin base + integración contra Postgres y la API reales).
- `ruff` y `sqlfluff` limpios; los hooks de pre-commit corrieron completos, gitleaks incluido.
- Los 5 deployments registran bien y los cron se activan solo con `ENV=prod`.
- ETL de monedas corrido contra la base real: 30 filas, sin tocar las 265k de cotizaciones.

## Pendiente (no bloquea)

- Seis hallazgos en el bridge de logging, tres con impacto observable: `make ingest` no muestra nada bajo WARNING, `DEBUG=true` no da logs de dlt (hace falta `RUNTIME__LOG_LEVEL`), y el progreso de dlt sale por stdout en vez de la UI de Prefect.
- Decidir si `/app/.dlt` y `/app/logs` llevan volumen en prod (hoy son efímeros) y activar `LOAD__DELETE_COMPLETED_JOBS`.
- Correr `scripts/setup_branch_protection.sh`: todavía no hay rulesets, así que hoy se puede pushear directo a `dev` y `main`.

author: caeldeth
body:
Three cards. Two were on your list; the third was found while writing HTOO-287's scope table.

## HTOO-379 part two — a file collided with its own new name

The editors asked `fs:exists` before a rename and refused a destination that answered yes. **On
Windows that question is answered case-insensitively**, so renaming `abel.xml` to `Abel.xml` was
refused as a collision with itself — the rename a person most often wants, and the one that could
not be done at all. Two callers asked the question, so the rule had two homes and one of them could
drift.

The check now lives in `moveFile`, and identity is decided by `realpath` rather than by whether a
path answers to a name:

- Case-insensitive filesystem — both spellings resolve to the one entry on disk, so a case-only
  rename is a move of a file onto itself, and it proceeds.
- A genuinely different file at the destination resolves to a different real path and is still
  refused, which is what the check existed for.

Both call sites drop their `exists` and take the answer from the move. `moveFile` throws before it
writes anything, so a refused rename still changes nothing on disk.

**The guard this card asked for now exists.** `editorRenameCoverage.test.ts` asserts, per editor,
that it renders a filename field, decides whether the save is a rename, honours it with `moveFile`,
and does **not** pre-check with `exists` on that branch. Scoped to the branch, not the file, because
`exists` is correct elsewhere in both pages — a rule that reads as stricter than it is gets deleted
the first time it is inconvenient. Proved red by planting the call back in.

## HTOO-449 — two archives opened by a name we chose

Found while writing HTOO-287's table. `mapRenderer.ts`:

```ts
const seoBuf = await window.api.readFile(`${key}/seo.dat`)
const iaBuf  = await window.api.readFile(`${key}/ia.dat`)
```

Every other client-file boundary in the repo already asks the directory for the real casing. These
two were missed, and they are the two the isometric renderer cannot start without — so on a
case-sensitive filesystem holding a tree that spells either archive with a capital, **nothing
isometric draws at all**. Windows folds case on lookup, which is why it was invisible here.

`clientFileCaseCoverage.test.ts` walks the source and fails on either shape of a literal join, so
HTOO-287's sweep does not have to be repeated by eye. It does not match a bare `'ia.dat'` in quotes,
which is a lookup key for `archive.get(...)` or the `name` argument to `resolveClientFile`. Also
proved red, and it names the file.

## HTOO-448 — shift-drag to copy

Drag moves; Shift held at release copies, leaving the original where it is. It goes through
`placeCopy`, so a copied NPC still arrives with its name cleared. The shift is read **at release**,
not at the start, because a person can reach for it mid-drag. The cursor shows which will happen. A
shift-drop back onto the starting tile does nothing — that would put a second node on an occupied
tile, and for a warp that is a lost warp.

## Verification

`typecheck`, `lint:check`, `test:coverage` (117 files, **1799 tests**), `build` all pass. 20 new
tests, two of them source-reading guards proved red by planting the fault.

One flake seen on the first coverage run and not on two re-runs: `AssetPackPage.integration`'s
round-trip timed out under full-suite load. Same family as HTOO-157.

## Click-through

Rename a map by changing only its capitals, and check the file on disk changed. Rename one onto a
name another map already has, and check it is refused and nothing moved. Shift-drag a reactor, then
shift-drag an NPC. Open a map and check the isometric view still draws.

author: ajpaulingalls
body:
Close-review Block `ac8ecf84d3eb`: deleting the instruction-time `!` lines left
`_preload_liveness.sh` reachable only through `_preload_base.sh`, which runs only
from `preload_injection.py`. The check that reports a dead hook runtime is now
reached from inside that runtime.

## What this story does, and deliberately does not

It **narrows the claim** and **sweeps the grants**. It builds no replacement
channel. Plan review established that the channel already has an owner —
deferred story-009, whose AC2 is "a harness that silently skips untrusted
hooks… remains detectable by whatever channel survives the preload change" and
whose AC3 forbids liveness machinery on the daily solo path. An earlier draft
put recognition prose in 19 SKILL.md bodies, which contradicted AC3 and the
customer decision that scoped liveness out of the preload work. Dropped by
customer answer, and story-009 is un-deferred as its home.

- **AC1/AC2** — two runtime states split. *Running but not heartbeating* (stale,
  unreadable, teammate borrowing the lead's) still fires the banner and is what
  the fragment now exists for. *Never loaded* is unreachable from a file nothing
  runs; story-009 owns it. Three prose sites rewritten to claim only the first.
- **AC3** — 14 dead grants removed, kept on `xp-end-session` and
  `xp-work-selection` with their runtime uses named in the pin.
- **AC4** — the grant pin is red before the sweep as well as after.

## Notable

- **The obvious pin was vacuous and was refused.** "Runtime dead, so nothing is
  emitted" passes against a do-nothing implementation, a deleted check and a
  correct one alike, because with the runtime dead the preload is never invoked.
  The coupling is pinned instead — one sourcing site, nothing outside the
  resolved preload set sources the base. Plan review named this before it was
  written.
- **The pin caught its own defect on first run.** A substring scan read
  `_preload_markers.sh` as a second caller because that file NAMES the fragment
  in a comment. Keying on a mention rather than the act is story-017's defect one
  layer up; the predicate now requires a `source`/`.` directive.
- **My plan's grant count was wrong and the original concern was right.** I said
  10 dead; it is 14. Six skills declare a bare `Bash`, which subsumes any
  pattern grant — including all four close skills I had argued to keep it on via
  injected shared prose. Legs point opposite ways, so `_needs_the_grant`
  short-circuits on bare Bash first.
- **Two gates were obeyed rather than silenced.** `test_preload_liveness.py`
  crossed the 450 band floor, so the coupling class was extracted on a
  difference in kind rather than taking a recorded ceiling; `hook_liveness.py`'s
  docstring was trimmed four times to keep its rationale-comment headroom rather
  than re-recording the prose ceiling.

Full suite: 10265 passed, 29 skipped. Acceptance: 23 passed.

author: mattmillerai
body:
## ELI-5

`nodes(action="path", from_type="MODEL", to_type="IMAGE")` is how an agent asks "what chain of nodes gets me from a model to an image?". On some comfy-cli versions it answered with nodes that do not accept a MODEL socket at all — a checkpoint loader here, a text-to-image generator there — while the reply looked perfectly well-formed. The canonical `KSampler -> VAEDecode` answer was missing, every step's `from_type` was blank, and asking for a route that does not exist got you an unrelated node instead of "there isn't one". Nothing in the payload said any of that, so an agent had no way to tell a wrong answer from a right one. This PR notices when it is talking to one of those engines and asks the question a different way, which that engine answers correctly.

## Summary

comfy-cli's `nodes path` takes `--exact` (its default) or `--loose`. Both walk the engine's consumers index, which is keyed on socket type — but only since comfy-cli [#695](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-cli/pull/695), released in **1.16.0**. Before that, `--exact` used a different walker (`exact_paths`) that iterated **every** node and admitted any whose *required link inputs* were already satisfied. That is vacuously true of a node with no link inputs at all, so it returned widget-only loaders and generators that never consume `from_type`.

This server's enforced floor is comfy-cli **1.13.0** (`_MIN_COMFY_CLI`), so 1.13.x–1.15.x are inside the supported range and this verb answers wrong on all of them.

The fix: ask in the engine's own default mode, and re-ask in `--loose` **only** when the reply comes back in the pre-1.16.0 contract. The tell is the `mode` key, which comfy-cli added to the `nodes path` payload in the very commit that made `--exact` type-constrained — so the discriminator is the engine's own statement about itself, not a release-number table this repo would have to keep in sync. Everything still goes through `_run_comfy` and the payload is relayed verbatim; no graph is parsed here and no verdict is derived here.

## Changes

- `_nodes_path_sync` issues the default-mode call, and on a payload lacking the post-fix marker re-issues the byte-identical argv plus `--loose`. Up-to-date engines pay exactly one call and behave as they do today.
- `_nodes_path_is_type_constrained(data)` — the one-line contract check, with `_PATH_TYPED_EXACT_MARKER` naming the key it reads. Unreadable shapes (a list, `None`, a scalar) count as the old contract: fail toward the mode that is sound on every supported engine.
- `nodes` tool docstring + README row: the `path` action now states that every step is a real socket link and that no route means no paths, and the README explains the version split and what `--exact` uniquely reports.
- Tests: default-mode-only on a post-fix payload, the `--loose` re-ask on a pre-fix payload (reproduced from comfy-cli's own fixture output), the relayed canonical route, an empty result relayed rather than replaced, and unreadable-payload fallback. The `nodes` docstring token budget goes 500 -> 508, with the reason in the same comment as the previous bump.

## Motivation

Not a passthrough that lost data — a passthrough that faithfully relayed a wrong answer. Every symptom below is reproduced end to end below, so this is a traced root cause rather than a hypothesis.

The originating report's own hypothesis was *"matching on input name `model` / COMBO widget rather than the MODEL socket type."* That turns out to be close but not what happens: the offending node is not matched on `model` at all — it is matched on *requiring nothing*, and its step's `from_type` is blank precisely because there was no consumed type to name. Same observable symptom, different mechanism, and worth stating because the name-matching theory would have pointed the fix at the wrong layer.

## Testing

- [x] Existing tests pass (`pytest`) — 2123 passed, 1 skipped
- [x] Lint passes (`ruff check .`)
- [x] Format check passes (`ruff format --check .`)
- [x] Tested manually — see below

Both engines were built from source and driven through the **real `comfy` binary** against comfy-cli's own `nodes_path_object_info.json` catalog fixture (a real `/object_info` payload, which is what the acceptance asks these be checked against). Pre-fix = comfy-cli at `#695^`; post-fix = comfy-cli `main`.

`comfy --json nodes path MODEL IMAGE --max-depth 4 --max-paths 3` — **pre-fix engine, default mode** (what ships today):

```
payload keys: count, exact, from, max_depth, max_paths, paths, to     <- no `mode`
paths: [ByteDanceImageNode(from_type="")]
       [CheckpointLoaderSimple(from_type=""), ByteDanceImageNode(from_type="")]
       [EmptyLatentImage(from_type=""), ByteDanceImageNode(from_type="")]
```

`ByteDanceImageNode` is one of the three classes the report named, and it takes no MODEL link. Same engine, same query, **`--loose`** (what this PR re-asks with):

```
paths: [KSampler(from_type="MODEL"), VAEDecode(from_type="LATENT")]
       [KSampler(from_type="MODEL"), VAEDecodeTiled(from_type="LATENT")]
```

The routeless direction, `IMAGE MODEL`, on that same pre-fix engine: default mode answers `CheckpointLoaderSimple` (a node that consumes nothing, dressed as a one-step path); `--loose` answers `count: 0, paths: []`.

**Post-fix engine, default mode** — one call, no re-ask, and strictly more than `--loose` gives:

```
payload keys: ..., mode, not_searched, truncated, ...                 <- `mode` present
mode: "exact"   exact: true
paths: [KSampler(MODEL->LATENT), VAEDecode(LATENT->IMAGE)]  support: [VAE from CheckpointLoaderSimple, ...]
       [KSampler(MODEL->LATENT), VAEDecodeTiled(LATENT->IMAGE)]
IMAGE -> MODEL: count 0, exact true   (`exact: true` + empty == a proof no route exists)
```

That last line is why this is a fallback and not an unconditional `--loose` pin: on an up-to-date engine `--exact` is `--loose` **plus** a satisfiability filter, and it is the only mode that reports per-path `support` and can claim `exact: true`. Pinning `--loose` would have stripped both from every current install to fix an engine most of them are not running, and would have re-admitted routes whose steps cannot actually be wired — a milder version of the same complaint.

**Capability check (no dead-end shipped).** This change makes the routeless case return *fewer* rows, so the denial was falsified before shipping rather than asserted: the removed rows were driven through the real binary and are nodes that consume nothing, and the same tool on the same engine still finds real routes where they exist (MODEL -> IMAGE above). No path is closed off; only fabricated ones stop appearing.

## Additional Notes

**Acceptance, criterion by criterion.** Canonical `KSampler -> VAEDecode` present, every step naming the socket type it traversed, `max_depth` honoured (two-hop routes returned at `max_depth=4`), matching on socket type rather than input name or COMBO widget (both surviving modes walk the consumers index, which is built from link inputs only — an enum is not a link), and an unroutable pair reported as no paths: all met and all shown above against a real `object_info`.

**One criterion is met differently than written, and that is a judgment call worth flagging.** The ask was a "regression test pinning the MODEL -> IMAGE case against the bundled catalog." There is no bundled catalog in this repo and there cannot be one: `AGENTS.md` requires tests to mock comfy-cli, and a catalog vendored here would be a second source of truth for the engine's graph — the derive-it-locally breach the architecture rule exists to prevent. The case is instead pinned in three places: the mocked contract tests here (which pin the *decision* — which mode is asked for, given which reply), the gated live `tests/e2e/test_smoke.py` case (which pins the *semantics* against whatever `object_info` the machine has), and the fixture runs above (which pin the *engine* behaviour on both sides of the version split). author: ronaldlokers
body:
Left over from #517. The companies/people view rendered `role="tablist"` with **no tabpanel anywhere** — the tabs announced themselves as controlling something that didn't exist in the accessibility tree.

The issue expected this to require threading props through `CompaniesTab` and `ContactsTab`. **It doesn't** — the panels are siblings of the tablist in `App.tsx`, so the wrapper there carries the role, id and label, and neither component changes.

`PillTabs` now points only the *active* tab at a panel, matching the change TabBar got: both call sites render one panel at a time, so `aria-controls` on the others named ids that exist on no render.

### Two things about the browser coverage

**The role assertion looked like it survived deletion of `role="tabpanel"`.** It hadn't — prettier reindented `App.tsx` after I wrote the mutation string, so the replace silently matched nothing and the test ran against unmodified code. This is the third silent no-op replace to fool me this session; the falsification now asserts the mutation applied before trusting the result. With that, it fails properly.

**The arrow-key test asserts selection, not focus — deliberately.** Measured with the focus move deleted from `tablist-keys.ts`: this view still ends with focus on the newly selected tab, because these tabs are *routes* and the re-render comes from the router.

```
before: network-tab-companies
after:  { id: "network-tab-contacts", sel: "true" }   ← with the focus move REMOVED
```

So a focus assertion here would pass either way. Rather than leave a test that looks like it covers something it can't, it says so and points at `src/components/tablist-keyboard.test.tsx`, where removing that same line does fail.

```
tabpanel-role-removed  exit=1
```

1070 green, e2e 20/20, tsc, build, lint, types, coverage floor.

## 基线（`origin/main` = `a6770d70`，本地 Docker，均**未碰生产**）

    test643-transient-hub-legacy-repair rc=0  PASS
    test671-task-runtime-evidence-hub   rc=0  pass=14 fail=0
        MUTATION_RED: clear-task-lifetime-evidence-on-retry rc=1
        MUTATION_RED: unlink-scheduler-task-id             rc=1
        MUTATION_RED: unlink-rest-task-id                  rc=1
    test688-owner-gated-schedule-hub    rc=0  10 tests / 0 fail / 77 expect

六条都是**真绿**，其中两条共带 **5 条见证红**，所以直接做阻塞门，**不套 known-failure 棘轮**
（给真绿的套件套棘轮，只会让它以后真变红时不红）。

## 🔴 这个 PR 里唯一值得细看的一处：build-arg 名不硬编码

这六个套件有**四种形状**：

    qa-hub-17 / qa-hub-19        无 ARG
    test643 / test688            SOURCE_COMMIT
    test635                      TEST635_SOURCE_COMMIT
    test671                      TEST671_SOURCE_COMMIT

所以 step 里是**从 Dockerfile 读**：

    while read -r name; do
      [ -n "$name" ] && BUILD_ARGS+=(--build-arg "$name=$GITHUB_SHA")
    done < <(grep -oE '^ARG [A-Z0-9_]+' "$DF" | awk '{print $2}')
    echo "detected build args: ${BUILD_ARGS[*]:-(none)}"

**为什么不硬编码**：我在 `test638-server-aggregate-isolation` 上栽过一次 ——
它的 ARG 叫 **`TEST639_SOURCE_COMMIT`**（目录 638、变量 639），我按 `SOURCE_COMMIT` 传，套件报

    FAIL: source provenance mismatch image=unset expected=unset

**那是调用错了，不是套件坏了。** 硬编码会让这类误用反复发生，
而且它的报错长得像「套件有问题」—— 最容易把人引向修一个没坏的东西。

那行 `echo "detected build args"` 是故意留的：**下次再出这种事，日志里直接看得见传了什么。**

## ⚠️ 不加 `--network none`

基线就是这么跑的。我在 test631 上踩过：断网让它 `rc=1`，
**那是跑法造成的红，不是套件缺陷**。不往 workflow 里写没验证过的变体。

## 触发路径

六个套件目录都加进 `pull_request` / `push` 两处。
**存在、挂上、会被触发是三件事**，今晚栽过一次（#1017 改了 test225 的夹具，
27 个 check 全绿而 CI 从没执行过它）。

## 本地已验

那段 ARG 检测逻辑我拿**真 Dockerfile** 跑过一遍，四种形状都解析正确；
step 的 bash 片段也过了 `bash -n`。

author: m9mike
body:
Sixteen of Bandit Keith's cards, most rewritten rather than adjusted.

## The cards

| Card | What it does now |
|---|---|
| **Barrel Dragon** | Once per turn, flip 3 coins. Each head: +100 ATK (permanent), then destroy 1 random monster they control — else 1 random Spell/Trap (Field Spell counts) — else they discard 1. |
| **Slot Machine** | Once per turn, roll 3 dice; if any two, all three, or all three with one subtracted total 7 → +700 ATK and DEF, permanent. Every destruction it faces, by battle or effect, re-rolls the same three dice. |
| **Machine King** | +200 per Machine on the field, +100 per Machine in his Graveyard, and a standing +400 to every Machine you control — live, not on summon. |
| **Blast Sphere** | Destroyed by battle: kill the attacker, destroy their whole backrow, and every Spell and Trap in their hand. No damage. |
| **Zoa** | Destroyed by battle or by effect: Special Summon 1 Metalzoa from hand or Deck. |
| **Metalzoa** | On summon also empties their hand of Spells and Traps; attacks at double ATK; halves whatever attacks it. |
| **Metalmorph** | +300 ATK, doubled when attacking, piercing. When the equipped monster is destroyed: Special Summon 1 Zoa from hand or Deck. |
| **Time Machine** | The revived monster gains 700 ATK if it is a Machine. |
| **Machine Conversion Factory** | Special Summon up to 2 Level 5 or lower Machines from hand; they gain 200 ATK. |
| **7 Completed** | Equips only to a Machine; +700 ATK, and it cannot be destroyed by battle **or** by card effects. |
| **Steel Ogre Grotto #1** | While you control another Machine it Special Summons itself from hand. Sent to the Graveyard: add 1 Pendulum Machine from Deck. |
| **Pendulum Machine** | Special Summon from hand by banishing 1 Steel Ogre Grotto #1 from your Graveyard. On summon destroy 1 Spell/Trap they control. +1250 ATK against a Defence Position monster, and it pierces. |
| **Ground Attacker Bugroth** | Sent to the Graveyard: add 1 Level 4 or lower Machine from your Deck — you pick. |
| **Cannon Soldier** | Once per turn, discard your entire hand (at least 1 card): destroy 1 monster you control, damage equal to its ATK. |
| **Robotic Knight** | On summon, +100 ATK for each Machine in your Graveyard. |
| **Mechanicalchaser** | On summon, +50 ATK for each card in either hand. |

The seven-from-three-dice odds are derived from the rule rather than tabulated, and come out at 132/216 — the 61.11% asked for.

## Engine support

Multi-coin flips with one tallied announcement; a seven-making dice roll that prints its working; a `cascade` that falls through to the first branch that can pay; a survival roll priced with the other costs rather than with the immunities; double-when-attacking and halve-the-attacker as flags the battle code reads; a bonus that only counts against Defence Position; whole-hand and banish-a-corpse costs behind the one gate the button and the AI both consult; and `onHostDestroyed`, so an equip can tell its monster dying from its own destruction.

## Fixes found while pinning these

- `Selector.filter` was silently ignored by `summoned`, `attacker` and `attackTarget` — a filter written on one of them was a sentence the engine could not read. No card was relying on the silence.
- The hand's self-summon button priced every such card at "discard 1" — true of the batch that introduced the trigger and of nothing since. It now reads the price, label and refusal off one shared gate.
- The AI had no self-summon route at all, so four cards across two decks could only ever arrive the slow way.
- `damage` declared a `destroyedAtk` scale that nothing read.

## Harness fixes

Each of these had been reporting a correct card as broken, or a broken one as correct:

- The text check now accepts `onDestroyed` for "destroyed by battle" (it fires on battle destruction too), and a battle-time flag for "when it attacks".
- The audit stocks a host an equip actually fits, re-rolls a gamble rather than excusing it, and fails a branch construct whose every branch is empty instead of filing it as unobservable.

Both widenings were falsified: a card that truly promises and doesn't deliver is still caught.

## Testing

1036 rules assertions, 481 audit checks, text/playable/picker/gods/banner/ra/premade/race all green, 400 simulated duels with no rule errors, and HTTP e2e + e2e-ai + e2e-tournament against a production build.

Every card change was falsified individually — 35 sabotages, each one confirmed to turn its own pin red naming the right thing, then restored. Five pins that came back green on the first pass were rewritten: four were exercising engine flags I had set by hand rather than the cards themselves, and one tolerated a Barrel Dragon that flips no coins at all.

Lint is unchanged at 11 pre-existing problems (verified against a clean stash).

author: mnovelo
body:
## What happened

`PgBouncer tx-mode · PG 18` in run 32185297198 sat in `Install PgBouncer` for 18 minutes and had to be cancelled by hand. The identical step on `PG 16` finished the whole job in 45 seconds. On re-run, PG 18 passed in 49 seconds — so this was an apt mirror stall on the runner, not anything in the code under test.

Two things turned a transient stall into an 18-minute hang with nothing to look at:

No workflow in this repo sets `timeout-minutes`, so every job inherits GitHub's 360-minute default. And both apt calls used `-qq`, so after 18 minutes the log was empty.

It also blocks merges rather than merely wasting minutes: `ci-gate` declares `needs: [unit, postgresql, mysql, sqlite, pgbouncer]` and aggregates all five results, and the `main` ruleset requires `ci-gate`. A hung job leaves that check pending forever.

## What this changes

**Every job gets `timeout-minutes`**, sized well above its observed p100 from that run so a slow runner cannot flake it:

| Job | Observed | Cap |
|---|---|---|
| unit | ~30s | 10m |
| postgresql | ~2m | 15m |
| mysql | ~3.5m | 15m |
| sqlite | ~70s | 10m |
| pgbouncer | ~50s | 10m |
| ci-gate | ~3s | 5m |

**The install step is fixed at the cause, not just capped.** apt gets `Acquire::Retries=3` and a 15-second connect timeout, so an unreachable mirror fails and retries instead of blocking — a job cap alone would only have shortened the hang, not avoided it. `apt-get update` keeps its output so a future stall leaves something readable. `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive` removes the other classic hang. And the step carries its own 5-minute cap, roughly twenty times what the install actually takes, so the ceiling is a last resort rather than the mechanism.

## Not included

`rubocop.yml`, `security-scan.yml` and `gem-publish.yml` also lack timeouts. They are short and have not misbehaved, and adding them would mean reasoning about three more workflows to fix one observed failure. Easy follow-up if you want the whole set covered.

## Verification

The YAML parses and both changes are where they should be — six jobs carrying `timeout-minutes`, the install step carrying its own plus the apt options. The real proof is the next PgBouncer run on this branch, since that is the job the change is aimed at.

author: evanspn
body:
Everything here came from using 1.0 on the hardware.

## The bottom nav was unreadable on any library with more than one page

A screen carrying the four tabs cannot also put First/Prev/Next/Last in the bottom strip — same strip, both drawn, so the bar read `Library First TodayPrev DisCoveNr Sesttings`.

Paging is now the **page indicator itself**: `‹ 2/3 ›` at the right end of the title bar, each chevron a title-bar-height tap zone. One `title_pager_zones` feeds drawing and hit-testing, and it is checked ahead of everything else the bar does, so a chevron can never toggle the library view by accident. No extra row, so the shelf keeps its row of covers.

## Today is the landing screen

It opens on the chapter you were mid-way through and what is waiting unread. The Library is one tap away — and it is a destination that replaces the root, not a pushed screen (which is what briefly took the nav bar away).

## The lamp is in the quick sheet

Brightness and night warmth as sliders above the tiles. A tap sets the level to where you tapped, rounded so the track's middle is 50 and its end is 100. No lamp, no sliders — a control that cannot do anything is worse than none. Levels persist through the existing `PersistedLights` wrapper.

## Colour in blocks the filter can carry

Section headings sit on a wash of the profile's accent instead of carrying a tick beside them, and the accent marks are ~50% wider. The colour layer resolves at half the black resolution, so a 2px mark is a grey smudge on the panel however clean it looks on a monitor. The wash is derived from each profile's accent rather than stored per profile, so a new profile cannot forget it, and it is pinned light enough to hold black text.

## The MAL metadata was never going to arrive, and now refreshes on a cadence

`cache_series_metadata` only ran on the tail of a *download*, and only for a series already in the index — so anything sideloaded over USB, or downloaded before that code existed, kept `meta: None` forever. That is most of a real library, and it is why score, status and genres are blank on the device while the mockups show them.

`backfill_series_metadata` fills them in for series the library already holds. A sideload gets a minimal index entry so the metadata has somewhere to live, with its source fields left empty — inventing a source would make it look downloaded. It runs in the background at launch, does nothing offline, never fails outward, and is bounded to 8 lookups per pass so opening a 200-book library is not 200 requests.

Metadata is then **stored with the manga and trusted for a fortnight** (`SeriesMeta::fetched_at`). A score and a genre list do not move; the chapter count does when chapters land, and a score can slide after a bad ending. Cached-before-the-stamp reads as due once, then falls into the cadence; a stamp from a wrong clock reads as just-fetched rather than as an age of two billion seconds.

## Profiles are a sheet

Switching profile is something you do to what is already on screen, and it was handing you off to a full-screen list styled like nothing else left in the app. The active one is marked with the word "reading" rather than a 6px dot — the first thing the colour filter eats.

**No profile data path changed**: same `switch_profile`, same library directories, same progress store, same settings files, same default-profile conversion. Only the picker's drawing and hit-testing moved.

## The test that should have existed

Three of the defects above are one statement: *on a top-level destination, the bottom strip belongs to the nav bar and to nothing else.* `every_top_level_destination_owns_its_nav_strip` walks all four tabs in both library views, with enough series to paginate, renders the nav bar alone onto a blank page, and requires the screen's strip to match it pixel for pixel. Extra ink fails, missing ink fails, and a "destination" that turns out to be a pushed screen fails.

It found a fourth on its first run: `goto_root` left an open sheet up, so navigating with the quick sheet raised left it floating over a screen it says nothing about, covering that screen's nav bar.

## Verification

Full workspace suite green on both feature sets (338 tests), clippy clean under `-D warnings`. Every screen was rendered at 1264×1680 and looked at, paginated and not, in both library views.

author: vshulcz
body:
Found by the night hunt, iteration 70, from the hypothesis list after 35: the invariant written in prose at `warmup_status.go` — *"Written whole and renamed: a reader must never see half a record."*

It held for one writer. The temp name was derived from the destination, so two writers shared it — and two is ordinary, since two agents starting together each spawn a detached `deja index`. One truncates what the other is renaming. Measured before the fix, four writers and one reader on the status file:

```
reads 18049, empty 5, unparseable 180
```

Every one of those told the agent nothing was building while a build was running: `readWarmupStatus` returns nil on a record it cannot decode, and then `buildingNowForAgent`, the brief and the status line all go quiet — in the one state that sentence exists for. After: `reads 12031, empty 0, unparseable 0`.

New `internal/atomicfile` writes to a unique temp beside the destination and renames. Asking where else the same cause lives found four more writers with no lock excluding them, and review named three of them:

- the usage log's rotation and the snapshot file — the one part of deja that is lock-free by design, where a torn publish loses the whole window rather than the one event the design accepts losing;
- the embedding sidecar, which `EmbedIndex` writes without a lock;
- the notes rewrite behind `deja remember` and `deja forget`.

Everything under `lockDir` is left alone: the lock is what excludes the second writer there, and its fixed temp names are fine.

One thing the unique name costs: it is never reused, so a process killed between creating it and renaming leaves a file behind where the fixed name would have been overwritten. `sweepStale` clears siblings older than an hour, once per directory per process — a live temp file belonging to another writer is not touched.

`TestForgetPromotedTitlesKeepsTheNotesFileOnFailure` forced its failure by putting a directory where the temp file would go. That trick was the bug, so the test now makes the directory read-only instead, and skips where that does not hold.

Tests: four writers publishing only whole records, the same for the warmup status through its real flush path, no temp left after a failed rename, the caller's mode kept, and stale temps swept while live ones are not. Six mutations verified, two of which caught blind tests.

author: jbtk-cell
body:
Everything that would have failed quietly after a public launch. Every defect below was found by driving the deployed site — axe-core over both themes, Playwright blocking specific hosts, and pulling the network down mid-session — not by working through a checklist.

## What was broken

| Found | Effect | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python came from one CDN | jsDelivr is DNS-blocked across mainland China and on many school networks. Blocked means no course at all, since every exercise needs the interpreter. The only signal was `Failed to fetch dynamically imported module` in 11px type. | Four sources, each probed with an 8s deadline so a blackholed host cannot eat the boot budget. Total failure now gets a panel that explains it and offers a retry. |
| The editor swallowed Tab | A keyboard-only learner could enter the editor and never leave it. WCAG 2.1.2 Level A — the only exit was closing the tab. | Escape then Tab moves on, stated on screen under the editor. |
| Contrast failed WCAG AA | Muted text in both themes, and white-on-vermilion at 3.07:1 on the primary button, the skip link and the progress ticks. | Tokens recomputed against the lightest surface each sits on. The button label became a per-theme token: 6.08 dark, 5.21 light. |
| "Works with the wifi off" was false | The service worker precached the shell only, so the trace panel, the tracer and all 74 lesson files existed offline only if already visited. Offline at lesson three meant no lesson four. | The whole curriculum is precached from the manifest, about 400 KB. |
| Screen readers heard "Not yet" | The reason lived in a panel nothing announced, so a blind learner could not tell why an answer was rejected. | The announcement carries the first failing check and its message. The trace slider reports which line each step is on. |
| Old browsers got a blank page | Module workers need Chrome 80, Safari 15, Firefox 114. | A `nomodule` fallback, plus a lazy probe that names the cause when boot fails. |

## Two things that were missing rather than broken

**Safari and Firefox were never tested.** Foothold leans on a module worker, a dynamic import inside it, and WebAssembly compilation — the three things those engines shipped later than Chrome. Both pass today: Python boots, a program runs, the trace records. `tools/check_engines.mjs` now keeps it that way as a third CI job.

**There was no privacy statement.** The front page said "nothing you write is sent anywhere" and it was true, but an IT administrator cannot approve a tool on a sentence in a hero. `PRIVACY.md` names the two requests that leave the device on first load, the two `localStorage` keys that stay on it, and why a child cannot be identified. For institutional adoption this is the blocker, not paperwork.

## Also added

A content security policy; PNG and maskable icons so Android offers to install and iOS stops screenshotting the page; `robots.txt`, a sitemap, a canonical link and Course JSON-LD; a 404 that returns people to the course; a report link on every lesson that prefills the issue template; `SECURITY.md`, `CITATION.cff`, a changelog, and Dependabot on the pinned actions.

## Holding it in place

`tools/check_access.mjs` runs in CI: axe-core over both themes, a lesson completed on the keyboard alone, what a screen reader is told, the CSP under enforcement, jsDelivr blocked, every source blocked, and the network pulled down to confirm an unopened lesson still opens.

## Verified

- `validate.py` — 60 lessons, 14 modules, parser parity
- `test_tracer.py` — pass
- `lint_prose.py` — 0 errors
- `smoke_test.mjs` — 38/38
- `check_in_browser.mjs` — 60/60 solutions pass in Pyodide
- `check_access.mjs` — 22/22
- `check_engines.mjs` — 10/10 in WebKit and Firefox
- Mobile at 390px and 412px: no horizontal scroll, no page errors

One thing needs a human: the GitHub repo social preview can only be set through Settings, not the API. `web/assets/social.png` is the file to upload.

body:
test_owner_lock_allows_renamed_pipeline and every other test in TestCheckpointSync, plus test_iceberg_ordered_resume_skips_ingested, have hung in CI waiting for /completion_status or /checkpoint_status to report done on a multihost pipeline that had, per /stats, already finished (feldera/cloud#1897 is the same shape). The completion/checkpoint counters are updated correctly and published to the coordinator's watch channel, but the coordinator's cached view of them can go stale if the underlying h2 stream stalls without erroring.

Turn on h2=trace,actix_http::h2=trace (via the pipeline's `logging` runtime config, which both the pipeline and coordinator processes read) to capture frame-level state -- window updates, send capacity, wakers -- for whichever stream gets stuck next time this reproduces.

I've tried running this several times in CI but haven't managed to reproduce the hang yet, so I'm proposing to merge this for now until we figure out the real problem; then, after we fix it, we can revert this.

- Grey at zero was explained as *"you haven't opened your bank this session"*. That stopped being true once bank contents were remembered between sessions.

Both spotted from screenshots of the current build rather than from reading the code.
